HarvestBossIntroTwo.text: Behold, the first daughter of Wraeclast.

HarvestBossCombatFour.text: Your flesh will nourish the soil!

HarvestReBossIntroOne.text: Exile... I was wrong. It cannot be controlled.

HarvestReBossIntroTwo.text: It must be destroyed. I must be destroyed!

HarvestReBossIntroThree.text: Lifeforce... corruption... it is all the same.

OshabiHighLevelIntroduction.text:
I am Oshabi, a child of the Azmeri. I was born on Wraeclast, I have lived my whole life on Wraeclast, and I will die on Wraeclast. And when that day comes, with its blessing, I hope I will stay dead. 

We Azmeri are few, but when the land's whispers grew silent, my brothers and sisters turned their backs on me. In that, Exile, we have something in common.

I have made this long journey in search of one like yourself. You possess might and power. Though you are in no need of a job, I have one to offer you anyway. 

On your journeys, you may come across a blister in the land, within which hide seeds. Seek these seeds out, and when you do, I will seek you out.

OshabiHighLevelFirstMissionOne.text: These are the very seeds we discussed. Take the seeds and follow me. I have something to show you.

KuraiTownIntro.text: My apologies, Exile, but I'm waiting for someone. Perhaps you could attend to the needs of the others here.

KuraiAccessGranted.text:
Do I hear the clink of markers in your pockets? Claimed from one of your victims, or perhaps from the victim of one of your victims. It is impossible to know how far back that chain could unwind, but now they belong to you, and you seem to be in good health. To the victor, et cetera. It seems you are the one I have patiently waited for. Yes, you will do just fine. 

Take a marker in your hand. Speak these words into your mind: The Ring binds us all, and to all within I shall do no harm.

I will see you soon.

KuraiHubIntro.text:
Welcome, Exile, to the Ring. I am Kurai. While you are here, you will do no harm to any of its members. You are a guest of the Ring, and the Boss has no tolerance for guests who do not obey his rules. What goes around, comes around, if you will excuse the aphorism.

Take your time and look around. Introduce yourself to the others here. When you are ready, find me. The Ring has a job for you, if you are willing.

KuraiTheRing.text:
The Ring operates outside whatever semblance of the 'law' remains out here. But lawlessness does not exclude civility, and does not need to create chaos. If someone is intent on taking what is not theirs, better to have a professional handle it and avoid unnecessary violence and confusion. 

The Ring is contracted by those who seek a solution to the... misallocation of resources. We assign members based on the needs of the job, and we take a small cut. Everyone wins, other than the target of our work.

KuraiFirstMission.text:
A client wishes to utilise our services. The Boss would like to offer you the opportunity to assist member Karst on this job. There is room yet in the Ring, if you can handle the work. The details are on the contract. I suggest you review it before you set off.

Speak to Adiyah when you are ready. She will get you within range of the mark.

And try to keep your partner safe, so he may do what he is best at. Karst is not as tough as he believes, but the Boss has never seen another Lockpick as talented.

KuraiFirstMissionComplete.text:
I hope you enjoyed your first job. Karst spoke highly of you. Well, he did not outright speak poorly of you, which, for Karst, means a great deal. 

The items you procure should be exchanged with Faustus for markers. In addition to allowing entry onto Ring premises, markers can be redeemed with the residents of the Ring for various goods and services, including Blueprints. Please, do not hesitate to speak to me if you need further elucidation.

I suggest you return to your ordinary duties, whatever they may be, until another Contract crosses your path.

KuraiSeals.text: The Ring operates based on favours. Markers allow us to track those favours, and to ensure no one is taking advantage of, or being taken advantage of, by any other Ring member. They are also how you got here. You'll excuse me if that seemed obvious. At times I must deal with people whose talents are... not intellectual in nature.

KuraiContracts.text:
What is valuable to you or I may not be valuable to the Boss or Faustus. Where you see a worthless trinket, another may see a precious heirloom, or the final piece in a life-long collection. Contracts allow our clients to hire the Ring to pursue goods that hold no objective value on the client's behalf. Sometimes that value comes from knowing the original owner no longer has it. 

The Ring makes few moral judgements on what it is hired to obtain. So long as it is not breathing and it is not liable to put the entire Ring at risk, we will not turn a contract down. And neither should you.

KuraiBlueprints.text:
Though Contracts allow the Ring to keep spinning, we are skilled professionals, and skilled professionals wish to test the limits of their skills. The Ring has obtained the layouts of locations known to hold objects of great value. Naturally, these locations are heavily protected and patrolled, and to pull off a job in such a location requires a team. 

The Boss is happy to provide blueprints for these highly secure locations and access to the skills and resources needed to strip such a location bare... for a price. Complete contracts, earn markers, and you will be able to utilise those services.

KuraiTheBoss.text: The Boss is an extraordinarily busy man, so I enact his orders and allocate tasks to members as needed on his behalf. I am, for all intents and purposes, his administrator. If you have any issues, please take them to me and I can raise it with The Boss when he is available.

KuraiVoxTwins.text:
The Vox family has enjoyed a place among Oriath's nobility for several generations, but in recent years, Victario and Vincent Vox have used coercion, blackmail, and violence to ensure the family sits at the centre of Oriath's business and social ecosystem. The twins enjoy a legitimate public persona, all while they bury their hands deep in the criminal underworld.

The Boss would, of course, love to see the Vox criminal enterprise dismantled. The Ring competes with the Vox crime family for many of the same jobs. But removing competition is secondary to freeing hard-working families from their looming threat. The Boss is shrewd, not heartless.

KuraiDominus.text: Dominus was a terrible human being, but the Ring owes a great debt to him. Without his overzealous exilings, the Ring would not have a rich pool of talent to draw upon. The Boss himself learned a great deal about the power of anonymity and mythos from Dominus. Lessons he employs today.

KuraiKaom.text:
A king is human, mortal, vulnerable to the same temptations and vices as are we all. A legend lives on for as long as it is told, its meaning and message shifting to fit the needs of the speaker or the audience. Kaom seems to have found himself stuck somewhere in the middle. 

The greatest lesson to take away from the story of the fallen Karui king is this: A leader is nothing without the loyalty of their followers. And, I suppose, that those followers should still have their heads attached.

KuraiOriath.text: I do not like to talk about my younger days, except to say that I did what I had to in order to survive, and I am glad that time is behind me.

KuraiOriathPostFall.text: While I feel for those lost in the wake of Oriath's fall, forgive me if I do not shed a tear for the city which, even now, fills my nights with terror.

KuraiTheGods.text: It takes a lot to surprise me, but I must admit, I did not expect to contend with the divine in my lifetime. It goes to show that there's a seed of truth in every story.

KuraiContractOne.text:
You've got a contract I have taken out. Excuse me if you know the tale, but I find a well-informed thief is a better thief. 

A few hundred years ago, Kaom, a Karui king of note, landed on the shores of Wraeclast and began an ill-fated conquest north. He won a decisive battle against the Eternals with the help of his niece, Hyrri. She and many other women took up bows and ambushed General Lioneye when hubris got the better of him. It was an ingenious workaround of a restriction of the Karui Way. 

The poet Victario was present at the battle and later gifted Hyrri with a signed copy of "O' Eternal", one of his works. It now sits in the vault of an Oriathan nobleman. I'd like you to bring it home. It should be a straightforward job.

KuraiContractOneCompleted.text:
You got the book. Some moisture damage, but otherwise it seems to be in good condition.

<italic>{To my Karui Queen,
The Ngamakanui rose has never been so beautiful
nor its thorns so deadly.
Let your aim never waver,
And your story ever be told.}

Thank you. I'll make sure it finds its way back to Ngamakanui, where it belongs.

KuraiContractTwo.text:
This job is a bit... unorthodox. Do you recall the book I had you rehome? Well, its owner was quite fond of it. He took out a contract and, it seems, wants to negotiate for the book's return. 

I don't wish to involve The Boss in this, since the original contract was mine. I'm going to travel with you to meet the client to make sure there's no funny-business.

KuraiContractTwoVicToKuraiOne.text: Well would you look at that. Didn't think you'd come in person! How are you, lady Kurai? Did you enjoy the book?

KuraiContractTwoKuraiToVicOne.text: We can skip the pleasantries, Vox.

KuraiContractTwoVicToKuraiTwo.text: If you wish for this to be unpleasant, so be it. I want my book back.

KuraiContractTwoKuraiToVicTwo.text: <italic>{The} book is no longer in my possession.

KuraiContractTwoKuraiToVicThree.text: Where it belongs. Are we done?

KuraiContractTwoVicToKuraiFour.text: Kurai, Kurai, Kurai... Don't you feel you're being unfair? You did, after all, break into my home. You took something which I value. O' Eternal. A first edition. Signed by Victario himself. My parents, rest their souls, were so fond of his work that I was named after him! Am I not owed some sort of... reparations?

KuraiContractTwoVicToKuraiFive.text: I want <italic>{my} book. And since you don't have it... Kurai, I presume this is the thief? I know you don't do your own dirty work.

KuraiContractTwoVicToKuraiSix.text: Tell you what... You can keep the book. Give me the thief's head, and we'll call it even.

KuraiContractTwoVicToKuraiSeven.text: I am deadly serious. Kill them. Now. In front of me.

KuraiContractTwoVicToKuraiEight.text: Then I will consider the theft an act of aggression against the Vox family. An act of war.

KuraiContractTwoKuraiToVicEight.text: You leave me no choice. I'm sorry, Exile. Victario Vox... it appears we are now at war.

KuraiContractTwoVicToKuraiNine.text: A stupid decision by a weak little girl.

KuraiContractTwoKuraiToVicNine.text: Goodbye Mr. Vox. And regards to your brother.

KuraiContractTwoVicToKuraiTen.text: Every war has casualties, Kurai! Any bloodshed is on you!

KuraiContractTwoCompleted.text:
I should have known better. The meeting was pointless from the start. It was a distraction, Exile. They took Hana, my cat, and left a note saying they would be in touch. It was all just a setup. 

This is only the beginning, I fear. I'm deeply sorry that I got you involved.

Be careful.

KuraiContractThree.text:
The Vox twins are offering to return Hana and negotiate a truce, so long as we are willing to meet them in person once more. I doubt this meeting will be any more useful than the last. In fact, we may be walking into an ambush, but I want Hana back. I've put all members on high alert while we are gone, and Adiyah is ready to help us escape if it comes to that.

We'll go when you're ready.

KuraiContractThreeVinnyToVicOne.text: Look, brother! At last, the guest of honour has arrived, with company.

KuraiContractThreeVicToVinnyOne.text: The weak little girl brought her big strong bodyguard!

KuraiContractThreeVinnyToKuraiOne.text: You were <italic>{meant} to come alone! What's wrong Lady Kurai? Are you afraid of us?

KuraiContractThreeVinnyToKuraiTwo.text: You kept us waiting so very long that we got bored. We decided to pass the time. We were playing with little... Hana, was it?

KuraiContractThreeVicToKuraiOne.text: Lovely name. Beautiful cat. And so affectionate!

KuraiContractThreeVinnyToKuraiThree.text: Very affectionate! And we were having such a pleasant time with her! But then things took a turn!

KuraiContractThreeVicToVinnyTwo.text: Hana swiped at us. Attacked us. We don't like being attacked, do we Vinny?

KuraiContractThreeVinnytoVicTwo.text: Not at all. Beautiful little Hana was being vicious. Mean.

KuraiContractThreeVinnytoKuraiFour.text: So we did to Hana what we do to anyone who attacks a Vox.

KuraiContractThreeKuraiToExileTwo.text: Do you see them anywhere? I--... Oh... oh no. No, no, no...

KuraiContractThreeVicToKuraiTwo.text: Hana attacked her betters. She crossed a line. Do you see, Lady Kurai? Do you <italic>{understand}?... Hellooooo? Are you deaf?

KuraiContractThreeVinnyToKuraiFive.text: Good. Then we have a proposal for you. Very favourable. A truce, as long as you never interfere in Vox business again. ... Lady Kurai?

KuraiContractThreeKuraiToVinnyThree.text: ... I have a counter-proposal. How about we kill you, Vincent. And you, Victario. How about we kill both of you, and every member of your wretched family. How about <italic>{that}? How does <italic>{that} deal sound!?

KuraiContractThreeCompleted.text:
Vic and Vinny are monsters, Exile. Monsters. They terrorise anyone who does not submit and swear fealty. <italic>{They killed Hana}. 

When it comes to business, The Boss does not normally take personal feelings into consideration, but he has made an exception here. He wants the Vox family dead. Plans are in motion. Stay alert.

KuraiContractFour.text:
We have been monitoring communications in the Vox crime family for some time. Vic and Vinny have been careful to remain separate, so as not to invite an ambush, but we believe they are uniting very soon for a celebration. 

This is the best time to strike. Please ready yourself.

KuraiContractFourBeginning.text:
The Boss expects we will face enormous resistance. If you wish to back out, speak up. I will understand.

...

...Thank you. Everyone.

KuraiContractFourVinnyToKuraiOne.text: Lady Kurai? How nice of you to join us.

KuraiContractFourVicToKuraiOne.text: Unfortunately, the party has drawn to a close.

KuraiContractFourVinnyToKuraiTwo.text: But the fun is just beginning!

KuraiContractFourKuraiToVoxsTwo.text: You petulant, overgrown children! Today you face justice.

KuraiContractFourVicToKuraiTwo.text: All this... f-...for a book? For a cat?

KuraiContractFourVicToKuraiTwoAlt.text: Enough, enough! You win... what do you want?

KuraiContractFourVinnyToKuraiThree.text: All this... f-...for a book? For a cat?

KuraiContractFourVinnyToKuraiThreeAlt.text: Enough, enough! You win... what do you want?

KuraiContractFourCompleted.text:
Death cannot bring back the dead, but it can bring peace to the living. The Vox family was a source of anguish for more people than I care to mention. With the twins gone, their hold on civilian life is relinquished, at least for now. The increased business we will now receive is a simply a happy coincidence. 

And I know, somewhere in Hinekora's hallowed halls, Hana is sinking her claws deep into Vox flesh.

The Boss has authorised me to give you a bonus. Thank you again, Exile.

KuraiFarewellFiveA.text: I'll be here when you need me.

KuraiFarewellFiveB.text: I'll be here when you need me.

KuraiFarewellFiveC.text: I'll be here when you need me.

TullinaIntro.text: I'm Tullina. Not Tully, not Lina, not Lin, not even Tee. Tullina, got it? Good. If you know when to speak and know when to keep your mouth shut, we'll get on just fine. I'm here to make bank, not friends, and I'm very good at what I do.

TullinaAboutTheBoss.text: The Boss is private to the point of paranoia. I've never visited his home, but I've heard he has some very particular requests of his guests. No boots. No cloaks or coats. No hats. No slacks. No dresses. Undergarments are strongly discouraged. You're given a robe for privacy. It has no sleeves. You're never to enter his kitchen or approach him from behind or from the side. Or above. Absolutely never above. No mention of approaching him from below, but I've also heard he lives underground, so that would be quite a task.

TullinaContractOne.text:
Look, as a rule I don't ask for help. I don't need someone getting involved in my business and messing everything up. Unfortunately, I must now break that rule. I need... I-... Ugh. Why is this so hard? Ineedyourhelp. There. I said it.

Before I was exiled, I was romantically involved with a man from a very good family. We kept it secret while he tested the waters with his mother and father -- it's not exactly ideal for the nobility to be fraternising with the 'uncouth', as they say. Less than a week before I was heaved overboard and my exile began in earnest, he proposed. 

I know it's crazy, and I know it's almost certainly impossible, but I want so desperately to marry that man. Just taking his name would wash clean my past, and I know I could find happiness. 

So I need a dress. When Merveil and Daresso wed, they held a most elaborate ceremony. Merveil was said to be the most beautiful visage ever to walk down the Basilica aisle. It took six people to carry the train on her dress. I want that dress. I need that dress. My beloved deserves to see me in that dress. So you're going to help me get it, got it?

TullinaContractOneEnd.text:
The Lady Merveil's dress is even more beautiful than I'd imagined. It's held up well over the years, and fits nearly perfectly. 

I appreciate your help on this matter. I'll add you to our invitees. No plus-ones.

TullinaContractTwo.text:
I'm fine. Sorry, I mean, hello. But, really, I'm fine. I don't need your help. 

...Wait. 

I... I do need your help. It's time to face reality. The wedding's off. Given our wildly different lifestyles, it no longer seems possible for my fiance and I to live happily ever after. Whakano has kept abreast of his movements, and, though he has remained faithful, he is... unhappy. I don't think it's because they have locked him up in an attempt to draw me out, but it couldn't have helped. I miss him dearly, and he misses me, but we cannot meet in person without jeopardising his safety or my freedom. He needs to move on, and so do I. 

I want to return our engagement ring. He'll understand. I cannot bear to do it myself, hence the contract. 

...Please?

TullinaContractTwoEnd.text:
So... it's done. We're done. I feel... absolutely awful, actually. But I also feel lighter. He will no doubt grieve for a long time, and will, of course, never find another woman that meets the lofty bar I set, but he will meet someone eventually. He will fall in love. He will propose to her. She will be delighted. They will marry and start a family, and they will have their happy ending. It was the right thing to do, for both of us. 

Thank you for your help, and your discretion. I'm keeping that dress, by the way. Lady Merveil's? That's mine now.

TullinaSelectedforContractOne.text: You need the best? Well here I am.

TullinaAgilityFive.text: Okay, Tullina, just like you practised.

TullinaDisarmTrapOne.text: I see what they've done here...

TullinaLockpickFour.text: This might take some time, okay?

TullinaLockpickFive.text: I can do it, but it won't be quick.

TullinaBusyThree.text: Perhaps you should've planned this better.

TullinaBusyFour.text: I can't be in two places at once.

TullinaInterruptedOne.text: If I wasn't busy you'd be dead.

TullinaInterruptedThree.text: I can't work while I'm being attacked.

TullinaCombatStartTwo.text: We've got a fight on our hands.

TullinaCombatStartThree.text: You want to dance? Let's dance.

TullinaCombatEndFour.text: We have a job to do.

TullinaLootThree.text: Good find, but don't lose focus.

TullinaLootFive.text: Not bad. Not bad at all.

TullinaAlertThresholdThree.text: Clumsy work is going to get us caught.

TullinaAlertThresholdFour.text: Messy. I don't like where this is headed.

TullinaAlarmOne.text: Head for the exit. Quick as possible!

TullinaEarlyAlarmTwo.text: We've screwed this up. Time to leave!

TullinaEarlyAlarmThree.text: Ugh, what a mess. What an absolute mess.

TullinaFinalRoomOne.text: We're here, but it isn't over yet.

TullinaFinalRoomTwo.text: Good. Now, take it and get ready to run.

TullinaFinalRoomThree.text: Ready? This is where it gets hairy.

TullinaFinalRoomFive.text: That's the mark. You got it?

TullinaObjectiveLootedThree.text: Don't get overconfident. We're not done yet.

TullinaEntryBanterExileOne.text: Most people think I don't like small talk...

TullinaEntryBanterExileTwo.text: Hope you know what you're doing.

TullinaEntryBanterExileThree.text: On a job like this, careful maneuvering is key.

TullinaEntryBanterExileFour.text: Limbered up and ready to go.

TullinaEntryBanterExileFive.text: Once we get in there, we have to have each other's backs.

TullinaExitBanterExileOne.text: Not as smooth as I'd hoped, but not too bad!

TullinaExitBanterExileTwo.text: Well done! Not as messy as I'd feared!

TullinaExitBanterExileThree.text: That could've gone better, but it could have gone a LOT worse!

TullinaExitBanterExileFour.text: If you plan on working with me in the future, you ought to get used to the feeling of success.

TullinaExitBanterExileFive.text: Ah, that's one for the books.

TullinaAgilityLoudFive.text: This is what you've been training for!

TullinaAgilityLoudSix.text: Fine, but you should know I hold grudges!

TullinaTrapDisarmLoudThree.text: I think I've got this one figured out!

TullinaTrapDisarmLoudFour.text: Even without this racket, it'd take me a while...!

TullinaTrapDisarmLoudFive.text: I'll be as quick as I can, but that still won't be quick.

TullinaTrapDisarmLoudSix.text: Wish we'd sorted this before we had to run!

TullinaLockpickLoudFour.text: This is going to take some time!

TullinaLockpickLoudFive.text: Just keep us safe while I work!

TullinaLockpickLoudSix.text: You just make sure we're all still alive when I'm done.

TullinaBusyLoudFive.text: Not now! This mess is on you!

TullinaCombatStartLoudFour.text: You must not value your lives!

TullinaLootLoudOne.text: If we die because you slowed us down, I'll kill you!

TullinaLootLoudThree.text: Fine, but we have to keep moving!

TullinaLootLoudFour.text: You're pushing it! Not in a good way!

TullinaLootLoudFive.text: The stealing was meant to happen earlier!

TullinaFinalRoomLoudFour.text: We're not done yet! Grab it!

TullinaFinalRoomLoudFive.text: Get it! Now! What a mess...

IntroductionTullinaTibbsToExile.text: I've brought an old mate of mine along for this job. Her name's Tullina.

IntroductionTullinaTibbsToExileTwo.text: She might not look like much--

IntroductionTullinaTibbsToExileThree.text: --but she can get into places no one else can.

IntroductionNenetTullinaToExile.text: Before we set off, I'd like to introduce you to an associate of mine. This is Nenet.

IntroductionNenetTullinaToExileTwo.text: See? She's got better eyesight than anyone I know.

IntroductionNenetNenetToExileTwo.text: I can see a man's heart beat its last from a distance of two thrown stones.

IntroductionNenetTullinaToExileThree.text: I believe she will be an asset in the future.

EntryBanterTullinaToTibbs.text: Only do what's essential. Anything else makes you a bigger target.

EntryBanterTullinaTibbsReply.text: Not sure I could be a much bigger target...

EntryBanterTullinaToKarst.text: Remember, look out for each other when we get in there.

EntryBanterTullinaKarstReply.text: Yeah. Unless things get bad, then scramble.

EntryBanterTullinaToIsla.text: Keep it down when we're in there. That means no unexpected explosions, Isla.

EntryBanterTullinaIslaReply.text: Pfft. It was hardly unexpected. Just early!

EntryBanterTullinaVinderiReply.text: For the job? Or just generally...? I s'pose the answer to both is no, really.

EntryBanterTullinaToNenet.text: Any words of wisdom before we head in, Nenet?

EntryBanterTullinaNenetReply.text: The dead own nothing and feel nothing.

EntryBanterTullinaNilesReply.text: Luck is just another word for faith, which we all know is meaningless. You're telling everyone good nothing right now.

EntryBanterTullinaToExile.text: Remember what Huck says: Heads on a pike--

EntryBanterTullinaToExileThree.text: Kill any guards you come across quick.

EntryBanterTullinaGiannaReply.text: Uh, yeah, but make sure it isn't actually me.

EntryBanterTibbsToTullina.text: Nerves are gettin' to me again.

EntryBanterTibbsTullinaReply.text: Try not to focus on how badly everything could go and how hurt everyone could get. Better?

EntryBanterKarstToTullinaTwo.text: -- you got spare picks just in case, right?

EntryBanterIslaToTullina.text: Tullina, how do you feel about having large, electrified metal rods jutting from your spine?

EntryBanterVinderiToTullina.text: Who would like to hear my bordello story?

EntryBanterVinderiToTullinaTwo.text: I promise it is very, very graphic.

EntryBanterNenetToTullina.text: Time passes through us like a ghost.

EntryBanterNenetToTullinaTwo.text: There is no speed great enough to escape death.

EntryBanterNilesToTullina.text: Tullina, might I slip into that brain of yours for just a moment? I wish to feel lithe. Provocative.

EntryBanterNilesTullinaReply.text: Do you also wish to feel a dagger in your eye socket? No? There's your answer.

EntryBanterHuckTullinaToExile.text: And stay out of my way.

ExitBanterTullinaTibbsReply.text: Agreed. I've seen how bad it can get.

ExitBanterTullinaKarstReply.text: Yeah, round of applause, then a round of drinks.

ExitBanterTullinaToIsla.text: That went as smooth as could realistically be expected.

ExitBanterTullinaIslaReply.text: Smooth... Smooth... Hey, Tullina, what about a helmet that dissolves your hair while you wear it?

ExitBanterTullinaToIslaTwo.text: ...I need less of you right now.

ExitBanterTullinaVinderiReply.text: No, we're all still quite separate.

ExitBanterTullinaNenetReply.text: By our unity, we escaped with our lives.

ExitBanterTullinaToNiles.text: Let's get back and enjoy the fruits of our labour.

ExitBanterTullinaNilesReply.text: Oh, how one quivers with anticipation at the thought of such sweet fruits.

ExitBanterTullinaToHuck.text: That was one I'll be telling my kids about.

ExitBanterTullinaHuckReply.text: Seems irresponsible to tell your kids about your robberies.

ExitBanterTullinaHuckTwo.text: Hmm. You're right. That was one I'll never tell my kids about.

ExitBanterTullinaToGianna.text: I can already tell I'll be sore tomorrow.

ExitBanterTullinaGiannaReply.text: That reminds me! Tullina, I simply must know your workout regiment. Your core is to die for.

ExitBanterTullinaToAdiyah.text: Adiyah, get us home to a cold drink and a warm fire.

ExitBanterTullinaAdiyahReply.text: I can get you to a stale mead and several scattered lanterns. Will that suffice?

ExitBanterTibbsTullinaReply.text: And barely any spiders are on you this time!

ExitBanterKarstToTullina.text: Nothin' like a good job well done, eh?

ExitBanterIslaToTullinaTwo.text: No reason. Totally unrelated, how upset would you be if everything you owned was shredded by a rogue mechanical spider?

ExitBanterVinderiToTullina.text: I always get a little sad when a job like this ends.

ExitBanterVinderiTullinaReply.text: It's alright, Vinderi. There will be more.

ExitBanterVinderiToTullinaTwo.text: I know, I know... But I really enjoyed this one.

ExitBanterNenetToTullina.text: The snakes leave the rabbit's nest bare and barren.

ExitBanterNenetTullinaReply.text: You should write that down, Nenet. That was beautiful.

ExitBanterNenetToTullinaTwo.text: I do not have a diary, and do not dare look for it!

ExitBanterNilesToTullina.text: Glorious, glorious, glorious. I sup the wine of victory from fate's breast.

ExitBanterNilesToTullinaTwo.text: When we return, I shall paint it for you. A gift.

ExitBanterHuckToTullina.text: I love it when a plan comes together.

ExitBanterHuckTullinaReply.text: Savour it. It doesn't happen all that often!

ExitBanterGiannaToTullina.text: A stellar performance! Five stars! Two thumbs up!

ExitBanterGiannaTullinaReply.text: Worth the price of entry, that's for sure!

ExitBanterAdiyahTullinaReply.text: Oh, come on Adiyah. I can see you holding back a smile.

ExitBanterAdiyahToTullinaTwo.text: No. That was... That was about something else. Please return now.

SelectionBanterTullinaToKurai.text: I'm here. Plans all drawn up?

SelectionBanterTullinaKuraiReply.text: Doing that as we speak. Did you want any input?

SelectionBanterTullinaToKuraiTwo.text: If you're overseeing them, I'm not too worried. Any word from the Boss?

SelectionBanterTullinaKuraiReplyTwo.text: Nothing specific, but he is aware of this operation, and he wishes us good fortune.

SelectionBanterTullinaToTibbsTwo.text: You never were fond of heights.

SelectionBanterTullinaTibbsReplyTwo.text: Everything's just a bit higher up for me than most people.

SelectionBanterTullinaTibbsReplyThree.text: All the eyes and legs! Who needs that many?

SelectionBanterTullinaTibbsReplyFour.text: What're you supposed to do when a ghost attacks! Kill 'em? They're already bloody dead!

SelectionBanterTullinaToKarstThree.text: It's... complicated. I'd rather we just focus on the job, if you don't mind.

SelectionBanterTullinaKarstReplyFour.text: We'll have a catch-up later, ay?

SelectionBanterTullinaToIsla.text: Heard you might need me for a job?

SelectionBanterTullinaIslaReply.text: Only if I can't get my wall-crawler up and running in time.

SelectionBanterTullinaToIslaTwo.text: That sounds like some sort of horrifying mechanical spider.

SelectionBanterTullinaIslaReplyTwo.text: Couldn't be more wrong. It's a brilliant, beautiful mechanical spider.

SelectionBanterTullinaIslaReplyThree.text: No, but that's what this is for, right lady Kurai?

SelectionBanterTullinaKuraiToIsla.text: ...This is the first I've heard of your invention. May I suggest you bench it and we review its progress next time?

SelectionBanterTullinaVinderiReply.text: Tullina! I was just talking about you.

SelectionBanterTullinaVinderiReplyTwo.text: Yes. I was just saying to Tullina that I was talking about her.

SelectionBanterTullinaVinderiReplyFour.text: That reminds me! Did I tell you that I was just talking to Tullina? She says hello.

SelectionBanterTullinaNenetReply.text: We are to gain entry to this location and take everything we can carry.

SelectionBanterTullinaToNiles.text: Hope I didn't keep you waiting.

SelectionBanterTullinaNilesReply.text: What exquisite torture it is to wait for one as beautiful as yourself.

SelectionBanterTullinaToNilesTwo.text: Niles, do we really need to do this every time?

SelectionBanterTullinaToNilesThree.text: Or, I suppose, until I slit your throat?

SelectionBanterTullinaKuraiToBoth.text: Quiet. Both of you. Tullina, no more threatening Niles. Niles, stop making everyone uncomfortable.

SelectionBanterTullinaNilesReplyThree.text: Ha! I doubt I'm making everyone--

SelectionBanterTullinaToHuckTwo.text: The Sin is in the details.

SelectionBanterTullinaHuckReplyTwo.text: Don't I know it. The number of times I've seen an operation turn to chaos because we didn't know about a door--

SelectionBanterTullinaHuckReplyThree.text: --or even a door that is open when we expected it to be closed.

SelectionBanterTullinaToHuckFour.text: Well, I'm glad we can discuss doors in such detail.

SelectionBanterTullinaToGiannaTwo.text: Anywhere but here. Meetings make me fidgety.

SelectionBanterTullinaGiannaReplyTwo.text: I've always kind of enjoyed them. Feels like I only really get to talk to you during these meetings.

SelectionBanterTullinaToGiannaThree.text: That can't be true. What about...

SelectionBanterTullinaToGiannaFour.text: ... Huh. Sorry... If it helps, it's nothing to do with you. I guess I'm not much of a people-person.

SelectionBanterKuraiToTullinaTwo.text: New contracts are coming in steadily, but today we're planning something larger.

SelectionBanterKuraiToTullinaThree.text: Mmhm. The latest information indicates it will be quite lucrative.

SelectionBanterKuraiTullinaReplyThree.text: Well, I'm keen. If you'll have me, that is.

SelectionBanterKuraiToTullinaFour.text: The boss is always eager to have you involved.

SelectionBanterTibbsToTullinaThree.text: I still have those nightmares. I wake up feeling like I'm covered in spiders.

SelectionBanterTibbsTullinaReplyThree.text: Well now we know to look for webs. And eggs. And legs. And, if it happens again, I'll put you out of your misery. Sound good?

SelectionBanterKarstToTullina.text: Tullina and Karst, together again at last! How ya doin' beautiful.

SelectionBanterKarstTullinaReply.text: A little anxious, but, you know...

SelectionBanterIslaToTullina.text: I've just had the best idea.

SelectionBanterIslaTullinaReply.text: We're actually in the middle of--

SelectionBanterIslaToTullinaTwo.text: Picture a wall, but completely transparent. You can stand on one side and see everything on the other side, but you can't touch it.

SelectionBanterIslaToTullinaThree.text: That's--, no, that's different. Windows are different. This is larger and more transparent. You're just not getting it. Just forget about it. What's your thing?

SelectionBanterVinderiToTullinaTwo.text: Ah! Isla, how are your brilliant inventions?

SelectionBanterVinderiToTullinaThree.text: Wonderful. Is that some new slang term?

SelectionBanterVinderiToTullinaFour.text: These plans are absolutely, what was it? Tullina? These plans are tullina, pal!

SelectionBanterVinderiToTullinaFive.text: Thank you for introducing me to this tullina new word, Isla.

SelectionBanterNenetTullinaReplyTwo.text: Another job is in the works.

SelectionBanterNenetToTullinaFour.text: Then I will watch in silence. Proceed.

SelectionBanterNilesToTullinaTwo.text: What a pleasure to be called into service by your side.

SelectionBanterNilesToTullinaThree.text: But it remains my pleasure, and for that, I simply must thank you.

SelectionBanterHuckTullinaInteruptThreeA.text: I was just going to ask--

SelectionBanterHuckKuraiToBoth.text: How about we just have a little quiet time, hmm?

SelectionBanterGiannaToKurai.text: Plans look to be progressing nicely. Lady Kurai, while I'm here, has the Boss' schedule opened up at all?

SelectionBanterGiannaToTullinaTwo.text: Shame... Tullina, would you mind running lines with me later?

SelectionBanterGiannaTullinaReplyTwo.text: I was planning to take a nap...

SelectionBanterGiannaTullinaReplyThree.text: ..but I suppose I can squeeze you in beforehand?

AdiyahIntroForFemale.text: I am Adiyah. You may rely on me for travel to and from locations of interest.

AdiyahIntroForMale.text: I am Adiyah. I will enable your travel to and from locations of interest.

AdiyahHarbourForFemale.text: This place runs foul with thieves, cutthroats, and loudmouths. They cannot be trusted. You and I will have to work together to avoid errant knives.

AdiyahHarbourForMale.text: This place runs foul with thieves, cutthroats, and loudmouths. I am likely the only one here that would not betray you for coin.

AdiyahAboutBoss.text:
I once served a worthy Sekhema. The Boss is no Sekhema. He rules through deception, obfuscation, and manipulation. However, if he agrees to do something, he will do it. That in itself is a form of honour which I can respect.

He expects the same of us. In exchange for a place here, I have agreed to use my skills to enable the travels of this wretched heap of rhoa dung, and that is what I will do. My word is my bond.

AdiyahTravelTwo.text: Where would you like to go?

AdiyahTravelFive.text: I hope everyone knows the plan.

AdiyahCombatEndFour.text: I am uninjured. I can continue.

AdiyahContractOneStart.text:
This contract touches upon my very reason for being here. It concerns my sister, Nashta, and a Spear. Growing up, Nashta was unable to follow the traditions of our people. She chafed at the rules. She earned many tattoos of shame for her violations, and each time she was punished, she only grew more rebellious.

Not long ago, she fled from the Plains of Vastiri entirely, and scores of delinquents went with her. They have since terrorised many with their banditry, but duty required I track her down when she stole Solerai's Spear from a Sarn merchant of ill repute. I live among these thieves and scoundrels because this is her world, and in this place I hear more about her activities in a single moon than I would in a year spent looking for her on my own.

We must retrieve the Spear. We cannot allow her to wield a weapon of Maraketh tradition in so disrespectful a manner. This is my duty, as Nashta is my sister. This contract makes it your duty as well.

AdiyahContractOneEnd.text: This Spear is a tremendous weapon, one fit for a goddess. The merchant Hargan expects its return, but he shall be disappointed. When I bring it home to my <i>{akhara}, our honour will be partially restored in the eyes of our fellow warriors. You did well, Exile.

AdiyahContractTwoStart.text:
My sister, Nashta, and her bandits have responded to our retrieval of Solerai's Spear by targeting their raids against other Maraketh caravans. That in itself is not shameful, but she is doing so while wearing the colours of my <i>{akhara}. She is trying to start a war among our people, and we can hardly afford conflict when our survival already hangs by a thread.

You and I must infiltrate her stronghold and retrieve her war plans. With that proof, we can ensure that the Sekhemas know who is truly to blame.

AdiyahContractTwoEnd.text: This war journal contains exactly what I hoped. This, combined with my word, should be enough for the Sekhemas to believe that Nashta is acting on her own. I thank you, Exile.

AdiyahContractThreeStart.text:
I know my sister. Nashta responds to adversity by invigorating her resistance, not backing down. We retrieved Solerai's Spear and thwarted her attempt to spark a civil war among the Maraketh, but that will only cause her to up the scale of her banditry. We must face her before she causes a disaster that our people can ill afford in these dangerous times.

This will not be a matter of stealth, exile. Be prepared to fight if she will not listen to words.

AdiyahContractThreeToNashta.text: Nashta! It is time to come home.

AdiyahContractThreeNashtaReply.text: You know I cannot, sister. My soul yearns for freedom!

AdiyahContractThreeNashtaReplyTwo.text: I cannot live under those tyrants.

AdiyahContractThreeToNashtaThree.text: I understand. I will give you the only freedom I can.

AdiyahContractNashtaPhaseTransition.text: I would rather die than go back!

AdiyahContractThreeToNashtaFour.text: You fought well, Nashta. I am proud of you.

AdiyahContractThreeEnd.text:
This was the best end I could have wished for Nashta. I think it was what she always wanted: not to live under the heavy oppression of a rigid set of rules, but to die fighting, as a true <i>{dekhara}. In death, by standing and fighting, she has cleared her shame. She will be remembered as a woman filled with the irrepressible spirit of the warrior, one with so much aggression that she had no place in this civilised world.

I will retrieve her body. Leave me now. I have some final things to say to my sister that are not for a <i>{jingakh} to hear. Go well, my friend.

AdiyahGossipAboutNenet.text:
Nenet is from a people that currently call themselves the Faridun. They are our rejects. Those we Maraketh left to die in the desert as children for being unworthy or flawed. I do not think ill of Nenet. I do not think of her at all.

I am not cruel, exile. It is simply that scattered groups of pariahs wandering in the desert have no effect on the world. She will not find the home she yearns for among these scoundrels.

AdiyahGossipAboutHome.text:
I prefer not to name my <i>{akhara} in the presence of these persons of ill repute, but I can say that I am from the northern reaches of the Plains of Vastiri. My home caravan has ninety-two carts, all of which are beautifully set with colourful tapestries and shaped metal. It is a life and land unlike this one. Difficult, duty-bound, but rewarding. I will return there someday, when my duty here is at an end.

I still owe a debt to the Boss for allowing me a place here. Nashta may be dead, but I will stay here for a few more moons.

ExitBanterTibbsAdiyahReply.text: This way, Mr Tibbs. A warm bath awaits you.

ExitBanterTibbsAdiyahReplyTwo.text: We are not strangers. Countless bubbles.

ExitBanterAdiyahToTibbs.text: It appears you met great success.

ExitBanterAdiyahToTibbsTwo.text: I am pleased for you, Mr Tibbs.

ExitBanterNenetToAdiyah.text: Left any children to die lately, Maraketh?

ExitBanterNenetAdiyahReply.text: Not personally. I prefer to cook and eat them.

ExitBanterNenetToAdiyahTwo.text: So you admit you are evil!

ExitBanterAdiyahToNenet.text: Why do you hide your face, Faridun?

ExitBanterAdiyahToNenetTwo.text: Certainly it cannot be that bad?

ExitBanterAdiyahNenetReplyTwo.text: My own mother was willing to abandon me over it.

ExitBanterAdiyahToNenetThree.text: The desert is a harsh Sekhema.

ExitBanterNilesToAdiyah.text: Have I ever told you that your mind is incredibly ordered?

ExitBanterNilesToAdiyahTwo.text: Or oppression. I know a little about that.

ExitBanterAdiyahToNiles.text: Niles, do you still reject the gods?

ExitBanterAdiyahNilesReply.text: You cannot reject that which does not exist!

ExitBanterVinderiToAdiyah.text: You've got fire magic, don't you, Adiyah?

ExitBanterVinderiAdiyahReply.text: I do. I use it sparingly.

ExitBanterVinderiToAdiyahTwo.text: Where do you draw it from? Is it in the palms? The fingers? If your hand were accidentally severed, could it still light a flame?

ExitBanterVinderiAdiyahReplyTwo.text: I prefer not to answer that.

ExitBanterAdiyahToVinderi.text: How did your explosions fare, Vinderi?

ExitBanterAdiyahVinderiReply.text: They went off with a bang! Which was quite a lot quieter than I'd intended, actually...

ExitBanterGiannaToAdiyah.text: You've got quite the stature, Adiyah. Have you ever considered acting?

ExitBanterAdiyahHuckReply.text: Always happy to see your portals, Adiyah. And... Call me Huck.

ExitBanterKarstToAdiyah.text: Adiyah, you've never looked more lovely. Take us home, yeah?

ExitBanterKarstAdiyahReply.text: Of course. It is my duty.

ExitBanterAdiyahToKarst.text: Did it go as planned? Any injuries? Karst?

ExitBanterAdiyahKarstReply.text: I'm fine, beautiful! Top o' the world!

OtherBanterWhakanoAdiyahReply.text: I do not have tattoos, Karui, because they are marks of shame or criminality.

TibbsIntro.text: Round here, people call me Tibbs. Not the quietest little sneak, and I'm not exactly nimble with these big sausage fingers, but if you find yourself on the wrong side of something heavy, you'll wish you thought to hire me.

TibbsAboutBoss.text:
Heard the Boss got his start as a stable boy in the Grand Arena. Used to feed and care for the chariot horses. That was his first job, and it led to his first ... err, 'job'. 

Apparently, someone asked him to slip something into the feed of the Octavius family's finest stallion, greatly favoured to win the race. Paid him a week's worth of his normal wages. Boss figured it was some sort of poison. So he watched the man place a bet, and poisoned that horse as well. Neither died, but neither won, and the Boss, betting his wages on a horse he knew to be fit as a gladiator, took home a killing. 

'Course, that was also his last day of gainful employment at the arena. The man stalked those stables for months trying to find him.

TibbsContractOne.text:
Ah, my contract! A man of my build gets a lot of attention. By the time I was thirteen, I was taller than most adults. By my next birthday I was invited to join a little circus of sorts as the strongman. That's where I met Tullina, by the way.

One day, someone left a baby girl, named Opal, for the troupe leader. She had bright red eyes, but the most pale skin and whitest hair I'd ever seen. She became a sort of daughter of the whole troupe. We took turns looking after her. 

By the time she was about seven, I'd grown quite attached to her, and she to me. The hardest part of being exiled is not knowing what has happened to her. So I want to find out. I know the troupe is disbanded, so I just want to make sure she's found a good home.

TibbsContractOneEnd.text:
Well, it ain't great news. Templar took an interest in her because of her unique traits, but she dropped off the map before they could get her. Good instincts. 

I have a hunch that she might've found some of the old troupe members. I'll see what Whakano can dig up.

TibbsContractTwo.text:
Got an update on Opal! She's living on the fringes with some of the old troupe, like I thought. Tough people to track down, but at least I know she's safe. 

I want to keep it that way. I want to make sure she doesn't need to put herself at risk to work or eat, so we're going to do what is, essentially, the opposite of a bank robbery. We're breaking in to leave enough wealth for her to live safely out of harm's way in a vault under a pseudonym.

TibbsContractTwoEnd.text:
I know I'm a lot poorer than I was a few days ago, but I feel like I've done some real good. Opal's a smart kid. She'll put that money to good use. Better than I would've anyway.

Thanks, Exile. Really.

TibbsSelectedContractOne.text: Just don't ask me to help you move.

TibbsSelectedBlueprintThree.text: Hey, as long as I don't have to do any of the planning...

TibbsForcingObstacleFour.text: Lemme jus' get this outta the way for ya.

TibbsForcingObstacleSix.text: Oh, I'm going to be sore tomorrow.

TibbsDemolitionFour.text: If it ain't broke, it will be...

TibbsDemolitionFive.text: This one might take a bit, but we'll get there.

TibbsDemolitionSix.text: I think it'd look better in pieces too.

TibbsBusyTwo.text: In the middle of something here.

TibbsBusyFive.text: When I'm done with this, yeah?

TibbsCombatStartFour.text: Hate this part of the job.

TibbsCombatStartFive.text: You're gonna be sorry. Then I'm gonna be sorry.

TibssCombatEndOne.text: Right, well, carry on I guess.

TibbsLootingThree.text: Now who just leaves something like that lying around?

TibbsLootingFive.text: Oh, know a girl who'd love that.

TibbsAlertThresholdTwo.text: I'm gettin' a bad feeling, mate.

TibbsAlertThresholdThree.text: Reckon we're cutting it close now.

TibbsAlertThresholdFour.text: Right, we gotta make tracks soon.

TibbsEarlyAlarmThree.text: Now you've gone and done it.

TibbsFinalRoomOne.text: Think this might be what we're after.

TibbsFinalRoomThree.text: Right, let's nab it and go.

TibbsFinalRoomFour.text: Here we go. Make it quick.

TibbsObjectiveLootedThree.text: Now we just gotta make it out alive!

TibbsEntryBanterOne.text: Always get butterflies before a job...

TibbsEntryBanterTwo.text: Whew, I'm sweating. Just nerves. Just harmless nerves.

TibbsEntryBanterThree.text: I always think this time I won't get nervous, and I always do.

TibbsEntryBanterFour.text: Come on, Gil. You've got this. Easy as. Eeeaaasy as.

TibbsEntryBanterFive.text: You ever get the feeling--... Nah. Nevermind.

TibbsExitBanterTwo.text: We bloody did it mate! We bloody did it!

TibbsExitBanterThree.text: Yes! I'm comin' home with the goods!

TibbsExitBanterFour.text: Honestly, for a while there, I thought we were done for.

TibbsExitBanterFive.text: I'ma be sore tomorrow for sure! Good sore.

TibbsForcingObstacleLoudFive.text: I'll do my best, but damn!

TibbsForcingObstacleLoudSix.text: I'm taking the longest, bubbliest damn bath after this!

TibbsDemonlitionLoudSix.text: This is gonna leave a mark!

TibbsInterruptedLoudOne.text: I can't work under these conditions!

TibbsCombatStartLoudFive.text: "Go on Tibbs, you're a big guy!"

TibbsCombatEndLoudTwo.text: Part of the job. Part of the job.

TibbsLootingLoudTwo.text: Better be worth the delay, mate!

TibbsLootingLoudFour.text: Your greed better not get us killed!

TibbsFinalRoomLoudFour.text: That's our mark! Grab it and go!

EntryBanterTibbsKarstReply.text: Why would you say that!? Now you've definitely jinxed us.

EntryBanterTibbsToIsla.text: Stick to the plan and this'll be quick and easy.

EntryBanterTibbsIslaReply.text: That's genius! If we make the plan sticky, we're less likely to drop it. I'll jot that down!

EntryBanterTibbsVinderiReply.text: Reddy! I'd always wondered what your first name was. Teddy Ribbs. Got it.

EntryBanterTibbsToNenet.text: It never goes as bad as you expect. Remember that.

EntryBanterTibbsNenetReply.text: I expect us all to die. Any better than that is a victory.

EntryBanterTibbsToNiles.text: Check your gear, say a prayer, whatever you need to do before we go in.

EntryBanterTibbsNilesReply.text: A prayer? I might as well ask the Solstice Rhoa for an albino egg! Equally absurd!

EntryBanterTibbsToHuck.text: Remember the target. Don't get too sidetracked.

EntryBanterTibbsHuckReply.text: Sound advice for life in general, really.

EntryBanterTibbsToGianna.text: Safety first. If it gets too dangerous, leave.

EntryBanterTibbsGiannaReply.text: Helps to know you're looking out for us, Tibbs.

EntryBanterKarstToTibbs.text: Try not to hit your head on the way in, ay big boy?

EntryBanterKarstTibbsReply.text: Thanks for the... heads up! ... Nothing?

EntryBanterNenetToTibbs.text: There is death on the wind. Beware.

EntryBanterNenetTibbsReply.text: Not the sort of thing I like hearing before a job.

EntryBanterNilesToTibbs.text: Tibbs, could you please lower your anxiety? It's seeping into my brain.

EntryBanterNilesTibbsReply.text: Maybe you shouldn't be snooping around in there.

EntryBanterHuckToTibbs.text: What's the rule, everyone? Be efficient, and...?

EntryBanterGiannaToTibbs.text: How's my scary voice? You there! I'll break you in half!

EntryBanterGiannaTibbsReply.text: Ehh... Sorry Gianna. Maybe practice that one more.

ExitBanterTibbsToKarst.text: Can't believe we pulled that off. Even Karst did good!

ExitBanterTibbsIslaReply.text: Tibbs, are you left or right handed?

ExitBanterTibbsIslaReplyTwo.text: So the evil reflection is still at large...

ExitBanterTibbsToVinderi.text: I think we've all earned an evening off.

ExitBanterTibbsVinderiReply.text: And if anyone else gets sad when they're alone with their thoughts, I'll be at the bar!

ExitBanterTibbsToNenet.text: I had a terrible feeling about this earlier. So glad I was wrong.

ExitBanterTibbsNenetReply.text: The day is not done yet. Our 'friends' back home might backstab us to take our spoils.

ExitBanterTibbsToNiles.text: That could've gone a lot worse!

ExitBanterTibbsNilesReply.text: And of course it was because of some god's intervention, right? So predictable.

ExitBanterTibbsToNilesTwo.text: ...what did I even say to warrant that? Honestly.

ExitBanterTibbsToHuck.text: Nearly more loot than I can carry!

ExitBanterTibbsToGianna.text: Good job everyone, let's head back.

ExitBanterTibbsGiannaReply.text: Thanks for keeping us all safe, big guy.

ExitBanterKarstToTibbs.text: Good stuff! Let's celebrate! First round is on Tibbs!

ExitBanterKarstTibbsReply.text: Fine, but you're only getting pondwater, Karst.

ExitBanterIslaToTibbs.text: Barely any malfunctions and plenty of data.

ExitBanterVinderiToTibbs.text: Gods I feel so young again! Tibbs! Let me lift you up!

ExitBanterNenetToTibbs.text: I believed we would face our deaths in there. I am glad to have been wrong.

ExitBanterNenetTibbsReply.text: Wait... You thought we were going to die?

ExitBanterNenetTibbsReplyTwo.text: And you didn't want to tell us?

ExitBanterNenetToTibbsThree.text: I did not see the need.

ExitBanterNilesToTibbs.text: This was a wondrous return to the glory days of the Templars.

ExitBanterNilesToTibbsTwo.text: Well, all the killing and mind-crushing. It was... nostalgic.

ExitBanterHuckToTibbs.text: Gravicius himself couldn't have planned a better operation.

ExitBanterHuckTibbsReply.text: You've set the bar pretty low, mate.

ExitBanterGiannaToTibbs.text: We did it! Three cheers! Hip-hip?

SelectionBanterTibbsToKurai.text: Heard you could use a bit of muscle!

SelectionBanterTibbsKuraiReply.text: The Boss is always happy to have you involved, Tibbs. How are your nerves?

SelectionBanterTibbsToKuraiTwo.text: Every time, I think I might get used to the stress, but...

SelectionBanterTibbsKuraiReplyTwo.text: I understand. Please look after yourself.

SelectionBanterTibbsKuraiReplyThree.text: That includes physically. You start feeling the wear and tear of the work, you tell me, understood?

SelectionBanterTibbsToKarstTwo.text: Do we have to do this every time?

SelectionBanterTibbsKarstReplyTwo.text: Oh c'mon. Just havin' a little fun.

SelectionBanterTibbsKarstReplyThree.text: Tibbs is so tall, that he... uh... He's so tall, that...

SelectionBanterTibbsKarstReplyFour.text: Just wait. He's so tall... that...

SelectionBanterTibbsKarstReplyFive.text: ... Look how tall Tibbs is everyone!

SelectionBanterTibbsToKarstFive.text: Good try, champ. Now we grownups can focus on the job.

SelectionBanterTibbsIslaReply.text: The usual. Steal ALL of the THINGS!

SelectionBanterTibbsToIslaTwo.text: My favourite kind. You bringing any new gadgets with us?

SelectionBanterTibbsReplyTwo.text: Afraid not. The bone decoupler decoupled itself. The test bone is fine, though there are now several thin metal strips deeply embedded in it.

SelectionBanterTibbsIslaReplyThree.text: Gave me an idea for intra-muscular springs. Tibbs, would you like to test something with me after this job?

SelectionBanterTibbsVinderiReplyTwo.text: Tight! Ribs! Err, right! Tibbs! I've got a new formula for you to try.

SelectionBanterTibbsVinderiReplyThree.text: Just like the last one, but I've enriched the quicksilver with Chimeral blood. Really gives it a kick.

SelectionBanterTibbsVinderiReplyFour.text: Just don't give it an actual kick.

SelectionBanterTibbsToVinderiFive.text: Good. I won't. Thank you for the warning.

SelectionBanterTibbsToNenetTwo.text: I always worry I'm late, even when I'm early.

SelectionBanterTibbsNenetReplyTwo.text: You worry about much. Why is that?

SelectionBanterTibbsToNenetThree.text: That... is a really tough question to answer.

SelectionBanterTibbsNenetReplyThree.text: I never worry, because the worst has already happened to me. This isn't even my life. It's just a shadow. Do you worry about stepping on your shadow?

SelectionBanterTibbsToNenetFour.text: Wow, Nenet, you're really quite profound. Anyone ever told you that?

SelectionBanterTibbsNenetReplyFour.text: Not my mother, that's for certain.

SelectionBanterTibbsNilesReply.text: Are you sure? Are there no... large words I should explain to you?

SelectionBanterTibbsToNilesTwo.text: Niles, do you think I'm stupid because I'm strong?

SelectionBanterTibbsToNilesThree.text: You think that a strong man cannot be a smart man, eh? The two are somehow mutually exclusive?

SelectionBanterTibbsToNilesFour.text: You're a mindreader, right? How about you jump on in here and have a look around.

SelectionBanterTibbsNilesReplyFour.text: I-... I rescind my statement. I apologise for my preconceived notions.

SelectionBanterTibbsHuckReply.text: Joining us on this job, Tibbs?

SelectionBanterTibbsHuckReplyTwo.text: That's a relief, honestly. Normally I'm the largest target.

SelectionBanterTibbsToHuckThree.text: Ha! You're still a plenty big target.

SelectionBanterTibbsHuckReplyThree.text: I look like Kurai next to you!

SelectionBanterTibbsGiannaReply.text: Tibbie! Always love a job with you.

SelectionBanterTibbsToGiannaTwo.text: Thanks Gi. How was your date with--

SelectionBanterTibbsGiannaReplyTwo.text: Uhh, yeah, that was... a mistake.

SelectionBanterTibbsGiannaReplyThree.text: Well, let's just say he looked a lot more than he listened.

SelectionBanterTibbsToGiannaFour.text: Ah. Well, always more men in the sea.

SelectionBanterKuraiTibbsReply.text: Thanks, Ku. How's the Boss doing?

SelectionBanterKuraiToTibbsTwo.text: Busy. Stressed. Worried for the safety of those in his care.

SelectionBanterKarstToTibbsTwo.text: Oh! You're workin' this job too?

SelectionBanterKarstTibbsReplyTwo.text: Yeah? Wait, what did you--... No, you know what, nevermind.

SelectionBanterKarstToTibbsThree.text: Guess the blood struggles to get all the way up to 'is brain, eh? eh?

SelectionBanterIslaToTibbs.text: Made it! Had to put out a small fire, but I made it.

SelectionBanterIslaToTibbsTwo.text: No, sadly someone beat me to that invention a long while ago. And this particular fire completely engulfed my heat-powered-exo-strider.

SelectionBanterIslaToTibbsThree.text: Exo-strider. Yes. Put a few burning embers in the converter and off you stride! Just a prototype made of cheap materials, scrap metal, wood, oil-soaked rags--oh, dammit, Isla! You're better than this.

SelectionBanterVinderiToTibbsTwo.text: Never better, never better. Spent the last hour in a very enclosed space with far more voltaxic sulphite than I've ever laid eyes on before, and I must say, I do not see what all the fuss was about. So, what's this we're looking at. Some sort of cuboid creature? Where's the heart?

SelectionBanterVinderiToTibbsThree.text: Did it step in paint? Can we just trace the prints back and find its nest?

SelectionBanterVinderiToTibbsFour.text: Ah! A job! I see it now. Yes. Good. This means I'll need to prepare more sulphite.

SelectionBanterNenetToTibbsTwo.text: I see you also, large man. These plans appear adequate.

SelectionBanterNenetKuraiReply.text: Thank you, Nenet. Can you be of service?

SelectionBanterNenetToKuraiThree.text: Always for you, lady Kurai. It would be a great honour.

SelectionBanterNenetToTibbsFour.text: Mister Tibbs, do you ache in your large skeleton?

SelectionBanterNilesToTibbs.text: I'm here, no need to make a fuss.

SelectionBanterNilesToTibbsTwo.text: And to you. You know, I've always wondered, where do you get your clothes?

SelectionBanterNilesTibbsReplyTwo.text: Actually, I make them myself. Started sewing at a young--

SelectionBanterNilesToTibbsThree.text: Fascinating. To see a man of your stature wield a sewing needle must truly be something to behold.

SelectionBanterNilesTibbsReplyThree.text: I mean, I can show y--

SelectionBanterHuckTibbsReply.text: Hey mate. Hey, how come you're always in your armour, even around here?

SelectionBanterHuckToTibbsTwo.text: Ah, blackguard training. Never leave yourself undefended. I used to sleep with my blackguard kit on. Got to the point where I couldn't sleep without it.

SelectionBanterHuckToTibbsThree.text: Hah, no, no... I've a lighter chainmail for bedtime.

SelectionBanterGiannaToTibbs.text: Fingers crossed this one goes better than our sewer scrape, eh, Tibbie?

SelectionBanterGiannaTibbsReply.text: I've got a change of clothes laid out just in case.

SelectionBanterGiannaToTibbsTwo.text: Did you ever find out where those busts were?

SelectionBanterGiannaToTibbsThree.text: That was a lot of platinum!

SelectionBanterGiannaToTibbsFour.text: Could've bought an island with that platinum.

KarstFirstMission.text: 'Ello rookie! Found a few markers, did ya? Apparently the Boss sees somethin' in you, but we won't know for sure 'til you're on the wrong side of a lance. I'm Karst, and there's not a lock in this world that I can't open. All you have to do is make sure I live long enough to open 'em. Adiyah'll get us to the job, and I'll show ya the ropes. Don't get tangled in 'em, 'cause it ain't my job to cut you free.

KarstEnterArea.text: First things first; Client wants us to find an urn. Reckons the mark has it locked up. Thing is, it's pretty suspicious if that's the only thing that goes missing. Not really our problem, but taking heat off the client makes us look good, and we get to keep whatever else we find. Get where I'm going with this?

KarstFirstDoor.text: I'll pick any locks that get in our way. You keep me alive, yeah?

KarstDoorOpen.text: Hear that? We ain't alone. Place is crawling with guards. You're here to make sure they don't kill us both.

KarstAlertRaised.text: Consider your actions, yeah? We don't want too much attention.

KarstNearObjective.text: Urn's on the other side of this door. Grab it so we can get out of here.

KarstObjectiveObtained.text: Perfe--... Wait, hear that? We've been made. Grab what ya can and head out.

KarstAfterAlert.text: Back the way we came, rookie!

KarstAfterExit.text: We're still breathin, rook, so you ain't done half bad. Take that urn to Faustus, yeah? He'll sort you out.

KarstIntroduction.text: I'm Karst. Rather than waste my youth readin', I put that time to better use. Now I can pick just about any lock you're likely to come across.

KarstAboutTheBoss.text:
A man of style, the Boss. A thief of course wants to be rich and live a life of luxury, but once you hit a certain point of wealth, I imagine you might be motivated by other things.

Apparently, the Boss was living very comfortably indeed, but felt the need to challenge himself. He entered the First Bank of Theopolis in the middle of the day, entered the vault, and just started... movin' stuff around. Octavius family fortunes into the Maxius deposit box, Avarius riches split across every small safe, each of which he popped open as if there weren't even a lock on 'em. Mixing all the money up like it were caught in the tides. Then he goes and finds the records of deposits and withdrawals, and sets 'em on fire. Walks out like nothing happened.

Well, of course the bank puts the fire out, but the records are gone. So they notify all the big customers, telling them to come in with their copy of the deposit slips... and wouldn't you know it, they're gone too. 

No bloody idea how he pulled it off. 'Course, the bank and all the clients will deny it ever happened. Be foolish not to.

KarstContractOne.text:
Got my contract, do ya? Ran with some low-life criminal scum in the back alleys of Oriath in my younger days. Real good blokes. Loyal to the last, or so I thought. Right before I was exiled, they beat me half to death and took off with my finest lock picks. If I'd had 'em when the Law came for me, I probably wouldn't be here, so in a sense, I 'spose I should be thankful, eh?

Well I'm not. I want those picks back, and I spent a lot of markers to find out where they went. Now I know, and you're gonna help me get 'em.

KarstContractOneEnd.text:
Strange. I thought having these picks back would make me feel whole again, but... 

Well, it's not your problem, rookie. Not yet.

KarstContractTwo.text:
Been good having my old picks back. Real good. Just not good enough. It's like there's a lock inside me, and not even my beautiful antique picks can open it. But I been thinkin' about it long and hard, and I reckon I know what might.

Revenge.

One of me old crew recently got out of the game. Livin' a life of luxury now while everyone around him is suffering and strugglin' just to survive. That should've been my life, but he took it from me when he took my picks. I want to send him, and the rest of my old crew, a message. So, rather than take something, we're going to leave something. Something that'll put the fear of Sin into the lot of 'em.

KarstContractTwoEnd.text:
Bet you're wondering what happens now, eh? Interesting little toxin we left. Slowly fills the air, then the lungs. Never leaves the body. Just keeps building up. First you start feeling light headed. Then you start hearing things, start seeing things. Start getting paranoid. A day or two later, you feel tingly. The tingling turns to pain, and the pain keeps building until your heart just stops beating.

I'd wash your hands if I was you.

KarstContractThree.text:
Word of our last job has started gettin' round. Unfortunately, all the credit is goin' to an old rival of ours. That don't sit right with me. It's one thing to steal a man's property, but to steal a man's hard work? No, I ain't gonna let that stand.

So we're going to leave a little present at my ol' rival's abode. One of my prized lockpicks, dipped in the very same toxin.

KarstContractThreeEnd.text:
You know what, rookie? I do believe I feel whole again. It's only a matter of time 'til that old rival of mine suffers the same fate as my traitorous crewmate. With both the bastards dead, and my pick the only common thread, the message is crystal clear:

Don't steal from a thief.

IntroductionKarstToHuck.text: Forgot to tell ya, bringing this lug with us on this job.

IntroductionKarstToHuckTwo.text: He's an absolute nutter. Ain't ya Huck?

IntroductionKarstHuckReplyTwo.text: Not really? I suppose the Blackguard training did leave me a bit... rough.

KarstBlueprintSelectOne.text: Hope this ain't all on me.

KarstBlueprintSelectThree.text: Just don't get in my way.

KarstVaultcrackingFour.text: Curiosity always gets the better of me...

KarstSurpriseAlarmTwo.text: You hear that? That's your fault.

KarstFinalRoomOne.text: Got us here safe 'n' sound, didn't I?

KarstFinalRoomFour.text: Almost there. Don't screw it up.

KarstFinalRoomFive.text: I think this is what we're here for.

KarstObjectiveTwo.text: Aw, I wanted to hold it. Fine. Whatever. Let's just go.

KarstObjectiveThree.text: Is it just me or is this as good as it gets?

KarstEntryBanterTwo.text: Reckon I'll have a night out with the lads after this one. Can't remember the last time I blacked out.

EntryBanterNilesKarstMockingReply.text: Confidence, not cockiness, will ensure success.

ExitBanterVinderiToKarst.text: Wait, is this where we came in?

SelectionBanterKarstGiannaReply.text: Keep it in your tights, Karst.

IslaIntro.text: Got somethin' needs made? Or unmade? I can take 'em apart as fast as I put them together, sometimes faster. Or is it the other way 'round? I've had an idea just now for a spinning device that - oh, yes, my name is Isla. I'm an engineer. Welcome.

IslaAboutBoss.text: The Boss? Oof, it's inefficient to ask about the Boss. Believe me. You'll go round and round, a spinning gear 'na machine made of secret parts. The one thing you should never rely on is a mechanism you don't understand. It's liable to implode, or <i>{ex}plode. Neither is pretty when your arse is sittin' upon it hopin' to fly somewhere. The Boss put in an order for an air-sail once, for a job. Impossible, I told Kurai. Turned out it worked! It just didn't go with the poor sod we hired. It stayed with us in flames while he took to the skies. He achieved a perfect parabolic arc right onto the tower we were aiming for. Survived the trip, too, judgin' by the screaming. But getting back down? Oof, the Boss never ordered a falling machine. That's on him. Gotta think things through, mind you!

IslaContractOne.text:
<i>{You} want to work with <i>{me}? I didn't realize we were that close. This is fantastic! I'll need a partner to retrieve my early prototypes from the hands of the Templars. I made a series of precursor contraptions before I was exiled that would have led to some of my greatest achievements. If you can imagine it, my inventions could have done it... eventually.

I didn't realise who I was working for until it was too late. They seized my prototypes and exiled me for the damage I caused in the process of building them. What's a few implosions in the pursuit of progress? Or maybe it was the sea tide of acid... or the glowing rock that made people sick... oh, yes.

Care to help me steal those prototypes back?

IslaContractOneEnd.text: My inventions! My babies! I missed them so much. I would never have found the proper materials to recreate them here on Wraeclast, not with all the horrific creatures roaming about. Thank you, Exile!

IslaContractTwo.text:
As I studied the prototypes you helped me retrieve, I realized that they'd already been examined... by someone else. The Templars must have lied about declaring my work heretical. They're trying to build them for their own gain! I cannot imagine what disaster they'll bring upon us if they manage to do so.

We already have the prototypes, so now we must steal the designs they created based on them. We'll need to steal the blueprints for my Extreme Warmth Beam, my Storm Wooing Rod... hmm, the Mind Sublimator... and the Unbreakable, of course! I don't claim to be the most imaginative namer, but it is what it is. They're all related, eventually intended to be part of one single superweapon, so the designs should all be in one place.

Let's go retrieve those blueprints!

IslaContractTwoEnd.text: We did it, Exile, at least in part. The designs for the Unbreakable were missing... I fear that they may have begun construction on it. If they complete the Unbreakable, we'll never be able to... break it. Science deserves better masters than the Templars!

IslaContractThree.text:
My instruments have started going haywire. I believe the Templar have managed to build the Unbreakable, <i>{my} greatest achievement. Normally, I would be thrilled at seeing my work given life, but I have a feeling the Unbreakable will be used against us, not for us.

It's time to do some deconstruction. You're good at smashing things, yes? Then perhaps you can break the Unbreakable.

IslaContractThreeEncounterStart.text: Stop, in the name of science!

IslaContractThreeEncounterEnd.text: My baby... my proudest work... Wait! I still have the blueprints! Let's go, Exile!

IslaContractThreeEnd.text:
The Unbreakable has been broken. You know what that means, don't you?

The Templar didn't build it right. I'll have to continue my work to prove it can be done!

IslaSelectedContractOne.text: My mental gears are already turning!

IslaSelectedContractThree.text: Long as I can bring my gadgets.

IslaSelectedBlueprintThree.text: Just tell me where to build!

IslaEngineeringFive.text: You put the axle in, you take the ball-bearing out...

IslaEngineeringSix.text: Sometimes there's an elegant solution... sometimes.

IslaEngineeringSeven.text: I've got just the contraption for this!

IslaEngineeringLoudFour.text: Must go faster, must go faster.

IslaEngineeringLoudFive.text: Can't think with all that racket!

IslaDisarmTrapTwo.text: Let's throw a wrench in the works.

IslaDisarmTrapFour.text: Construction, deconstruction... it's all the same, in the end.

IslaDisarmTrapFive.text: A beautiful design. A shame I have to wreck it.

IslaDisarmTrapSix.text: Traps are the arse end of engineering. No artisanship.

IslaDisarmTrapLoudFour.text: I'm just going to smack it with a wrench!

IslaDisarmTrapLoudSix.text: I can't even hear myself think!

IslaCounterThaumaturgyFour.text: The mind is just another system of gears.

IslaCounterThaumaturgyFive.text: Your mental machinery is mine to mould!

IslaBusyThree.text: I'm in the middle of something.

IslaInterruptedTwo.text: Aren't you supposed to defend your engineer?!

IslaInterruptedFour.text: I can't think when I'm under attack!

IslaCombatStartTwo.text: Oh my, someone must do the fighting now.

IslaCombatStartThree.text: I hope you don't expect me to fight.

IslaCombatStartFour.text: A better plan would have avoided this.

IslaCombatStartFive.text: Not good. Not good at all!

IslaLootingFive.text: I believe they call that loot.

IslaLootingLoudThree.text: Now's not the time for looting!

IslaLootingLoudFive.text: Why are you doing that now?!

IslaAlertThresholdTwo.text: This clock is on the verge of chiming...

IslaAlertThresholdThree.text: We can afford no more unanticipated variables.

IslaAlertThresholdFour.text: We will be detected if we are not careful.

IslaAlarmOne.text: The clock chimes at the appointed hour!

IslaEarlyAlarmThree.text: Our design appears to have been flawed!

IslaFinalRoomTwo.text: Phase one complete. Acquire the treasure.

IslaFinalRoomThree.text: Remember, this is only the midpoint.

IslaFinalRoomFour.text: From the blueprints, I thought it'd be bigger.

IslaFinalRoomFive.text: I haven't even used half my contraptions yet!

IslaObjectiveLootedTwo.text: Apex of the plan accomplished. Now, to survive!

IslaEntryBanterOne.text: A strong plan is the best path to success.

IslaEntryBanterTwo.text: We can account for all the variables. No deviating!

IslaEntryBanterThree.text: I hope I get to use my contraptions.

IslaEntryBanterFour.text: Is this the part where we make nervous small talk?

IslaEntryBanterFive.text: You do know what you're doing, yes?

IslaExitBanterOne.text: The real treasure is the knowledge we gleaned along the way!

IslaExitBanterTwo.text: Does this mean we're friends now?

IslaExitBanterThree.text: Is this the part where we make relieved small talk?

IslaExitBanterFour.text: Plan, execute, success! I love logic!

IslaExitBanterFive.text: This has inspired an idea for a new invention!

SelectionBanterKuraiToIslaTwo.text: Unless you're thinking about one of your inventions.

SelectionBanterIslaToKuraiThree.text: It's not a major concern. The spores are currently harmless. Just have to be back to my devices before my vivarium germinates.

SelectionBanterIslaToNenet.text: Oh, Nenet, there you are. I had a minor breakthrough on that humanoid golem you asked for.

SelectionBanterIslaNenetReply.text: Why are you bringing that up here?!

SelectionBanterIslaToNenetTwo.text: The thing is, I can't get his movement right. He's as stiff as granite, which is to be expected. Also, he doesn't cook very well.

SelectionBanterIslaNenetReplyTwo.text: Sands swallow me, so that I die right here...

SelectionBanterNilesToIsla.text: Ah, Isla, our woman of science! It's the young ones that are wrong, not we.

SelectionBanterNilesToIslaTwo.text: The same thing I always rant about, my dear.

SelectionBanterNilesIslaReplyTwo.text: One of my machines detects divine energies. Divinity is real.

SelectionBanterNilesToIslaThree.text: Your machine is broken, and so are you!

SelectionBanterIslaToNiles.text: If I use two parts Voltaxic Sulphite with three parts Trarthan... oh my, who are you?

SelectionBanterIslaNilesReply.text: We've met a hundred times. We've gone on heists together.

SelectionBanterIslaToNilesTwo.text: Oh yes, yes, I have trouble with faces. Especially handsome faces.

SelectionBanterIslaNilesReplyTwo.text: Your thoughts... how vile! That is not how it works!

SelectionBanterIslaToNilesThree.text: The human body is just another machine, my dear... joints... pistons...

SelectionBanterIslaNilesReplyThree.text: You stay away from me, witch!

SelectionBanterVinderiToIslaTwo.text: The new moon approaches. Shall we have that competition of explosions we spoke about?

SelectionBanterVinderiIslaReplyTwo.text: My inventions aren't supposed to explode.

SelectionBanterIslaVinderiReply.text: I... I don't remember. Do you?

SelectionBanterIslaVinderiReplyTwo.text: Badwyth Nems? Is that Ezomyte? I'll write it down so I don't forget. Right under Vinderi. I think that's the tall lad.

SelectionBanterHuckToIsla.text: Good, Isla's here! A unit's only as good as its engineer, I always say.

SelectionBanterHuckToIslaTwo.text: Not that I... meant anything by that...

SelectionBanterIslaToHuck.text: You wanted to see me, Huck?

SelectionBanterGiannaToIsla.text: I'm here. Isla, will we be seeing some new inventions for this job?

SelectionBanterGiannaToIslaTwo.text: But you've tested them at least, right? ...Right? ...Isla?

SelectionBanterIslaToGianna.text: Can I bring my glowing red rocks along on this mission?

SelectionBanterIslaGiannaReply.text: The ones that make people sick?

SelectionBanterIslaToGiannaTwo.text: The rocks don't make people sick. It's the Corruption they leak that does that.

SelectionBanterIslaToGiannaThree.text: Wear a dress lined with six-inch-thick armour and you'll be fine.

SelectionBanterIslaGiannaReplyThree.text: Just what every man likes to see.

EntryBanterNilesToIsla.text: No useless prayers today. I put my faith in science!

EntryBanterIslaToNiles.text: Niles, have you thought about those interrogation devices I suggested?

EntryBanterNilesReply.text: There's torture, and then there's nightmare. You are a demon with a pleasant smile.

EntryBanterIslaToNilesTwo.text: You think I've got a pleasant smile?

EntryBanterHuckToIsla.text: I'll watch your back, keep you safe.

EntryBanterHuckIslaReply.text: How about you go in front instead of behind us?

EntryBanterHuckToIslaTwo.text: It was a figure of speech.

EntryBanterIslaToHuck.text: You can rely on my contraptions, Huck! Have no fear!

EntryBanterIslaHuckReply.text: Fear keeps a disciplined man alive.

EntryBanterIslaHuckReplyTwo.text: I'm never going to wear that infernal thing, Isla. Stop asking, I beg of you.

EntryBanterVinderiToIsla.text: Do we really need to infiltrate anything? Between you and me, Isla, we could just blow the whole thing up.

EntryBanterVinderiIslaReply.text: But then what would we take? Oh, the scrap! Of course!

EntryBanterIslaToVinderi.text: Just remember when we're in there, combustion is the mother of invention!

EntryBanterIslaVinderiReply.text: Never met the lad. Knew a concubine, though. Loads of children.

EntryBanterGiannaToIsla.text: You know what we could really use...?

EntryBanterGiannaIslaReplyTwo.text: --that focuses all the light to a white-hot point, and sets everything it touches on fire!

EntryBanterGiannaToIslaThree.text: Or just a normal mirror! For makeup!

EntryBanterIslaToGianna.text: I'll be watching your art. I'm not great with people.

EntryBanterIslaGiannaReply.text: Ah, but a watched rose never blossoms, my dear.

EntryBanterIslaGiannaReplyTwo.text: Thank you. But seriously, if you stare at me, we WILL be caught.

ExitBanterNenetIslaReply.text: Told you I'd never let anything happen to you.

ExitBanterIslaToNenet.text: Your skills and my inventions carried the day!

ExitBanterIslaNenetReply.text: It is remarkable how we beat the odds when we are together.

ExitBanterNilesToIsla.text: I... I really thought we were going to cash in our Markers on that one.

ExitBanterNilesIslaReply.text: Nonsense. A good plan always succeeds.

ExitBanterNilesToIslaTwo.text: How was that according to plan?

ExitBanterNilesIslaReplyTwo.text: Oops, did I not tell you the contingencies? No wonder you were terrified!

ExitBanterIslaToNiles.text: That was impressive. I should study your brain.

ExitBanterIslaNilesReply.text: Can you do that without drills?

ExitBanterIslaToNilesTwo.text: No drills, I promise. I could do it with a trepan.

ExitBanterHuckToIsla.text: At some point, after so many close calls, a man's gotta admit he's just tired.

ExitBanterHuckIslaReply.text: I could replace your muscles with pistons if you like.

ExitBanterHuckToIslaTwo.text: How about that? A second wind! I'm fine now, plenty fine.

ExitBanterIslaToHuck.text: Your chances for survival would have been much better with my Voltaxic-powered battle armour.

ExitBanterIslaHuckReply.text: That thing ripped a mannequin in half!

ExitBanterIslaToHuckTwo.text: I thought you were STRONGER than a mannequin...

ExitBanterIslaHuckReplyTwo.text: Oh, I am! I-, I am!

ExitBanterVinderiToIsla.text: This mission is going to be spectacular. I've got all sorts of explosives to set, and they'll never even see it coming.

ExitBanterVinderiIslaReply.text: We just did the mission. We're going home now.

ExitBanterVinderiToIslaTwo.text: You'll have to excuse me for a moment once we're back home, then.
