ExitBanterIslaToVinderi.text: What are you going to do with your share, Vinderi?

ExitBanterIslaVinderiReply.text: Try out new powders, of course!

ExitBanterIslaVinderiReplyTwo.text: No! It's MY share, and that includes any notes in it!

ExitBanterGiannaToIsla.text: I have to admit, engineer, you make quite the spectacle yourself sometimes!

ExitBanterGiannaIslaReply.text: If I'm not making people cower in terror from the inexplicability of my inventions, then I'm not really doing science right!

ExitBanterGiannaToIslaTwo.text: I have so much to learn about science...

ExitBanterIslaToGianna.text: If I copy what you did with your art, will I have the same effect on men?

ExitBanterIslaToGiannaTwo.text: First thing I'm going to do is go terrorise Niles some more.

ExitBanterIslaGiannaReplyTwo.text: Normally I'd disapprove, but it's Niles, so...

WhakanoBanterAFaustusReply.text: The Marylene? Oh, you know... Get a bunch of men in a small space and there's bound to be bickering and brawling. The ol' lashing arm's been getting a good workout, I must say.

WhakanoBanterAFaustusReplyTwo.text: Well they don't exactly know I'm here, per se, but I imagine, rapscallions that they are, they savour any time where the man-in-charge is absent. In my day, we'd tie up the first mate, break into the swill, and see who could down the most before passing out or dying.

WhakanoBanterAFaustusReplyThree.text: Oh, no. No no no. Most of us came from good, Innocence-fearing families. The captain knew that raising a hand to us would put him in hot water back home. We got away with murder, really. No, really, a few of the boys beat a galley slave to death. Barely got a talking to. Nowadays, of course, Admiral Darnaw lets damn-near anyone join the ranks. Horrible policy. I do enjoy doling out the punishments, though.

FaustusBanterAWhakano.text: What do your people think about what happened in Oriath?

FaustusBanterAWhakanoTwo.text: Karui! Are they dancing round their totems singing the praises of the return of their saviour?

FaustusBanterAWhakanoThree.text: Eh? I thought that was, uh, hinny--something.

FaustusBanterBWhakano.text: Strange turn of events, eh Karui?

FaustusBanterBWhakanoTwo.text: Never imagined my people living peacefully with your people, let alone on your lands!

FaustusBanterBWhakanoThree.text: Well, they were our islands by then, weren't they? Anyway, perhaps I should thank you.

FaustusBanterBWhakanoFour.text: Though our beautiful metropolis is now but smoldering ruins, you have given us a new home. A chance to build society anew. Hope.

FaustusBanterBWhakanoFive.text: You know what I mean! Learn to accept a compliment.

FaustusBanterBWhakanoSix.text: You're very welcome. See? It's not hard.

GiannaIntroduction.text:
Hey good lookin'. Huh. Most people recognise me. I'm Gianna. Worked a spell in the Chitus Theatre, back when you could leave your house without being followed by Templar secret police. I was Shavronne in <italic>{An Axiom Tragedy}. I played Dialla, the Gemling Queen, in <italic>{Purity Tales}, and the fair lady Merveil in <italic>{Daresso and Merveil}, for which I was very nearly nominated to receive a 'Tario. 

No? Not a fan of the theatre, I suppose? That's-... That's fine. That act of my story has drawn to a close anyway, but I'm always looking for the next great role. Nothing's quite so thrilling as immersing oneself among the people, and seeing if you can, in fact, pass for the real deal.

GiannaAboutBoss.text:
I wasn't exactly planning on a life of crime. Yes, most in my profession do end up begging or stealing, but my career was on the up and up, until I was accused of <italic>{Pecuniary Lust} and exiled.

It just so happens that the Boss, cultural elite that he is, saw me in a few shows. He must have noticed my ability to fully embody any role, to become not just the character, but the person. I'm told he was a practitioner of the performing arts himself, in his youth. Obviously, he has a keen eye for talent. 

I'm dying to perform a dialogue with him. Good material is hard to come by 'round here, but I did find a piece by a Bestel floating in the foam. Not particularly engaging, and a frankly unhealthy focus on the female lead's figure in the stage direction, but it's something, at least.

Alas, Kurai maintains the Boss' schedule, and I'm told he is booked up indefinitely. Imagine having lucrative work for months to come! A performer can only dream...

GiannaContractOne.text:
Just my luck! Of course you are put on my contract. Do you even know anything about the theatre? The cursed play? The one no performer should ever name, lest they end up consumed by the phantom that haunts it?

It's said that the play's author wrote it while high as an eagle on ergot. He didn't know, of course, and died upon penning the final word. 

The play, whose name I shall not utter, is about a beautiful young lady who finds herself swept into a world beneath the sands of the Vastiri, where the dead have built a city of bones. She marries a statue, becomes the queen of this city, and then her skin peels off and a hundred little versions of her spill out. Completely nutty. 

It's locked up with the rest of the works deemed distasteful by the Templar, and I simply must have it.

GiannaContractOneEnd.text:
<italic>{Marilla turns to her beloved's unmoving face and speaks the blessed words:

Marilla: Two into one, one into many, to churn the world beneath the crashing dunes. 

Marilla's body shatters like porcelain, each fragment becoming Marilla. Each new Marilla shatters again, and again, each fragment becomes whole. The stage is flooded by Marilla. All is Marilla. The statue rises and exits stage right. 

Fin.}

Wow. I mean... wow. That was something! Right? That... that was something, right? 

I think I might just stick to the unbanned works for a little while, actually. Thanks, though.

GiannaContractTwo.text:
You're handling my contract again? I thought I specifically requested someone with a working understanding of the arts! Fine, fine. It's just a job. Well, I'm sure you've done the necessary reading, but I'm dying to gab a bit. 

When I worked with the Theopolis Thespian Society, there was an old, old, <italic>{old} woman. I mean, at <italic>{least} forty. She was our seamstress. She created these costumes that looked just like the real thing. Blackguard uniforms, Templar outfits, you name it. Well, one day she vanished, but the costumes remained. 

I want to get ahold of that old woman's costumes. They were just so... believable! With those, it'll be much easier to slip into a role undetected.

GiannaContractTwoEnd.text:
I don't know how she did it. Each outfit so perfectly matches the original piece. It's almost as if-...what!? <italic>{Property of Templar Logistics Office}!? They're the genuine article! That woman stole real bloody uniforms! Well, I guess that explains why they always looked so genuine. It also explains why we didn't ever see her again. 

Oh well, her loss is our gain!

IntroductionVinderiForGiannaTwo.text: Gianna! Yes! And she's a... erm...

IntroductionVinderiForGiannaThree.text: A performer actress! Right! And... ehhh...

IntroductionVinderiGiannaReplyThree.text: We met when Vinderi was hired to do the pyrotechnics for a production. He set the curtains on fire, but no one died. I'm here to help you with this job. And other jobs, later. If you want.

IntroductionVinderiForGiannaFour.text: Exactly! Anything you'd like to add Gianna?

IntroductionVinderiGiannaReplyFour.text: I think that covers it. Thanks, Vin.

GiannaPerceptionOne.text: I know set dressing when I see it.

GiannaPerceptionFour.text: Something about this doesn't ring true... Hmm.

GiannaPerceptionFive.text: It'd be easier to see with proper stage lighting...

GiannaPerceptionSix.text: All that time squinting at cue cards has trained me for this.

GiannaDeceptionOne.text: Back in line, soldier! I will inspect!

GiannaDeceptionTwo.text: Did I say you could speak? Let me do this.

GiannaDeceptionThree.text: Quiet. ... See? Nothing. I'll show you.

GiannaDeceptionFour.text: Are you drunk, soldier?! There's nothing on the other side.

GiannaDeceptionFive.text: Stay in formation! This is a drill!

GiannaDeceptionSix.text: Obey your orders! I'll take point!

GiannaSmugglerOne.text: I didn't hear nothin', but let's see.

GiannaSmugglerTwo.text: Oi, keep it down. Gettin' each other spooked. Here, I'll prove it.

GiannaSmugglerThree.text: Don't be so paranoid. Look, nothing's here...

GiannaSmugglerFour.text: You're just drunk, mate. Watch, it'll be empty.

GiannaSmugglerFive.text: Probably just the rats. Afraid of rats? Let's find out!

GiannaSmugglerSix.text: Nah, you're just losin' it. How could anything be here?

GiannaCultistOne.text: Ease off the elixir. Nothing is here. Observe.

GiannaCultistTwo.text: The fumes are affecting your judgement. I shall prove it.

GiannaCultistThree.text: Likely a mere apparition, but I'll make sure.

GiannaCultistFour.text: Perhaps you should rest. I'll check for you.

GiannaCultistFive.text: A hallucinatory phenomena. Anything you see is, as well.

GiannaCultistSix.text: Hearing things is a known side effect, but just to be sure...

EngineeringGiannaOne.text: Just like the stagehands taught me.

EngineeringGiannaFour.text: Not the sort of catwalk I thought I'd be walking...

EngineeringGiannaFive.text: We used one of these backstage, 'til it took a lad's head off.

GiannaBusyTwo.text: I need to finish this first.

GiannaBusyThree.text: You can't rush a good performance.

GiannaInterruptedTwo.text: Hey, you're hindering a great performance.

GiannaCombatStartTwo.text: We're just looking around, I swear!

GiannaCombatEndThree.text: Saw that ending coming a mile away.

GiannaLootTwo.text: That gives me an idea for a character.

GiannaLootFive.text: You've a keen eye for pretty little things, don't you?

GiannaAlertOne.text: Shh. We don't want an audience.

GiannaAlertTwo.text: Keep it down. There's a lot left to do.

GiannaAlertThree.text: Quiet, or we'll have to end early.

GiannaAlertFour.text: This is far more tense than I like.

GiannaSurpriseAlarmTwo.text: So much for the plan! Run!

GiannaSurpriseAlarmThree.text: That's not good! We need to rush!

GiannaFinalRoomOne.text: And there, before her, was everything she wanted...

GiannaFinalRoomTwo.text: They were so close, they could almost taste it.

GiannaFinalRoomThree.text: In most plays, this is where I'd double-cross you. ... I-... I'm not going to double-cross you.

GiannaFinalRoomFour.text: This is what we're here for. Go on.

GiannaFinalRoomFive.text: Well? Don't keep the audience waiting!

GiannaObjectiveOne.text: This is the part where you would double-cross me. Please don't.

GiannaObjectiveTwo.text: Now all that's left is to head for the exit.

GiannaObjectiveThree.text: That's a relief. I always expect a trap for some reason.

GiannaObjectiveFour.text: People have strange taste, don't you think?

GiannaEntryBanterOne.text: Ladies and gentlemen, the show's about to begin.

GiannaEntryBanterTwo.text: Stay on script and hit your marks.

GiannaEntryBanterThree.text: Take a deep breath before we head in. Might be your last.

GiannaEntryBanterFour.text: Focus. Watch your breath and move with caution.

GiannaEntryBanterFive.text: Take your time. This is just the warmup act.

GiannaExitBanterTwo.text: Take a BOW! That was phenomenal!

GiannaExitBanterThree.text: How about a bloody round of applause, eh?

GiannaExitBanterFour.text: By Innocence, I do love a happy ending.

GiannaExitBanterFive.text: Faultless! Stunning! An incredible performance! And you were also very good!

GiannaPerceptionLoudFour.text: I know there's something wrong here, just need a bit of time!

GiannaPerceptionLoudFive.text: A lot of work went into hiding something here!

GiannaPerceptionLoudSix.text: Some convincing fakes here! What are they hiding!?

GiannaDeceptionLoudOne.text: Open it! Let them through! Oh, I'll do it!

GiannaDeceptionLoudTwo.text: Stand back! I'll take them on single handedly!

GiannaDeceptionLoudThree.text: Make way! I must let the reinforcements in!

GiannaDeceptionLoudFour.text: Give passage! I have a plan!

GiannaDeceptionLoudSix.text: I'll open the passage, and you take them alive!

GiannaSmugglerTwoCopy.text: Wait, ain't they with us!? They is, right!?

GiannaSmugglerThreeCopy.text: Can't get 'em from this side! Pop 'er open!

GiannaSmugglerFourCopy.text: If we let 'em through, they'll be too confused to fight!

GiannaSmugglerFiveCopy.text: Oi, boss wants us to open the door!

GiannaSmugglerSixCopy.text: I ain't scared, mate! I'm opening it!

GiannaCultistOneCopy.text: Allow passage! We shall claim their ichors!

GiannaCultistTwoCopy.text: They beg to be sacrificed! I say we let them!

GiannaCultistThreeCopy.text: Their flesh demands passage! We must obey!

GiannaCultistFourCopy.text: We must unify! Open the gate!

GiannaCultistFiveCopy.text: Separation is trickery! Open the way!

GiannaCultistSixCopy.text: They test our faith! Let faith shield you!

GiannaEngineerLoudFour.text: We've got to get across as soon as it's ready!

GiannaEngineerLoudSix.text: This sort of thing always breaks when everyone's watching!

GiannaBusyLoudOne.text: I can play a thousand roles, but not at once!

GiannaBusyLoudThree.text: Can you see I'm in the middle of something!?

GiannaInterruptedLoudThree.text: Do something or this will take forever!

GiannaCombatStartLoudTwo.text: Let us through, or face your death!

GiannaCombatEndLoudTwo.text: It's like they forget they're the villains! Wait... Are they the villains? No, yeah, they're the villains.

GiannaLootLoudOne.text: Make sure that's not a posthumous award!

GiannaLootLoudTwo.text: Great find, but shouldn't we be leaving!?

GiannaLootLoudFour.text: Don't be blinded by all that glitters!

GiannaLootLoudFive.text: Wrap it up! I don't want this to be my final role!

GiannaFinalRoomLoudThree.text: Get it! I can't handle the suspense!

GiannaFinalRoomLoudFour.text: It's there! Grab it while we can!

GiannaFinalRoomLoudFive.text: We're so close! The tension is palpable!

GiannaObjectiveLoudTwo.text: Good! Now rush to the exit!

GiannaObjectiveLoudFour.text: Hope you're not waiting for applause!

EntryBanterGiannaToVinderi.text: Vinderi, ever thought about a keg that makes a lot of smoke but no explosion?

EntryBanterGiannaVinderiReply.text: Lass, that might be the stupidest idea I've ever heard.

EntryBanterGiannaToNenet.text: They say all the world's a stage...

EntryBanterGiannaNenetReply.text: And no one gets a happy ending. Yes?

EntryBanterGiannaNilesReply.text: Speaking of, would you care to accompany on a date, Gianna?

EntryBanterGiannaToNilesTwo.text: Niles! I said save it for later!

EntryBanterGiannaHuckReply.text: What an horrible, horrible thing to say.

EntryBanterVinderiToGianna.text: What happened to that little basement theatre where we first met, Gianna?

EntryBanterVinderiGiannaReply.text: Oh, the Wilted Quill? Yeah, burnt down.

EntryBanterNenetToGianna.text: All mortal endeavour is sand cast to the winds.

EntryBanterNenetGiannaReply.text: Yeah, but, acting... that endures. People care about good acting. The universe cares about good acting.

EntryBanterNilesToGianna.text: If harm comes to you, Gianna, I will hold myself responsible.

EntryBanterNilesGiannaReply.text: Good, I was planning to hold you responsible too.

EntryBanterHuckToGianna.text: Don't want to hear no complaints. We all signed up for this.

EntryBanterHuckGiannaReply.text: Actually, I auditioned! ... and I got the role.

ExitBanterGiannaVinderiReply.text: Please no, my bloody knees are giving me trouble.

ExitBanterGiannaToNenet.text: A performance worthy of an audience! Do they have plays where you're from Nenet?

ExitBanterGiannaNenetReply.text: No. All the battles are very real.

ExitBanterGiannaNenetReplyTwo.text: By surviving. The dead feel great boredom.

ExitBanterGiannaToNiles.text: That went so well I could kiss someone!

ExitBanterGiannaToNilesTwo.text: Oh, but Niles, what if I accidentally turn you into a prince? I sure would miss you.

ExitBanterGiannaToHuck.text: Did you see me in there? Damn, I'm good.

ExitBanterGiannaHuckReply.text: Yes, I did see you, which is very much the opposite of what we wanted. You got lucky.

ExitBanterVinderiToGianna.text: Worthy of a grand play, eh Gianna?

ExitBanterVinderiGiannaReply.text: Honestly? That went too smoothly. If one of us had died, that would have been dramatic!

ExitBanterNenetToGianna.text: That was a... five thumb performance, yes?

ExitBanterNenetGiannaReply.text: Five stars. The thumbs are a different thing.

ExitBanterNilesToGiana.text: At last. So how about that Date, Gianna?

ExitBanterNilesGianaReply.text: (<italic>{Laughs}) I can't remember the last time I laughed that hard! Thanks Niles!

ExitBanterHuckToGiana.text: Gianna, you nearly bloody blew it for us.

ExitBanterHuckToGianaTwo.text: You need to keep a lower bloody profile.

SelectionBanterKuraiToGiannaTwo.text: Say, before we get too deep into this, do you think my role could use an accent?

SelectionBanterKuraiGiannaReplyTwo.text: Well, it depends quite a lot on--

SelectionBanterKuraiToGiannaThree.text: Oh! What about a limp? Or an eyepatch!

SelectionBanterKuraiGiannaReplyThree.text: That might draw too much att--

SelectionBanterKuraiToGiannaFour.text: I'm Big Toe Gren, Captain of the Salty Hound.

SelectionBanterKuraiGiannaReplyFour.text: ... Good. Well, now I know we have that to fall back on.

SelectionBanterGiannaVinderiReply.text: Already? I thought we had at least a few weeks! What do we do?! WHAT DO WE DO!?

SelectionBanterGiannaToVinderiTwo.text: No, no! Vin! Me! I mean me!

SelectionBanterGiannaToVinderiThree.text: What did you think was happening?

SelectionBanterGiannaVinderiReplyThree.text: Nothing! Nothing! Just... if a living flame asks after me, I'm not here.

SelectionBanterGiannaToNenet.text: Hello all! Did I miss anything important?

SelectionBanterGiannaToNenetTwo.text: Oh. Can you catch me up?

SelectionBanterGiannaNenetReplyTwo.text: I can. We have a job. You have a role to play.

SelectionBanterGiannaToNenetFour.text: Well, uh, thank you Nenet. Very concise.

SelectionBanterNilesToGiannaFour.text: Wonderful. Just wonderful. And yourself? Wait, no, let me try to guess. I see... shoes. Boots. Steel toed. You wish to go hiking.

SelectionBanterNilesToGiannaSix.text: They're striking... some trousers. Black. Right in the in-seam. Over and over.

SelectionBanterNilesToGiannaSeven.text: Yes. A vivid imagination. Just wonderful.

SelectionBanterGiannaToHuckTwo.text: Your armour is looking sooo shiny today Huck.

SelectionBanterGiannaToHuckThree.text: Can't wait to see what's underneath.

SelectionBanterGiannaKuraiAboutHuck.text: Okay Gi, give it a rest. We have work to do.

SelectionBanterKuraiGiannaReplyFive.text: Thanks, lady Kurai. Good role for me today?

SelectionBanterKuraiToGiannaSix.text: That, I suspect, is up to you.

SelectionBanterKuraiToGiannaSeven.text: We still have a little more planning to do, but I hope you'll find whatever role you are given fulfilling.

SelectionBanterVinderiToGianna.text: Whoops, must've taken a wrong turn.

SelectionBanterVinderiGiannaReply.text: No, wait, you're meant to be here. We're planning a heist!

SelectionBanterVinderiToGiannaTwo.text: Well that's lucky! I'd just cancelled my plans for the rest of the day.

SelectionBanterVinderiToGiannaThree.text: Oh, just the usual armour. Helps protect the ol' bones.

SelectionBanterVinderiGiannaReplyThree.text: No, I mean, what were you doing later today?

SelectionBanterVinderiToGiannaFour.text: I'm afraid I'm busy, dear. Got a heist to plan. Very flattered though.

SelectionBanterNenetGiannaReply.text: Nenet! Mind if I practise your accent?

SelectionBanterNenetToGiannaThree.text: Actually, I think I do mind.

SelectionBanterNenetGiannaReplyThree.text: Eckchully, I tink I do mind.

SelectionBanterNilesToGianna.text: I'm needed? Oh, lady Gianna, what an incomparable pleasure.

SelectionBanterNilesToGiannaTwo.text: My Oriathan rose, my shimmering jewel among the rhoa dung.

SelectionBanterHuckToGiannaTwo.text: Ha. Really, what are my orders.

SelectionBanterHuckToGiannaThree.text: Gi, I think we need to focus.

VinderiIntro.text:
Hm? Ah! Right, Ahem. Vinderi. Pleasure to meet your acquaintance. Err, pleased to make you. Hello. 

Name's Vinderi. Did I mention that already? No one alive knows as much about the explosive arts as me. If you want something or someone, or several someones, turned into an unrecognisable, smouldering mess, I'm more than happy to oblige.

VinderiAboutBoss.text:
I was walking around the catacombs beneath the square, trying to find my way to the sewers under the courts. Had a huge sack of the blue stuff on my back. Leaving a little trail as I go so I can find my way out. Little azurite fuse trail winding its way back to the storehouse. Cost me an arm and a leg, that powder. Anyway, I'm right under where I thought the High Templar's office was. Start piling the powder up right under his fat arse. Planning to blow him back to Innocence. 

Well, I start hearing a hissing noise. And I start seeing the blue light down the end of the tunnel turning an angry red. It's moving towards me quick. And I'm thinking, this is it. This is where it ends for me, but at least I'll blow that high pain in the arse skyward. Then it stops. No hissing. No light. Just a silhouette. Tall as a man ever was. Taller than Tibbs. Don't know how he even got through the storehouse hole. This man... this glorious man! 

Put it down! He shouts. It's not worth the trouble. Come. It's time to go! So I put the bag down, and I start walking over to him. Running even. This man saved my life. I swear to myself I'll follow this Eternal Ideal of a man, this statue, this perfect specimen, as far as he will have me. And as I get close, my eyes adjust. This beautiful man comes into focus. His hand is extended to meet me. I reach out mine. There's an electricity between us. And as my fingers lock into his, he slaps a manacle around my wrist. I'm under arrest for attempted deicide and possession of a dangerous substance. Got me exiled, the pig. Once I got here I just started working for the boss.

What was your question?

VinderiOnNikoOne.text: Niko? Niko... Was he the lad with the club foot? No, wait, Niko was the haberdasher. The bordello owner? No?

VinderiOnNikoTwo.text: Niko... ah! Of course! The miner boy. That's miner, not, er, minor. I do believe he was of age when last I saw him. Strange lad. Always felt like he was talking at me, not to me, if you follow. Had an awful lot of yellow powder for sale. Wonder what ever happened to him? Lost track of many in that line of work. A shame, but not a surprise.

VinderiContractOne.text:
You've got a contract you want me to take a look at? Alright, why not.

Mmhm. Mmm. Yes. Well, everything seems to be in order. 

...

...Oh! This was mine! Well, the designs have changed a bit, but the fundamentals are the same. It's a grocery list, except instead of the markets, we're going to an alchemy storehouse I'm not supposed to know exists. And instead of groceries, we're going to collect a number of powders, ichors and minerals I'm running low on. And instead of paying for them, we are going to steal them. So in that sense, it is very unlike a grocery list. Straightforward enough. Ready to go?

VinderiContractOneEnd.text:
...Thirty three cubits of cerulean alloy thread, half an ounce of vitriolic talc, two quarts of bishop-blessed cleansing alcohol -- that's for me -- and enough barrel hoops to sink a bloated bonechewer. Perfect. 

...Wait. Hold on. Hold on one dang minute. Where the--... Where is the fumarole tar? Don't tell me I forgot the fumarole tar! Without the tar I might as well be baking a tray of Keth flatbread.

Oh dear. I didn't even have it on the list. Sorry, Exile, the error is mine. You've earned your markers. Hopefully I'll have enough left to take out another contract.

VinderiContractTwo.text:
Hmm? Oh! At last! The Fumarole Tar job! Gods, I've been chomping at the bit for this contract. 

I've drawn up plans for a bomb that, well, let's just say it'll put The Ring on the map. Or take it off the map. It might take quite a large area off the map, actually. 

I tend to deal with controlled explosions, but who doesn't love an uncontrolled explosion? Whoever's nearby, that's who! But other than them, they're great! And this is going to be really, really great.

There's only one place I know of that houses enough Fumarole Tar for the job, and it has all sorts of other experimental goodies that I'd like to get my hands on, too. 

Exile, this thing is really going to set your world on fire. I feel like a child again!

VinderiContractTwoEnd.text:
I've finished it, Exile. It's all done! The Vinderi Bomb is complete at last! I've named it after myself. It's my legacy. Or, the ruins it will leave in its wake will be my legacy. I wonder if it works... Shall we try it out?

 We only get one attempt! Let's do it!

VinderiContractTwoFireworks.text:
Bwaaahahaha! Had you going there for a bit, didn't I? I may be old, but I've still got a little pop left in my powderkeg. Did you really think I was about to blow us all to Innocence? Give this old man a little credit!

I just wanted to give the good folk here a little show. I call these beauties "Explodey-make-good-lookers". Catchy, eh? Reckon there might be a business in it!

Well, I hope you enjoyed it. Consider it a show of gratitude.

VinderiSelectedContractOne.text: Let me go get my things.

VinderiSelectedContractThree.text: Good timing. I've been looking for something to do.

VinderiSelectedBlueprintOne.text: Needed a reason to stretch these old legs.

VinderiSelectedBlueprintThree.text: Got the perfect powder for this job.

VinderiVaultBreakingThree.text: Let's pop this little sucker open.

VinderiVaultBreakingFive.text: Haven't come across this make before. Well, let's give it a go.

VinderiVaultBreakingSix.text: Ooh. Solidly built. Open up to me. It's okay, be vulnerable.

VinderiEngineeringOne.text: Now, how do I work this thing again?

VinderiEngineeringThree.text: You don't expect me to jump, do you?

VinderiEngineeringFour.text: I have the thing for this somewhere...

VinderiEngineeringFive.text: I did bring the thing. Did I? Thought I did...

VinderiEngineeringSix.text: I was hoping I wouldn't have to remember how to use this blasted thing

VinderiDismantleTrapOne.text: Ah, clever. Not clever enough, but still.

VinderiDismantleTrapTwo.text: Not the worst trap. Not the best, but not the worst.

VinderiDismantleTrapFour.text: Oh, those clever bastards. Hmm. Hmmmmmm.

VinderiDismantleTrapFive.text: Easy pe--...oh. Oh no. Oh? Oh.

VinderiDismantleTrapSix.text: Huh. Looks like a twist on a Maloney design.

VinderiDemolitionFive.text: Yes, yes... I have just the thing!

VinderiDemolitionSix.text: I've been saving this one just for you.

VinderiBusyFour.text: Oh, sure, rush the guy with the bombs.

VinderiBusyFive.text: "It was all going so well, then Vinderi blew us all up because I got impatient."

VinderiInterruptedOne.text: Pick on someone your own age.

VinderiInterruptedThree.text: Stop hitting me, you nitwit. I have BOMBS.

VinderiInterruptedFour.text: Idiot's trying to blow us both up!

VinderiCombatStartOne.text: I'm old, but you'll still die sooner!

VinderiCombatEndTwo.text: Whew, that gets the ol' heart racing.

VinderiLootingTwo.text: That, my friend, is very expensive looking.

VinderiLootingFour.text: In my younger days I'd fight you for that.

VinderiLootingFive.text: Bit of advice: keep that little find to yourself.

VinderiAlertThresholdTwo.text: We're going to get found out if we're not careful.

VinderiAlertThresholdThree.text: When even I think we're too loud, that's a problem.

VinderiEarlyAlarmTwo.text: That noise? That is not a good noise.

VinderiEarlyAlarmThree.text: I know that sound. That's a bad sound.

VinderiFinalRoomTwo.text: Well, go on then. That's what we're here for.

VinderiFinalRoomFour.text: We've made it this far. Why stop now?

VinderiObjectiveLootedTwo.text: Come on, legs, don't fail me now.

VinderiObjectiveLootedThree.text: Great! ...How do we get out of here again?

VinderiObjectiveLootedFour.text: How about you get us out of here, huh?

VinderiEntryBanterOne.text: Wait. Powder, sparks, probe aaaand... Yep. We're good.

VinderiEntryBanterTwo.text: Even at my age, the quiet before a job gives me goosebumps.

VinderiEntryBanterThree.text: Remember to breathe when we get in. Can't tell you how many good men and women I've lost to forgetting to breathe.

VinderiEntryBanterFourA.text: Bit of advice from an old hand: Whatever you do, and this is really, really important,

VinderiEntryBanterFourB.text: so listen carefully. Don't, and I repeat, don't, DO NOT, forget to follow this advice. Here it is:

VinderiEntryBanterFourC.text: I suggest you listen, because if you listen, you'll really take it on board.

VinderiEntryBanterFourD.text: Too many of your generation forget to listen, especially when good advice is being given.

VinderiEntryBanterFourE.text: Are you listening? Don't get distracted.

VinderiEntryBanterFourF.text: It's easy to hear someone, but listening and hearing are two totally different things. So don't just hear; listen.

VinderiEntryBanterFourH.text: What are you looking at me for?

VinderiEntryBanterFourI.text: We're on a job. Don't just stare at me. Focus!

VinderiEntryBanterFourK.text: Why do they keep taking on these glassy-eyed dimwits.

VinderiEntryBanterFive.text: People ask me why I do this at my age. People are rude.

VinderiExitBanterOne.text: Oh, me heart! I auugh-- ...Oh, thank the gods. False alarm.

VinderiExitBanterTwo.text: Glad I didn't tell you I nearly blew my arms off during prep!

VinderiExitBanterThree.text: You are mad, Exile. Mad! And I love it!

VinderiExitBanterFour.text: What a rush! Can't pay for that kind of experience. Even crazier that we're getting paid to do it!

VinderiExitBanterFive.text: Hahaha! I'd never've told my kids this, but gods, I love crime. I just love doing a good crime!

VinderiVaultBreakingLoudFour.text: "Vinderi, you're not busy running for your life are you?!"

VinderiVaultBreakingLoudFive.text: You're insane, you know that, right?!

VinderiVaultBreakingLoudSix.text: I don't work well under pressure!

VinderiEngineeringLoudTwo.text: How in the--... oh! Found it!

VinderiEngineeringLoudFour.text: You have the thing!? Wait, I have the thing!

VinderiEngineeringLoudFive.text: Ah! I've got the thing for this! Here we go--no, that's not it. AH! Here we go!

VinderiEngineeringLoudSix.text: A gap! I have just the tool for this. Somewhere. Did I drop it? Ha! I was holding it! Don't you just hate that?!

VinderiDismantleTrapLoudOne.text: This is meant to be DELICATE work!

VinderiDismantleTrapLoudTwo.text: The whole place is a damnable death trap!

VinderiDismantleTrapLoudThree.text: Wait! This thing's rigged to kill us!

VinderiDismantleTrapLoudFour.text: Gods! You were planning to blunder into this thing!

VinderiDismantleTrapLoudFive.text: Trap! Trap! Stop! There's a trap! A trap!

VinderiDismantleTrapLoudSix.text: This is exactly the sort of thing we should have handled earlier!

VinderiDemolitionLoudTwo.text: Can't even take the time to enjoy this!

VinderiDemolitionLoudFour.text: If I die, I hope this blows you up too!

VinderiDemolitionLoudFive.text: Gods, these are NOT ideal conditions for handling explosive materials!

VinderiDemolitionLoudSix.text: I wanted to save this one for a special occasion. You owe me a new bomb!

VinderiBusyLoudTwo.text: I don't have a twin you know! He's long dead!!

VinderiInterruptedLoudThree.text: Not like this! Not like this!

VinderiInterruptedLoudFour.text: Help! I'm too young to die!

VinderiLootingLoudOne.text: Why are you still grabbing things!?

VinderiLootingLoudTwo.text: Can't use it if you're dead!

VinderiLootingLoudFive.text: Great, now you got more loot than brains!

VinderiFinalRoomLoudThree.text: There it is! What are you waiting for?!

VinderiFinalRoomLoudFive.text: If you don't get it now, you don't get it at all!

VinderiObjectiveLootedLoudFour.text: Go on then! Make a path!

EntryBanterVinderiToNenet.text: Found a weird mole this morning. Nenet?

EntryBanterVinderiToNiles.text: You all know what we're doing, right?

EntryBanterVinderiToNilesTwo.text: Of course I do you freaky bastard. ...But I'll follow your lead. For safety's sake.

EntryBanterVinderiToHuck.text: Call out if you need a powderkeg.

EntryBanterVinderiToHuckThree.text: Bwaaahahaha! Still funny! So many times, and it's still very, very funny.

EntryBanterNenetToVinderi.text: The air is sour. Something is ami--

EntryBanterNenetVinderiReply.text: Gods, that stew was too old, wasn't it. Sorry, everyone.

EntryBanterNilesToVinderi.text: Perhaps we should take mental fortitude into consideration for future expeditions.

EntryBanterNilesVinderiReply.text: Why, you looking for a little time off? Ha!

EntryBanterNilesToVinderiTwo.text: Oh, I stand by what I said.

EntryBanterHuckToVinderi.text: Pace yourselves. Exhaustion down there means death.

EntryBanterHuckVinderiReply.text: Gods, you almost make it sound tempting. A nice, long nap.

ExitBanterVinderiToNenet.text: Did you see that back there?

ExitBanterVinderiNilesReply.text: Even if the gods did exist, which they don't, do you think they would care to hear your dull opines?

ExitBanterVinderiToNilesTwo.text: Best watch your mouth, interrogator. Got a powderkeg that fits right in it.

ExitBanterVinderiNilesReplyTwo.text: Oh, I'd love to see you try.

ExitBanterVinderiToHuck.text: Got enough loot in there to choke an ex-blackguard in his sleep!

ExitBanterVinderiToHuckTwo.text: Err, not you. Different guy. Goes by, uh, Buck.

ExitBanterNenetToVinderi.text: Victory, and yet the buzzards circle.

ExitBanterNenetVinderiReply.text: Oh, they're here for me. Buzz off! Blasted birds. I'm not dead yet!

ExitBanterNilesToVinderi.text: Humanity triumphs where the divine dare not tread.

ExitBanterHuckToVinderi.text: Better than I hoped. Much better than I feared.

ExitBanterHuckToVinderiTwo.text: Honestly, thought you'd blow us up.

SelectionBanterVinderiToKurai.text: Kurai! Just the lady I was looking for.

SelectionBanterVinderiKuraiReply.text: Oh? I was just about to look for you!

SelectionBanterVinderiToKuraiTwo.text: Looking for a reason to destroy Niles?

SelectionBanterVinderiKuraiReplyTwo.text: No, but it sounds like you might be.

SelectionBanterVinderiToKuraiThree.text: Not at all, no, nothing of the sort. Got plenty of reasons! Just looking for permission.

SelectionBanterVinderiToKuraiFour.text: Well, can I ask the Boss?

SelectionBanterVinderiToNenetTwo.text: The scale of the bomb... where are we supposed to get all the powder?

SelectionBanterVinderiNenetReplyTwo.text: It's a building, not a bomb.

SelectionBanterVinderiNilesReplyTwo.text: Let us put our differences aside. The job comes first.

SelectionBanterVinderiHuckReply.text: Vinderi, been meaning to ask you. Where'd you come up with the powder mixes?

SelectionBanterVinderiToHuckTwo.text: Trying to make me obsolete, are ya?

SelectionBanterVinderiToHuckThree.text: Gonna run back to Dominus with my precious formulas!? I know your game.

SelectionBanterVinderiHuckReplyThree.text: Forget it, Vin. Just making small-talk.

SelectionBanterKuraiToVinderi.text: Vinderi, thank you for joining us.

SelectionBanterKuraiVinderiReply.text: Not a problem. What do you need from me?

SelectionBanterKuraiToVinderiTwo.text: We're hoping you can help us on a job.

SelectionBanterNenetVinderiReply.text: Is she? Where's she hiding? Help me look... erm...

SelectionBanterNenetVinderiReplyTwo.text: Yes, help me look for Nenet, erm... uhh...

SelectionBanterNenetVinderiReplyThree.text: Ah! There she is. Thank you, uh, you.

SelectionBanterNilesToVinderi.text: Hello, hello. Ah. I see you'll employ absolutely any rabble.

SelectionBanterNilesToVinderiTwo.text: You know it was. I know you know it was.

SelectionBanterNilesVinderiReplyTwo.text: Keep your greasy little head out of mine, or else.

SelectionBanterNilesToVinderiFour.text: ...good... GOD... What--...No! Vile! What monster pictures such a thing.

SelectionBanterNilesVinderiReplyFive.text: I did warn you. I did warn him.

SelectionBanterHuckVinderiReply.text: A bloody big stupid head! Boom!

SelectionBanterHuckVinderiReplyTwo.text: Oh, come on. He was asking for it.

SelectionBanterHuckToVinderi.text: S'fine. Just focus on the job, yeah?

IntroductionVinderiNilesToExile.text: Exile, this is Vinderi. Expert demolitionist.

IntroductionVinderiVinderiToExile.text: Nice to meet you, Vinderi. My name's Vinderi too! Isn't that funny?

IntroductionVinderiNilesToExileTwo.text: Years of exposure to fumes has... affected him.

IntroductionVinderiVinderiToExileTwo.text: Sorry to hear that. Luckily I'm fiddle as a fit!

NenetIntroduction.text:
You are an exile? Then you, too, have had your rightful home stolen from you - unless you actually committed the crimes you were accused of.

But of course you haven't. We are all innocent here, yes?

NenetAboutBoss.text:
I have been looking for someone to follow my entire life. Someone to inspire me, to give meaning and community to my days. The Boss is... to put it bluntly, not that man. However, he is better than nothing.

Because of what he has built here, we unwanted scum have what some could call a society. Here, everyone is welcome regardless of station or ability, provided they are willing to work. The Boss has made it so.

NenetContractOneStart.text:
I am honoured, Exile, that one of your strength would even speak to me, let alone help me. I am an outcast, and it is that very status which drives me for this mission. I have traveled far, and for many years, to find the resources and allies to do what I intend. Here I am in this place, before you now, ready.

Where I am from, the Plains of Vastiri, the Maraketh hold no pity for the weak or the supposedly useless. The other outcasts found me and raised me, and though our lives are harsh, we have a meager culture of our own. We call ourselves the Faridun. The Maraketh believe we are worthless and flawed, but I am convinced I can prove that is not true.

There is a legend among my people of a bold warrior who tried to unite the scattered Faridun camps thousands of years ago. His name was Jamanra, and he wished only to unify us so that we might come into our own as a people. If I can prove that he existed by finding the Book of Jamanra, then I may be able to initiate a ritual challenge with the Maraketh to test Faridun warriors for worthiness. If we pass, they will have to accept us back into the lives we should have had! Will you help me win back my home, Exile?

NenetContractOneEnd.text:
Jamanra did exist, Exile... and they killed him. The Sekhemas agreed to meet with him to discuss recognizing the Faridun nation, but it was a trick. They poisoned him. The supposedly honourable high-and-mighty Maraketh poisoned our greatest leader.

I suppose I should have expected nothing less from this brutal world we live in, Exile. You and I know best that hope is an illusion, and that raw force is the only way to take anything for oneself. In any case, I thank you for aiding me.

NenetContractTwoStart.text:
I have come to a decision, Exile. I do not believe the Maraketh will ever willingly give us a home, or let us make our own. The Book you helped me retrieve tells Jamanra's tale, but it goes a bit further than that. It also tells of his final resting place. You can already guess what I intend, yes? In this land of madness where the dead rise and legendary figures return, I have a reasonable suspicion Jamanra can be found and released from his tomb.

If the Maraketh will not listen to our peaceful pleas, then perhaps we Faridun will carve a home for ourselves on the Plains of Vastiri with the sharp edge of a sword. Jamanra can finish what he began thousands of years ago, and if he is empowered by Corruption this time around, then no cowardly poison will be able to stop him.

Help me find Jamanra in his tomb and convince him to lead our cause, Exile!

NenetContractTwoEnd.text:
Jamanra was a raving mad monster... there is no hope, Exile. I appreciate your aid, but I no longer see a way forward. Who was I to think that I could change thousands of years of brutal tradition? This life of thievery and villainy is all that there is for me.

I think I'm going to take refuge in mead from now on.

NenetAboutIsla.text: Although Isla is often distracted, she is quite kind. She has a strength I have never seen before, one born of machines and intellect rather than fighting skill. I would never admit this to anyone, of course, but her steadfast support makes this place almost feel like a home. That is, when her mechanical spider isn't chewing my belongings.

NenetAboutPlainsOfVastiri.text:
It is an elegant lie, that name: the 'Plains' of Vastiri. I know it only as a harsh desert, a blasted wasteland of broken rock, crimson sands, and salted earth. Those who call it the 'Plains' see it as it was thousands of years ago. They are deluded.

But who am I to judge? I still believe I'll find a home someday, even with a face like mine. Perhaps we all need a few delusions to keep us sane. What's your flavour of madness, Exile?

NenetAboutStrangeVoice.text: Sometimes, when you are near, I hear whispers. Even though I have the best ears among all these thieves, I cannot make out the words... but they sound like my constant companions - my depression, paranoia, and hatred - when I am at my worst. Be careful, Exile.

NenetContractSelectedThree.text: Your orders shall be my law.

NenetBlueprintSelectedOne.text: I will not fail the group.

NenetBlueprintSelectedThree.text: You will not regret including me.

NenetPerceptionLongOne.text: Allow me a moment to focus...

NenetPerceptionLongTwo.text: Seeing sometimes relies on more than one's eyes.

NenetVaultLongOne.text: They might as well have left this unlocked.

NenetVaultLongTwo.text: Did they even try to secure this?

NenetVaultLongThree.text: I can break this vault. No problem.

NenetBusyThree.text: I'll be with you in a moment.

NenetBusyFour.text: I hear you, but cannot yet.

NenetCombatStartFive.text: Fight together and we shall overcome!

NenetCombatEndOne.text: Today is not the end, then.

NenetCombatEndTwo.text: I knew we could do it.

NenetLootOne.text: Take what you can. Live for now.

NenetLootThree.text: I hope you will share that.

NenetLootAlarmTwo.text: Should we really delay like this?

NenetAlertThree.text: We can ill afford any more mistakes.

NenetAlertFour.text: They will catch on to our presence.

NenetFinalRoomTwo.text: Do you remember what to do?

NenetFinalRoomThree.text: If you need help, I am here.

SelectionBanterKuraiToNenet.text: Nenet, good to have you here.

SelectionBanterKuraiNenetReplyTwo.text: Then I will do my best to serve!

SelectionBanterKuraiNenetReplyThree.text: Yes, we'll need your skills for this one.

SelectionBanterKuraiToNenetFour.text: I will not let you down.

SelectionBanterHuckToNenetTwo.text: Hah, I'm no Captain, but I appreciate it.

SelectionBanterNenetHuckReply.text: You better be. This is going to be a tough one.

SelectionBanterNenetToHuckTwo.text: Just tell me what to do!

SelectionBanterNilesToNenetTwo.text: Out of curiosity, pariah, do the Faridun worship any gods?

SelectionBanterNenetToNilesTwo.text: Niles, I can feel you trying to read my thoughts.

EntryBanterNilesToNenet.text: Oh bleak one, when a man believes he is doomed, he usually finds a way to make it happen.

EntryBanterNilesNenetReply.text: Good thing for you that I am not a man.

EntryBanterNenetToNiles.text: Perhaps this is the day that we shall die.

EntryBanterNenetNilesReply.text: In your mythology, what happens to the Faridun after death?

EntryBanterNenetToNilesTwo.text: I shall likely let you know soon.

EntryBanterHuckNenetReply.text: Like the ribcage of a dunewalker as the buzzards pick out his organs.

EntryBanterNenetToHuck.text: Where we go, death follows swiftly.

ExitBanterNilesToNenet.text: How come you and I never just talk?

ExitBanterNilesToNenetTwo.text: Oh! Want to exchange bleak tales of oppression after this?

ExitBanterNenetToNiles.text: This was a doomed run, yet we cheated fate.

ExitBanterNenetNilesReply.text: There is no fate but what we make!

ExitBanterHuckToNenet.text: Gods, I feel immortal! What a rush.

ExitBanterHuckNenetReply.text: Be glad that you are not. Immortality dulls the senses. To be mortal is to feel all life has to offer.

ExitBanterNenetToHuck.text: Death's pursuit is inescapable, but we have delayed it this day.

ExitBanterNenetHuckReply.text: Reckon that calls for a celebration!

NenetThaumaturgyLongOne.text: I'll crack their minds like so many rhoa eggs.

NenetThaumaturgyLongTwo.text: I can almost hear their thoughts...

NenetThaumaturgyLongThree.text: Isla says the mind is just another system of gears...

NenetEntryBanterOne.text: Thank you for letting me participate.

NenetEntryBanterTwo.text: I will not let you down.

NenetEntryBanterThree.text: I just want to be useful.

NenetEntryBanterFour.text: We will survive this. I trust.

NenetExitBanterOne.text: I knew we would make it.

NenetExitBanterThree.text: Let's return to that rat-ridden place we call home.

NenetExitBanterFour.text: I hope the Boss approves of my performance.

NenetExitBanterFive.text: My prediction of our deaths appears to have been wrong.

HuckIntroduction.text:
Sir! Sorry, old habit. You'll get used to it. Blackguard training did a number on me. I'm Huck. Served in the Oriath 3rd for five years. Dishonourably discharged, though I consider that an honour. 

My time with the Blackguards put a lot of things in perspective, least once I had some distance from them. What we do here might be illegal, but that don't make it wrong. 

You need something -- anything -- you come to me, yeah? We're family now. Family look out for each other.

HuckAboutBoss.text:
Haven't actually met him myself. Been dealing mostly with lady Kurai. Bit like the old days, really. Orders come down the chain and stop when they hit the right pair of ears.

I'm eager to meet him though. Owe him my life. Had some very dark days after I got discharged. Not a lot of people want to hire veterans, especially when they leave the service under less-than-ideal circumstances. But the Boss secured me a place to live, and gave me a steady income and work to keep me busy.

HuckContractOne.text:
Ah, my contract. Took it out not long after joining the Ring to track down a mate of mine. Man named Enoch. Not easy making friends at my age, but active duty has a way of forging near-unbreakable bonds. Enoch and I got real close. Might as well've been brothers. Right before I got discharged, Enoch was called up to a special unit we'd heard rumours about. A group under the direction of Piety, of all people. Supposedly some elite strike force, but no one personally knew anyone who was a part of it. 'Til Enoch, that is. 

After I started working for the Boss, I asked Whakano to find Enoch. Thought he might be a good fit. But Whakano found no traces. I want to break into the Blackguard Records and find out where he's deployed.

HuckContractOneDuring.text: Let's see... Good. Enoch's file is in here. Let's go.

HuckContractOneEnd.text:
Gods damn them. Piety, Dominus, Gravicius, the whole lot of 'em. They moved Enoch into an 'Unspecified Research' unit. Dead a month later, the cause listed as 'Severe reaction to subdermal augmentations'. They tried to turn him into a gods-damned gemling, and killed him in the process. Oh, Enoch. I'm so sorry, mate. 

I appreciate the backup, Exile. I need a bit of time to sort my emotions out, but I reckon I'll have more work for you soon enough.

HuckContractTwo.text:
Not long after we found Enoch's file, Whakano informed me that he'd found Enoch's family, and that even they had no idea where he was. They assumed he was still on duty.

Can you believe that? The bloody Templars had the gall to massacre Enoch and not even tell his family. That just don't sit right with me. 

His records don't list a final resting place, but I know that most blackguards who died on duty were cremated and put to rest in the tunnels beneath the city. It's a long-shot, but maybe we can find some trace of Enoch, to give his parents peace.

HuckContractTwoEnd.text:
Enoch was the sort of man who'd starve to make sure you had something to eat. The sort of man whose oath to protect and preserve informed everything he did. He deserved far better than he got, and we can do nothing for him now. But with his service records and his tags, we can at least let his mum and dad know what happened. 

Don't worry, Exile. I'll handle this messy part. You've done more than enough. Thank you.

IntroductionHuckAboutNiles.text: Thought we might be able to use another hand on this one. Meet Niles.

IntroductionHuckNilesReply.text: You don't like me, I can tell.

IntroductionHuckAboutNilesTwo.text: He used to be an interrogator for the Templar. Can read minds a little bit.

IntroductionHuckNilesReplyTwo.text: Now you really don't like me. Why is that, I wonder?

IntroductionHuckAboutNilesThree.text: Just remember that he's very useful. I find that helps.

HuckLockpickingOne.text: Standard issue lock. Shouldn't be too difficult.

HuckLockpickingSix.text: Ought to be able to open it.

HuckBruteforceSix.text: Looks heavy, but not too heavy.

HuckDemolitionFour.text: Stand back, this won't be pretty.

HuckDemolitionSix.text: Careful. Need to blow it up.

HuckBusyFour.text: I've got to finish this task first.

HuckInterruptedFour.text: Can't finish my task like this.

HuckCombatStartFive.text: Got a fight on our hands.

HuckAlertThree.text: Shh, we're making too much noise.

HuckAlarmSurpriseOne.text: Damn, might have to cut this trip short!

HuckAlarmSurpriseTwo.text: We're busted! Just try to escape!

HuckAlarmSurpriseThree.text: Might have to forget the target. Focus on survival!

HuckFinalRoomFive.text: Go get the target. I've got you.

HuckObjectiveFour.text: Protect it with--, well not your life, but protect it.

HuckEntryBanterTwo.text: The calm before the battle, eh?

HuckEntryBanterThree.text: Used to always hate the silence before a battle. Still do, actually.

HuckEntryBanterFour.text: Make sure you're good and ready before we head in.

HuckEntryBanterFive.text: Strike hard, strike true, get out. Got it?

HuckExitBanterOne.text: That mission was a damned success!

HuckExitBanterTwo.text: Look at me now, Captain Arturo!

HuckExitBanterThree.text: Victory! Didn't have many of those in my unit!

HuckExitBanterFour.text: I knew we could do it! Mostly!

HuckExitBanterFive.text: Savour it, Exile! Nothing's as sweet as success.

HuckBruteforceLoudFour.text: Gods, reckon I can handle it!

HuckLootLoudOne.text: Don't put me at risk for this!

EntryBanterNilesToHuck.text: As we stride headlong into mortal peril, remember: on the other side of death is nothing. You will simply no longer be.

EntryBanterNilesHuckReply.text: ...Yeah. C-Comforting words. Good. Right. Turn back? No. Right.

ExitBanterHuckNilesReply.text: You minimise our actions. Nothing is blessed or cursed. We just did a good job.

ExitBanterNilesToHuck.text: I worry I shall grow bored of success.

ExitBanterNilesHuckReply.text: Let's hope we live long enough to find out, eh?

SelectionBanterHuckKuraiReplyFour.text: Glad you could join us, Huck. We've got a job in the works.

SelectionBanterHuckToKuraiFive.text: I see! Well, I'm happy to help in any way I can.

SelectionBanterHuckKuraiReplyFive.text: I thought you might be. Before we set off, the Boss wanted me to check in with you.

SelectionBanterHuckToKuraiSeven.text: Still a bit... uneven. Still getting angry over little things.

SelectionBanterHuckKuraiReplySeven.text: I understand. The Boss is intent on giving you the support you need, but realise that if you harm any members again, you will be asked to leave.

SelectionBanterHuckToNiles.text: Sounds like we've got some work to do.

SelectionBanterHuckNilesReply.text: Oh yes. Violence, robbery... Nothing you're unaccustomed to, blackguard.

SelectionBanterHuckNilesReplyTwo.text: It is nothing to be ashamed of! Just as being an effective interrogator for the high templar himself is nothing to be ashamed of.

SelectionBanterHuckNilesReplyThree.text: Far from it. It means we are capable of carrying out orders, no matter how immoral.

SelectionBanterKuraiToHuckTwo.text: Whakano informs me you have been looking for old acquaintances.

SelectionBanterKuraiHuckReplyTwo.text: Yeah. Not looking to get back into the unit or anything, don't worry. Just miss a few people.

SelectionBanterKuraiToHuckThree.text: I see. In that case, the Boss will cover the costs of your search.

SelectionBanterKuraiHuckReplyThree.text: Oh, no, he doesn't have to do that.

SelectionBanterNilesToHuck.text: I knew I would be required.

SelectionBanterNilesHuckReply.text: That one of your mind skills, Niles? You can peer into the future?

SelectionBanterNilesToHuckTwo.text: No, my friend. Merely confidence. The idea that one can see events yet to unfold is a flight of fancy akin to that of divine intervention, spontaneous generation, or medicine. We are born, we live, we get a small cut, we die, and we are gone. That is how it has always been, and that is how it will always be.

NilesIntroduction.text: The name's Niles. I'm the resident thought extractor. Not got much to say to you just yet. Still uncertain whether I interrogated you before the Templars exiled you. Would put us quite at odds, wouldn't it? But I interrogated so many, I hardly remember their faces anymore. If I don't remember you, it probably means you broke easily...

NilesAboutBoss.text:
I know a thing or two about figureheads using mystery to evoke faith. It's how they deceive the masses, you see. One can never find fault with a god if one never meets him! Who, then, spreads all these tales? A Karui told me that Tukohama cut Kitava's face with a tooth. I asked him, how do you know about it if you weren't there for it? So, he stabbed me.

That's what you'll get if you start asking around about the Boss. A stabbing. Only - unlike Karui - this knife won't come from the front.

NilesContractOneStart.text:
Ah yes, Exile, I was hoping you would aid me. I have a very simple mission: to prove that gods do not exist. Yes, yes, I know that you believe you have faced them yourself, but I am intent on proving the fraud. You are a victim, like many, of an elaborate facade painted for you by clever con artists. In order to expose them, I shall need a certain piece of equipment, the Thought Extractor. Forced confessions shall save us from mysticism!

Are you ready to see the light?

NilesContractOneEnd.text: I immediately performed my tests with the device we stole, of course, but the random people I accosted with the Thought Extractor truly believed divinity is real. I don't know what else I expected. Instead of finding the truth, all we did was dig up the false narrative they hold dear. In order for this plan to work, we would have to force confessions out of the ones responsible for the divine facade, but if we knew who they were, then we wouldn't need their confessions! The Thought Extractor is useless! We shall continue our search for the truth some other way.

NilesContractTwoStart.text: Interrogation is a flawed art, as we learned together, but now I know of a better method to prove that divinity is false. I have learned the location of a renowned Azmeri artefact known as Viridi's Finger. It supposedly causes enormous plants to grow from almost any soil. Once it is in our possession, we can prove once and for all that Viridi's Finger is a fake and expose the liars for what they are. Prepare yourself, Exile!

NilesContractTwoEnd.text:
Hmm. Viridi's Finger did indeed cause enormous plants to grow. You know what that means, don't you?

We've fallen into one of their traps. Clearly, someone has created this to fool us. I don't know whether it is some unknown species of plant, or some sort of hypnotizer, or perhaps some sort of illusion machine, but Viridi's Finger is too dangerous. I shall destroy it, so that no one else will ever be fooled by it again!

NilesTheTruth.text: It seems only I am privy to the truth of this world. Innocence doesn't exist, Sin doesn't exist, and the Templar faith is a lie. You can tell them I said so. I'll go down shouting it! And the Karui and Maraketh gods are probably fake, too. It's all a scam, you see. A convenient belief system to keep the rabble in check. The Karui way, Maraketh tradition, the Templars' militant faith, and the Azmeri—well, they're fine actually. Inoffensive. You won't catch me living in the forest, though.

NilesGodslayer.text:
I don't know how you convinced a city full of people that you slew some sort of rampaging god, but I've seen artists' depictions of Kitava's supposed rampage. There is no way that the ground could support a being that large. Did you see the footprints? Clearly fake, carved by Templar artisans to deceive the populace. The river of blood was accomplished with diluted crimson mud from the Plains of Vastiri. It's really quite simple when you think about it.

As for your own experience, there are records of gasses seeping from the crypts that once caused a whole village to believe they were fish. They flopped on the ground, gasping for air. They even died! Have you considered you may be a victim of a similar occurrence?

NilesOutThere.text:
When I was younger, I served next to some very powerful men. I once caught a stray thought from the High Templar Venarius. A simple picture, nothing more, possible to perceive only because of his overwhelming fear at that moment. I have to assume he was insane, because the image he had in mind was that of a single beleaguered jewel adrift on an ocean of madness. If that was how I saw the world, it would almost be a comfort to believe in gods. At least then there would be somebody who could stand against the tide... but even then... against what I saw...
Just an old man's idle fears. Pay no mind.

NilesContractSelectedOne.text: Together we shall seek the truth.

NilesContractSelectedTwo.text: Time for us mortals to take action.

NilesBlueprintSelectedOne.text: I knew you were going to pick me.

NilesBlueprintSelectedTwo.text: I'll make them dance like puppets.

NilesThaumaturgyLongAlarmOne.text: Mind control is a delicate art!

NilesThaumaturgyLongAlarmTwo.text: I'll be as quick as I can!

NilesDeceptionLongTwo.text: This should be easy. Should be.

NilesDeceptionLongThree.text: Just another form of mind control.

NilesBusyFive.text: You have no idea what you're doing, do you?

NilesCombatStartFive.text: I really don't want to get stabbed again.

NilesCombatEndThree.text: No afterlife for them. A shame.

NilesCombatEndFour.text: Thank God we survived. Wait, I didn't mean that!

NilesCombatEndSeven.text: All this gore reminds me of home.

NilesCombatEndAlarmFour.text: It would seem our luck has not yet run out!

NilesLootTwo.text: Don't you owe me a few markers?

NilesLootThree.text: Avarice is not entirely without merit.

NilesLootFour.text: Not all treasure is silver and gold.

NilesLootAlarmOne.text: Leave it, there are more important matters!

NilesLootAlarmTwo.text: Are you seriously doing that right now?

NilesAlertOne.text: You do know we're about to get caught?

NilesAlertTwo.text: I sense suspicion. They may be on to us.

NilesAlertThree.text: To err is human, but one more mistake and we'll be ruined.

NilesAlarmTriggeredOne.text: Time to go, I take it?

NilesAlarmTriggeredTwo.text: This was part of the plan, right?

NilesFinalRoomThree.text: I half expected us not to make it this far.

NilesFinalRoomFour.text: There may be traps. You go first.

NilesFinalRoomAlarmThree.text: Move like your life depends upon it!

NilesObjectiveAlarmOne.text: Let's hope it's not too late!

NilesObjectiveAlarmFour.text: There must be some kind of way out of here!

SelectionBanterKuraiNilesReplyTwo.text: Then I assume I'll get stabbed again.

SelectionBanterKuraiToNilesThree.text: Do we pay you well enough to consider that an acceptable risk?

NilesEntryBanterOne.text: You handle the killing, and we'll do just fine.

NilesEntryBanterTwo.text: Mortal planning is all we have. There is no fate.

NilesEntryBanterThree.text: This will go as well as all our other misadventures.

NilesEntryBanterFour.text: I have a bad feeling about this one.

NilesEntryBanterFive.text: I sense a violent intent. Good, very good.

NilesExitBanterOne.text: That made me nostalgic for my interrogator days.

NilesExitBanterTwo.text: Hah! I survived! A great many betting rogues just lost a great many markers.

NilesExitBanterThree.text: I'm going to sleep in tomorrow. I've earned it.

NilesExitBanterFour.text: Nothing quite like the thrill of avoiding death one more day!

KuraiInterrupt4.text: Quiet, we're changing a few things.

KuraiInterrupt5.text: Shh. This is still being worked out.

KuraiInterrupt10.text: Sorry, we're making a few changes.

KuraiBossDoor1.text: Sorry, Exile. The Boss is out right now.

KuraiBossDoor2.text: Please don't go in there. The Boss is very busy and doesn't wish to be disturbed.

KuraiBossDoor3.text: I wouldn't go in there if I were you. The Boss has quite a temper.

KuraiBossDoor4.text: Stay out of that room, Exile. That's not for you.

KuraiBossDoor5.text: Please don't disturb the Boss right now. He's got a lot of work to do.

KuraiBossDoor6.text: If you need the Boss for something, please speak to me first.

TullinaFianceOne.text: Tullina sent you, didn't she? ...Oh no.

TullinaFianceTwo.text: Tell her I understand, and I'm sorry.

JamanraIntro.text: The Scourge of the Vastiri will ride once more. All will bow - or die!

JamanraPhaseOne.text: We who have nothing need nothing.

JamanraPhaseTwo.text: We who need nothing have everything!

DarnawIntro.text: How did you--... Faustus. Damn him! An admiral never cowers to threats. You want the fleet? Come and take it!

DarnawPhaseOne.text: The High Templar left me a few... gifts.

DarnawPhaseThree.text: I'll sooner sink the whole damn fleet than give it up!

TarolloIntro.text: You shouldn't have come here! Now I can't let you leave...

TarolloPhaseOne.text: Trying to save these worthless slaves? They'd just as soon cut your throat!

TarolloPhaseTwo.text: They're good for only one thing... Blood.

FaustusIntroduction.text:
Another green footpad? The turnover here... 

Listen carefully, for I do not like to repeat myself.

My name is Faustus. I am your fence. If you have something of value, you come to me. Understood? Every other day we have some braindead upstart who thinks they can circumvent the system. They go gallivanting around proclaiming they've found a gilded wonder or somesuch. Either the Templar, or another, less charitable, organisation gets wind of it, and we never see them again. Well, sometimes we see parts of them... usually on a pike or smeared across the ground at the base of the towers.

I am here for a reason. I am your protector. I am what stands between you and a very short life as a fugitive. I am your plausible deniability. Follow the rules, and you will grow wealthy and stay healthy.

FaustusFirstHandin.text:
Completed your first contract? Well, nearly. A contract isn't technically complete until the goods are in the hands of the client. You give me the urn, and I'll give you the markers you've earned. I yearn for the urn, to give you what you've earned! What fun. Don't go spending your markers all in one place! That, my friend, is a little joke. You see, they're only good here, so to imply you could spend them elsewhere is very humorous indeed.

I like you, Exile. Don't do anything stupid and ruin that.

FaustusFence.text:
A fence like myself provides a thief like yourself the means to offload ill-gotten goods for something you'll find more useful; in this case, markers. I take those goods and sell them to the nobility for something I find more useful -- coin and prestige. As a captain in the Navy, it's not entirely unusual to confiscate illicit goods from pirates and smugglers, and the nobility happily reward me for retrieving their valuables from the hands of evil.

Sometimes I'll even return it pro-bono, if the owner's station may afford me certain privileges down the road. The job carries with it certain risks, but were a thief such as yourself to try to speak out against me, well, you'd only be incriminating yourself in the process. It'd be your word against mine. And who is a judge more likely to believe?

FaustusAboutBoss.text:
Ah, the Boss. The big man. The man of a thousand faces, or no face, depending on who you ask. He's cultivated quite the reputation, hmm? 

I fancy myself a connoisseur of the truth, and I have yet to hear a story about the Boss that has the wondrous ring to it that only true stories have. But...

Well, I have certain connections, and those connections have certain connections who have turned up some very striking truths about this mysterious figure. 

I'm not about to run my mouth to a thief, but let me tell you, those definitely-not-true stories you keep hearing? The truth is even stranger.

FaustusKitava.text:
Awful business, what happened to Oriath. Terrible. Just terrible. I was lucky. Safely out at sea with my crew. 

I hope those responsible are held accountable, barring those with whom I have ongoing business, of course. I suspect they were merely in the wrong place at the wrong time. Can't blame someone for having rotten luck!

FaustusAdmiralDarnaw.text: I've been in the navy a long time. I've seen leaders come and go. Let me tell you; Darnaw is a fool. A bumpkin. A cretin! I've no doubt he is morally corrupt, but more offensive than that, he holds no regard for a man's heritage! Back in my day, the navy was where boys became men. Where well-bred Oriathans could earn their place among the elite, after a brief and relatively safe stint out at sea. Then Darnaw came along, and all of a sudden we have fellows from completely inconsequential families strutting around the cabins like they work there! Because they do! He lets them work there! Awful man, Darnaw. Just awful.

FaustusContractOne.text:
My contract! How delightful. A shrewd man knows when to be discreet, but I like you, Exile. I like your bravado. Your gumption. Your get-it-done attitude. You deserve a little background.

I was aboard my vessel, the <i>{Fair Marylene}, when I saw the first plumes rising above my beloved Theopolis. And thank Innocence! What those savages did... It is indefensible. But, it strikes me that within such a tragedy lies an opportunity. 

The Theocracy is all but dead, thanks to you, but the military structure, in large part, remains intact. That's a problem. Admiral Darnaw, Innocence save him, is a buffoon. He is such a buffoon, that I would be willing to bet he has documented his buffoonery. Prove me right, and I'll reward you handsomely. And richly! Ha! Do you get it? I was hinting at my natural good looks for humourous effect. Wordplay is so satisfying.

FaustusContractOneEnd.text:
Let's see what you've fished up. Hmm. Love letters? Well, nearly everyone's had their hand in Piety's cookiejar, so-to-speak, so that won't do. But these... Yes, these might work. Exile, have you already perused these papers?

Perhaps of little consequence to a layperson like yourself, these papers are irrefutable proof that Darnaw has been personally funding the activities of the Brinerot Pirates! 

What? Don't look at me like that. This is an entirely different situation. The Brinerot are awful, bootlegging buccaneers! You are a ragtag bunch of down-on-your-luck ne'er-do-wells just trying to make the best life you can in this crazy world. Plus, I do no business with the Brinerot. Completely different.

FaustusContractTwo.text:
Exile! How ever have you been since however long we uh--... Listen. That little job you pulled for me went nowhere. I showed Darnaw the papers, and he had the gall, the GALL, to shrug! At me! He said 'What are you going to do, arrest me?'. I said 'I might!' And now I'm blackballed! No orders coming through from him, and no communications coming from any of the other surviving vessels.

So, bit of a setback. Not the end of the world... Well, pending all this divine stuff going on. Plan B is underway. 

I've a bit of a rivalry with another captain. Fidium. Clean as a whistle, Captain Fidium. Barnacles wouldn't stick to his hull. He's long had it out for me. Suspects me of underhanded dealings, the clever sod. I want you to break into his home and plant Darnaw's incriminating papers there. Put them where he's likely to find them. Probably a desk, or the latrine. Ehhhh... Desk. Let's go with the desk idea. He'll find the papers, confront Darnaw, and, WHAM! Sink two ships with one larger, stronger, handsomer ship.

FaustusContractTwoEnd.text:
How did you do, Exile? Did you leave them by the latrine? Oh--wait, we settled on the desk, didn't we. Ah. Shame.

Hmm? What did you find there? Aaah... Ah HA! Fidium, you fool! These, my dear, useful friend, are Fleet Orders, direct from Darnaw himself. We now know the entire fleet's future movements, including Darnaw's.

Yes... Yes... A plan is forming. Leave it with me, Exile. There's work to be done.

FaustusContractThree.text:
Just the person I was looking for! And you even have my contract in hand. How fortuitous! I've spent a good long while thinking over our next move. There are many pieces in play, and we must act decisively if we are to enact the change I seek. We seek. The change WE seek. 

Here it is. We kill Darnaw. 

That's it. Brilliant, eh? We go to Darnaw's location, and we kill him. YOU kill him. You go to Darnaw's location and kill him. I'm going to stay here. Hands clean and all that. Couldn't be simpler!

Well, go on then!

FaustusContractThreeEnd.text:
Admiral Darnaw's dead? Then you should be addressing me more formally! For I, Faustus, am the new Admiral! Well, I will be very soon. I'll send a small crew to investigate Captain Fidium's residence. I suspect they may find some damning evidence of Darnaw's corruption that must have pushed fastidious Fidium into a fit of fury! A quick keelhauling, and presto! No loose ends. We'll have to use my ship for the keelhauling of course. Fidium's keel is notoriously clean. 

Thanks to your hard work, I can now consolidate the Oriath navy under my banner. The largest military force, mine to control, sitting at the centre of all trade! 

I do believe this deserves a toast. To me! Long live the Admiral!

EnvoyMavenQuest1.text:
Halt, and heed this warning. The Maven has come, Nomad. She has come to witness you struggle. She has come to witness you conquer. She has come to ensure you are adequately challenged, and that, should you falter, your death does not go unsavoured.

She is waiting for you, Nomad, and she is not known to be patient.

EnvoyMavenQuest2.text: You have called The Maven to this place, for I too heard it. She is near, and eager to witness your struggle.

EnvoyMavenQuest3.text:
The Maven has come once more, drawn by your beacon. Perform adequately for her, and you will be granted an invitation to a true test of your mettle.

You should not refuse it.

EnvoyIntroduction.text:
Good tidings, Nomad. I am a simple messenger from a place of great darkness and great distance, in a form most pleasing for those who must listen. 

Those great and unreachable have heard the Silence echoing from that which once hunted here, and they have turned their gaze to this place. Rejoice, Nomad, for she approaches, and she seeks to witness your struggle.

EnvoyThoseItServes.text: Beware what you ask, Nomad. Curiosity is a charming trait until it is not. Information will be volunteered, not coerced. It will create more questions than it answers. When at last their shadow is cast upon the firmament, it will take more than you can possess to bind and silence the screams within your mind.

EnvoyTheElder.text:
It lurched across these places with a hunger insatiable. It craved events past and prevented events passing. A mind like yours, so full of ideas and memories that flutter and swirl around you like smoke, would have been an irresistible temptation. 

It went by a great many names. The Unraveller. The Child of Decay. The echoing whispers of history here give a different name. The Elder.

It served greater forces, as I do. Those forces are still at work, but the servant is gone, the home left vacant. For now.

EnvoyTheMaven1.text:
For an eternity, the darkness swelled within a ceaseless churn of its feeding, and then... silence. Such silence is deafening to those who listen for it. The abyss cast its gaze upon its source. The first lurching movement of boundaries drawn long before the dawn. A claimant has arrived. You may know who. You wish to know why.

The Maven seeks new conflict. Bored, she is, with the realm she has given. She is not the only one. The silence is deafening to all.

You fear The Maven. You fear she is The Elder, returned and emboldened. She is, and she is not. 

The Maven serves not The Decay. She serves only her own amusement, passing eternity with an endless string of meaningless struggles. 

She is not The Elder, but you are right to fear her.

EnvoyTheMaven2.text: We are of one flesh, but two minds, two bodies. We are kin, both born of the tangled anarchy of the void, but we share not the same creator. She is my ward, and she is my prison. I am her protector, and I am her servant.

EnvoyGreetingT1MavenOne.text: They fought with such ferocity to protect the tree which held their nest. Now the woods burn, and smoke billows through the air, and their flapping wings only draw the flames closer. The fire is coming, Nomad, and it will consume us all.

EnvoyGreetingT1Maven2.text:
You think you are exploring the boundaries of existence. You are an insect charting cracks of the ancient stone on which you stand, blind to the dead stone forest that encircles.

It howls, Nomad. It weeps and howls and cries to be witnessed.

EnvoyGreetingT1Maven3.text:
Those I serve cast their eyes upon an endless, unchanging horizon, and have never had cause to look away. Without change, time passes like a tear in a stream. It is invisible, meaningless and insignificant to one with no beginning and no end. 

But then came the Silence, and it deafened them, and dammed the stream, and now they can see nothing else, and can hear nothing else.

EnvoyGreetingT1Maven4.text: Creation begets creation begets creation. Order and ambition urge progress, and time and entropy stay progress' hand. Her progenitor sought to test the limits of limitless power, to bear the burden of the creator and wade through time's mire. A meaningless obstacle in the face of eternity. But the Silence deafened all.

EnvoyGreetingT1Maven5.text: Woven, were we, from thread spun in long-dead stars, in its image, to take on the image of those who needed to hear its message. I try to remember its shape and cannot. Try to fall into my past and cannot. I am anchored by you, Nomad. Buried and drowned by your presence, by my duty, as, far above, the thread weaves on, a serpent swimming across the ocean surface.

EnvoyGreetingT1Maven6.text: She grappled with her being from the beginning. A lesson hid in everything that moved and everything that did not. What separated the two? Why did it move, why did it not? A life, she determined, was the difference. But she moved, and would never not, for that was my duty. Was she alive? She did not know, and I could not answer her.

EnvoyGreetingT1Maven7.text: Full of youth and vibrancy was she, that all was new to her. Imbued with a childlike wonder at once enlivening and exhausting. They sought novelties from far and wide at her insistence, never satisfying her curiosity, her lust for conflict and contest.

EnvoyGreetingT1Maven8.text: They cried out for the milk of the mother and it was given. They danced rapturously beneath the nourishing rain, suffocating in the tangled amnion, falling one by one to the selfish scramble for survival.

EnvoyGreetingT2MavenOne.text: I envy you at times, Nomad. You act in service of survival. You move with purpose, to protect a fragile existence. Your mind is assaulted by reality, that you are a mote of dust adrift a desert without end. Yet it shields itself with hope. A flimsy falsehood that halts the crashing truth of hopelessness all the same.

EnvoyGreetingT2Maven2.text: The Maven fixates on struggle and suffering. Such was the agony it created that it seeped deep into the fabric of the void. Its influence unseen but pervasive, filling every empty space with the recurring torment The Maven wrought. You feel it. You are filled with it. You are perpetuating it.

EnvoyGreetingT2Maven3.text: I saw in the Nomad the same lethal desperation for survival that I saw in the churning black masses. Its instincts took it this far, and it was right to trust them, but now it strayed to a place where nothing learned could be relied upon, where truth and lie could inhabit the same space, the same word, the same thought; the observer and the observed made one and the same.

EnvoyGreetingT2Maven4.text: I thought myself different from the countless reflections I saw etched in the darkness. I am free, I thought. They are not. And each had the same thought, and each took the same path, and each befell the same fate. But I am different, I repeated, and heard its echoes forever.

EnvoyGreetingT2Maven5.text: There was a time before time, and perhaps a time before that, it told us. A time of vast possibilities hemmed by petty squabbles. Constancy swept across like a veil, and all beneath its shadow was cooled and comforted and drawn into a steady sleep.

EnvoyGreetingT2Maven6.text: There came a time when time seemed to leave us, and nothing came to pass, for passage and time must dance together. The ants in their nests swarmed and swelled and died and were reborn, but in truth, nothing changed, and we looked upon the ants with envy. A waking, hypnotic slumber.

EnvoyGreetingT2Maven7.text: The stars watch in envy as life invades and envelops every open space, a cycle of birth and death that is as dynamic as it is rhythmic, while the stars themselves burn unceasingly and unchanging for countless lifetimes. Eternity is stagnation, and stagnation is torment.

EnvoyGreetingT3MavenOne.text: Time's tether tugs all life, like hounds on leashes, to the same terminus. Yet gleefully they canter along, always believing their master has their best interests at heart.

EnvoyGreetingT3Maven2.text: I followed her though I did not want to. I saw a moment, brief as a life, when I could stray and never return, and I did not take it. My thoughts were free and wandered and danced with abandon, but my form was ensnared and tethered.

EnvoyGreetingT3Maven3.text: The vanquished lay waiting for the time of victory to sink beneath the noise of memory. Castles of bone and clay hold their beating hearts in sacred secrecy for the era of loss and rebirth to come.

EnvoyGreetingT3Maven4.text: I set my eyes upon the great peaks of fire and light and watched them unravelled and devoured by the black sky above. I heard the choir of darkness sing as they drank their fill, and left the world below a frozen, lifeless shell. This was their gift to me, their eternal servant: to walk among the countless silent screaming dead and witness.
