CadiroNewIntroduction.text: My name is Cadiro Perandus, Lord of the Coin and the former Minister of Finance. There was a time when I had grown enormously comfortable in my opulence and influence; but alas, my fortunes were snatched away by the cruel hands of fate... stashed away in troves to evade the prying hands of Voll, the Usurper, and scattered hither and thither during that frightful Cataclysm. I have made every attempt to recover the lost caches of the Perandus family, with a substantial degree of success... thankfully, for I must appease the Lord of the Underworld to stay alive.

CadiroNewOnProspero.text: It has been over two hundred years since I signed a contract with Prospero – a deal which has prolonged my contented existence considerably. He was our household god, and our family paid homage to him in a tokenistic manner. It's one thing to make an offering here and there, or bat tithes in his general direction, but it's quite another to devote oneself utterly to his cause. I cannot imagine a life devoid of a partnership with him. Indeed, it would not exist. And I am all the happier for it... although it does come at a price.

CadiroOnPerandusFamily.text: Once, the Perandus Family presided over the city of Sarn. Our presence in Sarn began as a handful of merchant stalls. We were an affluent family, and accrued more wealth readily, but little did we know that our influence would one day expand into an Empire... although Chitus did have his sights set on the throne from a very early age. And, dare I say it myself, he could not have ascended to power without my assistance.

CadiroOnEmperorChitus.text: I nurtured that little tyke from cradle to the grave. I was closer to him even than his parents were. When he took the throne, I couldn't have been prouder... except, perhaps, for the day when he successfully navigated the Lord's Labyrinth. He was the first person to ever do it, too. And I was indispensable to his success.

CadiroOnNiko.text: It's a shame how the sulphite has addled his brain so irreparably. We have a thing or two in common, given that he resides in the mines, which fall under Prospero's domain. I do wonder if he ever encountered the god himself.

CadiroDuelistIntroduction.text: Ah, I was hoping it was you Prospero was sending me to do business with! He only mentioned a Duelist, not that I would be getting the best of the best, Oriath's greatest showman! I made a fortune dealing in bets on you. Not on your fights, mind you, but on which noblewoman you would bed next, and when you might finally get yourself exiled. Consider me your biggest fan.

CadiroShadowIntroduction.text: It's been many years since I did business with a member of the Brotherhood of Silence. Oh, sore spot? This hideout doesn't exactly look as opulent as those dens of old, so I assume you have had a falling out with your fellows. This place will do, however, as long as our dealings remain profitable.

CadiroMarauderIntroduction.text: It's rare that I've done business with a Karui. Your people and mine often had... less than diplomatic encounters. Personally, I believe each man should be free to seek profit on his own merits. I'm happy to set up shop here and support your pursuits.

CadiroWitchIntroduction.text: I don't know what deal you've made with Prospero to get me sent here, Witch, but I'll have you know that your dark powers will not work on me. My prices are not open to haggling or negotiation, no matter your... charms. Ahem.

CadiroRangerIntroduction.text: You're the one Prospero sent me to do business with, Ranger? You seem like the last person who might be interested in partaking in civilised trading. Oh well, treasure is treasure. Let's make a deal.

CadiroTemplarIntroduction.text: This must be a cruel joke on Prospero's part, sending me here to do business with a Templar! It was your kind that visited misery upon my line, and ended the otherwise 'Eternal' Empire. Though I suppose if you've been exiled, you hardly support those who would emulate Malachai... perhaps we can deal with each other cordially after all.

CadiroScionIntroduction.text: A woman of noble bearing and talent such as yours, exiled? Simply unthinkable. I am happy to set up shop here and do business with you, my lady. I have a feeling we shall get along famously.

CadiroOnAlva.text: That woman has a lust for gold that matches even my own. A shame about our multi-century age gap. She would have made a worthy Perandus wife.

CadiroNewOnEinhar.text: How do you know the Wandering Ezomyte? That strange man poached a few exotic animals from Perandus estates. Our soldiers never could track him down. Eventually, I just gave up and wrote off the losses. I'm rather astounded to see him still on the hunt...

CadiroOnTane.text: Poor fool. A rare learned Karui, but still so misguided. There is only one Intrinsic Darkness in the heart of man, exile, and you and I know it well... Greed.

CadiroOnJun.text: She is an enemy of the Perandus family. I do not care to discuss her.

CadiroOnZana.text: I do business with her as well, but she has asked me to keep those dealings private for now...

DiviniaAct2FellshrineQuest.text:
I am Divinia, a Templar academic and relic enthusiast. This little settlement is... quaint. Not the most respectable place, but I'm grateful that they've given me a warm welcome.

I've been waiting for a fellow explorer to make their way here. I've discovered an abandoned Templar enclave beneath the ruins of Fellshrine. Will you join me in uncovering its secrets?

DiviniaAct2OnFellshrine.text: Investigating this historical site is not an opportunity I can afford to miss, although it may be dangerous. It's fortunate that you're here.

DiviniaAct2OnEramir.text: Eramir is very kindly. We were discussing holy scripture, and he had many enlightening things to say. Our conversation brought a fresh perspective.

DiviniaAct2OnGreust.text: Greust seems... wholly unsavoury. He spat on me!

DiviniaAct2OnHelenaIfPresent.text: I recognise Helena from many years ago. We met during our studies, having pursued similar fields of research. I've always thought fondly of her.

DiviniaFellshrineRuinsIntroductionIfNotF.text: It's wonderful to see a fellow explorer! What a stroke of good luck. My name is Divinia – I am a Templar academic and relic enthusiast. I have stumbled upon an abandoned Templar enclave beneath the Fellshrine Ruins, not far from here. Will you join me in uncovering its secrets?

DiviniaFellshrineRuinsIntroductionIfFore.text: This may be a grim place, but it's an important historical site. We're not far from the Sanctum now. Let's make our way there.

DiviniaOnFellshrineRuinsWhileFollowingPl.text: This place is truly something to behold. History took place here, in these very wetlands. Archbishop Geofri, Maligaro the Inquisitor... They were real people, accomplishing real things that stood the test of time. It's like history is coming to life, and we are witnessing it firsthand.

DiviniaFellshrineRuinsSanctumSighted.text: That's it! The Sanctum. I can't believe we're here at last. We should make our way inside.

DiviniaFellshrineRuinsEntranceBarrierBro.text: Let's delve into history, shall we?

DiviniaAct7FellshrineSanctum.text: Something seems different in the Sanctum beneath Fellshrine. I think you should go and investigate it for yourself.

DiviniaAct7OnWildlife.text: Every time I took a stroll in the wilderness, I encountered vicious, mutated animals. It seems that the effects of the Cataclysm aren't solely limited to people.

DiviniaAct7OnGreust.text: The man who spat on me is now leading brigands? I'd believe it.

DiviniaAct7OnSupplyShortages.text: I miss the bittersweet tang of oranges. We can't grow them anymore, for even the soil is corrupted.

DiviniaAct10Introduction.text: [DNT-UNUSED] This is an absolute disaster! I am Divinia, a Templar scholar. I've returned to Oriath to perform some critical research, but the whole city is in chaos... I've heard the people here talking about you.

DiviniaAct10GoFindTexts.text: [DNT-UNUSED] If you're going into that madness, I have a favour to ask of you. Most of the Templars' secret archives have probably been looted or burned by now, but there's one trove only the Master Archivist and I knew about. It's hidden within my order's Ossuary. If you can, please go there and search for a particular tome. It's called the Mortinomicon, and supposedly contains everything the Templars know about battling immortal beings. I know you're dealing with Kitava and his cultists, but this may be just as important in the long run.

DiviniaAct10FoundQuestTexts.text: [DNT-UNUSED] You actually found it! I can't believe I'm holding, in my very own hands, the Mortinomicon Exitio Immortalis! You really are as capable as I've heard... if you're willing, I'm in dire need of further assistance.

DiviniaAct10FoundNonQuestTexts.text: [DNT-UNUSED] You actually found it! I can't believe I'm holding, in my very own hands - wait, what is this? It looks like the Mortinomicon, but the text is different... the historical references are all wrong... I might sound like a madwoman, but I think you've somehow found a tome from a different possible Wraeclast! Fortunately for us, there is only one Beidat, and this contains new information about his pacts...

DiviniaAct10MeetMeAtSanctum.text: [DNT-UNUSED] With this book, I might just be able to make some headway dealing with a very ancient problem. There's a certain forbidden Sanctum I'd like to show you, hidden under the ruins of Fellshrine for hundreds of years. Meet me there whenever you're done dealing with the chaos in Oriath. Believe me, this enigma isn't going anywhere anytime soon. That's the whole problem with immortality...

LyciaCombatIntroRandom.text:
It is irritating that you have progressed so far into my domain, but not surprising. I have seen many mortals undone by curiosity – for how better to ensnare them? Sure enough, now you find yourself in a predicament from which you cannot extricate yourself.

You have blithely wandered this prison for far too long. It is time for you to meet your end.

Lycia_Glyph_01.text: When I was young, I never questioned our faith. We pile the bones of former Templars in massive ossuaries that fill the spaces under the earth. Each one is hallowed, we are told. Each one is sacred. Yet as I stood there on that broken day, gazing at the bones I was supposed to join, I realised that I had no idea who any of these people were. Lip service. Meaningless. So many have been forgotten, but I will be remembered.

Lycia_Glyph_02.text: Their hypocrisy knows no bounds. I will see their destruction. All I must do is outlive them... Just like I'll outlive the adventurers who roam these halls.

Lycia_Glyph_03.text:
Time passes at an infuriatingly slow pace. There were no changes to demarcate it, so I began to create my own.

I built stone forms, animated them and made them talk. I raised a legion of undead – partly out of ennui, partly to see if I could. My creations are painfully dim, but to have them is better than enduring the passage of time without change.

I've lost count of the number of skeletons I've prised apart. I've even bottled fresh blood, harvested from curious adventurers...

Lycia_Glyph_04.text: My eternity passed unnoticed within the Sanctum. I knew I needed to amass great power in order to harvest the will of my prey. I commanded nascent energy, raw and shapeless, and over centuries, I gave it form. I opened gateways in the wilderness of Wraeclast – and even better, I managed to lure my quarry through them. Like rodents to rhoas, they were drawn into my domain... and not one has survived.

Lycia_Glyph_05.text: Leaving the Sanctum is a tempting prospect, but where better to ensnare hapless adventurers? There is ample treasure here, and glory for those who seek it. Better still, the glory-seekers provide entertainment. The more tenacity they have, the more fun it is... and the more sustenance they provide.

Lycia_Glyph_06.text: Knowledge is a far greater power than gold, for money cannot buy eternity.

Lycia_Glyph_07.text: I bargained with an entity far greater than the Templars, far greater than myself, far greater than any of the civilisations that have risen and fallen throughout Wraeclast. It blessed me immeasurably and cursed me insufferably. And, in a sense, it was a companion... almost a comfort. The adventurers will never understand the true price of having dominion over the Sanctum, nor of immortality. It is isolation. This is where the true torture lies.

Lycia_Glyph_08.text: Beidat is a cruel master. He calls himself the Archangel of Death, but there is nothing angelic about him. He is a demon-lord, and bargaining with him was like parting with my very soul. If only he had taken my emotions... It would have made eternity pass unnoticed.

Lycia_Glyph_09.text:
I learned a forbidden Templar secret: there are no records of the deceased. They are not 'hallowed, forever, together', like the priests told us as children. They are simply discarded, thrust away into crypts and buried haphazardly in the earth. The dead are simply... forgotten.

I wanted to be remembered, so I sought to become what they feared. I sought to live forever. I chased heresy and the unholy power of the demons... I raised the dead, and eventually, cheated death itself. It came at an inexorable cost – and, as fate would have it, I paid with my life. Perhaps there is an irony in this.

ChieftainPortalPlayerDied6.text: We shall leave that little mishap out of the tales of your deeds.

ChieftainPortalStashInHideout3.text: A good weapon is a warrior's only friend.

ChieftainPortalStashInHideout4.text: A good weapon is a warrior's only friend.

ChieftainPortalTradeInHideoutRandom.text: Why trade when you can conquer?

ChieftainPortalTradeInHideout2.text: Why trade when you can conquer?

ChieftainPortalTradeInHideout3.text: Warriors are remembered. Merchants are not.

ChieftainPortalTradeInHideout4.text: Warriors are remembered. Merchants are not.

ChieftainPortalTradeInHideout5.text: The glory of battle dims in the darkness of safety.

ChieftainPortalTradeInHideout6.text: The glory of battle dims in the darkness of safety.

EinharOnCrowbell.text: [DNT-UNUSED] There's a boss with a crow face and a bell, I want them

UnaIntroSon.text: Welcome to the camp of the lost. I am Una. <continue>I know you and I never met in the village, but Renly has been sick with worry about you since he got here. This is the first good news he's had, and for that, I am thankful to see you.

UnaIntroDruid.text: Welcome to the camp of the lost, honoured Druid. I am Una. <continue>I can only assume your presence here is a sign that the First Ones have taken notice of our dire plight. The very land cries out in pain, and you may be just the man we need.

UnaIntroMonk.text: Welcome to the camp of the lost. I am Una. <continue>This may sound strange, but I recently had a dream about a pagan arriving here... Perhaps you are here for a reason...

UnaIntro.text: Welcome to the camp of the lost, stranger. We survive, but we do not live. I am Una.

UnaDevourerDead.text: The 'Devourer' is just another victim of the sickness infecting our precious land. Many of Ogham's beasts are fearsome and dangerous... but not like this. <continue>The infection in the soil, water and air is changing them. <i>{All} of them. <continue>It is sad to see such a great creature slain... but it was no longer what it once was. I suppose it had to be done.

UnaLuteQuestStart.text: I don't know how to ask this of you... but I was forced to leave behind something of great importance to me when I fled—my lute. It was carved by my mother, when she first taught me to sing. <continue>It's in my... family home... in the farmlands... If you happen to travel near those ways, it would mean the world to me if you could look for it.

UnaLuteQuestEnd.text: You found my lute! I can't quite believe my eyes. This feels like having a small part of my family back again. I cannot thank you enough. <continue>I think I shall begin by composing a song about you. In the meantime, I would be happy to play for you, if you like.

UnaIronCountQuestGossipSon.text: You've lived in Ogham most of your life. Did you ever meet the Count before his madness took hold? As a child, I met him once, and he was kind to me. His smile was even - dare I say it - inspiring. <continue>The role of Count has always been reserved for the best of us, and yet here we are. Everything has changed. From the moment this curse fell upon our lands, our way of life has been slowly eroding. If the best of us can fall so far, what hope do <i>{we} have? <continue>Do what you must.

UnaIronCountQuestGossip.text: You must understand our way of life to know how dire this situation has become. The Count is the voice of our people, even above the Thanes. <continue>The role of Count was created to unify our clans against our Eternal oppressors, and it has always been reserved for the best of us. As a child, I met Geonor once, and he was kind to me. <continue>Everything has changed. From the moment this curse fell upon our lands, our way of life has been slowly eroding. If the best of us can fall so far, what hope do <i>{we} have? <continue>Do what you must

UnaEndOfActSon.text: You've done well. You have earned a prominent role in our song's story, and I shall sing it proudly. I know that Renly will dearly miss having you around... but he is also immensely proud of you. <continue>The darkness that crept upon our lands has been forced to flee, and I have a feeling you will pursue it to the end of the world. <continue>May the First Ones bless you.

UnaEndOfAct.text: You've done well, stranger. No - you are no stranger now. You have become part of our song's story and I shall sing it proudly. <continue>The darkness that crept upon our lands has been forced to flee, and I have a feeling you will pursue it to the end of the world. <continue>Good luck to you.

UnaTheHoodedOne.text: This shade is a curious one. It is quite odd to have a blue-eyed shadow in the camp watching us, but things truly have been taking a turn for the better since you freed him. <continue>Some of the folk here consider his presence a sign of good luck... though I wonder if it is actually you that brings us these better fortunes.

UnaRenlySon.text: He doubts himself, but I know he will find a way to protect us. As you well know, he is a good man. I am thankful for his presence. <continue>In many ways, he reminds me of <i>{my} father...

UnaRenly.text: He doubts himself, but I know he will find a way to protect us. He is a good man. I am thankful for his presence. <continue>In many ways, he reminds me of my father...

UnaFinn.text: He wears an eloquent mask of words. I doubt anyone here has seen what lies beneath. For many summers, I watched him cut smooth circles around the village square, moving from partner to partner, as if he was attending one of those famed Eternal masquerades. <continue>Always masked, always pretending to be something he wasn't, never serious. It's a shame, because when a masquerade ends, everybody that is real goes home, but he'll still be dancing, masked and alone.

UnaLeitis.text: Leitis is from a prominent family in her clan, so I didn't know her well, but I did take hope from her actions. If a noblewoman could marry a commoner, then perhaps a commoner would be free to marry whoever she wants as well. <continue>It makes me think about the last conversation I ever had with my father. It was... an argument. Though it tears at my heart, I choose to believe that deep down, he understood me.

UnaClearfell.text: Renly brings the strength, Finn brings the wit, and I'm doing my best to keep spirits raised with my songs. Hope is the only thing we have now, but it's in short supply.

UnaClearfellPostCount.text: This is home now. Our songs tell of times of renewal, when bloodshed, strife, and courage forge stronger bonds. That is how we will regard this era of Ogham, and how we will remember you in our songs.

UnaOldForest.text: The First Ones ran wild through the Grelwood of old, hunting and brawling as they saw fit. It is said that the spirits of the forest would watch them and be... entertained. <continue>Over time, the forest became abundant with the joy of those spirits and their old magicks. It was a haven for the unity of life and spirit. That place of beauty has now become shadowed and deadly. <continue>The curse upon this land has made the known paths of the Grelwood twisted and treacherous, so much so, that we can no longer even reach our home.

UnaGraveyard.text: The graves of our people lie beneath the Eternals' tombs. Despite their best efforts to bury our legacy, we remain. Now they are gone, and we live on. <continue>This is the cycle of life as we have always known it. Everyone dies, but the clan endures, and the greatest glory an Ezomyte can attain is to live on in a song or a poem. <continue>That is why we do not fight the wood and stone to reclaim our buried graves, and it is something the Eternals never understood: we don't need the graves. We still have the songs and the stories that matter. They could never take those from us.

UnaTheVillage.text: I survive, but all that I was is gone. Count Geonor has only been growing more and more cruel with his 'justice'. He arrested my father for bringing in the harvest one day late, and the rest of my family scattered and fled as the soldiers came for them. <continue> I was away... when it happened, but my neighbors warned me on my way home, and I fled. Clearfell is as far as I could go before the dangers of the forest closed in. <continue>There is scant hope in my heart for my father, but I must believe my mother and my two younger brothers escaped. Even though my heart tells me that they are just songs now, I keep longing for a ray of light to cut through the darkness of these bleak days.

UnaOnHoodedOneInTree.text: So this is the source of my shadowed dreams... Not the Tree, but the shade upon it. <continue>As strange as it sounds, I believe we should help this creature. For the Count to bind it to the tree, it must be involved in all of this somehow. There is something very wrong in Ogham, and it may know something of it.

UnaSong1.text: This one always makes me weep.

UnaSong2.text: Ah... a tale of the dangers of love.

UnaSong3.text: Izaro the wise... Izaro the mad.

UnaSong4.text: The mad emperor's song... not a tale the Eternals would tell.

UnaSong7.text: Ah yes... the hubris of men.

UnaTreeWillWaitHere.text: I'll wait here. The old magicks will protect me.

UnaTreeOutLoudReturningWithSpikes.text: You have them! Stab them into the runewood sites.

UnaTreeOutLoudReturningWithSpikesAgain.text: Stab the spikes into the runewood markings.

UnaTreeIdleCallOut.text: Don't worry—the Tree itself will not be harmed. What are you waiting for?

UnaTreeTheRedValeGossip.text: The Red Vale played host to the final and bloodiest battle of countless conflicts. It was in the heart of that vale that we fought for our freedom against the Eternals. <continue>We did win... in a sense... but the cost was far greater than anyone expected. <continue>Many generations of able-bodied men and women gave their lives to push off the boot of oppression. Ogham's clans haven't been the same since, even centuries on.

UnaEndTreeOfSouls.text: If nothing else, releasing the shade was an act of mercy. There is no telling what effect a small moment of kindness may have, all things considered. I have faith that we have done the right thing.

RenlyIntroSon.text: Where've you been, lad? I've been worried sick! I looked for you everywhere after those soldiers came for you, but when I found neither hide nor hair, I had to believe, well... <continue>It's a good thing you managed to escape the Count's 'justice', let's just say that. It seems the First Ones have graced us with fortune. <continue>We could sorely use your strength in these dark times.

RenlyIntro.text: Renly's the name. You're skilled with the violence, if what you did out there in the riverbank is any sign. Another refugee from the Count's 'justice,' I take it. <continue>Well have no fear. This place is something of a hideaway for many of us now, and we could sorely use your skills in these dark times. <continue>I'll smith for you what I can, if you're willing to bend your violence toward our defence.

RenlyDevouredQuestIntro.text: There's a beast of particular dark power stalking us out in the Felling. It moves unseen under the dirt, and attacks without warning. We can't leave the walls to find food, and I've been unable to corner and slay the beast myself. <continue>Now if you could channel your violence against this 'Devourer,' as Finn calls it, we'd be indebted to you.

RenlyDevourerKilled.text: Ahh, finally! Took down the Devourer, did you? That's incredible! This is the first real success we've had against the darkness. We can breathe a bit easier now, perhaps even go out and gather food. <continue>This won't cover our debt to you, not nearly, but take it as thanks.

RenlyDevourerAdvice.text: There is no time for forging runes, stranger. We suffer constant attack by the Devourer.

RenlyRuneSpikes.text:
Here are your spikes but... be cautious. They stayed warm after forging no matter how many times I quenched them. 
<continue>I would ask what you need these for, but I'm putting my trust in you.

RenlyBitterGuyPostFight.text: The Count's head servant is dead? That doesn't bode well for the state of the Manor.

RenlySiegeQuestIntro.text: We've been holding out for hope of rescue from the village, but many weeks have passed without word. You've shown yourself to be quite capable. Would you go to our home village and see if they require aid? If they're doing fine, which they probably are, I would appreciate you grabbing some forging materials I left behind at my smithy. We could use them for making weapons to defend Clearfell.

RenlySiegeQuestEnd.text:
So the village has been destroyed, then. Some survivors are already finding their way here, and it looks like Clearfell is home now. We can't thank you enough for what you've done.

This iron you've retrieved from my smithy... it's all I have left of the place now.

RenlyIronCountQuestIntro.text:
Our village, a burning ruin... we find ourselves in the darkest of days. One stark truth is clear: Count Geonor, tasked by birthright with stewardship of Ogham, has betrayed us. 
<continue>Enacting ruthless laws was bad enough, but actually attacking his own people? I despise myself for this request, but I must ask you to enter the Manor and remove him from power. 
<continue>He has become a tyrannical madman, and if you must resort to violence... so be it.

RenlyCountDead.text:
Count Geonor is dead. I never thought there'd come a day when such a statement brought relief.

<continue>We can finally start rebuilding our poor damaged Ogham. It's going to be a long and difficult struggle, but it's not nearly the first time we Ezomytes have had to rise from the ashes.

RenlyClearfellGossip.text: Well this place was never meant to house this many people, especially not the sick and injured, but there's nowhere else to go. <continue>The monsters creeping out of the forest keep us locked within these wooden walls, and the Count's tyranny has made outlaws of everyone here, so nobody is coming to save us. <continue>I don't have the heart to tell the others that I don't see a way to survive this. I put on a brave face, but it's the truth.

RenlyClearfellDevourer.text: With the Devourer dead, we can go out and gather food. We might actually turn things around! You've brought us hope in these dark times.

RenlyClearfellVillage.text: This place is our new start. Clearfell Encampment was just a logging site, but now it's the seed of the Ezomyte people in Ogham. We're gon'a have to fight back the darkness and rebuild. It'll take all the strength we have, and more, but I believe we can do it.

RenlyFinn.text:
I've had a few things go missing around the forge when Finn was nearby, but I can't begrudge the lad. His father refused to acknowledge him, so he was left clanless at an early age. 
<continue>Underneath that boastful exterior, there's just—well, I'm sure it's obvious, even to strangers. His mother was a kind and honest woman. Shame he doesn't take after her.

RenlyFinnAfterQuest.text: I misjudged the lad. He's worth more than he knows. Now I understand what he was doing when he convinced me to flee the village instead of stand and fight. All of the sick and wounded here at Clearfell would be dead if they'd been left defenceless.

RenlyUna.text:
The girl's a shining light in a time of darkness. If it weren't for her music, I - well, I don't know what I'd do. 
<continue>Every time I listen to her songs, I know I have to try harder to defend this place, any fear and excuses be damned.

RenlyLeitis.text: I've never met Leitis, but I knew of her. The nobles disapproved of her marrying a commoner... I can't believe how far they took that grudge. <continue>Her husband was a good man.

RenlyOgham.text:
This part of Phaaryl has been a fair home for many an Ezomyte generation. The clans didn't always get along, but we had to settle our feuds when the Eternals laid their savage boot upon us. 
<continue>We weren't able to take part in the Bloody Flowers Rebellion, but we had our share of conflict with them here. Their ruins run over top of ours, fighting a silent war in stone.

RenlyBranoc.text: It's a shame what happened to old Branoc. He was a kind man in life, but I can't say I'll miss the creature he became. <continue>He tried to batter his way in for five full days once he rose again. We thought we were done for, but then you came along... and I'm glad you did.

RenlyFatherhoodSon.text: I know I'm not your father, lad, but I've tried hard to raise you the best I can. I don't know how the Karui might have taught you, but I imagine you'd still be the man you are today. <continue>You've always had a strong will. That's what truly makes you an Ezomyte, no matter where you were born.

RenlyFatherhood.text:
Bad enough I have all these folk to protect. I've been worried sick about my son ever since the Count's men arrested him. 
<continue>I was hoping you might have seen him when you were in their custody. He's a big lad, and you can't miss him, because, well... he's not from around here. 
<continue>I found him washed up on the riverbanks when he was just a child, a Karui foundling, perhaps lost by some raiding party. Nobody ever came for him, though. 
<continue>Every day here in Clearfell, I keep my eyes on the river, hoping he'll miraculously wash up on its lonely sands just one more time...

RenlyTwistedAnimals.text:
A curse has befallen this land. That's what Una feels. That's what I say, too. The beasts of Ogham have been friendly to men until a shadow started oozing out of the Manor. 
<continue>These rabid and misshapen animals are not to blame. They've been driven mad by something we can't see, only feel in our bones. Last time I felt something like this, I was a much younger man...

RenlyOldForestSon.text:
That place used to be a kind and warm wood. I even took you to play there when you were younger, if you remember. 
<continue>It's a dark well now, with no way out for most. If you go there, be on guard, and remember the skills I taught you.

RenlyOldForest.text:
That place used to be a kind and warm wood. I even played there when I was young. 
<continue>It's a dark well now, with no way out for most. I'd go with you, but I've got people to protect here.

RenlyHoodedOneSon.text: That Hooded fellow is a strange one, but if you think he's trustworthy, then you've got my support. Let's hope you're right.

RenlyHoodedOne.text: This 'Hooded One' is here on your honour. Don't take this as a threat, but it's your head if he turns out to be as evil as he looks.

RenlyToolsIntroductionSon.text: So you're going back to the village, lad? You've probably been thinking this already, but we could do some proper smithing if you manage to bring back our tools. <continue>They should still be near the forge, right where I left them. Bring them here, and we'll set up a bench. Some honest work might do wonders to lift our spirits.

RenlyToolsIntroduction.text: I heard you're heading for the village. When I fled for my life, there was no time for me to grab my smithing tools. If you do manage to reach my forge, you should find them, and bring them here. I'll set up a bench, and we can see about working on your equipment.

RenlyToolsFoundSon.text: Our tools! Oh, this is wonderful, lad. Haven't felt right without a proper forge. Now I can set up a proper bench here for you.

RenlyToolsFound.text: You found my tools! Oh hoh, this is wonderful. Now I can set up a proper bench here for you.

RenlyGraveyard.text:
Tread as heavily as you like. The Eternals stomped their graves all over ours when they had a conqueror's foothold here. Now if those graves have turned up and released their dead, take our vengeance on them. 
<continue>Some even say, when the night is darkest, our ancestors still fight theirs among the tombs–and I don't doubt it. A true Ezomyte never surrenders their land, not even in death.

RenlyVillageSon.text: Be careful if you intend on returning to the village, lad. Those thugs Count Geonor hired are far crueler than our own soldiers. You've seen them. Each accusation is weaker than the last. <continue>When they came to my forge asking for free weapons, I refused. I'd already been looking for you for quite some time, and you were nowhere to be found, so I assumed the worst, and fled for Clearfell. <continue>I'm sorry, lad. I'm just glad you're alright.

RenlyVillage.text: I have a forge back home in the village, but I don't dare return. Count Geonor hired thugs that are far crueler than the Village Guard, and those mercenaries have been arresting more and more good folk. <continue>Each accusation is weaker than the last. A few of those hard-eyed men came around my forge asking for free weapons made, and I refused. <continue>I knew their ire would soon fall upon me, so I fled, and took up temporary lodging here at Clearfell.

RenlyVillageAfterQuest.text: The thought of our village on fire... oh, my heart feels heavy. We'll get back there someday. Reclaim our lands, rebuild. Mark my words. <continue>Part of me is angry I wasn't there to defend the place, but I know I was needed by these good folks far more. I can't imagine what would have happened if they'd been out here defenceless.

RenlyTheCount.text:
Some men do not have to earn honour. Some are simply born with it by virtue of their status. Geonor is doubly a monster for giving away what others have sought their entire lives. 
<continue>He was born into the role rather than being chosen by the clan, and now he has squandered that by serving himself above all others. I used to believe in him, but now I cannot even stand the thought of him.

RenlyEndOfActSon.text:
Go, lad. After seeing what you're capable of, I see now why the First Ones brought you here as a child. It's been my honour to raise you, but now you are your own man. 
<continue>Do what you must, and make it back home alive. I'll still be here when you do. I promise.

RenlyEndOfAct.text:
Now that the curse on this land has been broken, we can finally start rebuilding. 
<continue>There are certainly survivors scattered throughout Ogham. We'll find them, and we'll start down the long hard road ahead. 
<continue>I thank you, friend. I understand that you're leaving to pursue the ghastly thing at the heart of all this. May the First Ones grace your hunt with success.

RenlyTheCountSlayed.text: The Count's name will not be remembered in our songs. Hah! Good riddance.

IronCountIntroCamera.text: Criminals! Your sentence is to be hanged from the neck until dead. Let your souls feed the First Ones and your body feed the land.

IronCountEscapeIntFour.text: What? The witch is escaping! Kill her!

IronCountEscapeIntFourb.text: The Maraketh fiend is getting away! Stop her!

IronCountEscapeStrFour.text: Kill that Karui on sight! Don't let him escape!

IronCountEscapeStrFourb.text: Stop the foundling! Quickly, he's escaping!

IronCountEscapeDexFour.text: After her! Hunt her down! Quickly now!

IronCountEscapeDexFourb.text: What - no! Don't let the Azmerian escape!

IronCountEscapeStrDexFour.text: What?! Kill the Oriathan! Don't let him get away!

IronCountEscapeStrDexFourb.text: Quickly! Stop him! Take down the degenerate!

IronCountEscapeStrIntFour.text: What? Stop the old fool at once!

IronCountEscapeStrIntFourB.text: Capture him! Cut down the druid!

IronCountEscapeDexIntFourb.text: Recapture the pagan! Don't let him escape! Hurry!

IronCountIntroSorceress.text: Sorceress... You were banished by your akhara for experimenting with the elements. Arrogance has led you here and arrogance keeps you on those gallows. Speak your piece!

IronCountIntroWitch.text: Foul Witch, your very own coven cast you out for your forbidden pursuits. Your twisted necromancy ends here, at the end of a noose. Speak your last!

IronCountIntroRanger.text: Ranger... An outcast, lurking among the shadows of the trees like an animal. You murdered one of my soldiers in the name of a filthy thief. Your guilt is clear. Plead for mercy, if you must.

IronCountIntroHuntress.text: Feral Azmerian... Expelled from your mountain, you are wild at heart and wild of mind. Oh how the glory of the Azmeri has faded. I sentence you to death. Say your piece.

IronCountIntroMarauder.text: Karui Savage... Exiled from your tribe for following your own Way, it appears you find yourself at the end of a rope. Let your voice be heard, one last time.

IronCountIntroWarrior.text: Foundling... It is a pity to see you like this. You arrived on our shores a whipped and broken child. Our people made you strong. How were they repaid? Sedition and lies! Speak now, if you choose.

IronCountIntroShadow.text: Pathetic thief... You dance through the shadows, twisting your dagger and poisoning your victims. A dangerous outcast destined for death by my hand. Beg for mercy, if you dare.

IronCountIntroMonk.text: Pagan... You failed to liberate your brothers just as you have failed in poisoning my subjects against me. Call out to your Dreamer. Let us see if he answers.

IronCountIntroDuelist.text: Vain Oriathan... Once a staple of the Grand Arena, now a disgraced idol. You may search your soul for dignity, but you best make it quick. Any parting remarks?

IronCountIntroMercenary.text: Hired hand! Every life has a price... And your crossbow has kept your coinpurse full. Here you are judged and found guilty. What say you?

IronCountIntroTemplar.text: Templar... Pious to the end. Did your faith come to your aid when your Order expelled you? Where was your God then? Your time has come. Any last confessions?

IronCountIntroDruid.text: Primal Druid... A man torn between two worlds. But our forests have no place for another of your kind. Let the Greatwolf hear your final remarks.

IronCountStoryGlpyh.text: We have focused our excavations under the Manor, but we would be remiss to ignore other clan sites in our search for corpses that retain what we need. We should investigate the blasphemous graveyard the Eternals built atop our burial mounds...

IronCountStory2Glyph.text:
By decree of the Count of Ogham,

Effective immediately, all crimes are now punishable by hanging until death.

Hanged criminals will have their bodies thrown into the pit.

IronCountStory3Glyph.text:
By decree of the Count of Ogham,

Able-bodied men capable of excavation must present themselves at the Manor at once.

Failure to do so will constitute a crime.

IronCountStory4Glyph.text:
I have received reports of a number of villagers hiding at the Clearfell logging site. 

Travel there and convey my order to return. Anyone refusing my Authority should be considered a traitor and a criminal. 

Deal with them as you see fit, but bring their bodies back to the Manor.

IronCountCourtyardGlyph.text:
By decree of the Count of Ogham,

All men must work a third shift and continue excavating until further notice. Any man caught resting will meet the Executioner's axe... or the Gallow's noose.

IronCountTreeOfSoulsGlyph.text:
By decree of the Count of Ogham,

Those condemned to hang from these branches are to be left until their hearts no longer beat, their lungs no longer fill with air, and their flesh is no longer warm. In death, you are not forgiven. 

Your souls will remain trapped here by this ancient maw of maligned wood, and the Grove will be forever denied you. 

Rot here in the Grelwood for all time, and good riddance.

IronCountCanopyGlyph.text:
By decree of the Count of Ogham,

To the scoundrels and cowards hiding among the trees of the Clanless Perch,

As the loyal men of Ogham lay down their lives to protect those who support them, you hide. 
As the women of Ogham sweat and ache, skinning beasts upon which we feed, you hide.
As the children of Ogham play at war, preparing to serve the greater needs of the people, you traitors hide.

I will offer clemency only once. Return to the manor immediately and serve Ogham, as is your duty, and your punishment will be deferred.

IronCountCourtyardGlyph2.text:
Soldiers of Ogham,

The outside threat grows ever stronger. Whispers of betrayal echo within my very halls. We can no longer tolerate any risk. 

Use lethal force against those you suspect of foul play. Speak carefully with your men. Ensure they are who they claim. Hang any suspects. Seek out resistance within the village and raze their homes to the ground. 

We must send a clear message. Leave no stone unturned.

IronCountVillageGlyph.text:
By decree of the Count of Ogham,

Your whispering and conspiring has not gone unnoticed. I see your disloyalty. I hear your mockery. However, your plots against me all lay dead in their tracks. Every villager must report to the Manor immediately for questioning. I alone will crush this revolt. Anyone who resists will not only be considered a criminal, but an avowed traitor.

IronCountManorJournal1Glyph.text:
Outsiders can never understand the Ezomyte struggle. Our folklore goes back to the very Winter of the World, when we were but savages clawing grubs from the dirt. 

The Eternal Empire tried to crush us. They failed. Not even the event that destroyed the Vaal could end us. We strengthened in the wake of their Cataclysm, harnessing runes, mastering the world around us. 

We have always fought for survival, for home, for hearth. That is the bloodline I am proud of, stretching back thousands of years... That is what I must defend... To keep pure.

IronCountManorJournal2Glyph.text:
I sense Oriana knows... And I cannot deny that which I know deep down to be true. 

That fair haired villager, an Eternal descendent... She knew. 

At that moment when our eyes locked... We both knew. 

She clung to her children like I would end them then and there. She is of no risk now but... How many others must I fear? Is my blood truly impure?

Oriana assures me, we can right some of the wrongs of the past.
She promises a way forward for Ogham. A way forward for the clans and the clanless alike. And... A way forward for me. We must continue with our task.

FinnIntroWarrior.text: Oi, it's you! You're Renly's foundling—ah, Renly's <i>{son}, aren't you? Good to finally meet you. <continue>I am Finn, and I shall be your humble provider of useful and diverse objects that are most definitely <i>{not} scrounged or stolen. If I don't got it, I <i>{can} get it. <i>{You just let me know.}

FinnIntroRanger.text: Oi, it's you, the mysterious woman in the forest! We've never officially met, but you've certainly given me quite the fright a time or two. <continue>I am Finn, and I shall be your humble provider of useful and diverse objects that are most definitely <i>{not} scrounged or stolen. If I don't got it, I <i>{can} get it. You just let me know.

FinnIntroDruid.text: A Druid! I should have expected one of <i>{you} to emerge from the forest, given these dark days. <continue>I am Finn, and I shall be your humble provider of useful and diverse objects... that are most definitely not scrounged or stolen. If I don't got it, I <i>{can} get it. You just let me know.

FinnIntroMonk.text: Have we met? Ah, no, we haven't. Hard to tell monks apart. You lot let me stay in your enclave one winter. I was, ah... unfairly asked to leave, under suspicion of <i>{thievery}. Wasn't me, though. I'm well known as an honourable man around 'ere, ask anybody! <continue>The name's Finn, and I shall be your humble provider of useful and diverse objects... that are most definitely not scrounged or stolen. If I don't got it, I <i>{can} get it. You just let me know.

FinnIntro.text: Welcome, violent stranger! I am Finn, and I shall be your humble provider of useful and diverse objects that are most definitely <i>{not} scrounged or stolen. <continue>If I don't got it, I can get it. You just let me know.

FinnDevourerDead.text: You killed the Devourer in its own lair? That's mighty brave of you, hero. Now we at least won't starve to death! One less way to die, I guess.

FinnRedValeAdviceWarrior.text: Spirits in the trees be damned, you actually entered the Red Vale and survived? Every Ogham kid knows, <i>{"If you step one foot in there, you'll be skewered and eaten!"} Well, those kids that are lucky enough to have a mother, that is. <continue>Oh, shite—no offence. I was talking about me, not you... Although, I guess we do have that in common.

FinnRedValeAdviceGearSeenWarrior.text: Spirits in the trees be damned, you actually entered the Red Vale and survived? Every Ogham kid knows, <i>{"If you step one foot in there, you'll be skewered and eaten!"} Well, those kids that are lucky enough to have a mother, that is. <continue>Oh, shite—no offence. I was talking about me, not you... Although, I guess we do have that in common. <continue>How rusted is the gear? Any of it salvageable? Worth anything? Just... uh... thinking out loud.

FinnRedValeAdvice.text: Spirits in the trees be damned, you actually entered the Red Vale and survived? Every Ogham kid knows, <i>{"If you step one foot in there, you'll be skewered and eaten!"} Well, those kids that are lucky enough to have a mother, that is.

FinnRedValeAdviceGearSeen.text: Spirits in the trees be damned, you actually entered the Red Vale and survived? Every Ogham kid knows, <i>{"If you step one foot in there, you'll be skewered and eaten!"} Well, those kids that are lucky enough to have a mother, that is. <continue>How rusted is the gear? Any of it salvageable? Worth anything? Just... uh... thinking out loud.

FinnHuntingGroundsNoQuest.text: Now see, I used to frequent the clanless enclave that makes its home high in the trees near here. The locals call it Freythorn. A little while back, a group of strangers arrived out of the deep woods. <continue><i>{They} made altars like this, and started whispering to the others about their 'religion'. That was when I decided to move on. And judging by the size of this one, things have gotten worse. A lot worse. <continue>Something's wrong, hero. Something's definitely off. I thought I was imagining the whispers in the shadows at night up there. Thought I was just spooked by the cultists that had moved in... but maybe not. <continue>Though it is full of scoundrels, I was mildly fond of a fair few of them. Care to pay them a visit and see how they are doing?

FinnHuntingGroundsQuest.text: So... I was right to be worried. They're still making these damned altars. And this one's bigger. <continue>Something's wrong, hero. Something's definitely off.  I thought I was imagining the whispers in the shadows at night up there. Thought I was just spooked by the cultists... but maybe not. <continue>Please... check in on the enclave. I'm gonna get while the getting's good.

FinnTheOutcastQuest.text: I have a grand quest for you, hero. The kind that'll get you woven into legend. It's not at all a minor personal matter that you might ignore. <continue>How do I explain this? Before this dreary place, you could say I was something of a, uh... wanderer. There's a clanless enclave known as The Freythorn that makes its home high in the trees near the Hunting Grounds. They helped me out a time or two over the years. <continue>A little while back, a group of strangers arrived out of the deep woods. They made strange altars, and started whispering to the others about their 'religion'. That was when I decided to move on. <continue>See, now I got to thinking. If Count Geonor and his men are mad enough to burn the village, then maybe the clanless are in trouble, too. <continue>Will you pay them a visit? I used to be mildly fond of a fair few of them.

FinnQuestComplete.text: Everyone I knew in Freythorn - the lot of those miserable rascals, curs, and thieves - they're dead or insane. <continue>Clearfell's all I have left now. If I was a drinking man, it'd be a sobering thought.

FinnBurningVillageGossipWarrior.text: Una's house... <i>{your} house!... You lot had real places to live! I was always so envious, but I guess... you're like me now. Vagabonds. Vagrants. <continue>It begs the question... is this our home now? Does that make us bunkmates? I call the top bunk!

FinnBurningVillageGossip.text: Una's house... Renly's house... They had real places to live! I was always so envious, but I guess... they're like me now. Vagabonds. Vagrants. It begs the question... is <i>{this} home now? <continue>You've caught me in a moment of sappiness, hero. My apologies.

FinnTheCountPreManor.text: Never had any love for ol' Count Geonor. Give him a stab or two for me.

FinnEndOfActWarrior.text: The clan leaders are all dead, but there's one man who remains with the leadership to carry on. Your old man will take good care of us, as is his nature. <continue>We'll be just fine, hero. You can ride on out of here with your head held high. Seriously, though. I hope you return someday, if only to guard my back.

FinnEndOfAct.text: The clan leaders are all dead, but there's one man who remains with the leadership to carry on. Renly will take good care of us, as is his nature. <continue>We'll be just fine, hero. You can ride on out of here with your head held high. Seriously, though. I hope you return someday, if only to guard my back.

FinnOnFinn.text: <italic>{Oh, that Finn's a bad influence! No daughter of mine will consort with such a type! We should have the village guards give him a good beatin' just to teach him a lesson!} <continue>Though I suppose nursing a grudge is foolish, given they're likely all dead now...

FinnOnCount.text: I was first to notice the mad Count's fist closing around this land. He kept rounding up people like me... for reasons that smelled like wolf droppings. <continue>I'm a bit of a slippery fish though, so I dodged his nets. Then, his mercenaries started coming for people I actually liked, and that's when I knew something was up. <continue>The village folk kept defending his actions. I don't know why they couldn't see it. Maybe they didn't want to see it.

FinnOnLeitis.text: I always make sure to avoid noblewomen like Leitis. Her kind seem to think I'm <i>{insincere}, for reasons neither you nor I could <i>{ever} comprehend, I'm sure. <continue>Still, I certainly heard about her, and I've heard what she's said about the Manor. I know liars, hero, and she isn't one.

FinnUna.text: Oh, Una? Yeah, yeah, I know her. I was, um... elsewhere... when the Count tried to arrest her family, but I certainly heard about it! It's just a coincidence we both ended up here. <continue>Don't get the wrong idea. I didn't follow her or anything like that. It would be unheard of for a clanned girl and an outcast to—well, whatever you're thinking, don't. <continue>That's where I stand on it. You gotta be grounded in the real world. Don't get hung up on things that can never be. It'll just break your heart.

FinnClearfell.text: <i>{This} is a wooden tomb, if you care to see it objectively. We're not quite dead yet, but food supply is dwindling, and I've seen what hunger can make a man do. The monsters out there are not the ones that will get us in the end.

FinnClearfellAfterDevourer.text: Well, it seems we can venture out to gather food now, thanks to the timely intervention of our local hero against the dreaded Devourer. <continue>Congratulations, you've saved us from hunger. Now the monsters in the forest can kill us instead!

FinnTheHoodedOne.text: So, you found a shadow in the forest, and you brought it <i>{here}. Good. Great. Superb.

FinnTheHoodedOneTwo.text: Those glowing blue eyes make it hard to sleep at night. I'd wear something over my face to block out the glare, but, silly me, I left my sleeping veil back at my palace.

FinnCanopy.text: As an esteemed member of no clan at all, I had the distinct honour of wandering through the lovely sights of all four seasons. Summer heat, winter chill, take your pick. <continue>For company, it was my pleasure to sup with the outlaws, the deranged, and the unwanted. It's simply unthinkable that I never met a nice girl to settle down with, isn't it? <continue>It won't be like this forever. I'm going to build my palace someday. Been planning it since I was small and found myself on my own. Imagine with me, if you will, a vast span of wood above you in the trees. That's the foundation you're looking at. <continue>You ascend a tremendous spiral staircase around an ancient trunk, and find yourself approaching a treehouse worthy of the First Ones. Dozens of lavish bedrooms, two—<i>{two!}—stocked kitchens, tall spires, a tower that looks out over all of Ogham, and half of Phaaryl for good measure. <continue>Isn't it glorious? <i>{That's} where I really live. This cold, damp, hungry world is just an illusion.

FinnOnRenlyWarrior.text: Your old man's alright by me. Never said an unkind word. Treasure what you've got, you hear me?

FinnOnRenly.text: Renly's alright. Only man in the village that didn't run me out of town whenever he saw me. Maybe it's because he didn't have a daughter to protect.

FinnCanopySummonInFirstRitual.text: I... can't believe it. The whole bloody place has gone mad. Cursed cultists! <continue>Please, hero. Find the other altars and... dispose of them. Put an end to this. I'm going to check around here for any... sane survivors.

FinnCanopySummonInAfterKing.text: So, the cultists really did have a king lurking out there in the shadows. Shame. I might have followed him myself if he'd simply promised decent meals instead. <continue>Thank you, hero. It's not the result I was hoping for, but at least I know the truth. Clearfell's all I have left now. If I was a drinking man, it'd be a sobering thought.

FinnOnEinhar.text: Ah, you heard about him, have you? Some of the scoundrels up in the enclave would spin all sorts of tales after a few too many drinks. <continue><i>{"The Legend of the Great Hunter"} was one of their favorites. They say that many moons ago he'd frequent Ogham, specifically for the Hunting Grounds. Over time, he grew to be someone that the clanless idolised. <continue>But honestly, the whole idea of him to me sounds like some drunken man's dream.

FinnWildLeavingHuntingGrounds.text: Good luck, hero. For now, I'm gonna get while the getting's good.

LachlannWildShout_Random.text: Quickly! My family has been abducted!

LachlannGreeting.text: That bastard tyrant, Praetor Draven! He's taken my family hostage! They're being held somewhere beyond these gates. I never thought he would stoop <i>{this} low! <continue>I sent for reinforcements... but... it's been so long... I must get through the gate... The keys... where are the blasted keys? I... I believe those cowards took them...

LachlannWildOpeningGate.text: At last! It's open! Praise the First Ones!

LachlannFoundWife.text: I can hear Isabel... Where is she? She calls to me... but we cannot go without Calum and Torcall!

LachlannFoundBoys.text: My boys... I can hear them... They call to me! But we cannot go without Isabel...

LachlannFoundEveryone.text: My family... they are calling my name... but... but I can't follow... Why...? Why did the Eternals do this to us? They must pay for what they have done! I must make them <i>{suffer!}

LachlannWildFindGraves.text: Isabel... Torcall... Calum... the family of Count Lachlann of Ogham... My family! This doesn't make any sense! They're <i>{dead!} Those bastard Eternals... I must make them pay... I must make them <i>{suffer!}

LachlannOnPraetor.text: The Praetor...? Oh, the Praetor! That monster! He is the worst man the Eternals could have chosen as the custodian for this territory. Had he come to us in peace, the clans might have been willing to talk, but that damn swine regards us as nothing but dogs. <continue>He invaded the village in the night, without warning, without honour! He seized my family, to try to force us to surrender. <continue>The Eternal Empire cares for nothing but power! But mark my words, we will not be ground under the heel of tyranny!

LachlannOnUprising.text: Uprising...? The uprising! Of course! The clans are uniting to fight for their freedom. We are making our stand in the Vale...

LachlannOnHostages.text: Hostages...? Hostages! Praetor Draven is a coward, and without honour. He thinks he can keep us suppressed by holding my family hostage. He must pay for what he has done!

LachlannOnGraveyard.text: This graveyard is being built atop our clan graves by our oppressors, as an insult intended to crush our spirits. Misguided tyrants! We will never give up the fight. <continue>We're wearing them down, flesh and spirit. Conquerors they may be, but strong? Ha!

LachlannOnOgham.text: Ogham? Oh yes, Ogham... this is the oldest home of the Ezomytes as we know ourselves. Past generations departed from here to settle Ezomyr and the Isles of Skothe. <continue>We did not always call this part of Phaaryl our homeland... and now the Eternals have come with their armies and laid claim to this place. It'll be a cold day in the Vastiri Desert before we submit!

LachlannOnPhaaryl.text: Before... Phaaryl...? Ah... the songs are unclear after so much time. A great many generations ago, we were driven here from elsewhere. There was simply too much Corruption, too much darkness... It was a time of chaos and terror, and much was lost. <continue>Our clans swore that this was the last time we would ever be cast out of our homes. Rise up, Ezomytes! We shall drive off these Eternal bastards!

LachlannFamily.text: All I can think about is seeing my beloved Isabel again, and holding my two boys in my arms... Torcall... Calum... it feels like it's been so long...

LachlannOnAsinia.text: The Consort? Oh, Asinia! Curse the foul witch. She mired our lands with hexes upon our graves, so the dead may not die. <continue>She was but a servant girl to the Praetor's family... it was said she poisoned his first wife... aspired to replace her... She succeeded... and Draven... he was not dismayed by the darkness in her. He embraced it... and together, they conspired in their vile ambitions...

LachlannKilledPraetor.text: You <i>{felled} the Praetor? By the First Ones! I... I can't quite believe it. But... there's no time to waste. We must get through the gate. <continue>Find the Praetor's Witch... Find the other key...

LachlannKilledAsinia.text: You defeated Asinia? The Praetor will be devastated! He gets what he deserves. But... there's no time to waste. We must get through the gate. <continue>Find Draven... Find the other key...

LachlannOnReturnWithKeys.text: Do my eyes again deceive me? You have the keys! You showed those Eternal bastards! Use the keys to open the gate. Let's go and free my family!

LachlannOnTalkingAgainWithKeys.text: What? Enough talk! Open the gate!

LachlannWildGetOnWithIt_Random.text: Well, Don't just stand there. Get on with it!

LachlannWildGetOnWithIt_2.text: Well, Don't just stand there. Get on with it!

LachlannWildGetOnWithIt_3.text: Well, Don't just stand there. Get on with it!

LachlannWildGetOnWithIt_4.text: Well, Don't just stand there. Get on with it!

LachlannWildGetOnWithIt_5.text: Are you numb in the head? There's much to do!

LachlannWildGetOnWithIt_6.text: Are you numb in the head? There's much to do!

LachlannWildGetOnWithIt_7.text: Are you numb in the head? There's much to do!

LachlannWildGetOnWithIt_8.text: Are you numb in the head? There's much to do!

LachlannWildGetOnWithIt_9.text: What...? What's happening? Are you lost too?

LachlannWildGetOnWithIt_10.text: What...? What's happening? Are you lost too?

LachlannWildGetOnWithIt_11.text: What...? What's happening? Are you lost too?

LachlannWildGetOnWithIt_12.text: What...? What's happening? Are you lost too?

LachlannGraveyardGlyph.text:
The family of Count Lachlann of Ogham, murdered by the savage Eternals, laid to rest here for all time, together.

The Ezomytes will have their vengeance!

1215 I.C.

LachlannGrimTangleGlyph.text:
Finn:
There have been rumours that the forest paths have been somehow changing their shape. I can only ask the First Ones to aid this courier in finding his way to you.

I will not be able to bring potion supplies to the outcasts this High Moon. I've seen signs that the behavioural changes of the forest beasts may be afflicting men as well. There is something deeply wrong in the Manor; a leering energy that vitalises sickly men and slows the healthy. The shadows are starker, a glaring absence, as though darkness yearns to snuff out the light.

These fears must sound absurd, but I urge you to keep yourself and your fellow clanless safe. Pull up your ladders and do not eat the meat of the disturbed animals until we understand more.

Lachlann, Head Servant of Ogham Manor

LachlannVillageGlyph.text:
To Provost Connal Preas:
The Count's 'interest' in his heritage has grown into mania. At first, I thought our alliance with the outsiders was beneficial, but now I believe Ogham may be in great danger. The Manor's soldiers have been ordered to rip up the floor and dig, and I fear what they found beneath the layer of ash they hit this morning; twisted shapes, ancient agonies cast in stone, horrible proof of some event of colossal horror that burned the sky... I slipped away, that I might write to you. You were right. I was wrong.

Gather the village men as you planned. There is one final task I must endure for the Count, but when I return from the Eternal graveyard, I will give you entrance to the Manor in the dead of night, so that the Count can be secured and this madness put to an end. This is not a betrayal, it is a rescue. It is what our Lord needs to regain his sense. It is what we all need to quell our troubled dreams.

And that Maraketh wife of his, that Whisperer of Paranoias and Hatreds... I shall leave her fate up to you, Provost.

Lachlann, Head Servant of Ogham Manor

HoodedOneReleasedTalk.text: Thank you, mortal, for releasing me. I would join you, if you would accept my aid. Long have I walked this world, so I may be able to give you guidance.

HoodedOneGiveQuest.text: These strange occurrences. The wild beasts growing mad, the dead rising. These are not a coincidence. The source of this affliction may be found in Ogham Village. <continue>The count has stolen something. Something that can not be left in mortal hands. If we do not intervene quickly, we will all be at risk. <continue>The Tree of Souls is connected to this ancient forest. It knows a quicker way. I will... persuade it... to allow passage.

HoodedOneOldForestWildDepart.text: Go quickly. I will return to your 'Clearfell.' Seek me when you have need of guidance.

HoodedOneSeedOfCorruptionGossip.text: The boundless horrors of mishandled Corruption cannot be conveyed simply through words. Let us hope that we can find and contain the Seed before it is too late.

HoodedOneIronCountGossip.text: The Count accosted me and stole a very dangerous object. A Seed that I have kept hidden from humanity. Somehow he knew that I possessed it. He can have no idea how dangerous it is. His attempts to harness its power will court disaster. <continue>You must hurry to the Manor. At the very least, those who are still sane may be convinced to stop the inevitable course of events that will follow, if they feed and nurture the Seed of Corruption.

HoodedOneFirstOnesGossip.text: All children have imaginary friends. Most grow out of that phase. A rare few refuse to let go, creating real from unreal through sheer stubbornness. <continue>Gods born of man certainly exist, but did a gigantic red tiger named Farrul actually run the plains of the primordial world? There is no way to know. Will the world end if she and her savage ilk return? <continue>The answer, I imagine, is up to those who would stand and fight on that day. Be glad that today is not that day... as far as I know.

HoodedOneKilledLachlannGossip.text: Corruption once had a purpose. Let us term it a disorganiser of what would otherwise be ordered. One consequence of this chaos is the warping of pathways, both through the woods, and in the mind. <continue>The land so afflicted is never the same when trod upon a second time; men afflicted by Corruption know not where or when they are, only that they are in pain, and you appear as a horrible creature to their distorted senses.

HoodedOneReachedVillageGossip.text: The village has been destroyed? Then madness has already reached a boiling point in the minds of the Count's men. <continue>You must infiltrate the Manor and put a stop to this by any means necessary. The fate that befell Ogham Village is only a single raindrop in the storm that is coming.

HoodedOneReachedManorGossip.text: If you intend to face the Count, I must warn you: an ancient corrupting power has driven him to madness. There is no telling what you may find within the walls of the Manor. <continue>Where the Seed of Corruption takes root, life bends itself into unnatural shapes, and the minds of men grow fevered. Though you may face horrors beyond comprehension, it is this Seed that is the true danger at the heart of the Manor.

HoodedOneEndOfAct1Commentary.text: We must pursue Oriana! The Seed of Corruption has begun to grow, but there is still a chance that we can end this before it is too late. <continue>The fledgling Beast is leaving Corruption in its wake, so we have a trail to follow. When you are ready to part from this place, we can leave immediately.

HoodedOneGeonorDeathSequenceFirst.text: Allow me to clear your mind, if only for a moment.

HoodedOneGeonorDeathSequenceSecond.text: Where has she taken the Beast?

HoodedOneGeonorDeathSequenceFifth.text: We must make haste. Let us return to Clearfell to make our preparations.

EinharFourIntro.text:
You... are not from here. The way you move, the way you carry your weapon. You have not yet been grasped by the invisible tentacles of corruption that strangle both man and beast in these woods. It is unmistakable! You... are a survivor, just like Einhar.

And I... I am Einhar. You have heard of me, yes? The Einhar who ate two dozen rhoa eggs before I discovered they were not rhoa eggs at all but very soft rocks? The Einhar who wrestled a Blood Chieftain to the ground so I could take back my favourite leg bone? I can tell by the confused look on your face that you do recognise me. Good!

EinharFourHuntingGroundsMission.text:
It has been many years since Einhar scooped Necromancer face out of this mask. The smell has faded, even though I did not wash it even once! So, it is time to find a new mask. A fresh mask. But masks do not grow on trees! Believe me, Einhar has tried to grow many mask trees.

No, there is only one place to find a new mask with just the right smell. Come. We run!

EinharFourVillage.text: Einhar spent some time in the Village. If you plan to stay there for a long time, I would not mention that you know Einhar. We had a disagreement about which of the hounds were for eating. They said none of them, and Einhar disagreed.

EinharFourCount.text: I do not think Einhar met the Count, but I did hear many things about him while I stayed in the village. He is a believer in the First Ones too! But... He does not honour them. He does not hunt mighty beasts for sacrifice. He has men in armour do that for him. And some of the beasts the Count sacrificed were not beasts at all, but men! And not the men who were hunting beasts for them! And not just because they were not hunting beasts but men! The villagers stories were very confusing for Einhar. Beasts make for much better conversation.

EinharFourLocals.text:
The Ezomytes here are very different to Einhar. They have built barriers between themselves and the forest. It is a rejection of the First One's gifts! I think that is why the corruption is returning. 

It is a sign that the end is coming. Of that, I am sure.

GrimTangleGlyph1.text: <italic>{An 'ocean' rune has been carved in this ancient wayfinding stone. Someone seems to have scratched with their bare nails the words, 'Seek the mountain rune.'}

GrimTangleGlyph2.text: <italic>{A 'mountain' rune has been carved in this ancient wayfinding stone. Fresh but hurried etchings spell out, 'Seek the valley rune.'}

GrimTangleGlyph3.text: <italic>{A 'valley' rune has been carved in this ancient wayfinding stone. 'Seek the ocean rune' has been scrawled in blood, recently dried.}

MysticRankAndStatus.text: I have a very long official title, but you may simply address me as Zarka. The young ones will harp on and on about our strict traditions, but I'm old enough to get away with it, so I do! <continue>My role is that of a keeper of tales. I was chosen by my predecessor, rather than being allowed to become a <italic>{dekhara} or perform other duties. I am not permitted near combat, for the stories I keep are one of our most valuable resources. <continue>We understand the plains of Vastiri through the lens of these words handed down to us over the centuries. We see what used to lie where sand dwells now, and hear the bold proclamations and lamentations of yesteryear. That is my role, to be the worldly eyes and ears of the Ardura.

MatriarchGates.text: From what your shade has told us, the situation is dire. This <italic>{balbalakh} will live or die based on her usefulness in pursuit of the Seed of Corruption. Ask her what questions you will, then we Ardura will decide her fate.

MarakethMatriarchArea_g2_4_1.text: We know where the Lost City is, yes, for we would never forget the birthplace of our people. It has been reclaimed by the sands, though if what the <italic>{balbalakh} says is true about the Faridun scouts, recent sandstorms must have opened a path inside. Find that path, or make one yourself. We shall engage the Faridun elsewhere to distract them from your actions.

MatriarchGrantArea_g2_5.text: Though events demand you tread upon a valley of the dead, do not do so flagrantly. Keep your presence light, cleanse what Corruption you can, and we shall skirmish with the Faridun to protect your flank.

MatriarchGrantArea_g2_6.text: We will take you to the Valley of the Titans, though expect no aid in infiltrating that accursed lowland. The Maraketh do not step foot there. Instead, we shall guard the entrance, delaying the Faridun should they seek to stop you.

MatriarchGrantArea_g2_8.text: We have never made the journey to our Towers without bearing a fallen <italic>{dekhara} to bury in the sky. It is not a place for the living... this shall be a disquieting time. Tread lightly. We shall harry the Faridun and draw their ire while you work. We are not permitted to destroy our Honoured Dead... but you are. Do what you must to deny the enemy what he seeks.

MatriarchGrantArea_g2_10.text: [DNT-UNUSED] We have their trail now. They will not escape!

MatriarchGrantArea_g2_12.text: [DNT-UNUSED] Ah yes, there is something in the Wastes that we need. We have heard reports of a glowing rock that fell from the sky. I ask you to investigate this report.

MatriarchGatesVisitMeLater.text: Save the formalities. We must question this Defector. Meet me in the council den in the lead cart of my caravan.

MatriarchReturnedTusks.text: These tusks hold an inherent wisdom. They are the last remnants of a powerful race of creatures, a lesson carved in bone for those whose numbers dwindle from generation to generation.

MatriarchCommentsOnMastodons.text: [DNT-UNUSED] That valley of the Mastodons, where their bones lie rotting under the sun for all time, is proof that a culture can vanish entirely if the world changes too much. I will not let my people diminish and disappear the same way...

MatriarchBurnedWaterGoddess.text: So the water goddess was truly there, as Risu claimed. It is a shame that she chose to be burned alive rather than stand and fight, but it is not our shame to bear, only her own.

HoodedOneDockA2Intro.text: This outpost seems to be part of a trade route, so we should be able to find a Maraketh caravan. They are an honourable people, and I have no doubt they will assist us.

WaterGoddessSonConvoOne.text: I was mortal then... I was weak...

WaterGoddessSonConvoTwo.text: They told me you had died...

WaterGoddessSonConvoThree.text: Can you ever forgive my mistake?

WaterGoddessIntroSorc.text: A tale-woman? At last. <continue>Please... end my suffering. <continue>My followers are long since dust, and I am but parchment, my veins dry as sand.

WaterGoddessIntro.text: A mortal? Oh... at last. <continue>Please... end my suffering. <continue>My followers are long since dust, and I am but parchment, my veins dry as sand.

WaterGoddessSon.text: He was not my son. Not the one I knew. <continue>Corruption held his mortal soul in thrall, and you have finally given him peace...

WaterGoddessWisdomSorc.text: I sense great conflict in you. I have so much I could tell you, had I the strength; had you the time... <continue>But have no fear. Make your own path, and the river of your life will still find its way to the sea.

WaterGoddessPleaSorc.text: I ask you, tale-woman... <continue>To use that one element that may finally end me. <continue>My opposite... fire. It must be done.

WaterGoddessPlea.text: None remember my name, and none think of me. <continue>I awoke from my long slumber unable to move... My time has passed... <continue>I ask you, mortal, to use that one element that may finally end me. My opposite... fire. It must be done.

WaterGoddessGlyph.text: On this, the meeting place of seven waters, we lay the first stone of our new home. May Keth stand eternal, the heart of peace and prosperity, the bastion of our people!

WaterGoddessEssenceOfWater.text: Some Essence of Water remains. The last drops to be found in Keth.

RisuIntro.text: One thousand praises, my friend! I thought I would die here. <continue>Please, take me back to your caravan and I will tell you anything you want to know.

RisuIdentitySorceress.text: I am of the Faridun. You know us, tale-woman. We are your unwanted and forgotten. Some time ago, a foreign woman came to us, and offered us the power to seize what was ours. We took her deal. We had no idea what it would cost us. <continue>When she finally brought us the Beast, it was not the glorious power we'd been promised. It was horrifying. Those of us who did not want to make war, those of us who were afraid of the Beast... Jamanra sealed us in the mine when his Dreadnought was complete. <continue>This madness must end! Some may call me a traitor, but I do not seek the destruction of my brethren. I seek their salvation.

RisuIdentity.text: I am of the Faridun. We are the shadows of the Maraketh, the unwanted and the forgotten. Some time ago, a foreign woman came to us, and offered us the power to take back what was ours. We took her deal. We had no idea what it would cost us. <continue>When she finally brought us the Beast, it was not the glorious power we'd been promised. It was horrifying. Those of us who did not want to make war, those of us who were afraid of the Beast... Jamanra sealed us in the mine when his Dreadnought was complete. <continue>This madness must end! Some may call me a traitor, but I do not seek the destruction of my brethren. I seek their salvation.

RisuQuest.text: I know what Jamanra intends, for the Maraketh have made a grave error. Atop their burial spires lie their most honoured dead. Our new Queen demanded he seek any trace of ancient flesh from those of renown or power in life. <continue>He intends to feed their bodies to a horrific creature he keeps in a cage behind his throne. They call it the Beast. I have seen it, and the sight haunts my nightmares...

BalbalaSanctumQuest.text: We have met in battle, but not in peace. I am Balbala, once a traitor, long a sorrowed prisoner. <continue>As Djinn, here I shall serve as your guide. Together, we shall prove ourselves worthy.

BalbalaSanctumQuestCompleteSorc.text: You have danced with death... and survived. The trial is complete! <continue>Whether they like it or not, the others must accept you as a <i>{dekhara} now. The tale-woman life was never meant for you. I can see that, so perhaps they will come to see it as well. <continue>I will remain here for the time being. I am finally free, but I find I do not wish to rest just yet. <continue>This place is in disrepair. Though it may take another thousand years, I must restore it to its former glory. Should you need me, I will continue to serve as your guide here.

BalbalaSanctumQuestComplete.text: It is done! You are no longer a <i>{jingakh}! You now carry with you the spirit of a Maraketh <i>{dekhara}. <continue>I am finally free, but I find I do not wish to rest just yet. <continue>This place is in disrepair. Though it may take another thousand years, I must restore it to its former glory. <continue>Should you need me, I will continue to serve as your guide here.

BalbalaOnSanctum.text: I have had a great many years to think on my foolish choices, and now all I want is to earn my right to rest. <continue>This place was built to determine honour, to prove oneself worthy as a Sekhema. Tradition allowed for one <i>{dekhara}, and one advisor. <continue>If I aid you here, and if you succeed, then my crimes will finally be forgiven. Then, and only then, may I join those that have gone before.

BalbalaOnTraitor.text: I hardly know the woman I was before. I remember betraying my <i>{akhara}, but the reasons why now feel petty and small. <continue>If I could go back, if I could speak to the woman I was, I would tell her what a fool she was being. Would she listen? Probably not... <continue>The mistakes we make are shaped from who we are.

BalbalaOnImprisonment.text: The tale-women of many <i>{akharas} gathered on the day of my sentencing. Death was not punishment enough for my crime. <continue>They enacted the ritual, but my imprisonment as Djinn would not have been possible without my willful agreement. <continue>I accepted. I let it happen, because I deserved it. <continue>I have no idea how long I was trapped there, but it was as close to eternity as I can possibly imagine.

BalbalaOnAid.text: The role of advisor is strictly bound by tradition. I may offer you aid, but only in certain specific ways. <continue>Look to me in your times of doubt.

BalbalaOnDjinn.text: The river inside you, the essence of who you are, can be torn out of you under the right conditions. It can be speared, or bottled, or chained. <continue>A spirit without a body, especially one created in this manner, is called a Djinn. It has prolonged my existence, but it is not a form anyone should desire... <continue>I grow hungry, but cannot eat. I grow tired, but cannot sleep.
