This is a far cry from the saline depths of Tsoatha, a place which harboured boundless depth and majesty, and yet this is where we will carry out our finest work yet. Tsoatha was the domain I shared with The Brine King – may he rest forever in the depths of oblivion – but these caverns are ours to make our own! Go forth, my handmaidens, and enact the fates that wayward explorers deserve upon them; these voyagers must be punished for encroaching upon the infinite bounty of the ocean, which our kind shall have dominion over!

– Adrapheme, Voice of Death

SirenCaveGlyph02.text: This is a far cry from the saline depths of Tsoatha, a place which harboured boundless depth and majesty, and yet this is where we will carry out our finest work yet. Tsoatha was the domain I shared with The Brine King – may he rest forever in the depths of oblivion – but these caverns are ours to make our own! Go forth, my handmaidens, and enact the fates that wayward explorers deserve upon them; these voyagers must be punished for encroaching upon the infinite bounty of the ocean, which our kind shall have dominion over!

TwilightOrderPreacherInterrupt.text: Friend, I have urgent news for you. Time is short, and the unmaking of the world is nigh. Please listen to what I have to say.

TwilightOrderPreacherOnTwilightOrder.text: We are an order of true believers dedicated to the salvation of humanity. To that end, we have given everything, and will continue to give of ourselves until Wraeclast is saved. Surely, we are on the same side! Surely, you will pledge yourself to aid in the cause!

TwilightOrderPreacherNews.text: The end of days approaches. Something evil has awoken on Wraeclast. You have faced it, have you not? I can see it in your eyes. You have faced the wickedness in the hearts of men. They seek to conquer us, to rule us. They seek immortality at our expense. We must act! We must fight back!

TwilightOrderPreacherFightBack.text: Yes, we must fight back, together! Do you hear that, Kalguurans? Here is one who will join us in the fight! We will save this world. Utopia is a dream, but Wraeclast is a nightmare. Let us choose which we live in, yes?

TwilightOrderPreacherFightBackIsland.text: Yes, we must fight back, together! We will save this world. Utopia is a dream, but Wraeclast is a nightmare. Let us choose which we live in, yes?

TwilightOrderUtopia.text: We work toward utopia, even knowing it can never be real until the iniquities and inadequacies of life are defeated. Utopia is not possible while the wickedness in the hearts of men can be rewarded with immortality. Our Saviour will bring about that utopia, and in it, you shall be free. There will be none to rule you, none to tell you how to live. The struggle for freedom from tyranny will finally be over!

TwilightOrderLiberator.text: Our Saviour is not a god, not divine. Merely mortal, but alone among all humanity, the Saviour is being raised free from Corruption. If you wish to know more, you should visit our enclave. It is not too far from here! Already, the Karui are flocking to our island, eager to join the cause and save Wraeclast! Will you pledge yourself to the Twilight Order as well?

TwilightOrderPledge.text: Come to our island. Visit our enclave. There, you can take the pledge, and we can properly induct you. It may just be the most important thing you ever do!

TwilightOrderKalguurans.text: We do not despise the Kalguurans. We merely consider them lucky fools. In their faraway land, they have no Corruption or Divinity, so they do not take our struggle here seriously.

TwilightOrderInteractSinA.text: Foul creature! I have never seen one so obviously guilty of sin!

TwilightOrderInteractSinB.text: What manner of being are you, foul creature?

TwilightOrderInteractTujenB1.text: Hook-hand! Will you join us in the fight?

TwilightOrderInteractTujenB2.text: Hook-hand! Will you join us in the fight?

TwilightOrderShout1.text: The unmaking of the world is nigh! We must act!

TwilightOrderShout2.text: The unmaking of the world is nigh! We must act!

TwilightOrderShout3.text: The unmaking of the world is nigh! We must act!

TwilightOrderShout4.text: We must unite to seek salvation!

TwilightOrderShout5.text: We must unite to seek salvation!

TwilightOrderShout6.text: We must unite to seek salvation!

TwilightOrderShout8.text: Our Saviour will come, and we shall be freed!

TwilightOrderShout9.text: Our Saviour will come, and we shall be freed!

TwilightOrderShout10.text: Utopia is not a dream! It will be made real!

TwilightOrderShout11.text: Utopia is not a dream! It will be made real!

TwilightOrderShout12.text: Utopia is not a dream! It will be made real!

TwilightOrderClassCommentSorceress.text: A Sorceress, from the lands of the Maraketh!

TwilightOrderClassCommentWitch.text: A Witch, from the reclusive covens!

TwilightOrderClassCommentDruid.text: A Druid, from the forests of Ogham!

TwilightOrderClassCommentMarauder.text: A Marauder, son of the Karui!

TwilightOrderClassCommentWarrior.text: A Warrior, on the campaign trail!

TwilightOrderClassCommentMercenary.text: A Mercenary, a long way from home!

TwilightOrderClassCommentHuntress.text: A Huntress, of the humble Azmeri?

TwilightOrderClassCommentShadow.text: Oh my, a Shadow... walking about in broad daylight...

TwilightOrderClassCommentMonk.text: A Monk, from the distant Ogham!

TwilightOrderWelcomeMet.text: Welcome, friend! I'm glad you've decided to come learn more about our Order. Together, we might just save this world!

TwilightOrderWelcomeNotMet.text: Welcome, friend! This is the humble enclave of the Twilight Order. Are you here because you heard our important message?

TwilightOrderOnThisIsland.text: Ah, our beautiful little island! We came here and built this enclave so that we might better reach the Karui with our message. They are a strong people, a warrior culture, and have always rejected Corruption. Now we must teach them that they must reject Divinity as well. Many have already begun to question after the death of their god, Tukohama. The rest is up to us!

TwilightOrderOnTukohama.text: Yes, yes, twenty years ago, that mysterious Godslayer rampaged across Wraeclast and showed the world that it could be done! Tukohama died at the hands of a mortal! The gods can be defeated! Humanity does not have to suffer under the Yoke of Ambition!

TwilightOrderOnYokeOfAmbition.text: You really must return later for one of my sermons. I'll explain it all in detail! But to put it short, mankind can never truly be free so long as ambition can lead to godhood. Every warlord, every king, every Sekhema will eventually fall to temptation. The very existence of our faith in them corrupts them, changes them. It is a burden that makes civilisation impossible!

TwilightOrderOnCivilisation.text: That's what our Saviour will seek to bring, my friend. Peace. Prosperity. Utopia will be simple, once we no longer have to suffer the constant problems of Corruption and Divinity. It is a wondrous dream, is it not?

TwilightOrderOnTheSpear.text: You're looking for ancient ruins? On our little island? I suppose I've seen some old weathered stones here and there. Now that I think about it, I'm certain I've seen a graven image of that spear of yours. Do you mind waiting here while I ask the bishop? He would know better than I.

TwilightOrderReassures.text: Wait here. I'll be right back.

KingsmarchRogIntroduction.text: Oh, it's you! Welcome to my shop, Rog's Rare Reagents. Let me know if you have any questions.

KingsmarchRogOnKingsmarch.text: Oh, Kingsmarch? It's what we Kalguurans call this little port town of ours, and also the region around it. This has all been authorised by the king... and we certainly pay enough taxes that we can never forget that...

KingsmarchRogOnTheKing.text: There is no greater a concentration of loyal and dedicated followers of the King than here in this fair port town... <i>{friend.}

KingsmarchRogOnKalguurans.text: What to say about my people? Many of us here on Wraeclast are in various guilds. I'm in the Meridian Free Traders, that's the trade guild that owns the charter for Kingsmarch. You can't beat our logistics! Dannig is in the Artificers' Guild these days. Tujen's a freelance harbourmaster, but he stays close. You gotta keep the family together, you know?

KingsmarchRogOnShop.text: This shop is my pride and joy. I been dreaming of running my own place since my younger days, even though that was impossible back home. I always knew I'd have to leave. I was never one for grand quests, even though it was one of those that brought me to this land. Always preferred sorting logistics from the back. The wife says I'm the real hero, because I actually have a job and support my family. She might just be buttering me up, but I still take it to heart.

KingsmarchRogOnGrandQuest.text: The grand quest that brought me here? Oh, no, that's a long story. I couldn't possibly.

KingsmarchRogOnGrandQuestAgain.text:
Alright then, if you insist, I'll tell the tale! Two decades ago, our glorious leader, Dannig, led us on an expedition across the stormy and dangerous oceans to look for an artefact called the Triskelion Flame. Our search took us to the forsaken continent of Wraeclast, a land filled with horrible monsters and raving mad exiles!

But we excavated many ancient sites, uncovering some of the lost history of our people's short residence here. Long ago, Kalguurans tried to settle on Wraeclast, and, well... it didn't go well. In the end, they did not survive, and they lost the Triskelion Flame. We've been looking for it for over twenty years now, and, to be honest, we've gotten a bit sidetracked, but my wife refuses to give up on the dream.

KingsmarchRogOnWife.text: You'll run into her out there on the islands, I'm sure. She intends to excavate them all, one by one. At this point, I think she just enjoys digging up ancient relics. She gets excited for every single one, because there's always a chance, however small, that it'll all finally pay off. Me? I'm happy to stay here and watch the children. She's never gone too long.

KingsmarchRogOnPreacher.text: Business has been up ever since he took up residence outside my shop. People duck in here to seek refuge from him, and I make a sale while they hide. It's a win for everybody!

KingsmarchRogJustShip.text: I can sell this haul for you. Should be more than enough to hire a ship. The only captain available is new to the job, but I know her. Her name's Makoru. She'll get you where you need to go.

KingsmarchRogGenericMedicine.text: That is quite rare! I always like to find a use for... organic remains. I'll have to experiment on a few pieces of equipment to see what effect it might have. Take this for your troubles.

KingsmarchRogGenericTrophy.text: I don't even want to ask what manner of beast you slew to get that. If you're willing, I might be interested in buying that from you, so long as you don't tell anyone about your battle. If I had that trophy, then maybe it wasn't <i>{you} that won a legendary battle. Maybe it was <i>{me}. That'll impress the wife!

KingsmarchRogEyeballs.text: These... oh... these are <i>{eyeballs}. I should have eaten less for lunch. Ooh! There's a power about these squishy red orbs. I can feel it. I wonder what effect squeezing their contents onto a piece of equipment would have? I'd like to find out. Here, take this as fair trade.

KingsmarchRogTongue.text: Ah, I recognise that scent. Tongue of a sea serpent! It's a mighty fine delicacy, and a decent medicine besides. This one is unusually large... where did you get this? Wait, no, don't tell me. I'll buy it from you no questions asked. Fair trade.

KingsmarchRogSerpentHead.text: You've got the head of a sea serpent, have you? I'll buy that from you, fair trade, but I'm not entirely sure what I'm going to do with it. I'll be taking a loss on this one, but you've done right by us, so I don't mind. Wait... this is enormous! Where did you get this from? Wait, no, don't tell me. It's better that way.

KingsmarchRogLiver.text: This liver... it keeps healing when I test it with a knife. I simply must buy this wonder from you. It could be a perpetual source of medicinal compounds. Fair trade, as always.

KingsmarchRogSirenHead.text: There was a medusa siren in this region? And you cut her head off? I should probably buy her head from you before somebody accidentally gets turned into stone. Fair trade.

KingsmarchRogSirenCords.text: The vocal cords of a siren! These are a rare and powerful organ that I've seen used to forge incredible armour. Dannig could put this to use but it'll take a few years to cure them properly... I'll get back to you. In the meantime, here's something for your trouble.

KingsmarchRogLipRing.text: Is this the lip ornament of the sulphite tyrant? Why've you brought it here?! Ugh, it smells... I suppose I should buy it from you, since I'm never one to pass up a profit opportunity, and I know certain Karui who hated this man with a passion... fair trade...

KingsmarchRogLipRingDiskThing.text: Hmm.. I should call this the Kin King's Lip-Ring Disk Thing... heh heh heh...

KingsmarchRogScourgeOfTheSkiesTalon.text: I know more than a few Karui who would pay a hefty fee for proof that avian monstrosity is dead. It'll be a bit safer for them to poach Shrike eggs now. I'd be happy to act as arbitrage and buy that off of you. Here, fair trade.

KingsmarchDannigIntroductionSorceress.text: Ah, a Sorceress in Kingsmarch! What a strange sight. I've heard tales of your kind. My name is Dannig, and I am the blacksmith and leader of this fair port. This far from home, you must be on a grand quest of your own. We should exchange tales over an ale one of these days!

KingsmarchDannigIntroductionWitch.text: A Witch in Kingsmarch! Never a good omen. Dark times ahead, I take it. Conduct your black business and move along.

KingsmarchDannigIntroductionTemplar.text: A Templar! Still clinging to the old ways, eh? Welcome to Kingsmarch. I am the smith and leader of this fair port. We'll trade with you, but don't expect abundant kindness.

KingsmarchDannigIntroductionDruid.text: A Druid, in the flesh! Pardon my surprise, wise one. My people once had an order of Druids long ago. You have my utmost respect. I'm Dannig. Welcome to Kingsmarch!

KingsmarchDannigIntroductionMarauder.text: Ah, a fellow warrior! You and I must share tales of ancestral bravery over an ale one of these days. Welcome to Kingsmarch. I am Dannig, the blacksmith and leader of this fair port.

KingsmarchDannigIntroductionBrute.text: Ah, a fellow blacksmith! Or perhaps, former blacksmith, it seems. You and I must share tales of ancestral bravery over an ale one of these days. Welcome to Kingsmarch. I am Dannig, the smith and leader of this fair port.

KingsmarchDannigIntroductionGladiator.text: Welcome to Kingsmarch, stranger. I am Dannig, the smith and leader of this fair port. You seem like you know how to handle yourself. You'll fit in around here.

KingsmarchDannigIntroductionMercenary.text: Greetings, Mercenary. You'll find plenty of work here in Kingsmarch, if you're so inclined. I'm Dannig, the smith and leader of this fair port. Come to me for your equipment needs.

KingsmarchDannigIntroductionRanger.text: Don't worry, I won't try to shake your hand. I've seen a few recluses in my time, Ranger. You are safe here in Kingsmarch. I'm Dannig, the smith and leader of this fair port. Respect our laws, and we'll keep our distance.

KingsmarchDannigIntroductionHuntress.text: Hail, wildwoman. I am Dannig. This is Kingsmarch. Welcome.

KingsmarchDannigIntroductionAssassin.text: I can't say you're welcome here, Shadow, but we have no specific quarrel with you. I am Dannig, and this is Kingsmarch. Conduct your business and move along.

KingsmarchDannigIntroductionMonk.text: You're a curious one, Monk. Can't say I've ever seen one of your faith before, though we have more than our fair share of monks back home. This is Kingsmarch, I am Dannig, and you are welcome to practice your faith here if so inclined. Can't be worse than the preacher we've already got...

KingsmarchAlvaFarewell.text: [DNT-UNUSED] This is far as I can take you. I'm heading back to the jungle to search for more treasure.

KingsmarchAlvaIntroFirst.text: Ah, Kingsmarch! It's been months since I had a bath. If you're looking to hire a ship, you'll want to sell your share of these Vaal artefacts first. Talk to Rog here, he's our buyer. I'll have to... attend to a few things... but don't worry, we'll see each other again... when the time comes.

KingsmarchAlvaIntroSecond.text: Ah, Kingsmarch! It's been months since I had a bath. I'll have to attend to a few things, but don't worry, we'll see each other again... when the time comes.

KingsmarchDoryaniIntro.text:
[DNT-UNUSED] I do not recognise these 'Kalguurans,' but regardless of who inhabits the area, we must search the islands of this Archipelago. 

The pieces of the Weapon should still be radiating intense Corruption, even now. Look for unusual dangers... mutations, madness, and death. The pieces will make their presence known.

KingsmarchDoryaniOnePieceFound.text:
[DNT-UNUSED] Ah, so the pieces do still remain on these islands.

Interesting.... the symbols engraved on this piece. I think they line up with... give me your map!

KingsmarchDoryaniOnePieceFoundMap.text:
[DNT-UNUSED] Yes. These symbols are some kind of map. Find the other two pieces of the weapon. There are further mysteries here that we must uncover. 

Meanwhile, I will attempt to join this piece with the one that I have.

KingsmarchDoryaniEmptyHanded.text:
[DNT-UNUSED] Argh! These weapon pieces! We have tried the forge, the anvil, even Kalguuran 'runesmithing.' Nothing! They simply refuse to be joined. There is something missing.

Go! Find another of these confounded things. Perhaps then we will learn more.

KingsmarchDoryaniSecondPieceNoEmptyHands.text:
[DNT-UNUSED] Argh! These weapon pieces! We have tried the forge, the anvil, even Kalguuran 'runesmithing.' Nothing! They simply refuse to be joined. 

There is something missing... let me see the next piece.

KingsmarchDoryaniTwoPiecesFound.text: [DNT-UNUSED] So... this piece contains more of these symbols.

KingsmarchDoryaniTwoPiecesFoundMap.text:
[DNT-UNUSED] It is clear now that the weapon is showing us a location. We can only hope that it will contain the key to reforging it.

Find the last piece, and then I shall know more.

KingsmarchDoryaniThreePiecesFound.text: [DNT-UNUSED] At last! We have all the pieces of the Weapon... Let us find out where it leads us.

KingsmarchDoryaniThreePiecesFoundMap.text: [DNT-UNUSED] Yes. The fools likely have no idea what resides beneath their feet. We should ask them if they have seen any signs of precursor ruins on the island.

KingsmarchDoryaniSacrifices.text:
[DNT-UNUSED] It seems that Gems have changed since my time. Yours are notably weaker, but do not require the collection and expenditure of souls. I see, too, a connection between the abilities the gems of this era offer, and the beliefs of the currently dominant cultures of Wraeclast. 

Did our gems require the sacrifice of peasants simply because of the nature of our religion? Such a waste... it was always the critical flaw in our Empire's growth.

KingsmarchDoryaniKalguurans.text: [DNT-UNUSED] These Kalguurans have a strange heritage. They are, apparently, unable to use Gems in any way. What makes them different? Should I have the opportunity, I shall dissect one.

KingsmarchDoryaniOnPrecursorIsland.text:
[DNT-UNUSED] I should have assumed the Precursors would not be so easy to find. These islands have been inhabited for thousands of years, after all... but the power to sink and raise entire landscapes? 

To have such might, and to still succumb to the long entropy of history... how can any civilisation hope to endure?

KingsmarchDoryaniOnHoko.text:
[DNT-UNUSED] So, the Karui are still just as obsessed with strength as they were in my era. The fool! Track this 'Hoko' down and take the Weapon back by any means necessary. 

A word of warning. The effects on anyone exposed to it could be..... volatile.

KingsmarchDoryaniEndOfAct.text:
[DNT-UNUSED] The plan is sound, and the Weapon will work. It's on you to make sure nothing goes wrong.

A word of warning. The effects on anyone exposed to it could be..... volatile.

Oswald_G3_On_Alva.text: Everything always goes right for Alva, whereas every single trap in an ancient ruin salivates at the prospect of my approach. I've literally stepped exactly in her footprints in the dust, yet still triggered a near miss with death. <continue>How is that fair? I say it's not. So, you'll never catch me entering temples and ruins now. I'll direct the hunt for relics from safety, thank you. Let Alva lead her little charmed life as she goes merrily on her way past deathtraps that do nothing but smile and wave.

Oswald_G3_On_Servi.text: Servi has been crucial to our survival here. She takes a hefty fee, but she's worth it. Utzaal and its surrounding swamps and jungles are far more dangerous than any other excavation site we've visited. It's almost as if the city itself is a locus for evil... one might say... <i>{cursed}... if one were superstitious. <continue>I don't believe in any of that nonsense of course, but Servi and her tribe have survived here for countless generations, so if she wants to put up charms, say ritualistic phrases, make small sacrifices at idols, or avoid certain flowers and animals, I'm all for it.

Oswald_G3_On_Carver_Tribe.text: The Carver Tribe is free to roam this region now that you've lowered the water. I'm so positively giddy. I'll sleep very well tonight knowing they could be creeping around at any moment. <continue>At least with the Azakh-Kul, you know you're going to get a poison dart in the neck, eaten, or both. I have no idea how the Carvers might kill me, and not knowing is far more terrifying.

Oswald_G3_On_Chaos_Trial_Quest_Item.text: This is a strange artefact... wait, I think I know what this is! There's a door in the depths of the jungle that we've never been able to open. It's far older than Utzaal, and was built on higher terrain. <continue>From what I gather, only highly select Vaal could enter, and they would be faced with some sort of trial within. This thing... it essentially marks you as chosen, as an aspirant. It'll get you inside.

Oswald_G3_On_Chaos_Trial_Quest_Complete.text: That door in the jungle led to the Temple of Chaos? You <i>{met} the Trialmaster? I thought he was a myth! Does this mean that Chaos is real, too? You know the Vaal thought that Chaos was aware of every possible fate. <continue>That means that somewhere, I actually <i>{did} die all those horrible deaths I barely escaped... it's enough to make a man pale at his own mortality... in any case, congratulations on surviving the Trials of Chaos. I never doubted you for a moment. <continue>Of course, in some other fate, you're lying dead in that Temple, but who's keeping track? Besides Chaos, I mean...

Oswald_G3_On_Blood_Crucible_Summon_No_Po.text: Now you've done it. You've made me risk my own hide by coming out here. You're lucky, though, because you've just found the temple that supposedly guards the famed Blood Crucible. I've been searching for this for years... damn! It looks like it's been destroyed. The Crucible's probably crushed to pieces in there... a shame. I'll try to get some men here to excavate it, but there's little hope.

Oswald_G3_On_Blood_Crucible_Summon_Yes_P.text: Now you've done it. You've made me risk my own hide by coming out here. You're lucky, though, because you've just found the temple that supposedly guards the famed Blood Crucible. I've been searching for this for years... it looks like it's been destroyed by time, but we don't have to worry about that anymore, now do we? Take a little trip into the past and fetch me the bloody thing, and I'd be mighty grateful.

Oswald_G3_On_Blood_Crucible_In_Town_Prev.text: Do you remember that destroyed temple that I said houses the artefact known as the Blood Crucible? Well, I see a rather striking opportunity with this portal through time that you and Alva have found. What do you say about visiting that old temple in its heyday and nicking that prized relic for me? I'd be mighty grateful.

Oswald_G3_On_Blood_Crucible_In_Town_No_P.text: There's a destroyed temple in those sunken ruins that legend says was the home of a powerful artefact called the Blood Crucible. Well, I see a rather striking opportunity with this portal through time you and Alva have found. What do you say about visiting that old temple in its heyday and nicking that prized relic for me? I'd be mighty grateful.

Oswald_G3_On_Blood_Crucible_Return.text: I can't believe it! The Blood Crucible, in the flesh! So to speak. I don't have a clue what to do with it, but I'm sure Alva will have some ideas. This is a rather famous little device. She'll positively lose her mind! I greatly appreciate what you've done.

Oswald_G3_On_Time_Travel_Gossip.text: Ugh, time travel gives me a headache. I'm trying to understand. Vaal priests built a gateway to their future to escape a coming catastrophe. That I can see. They needed someone with Vaal blood to activate the gateway on the other end... the other end being now. Our time. <continue>Why didn't they just activate it themselves back then, so that it would still be active now? And isn't needing someone with Vaal blood on this end a critical flaw, given that they were trying to escape a disaster they feared might wipe out their people? <continue>Does time pass equally on both ends? Is a day here a day there? What happens when their side has been open long enough for it to be now there, but the far future here? <continue>Ugh, I'm probably overthinking this...

Oswald_G3_End_of_Act_Commentary.text: I can't pretend to guess the consequences of what you've done here. I'm not one to give lectures. If you think it's the best course of action, I can only hope that you are right. <continue>I promise you this: if I end up dead because of this Doryani fellow, I'm going to haunt you for the rest of time.

Oswald_G3_Going_To_Kingsmarch_Goodbye.text: Big moves. Big events. We came here to unearth history, and we ended up making it. Get on to Kingsmarch, with my good wishes. We'll see each other again.

Jacob Nesbit.
Days survived: Twelve
Climbed a tree to get a better view, slipped, fell, and was caught by a hanging vine. Neck snapped instantly.

Oswald_Journal_Glyph_02.text:
Osmund Laken.
Days survived: Forty-Five
Bitten by a snake on the ankle. Leg swelled up to three times the size. Servi attempted to amputate, but baby snakes burst out of the cutting, and we immediately set him ablaze. Should have slit his throat first. Sorry, Osmund.

Oswald_Journal_Glyph_03.text:
Cybil Launceleyn.
Days survived: Two
Died of old age shortly after arriving. Rather traumatising, that one. I was telling her one of my best stories when the ancient bat simply keeled over...

Oswyn Shipwash.

Stopped to pet a chimeral.

Oswald_Journal_Glyph_05.text:

Stabbed through the heart by the animated corpse of Oswyn Shipwash.

Oswald_Journal_Glyph_06.text:

Head eaten by the animated corpse of Florence Caley.

Martin Henshawe.

Vanished in broad daylight from the middle of our encampment.

Ants...

Oswald_Journal_Glyph_11.text:
Mabel Salle.
Days survived: Unknown
Kept to herself mostly. Vanished at some point. Nobody's sure.

Oswald_Journal_Glyph_12.text:
Denise Chernocke.
Days survived: Three-Hundred and Nine
Excessive night terrors.

Oswald_Journal_Glyph_13.text:
Godsgift Eldysley.
Days survived: Nineteen
Ate some vibrant berries. Guts ruptured. Face melted. Administered a black liquid by Servi to end his suffering. Didn't work. Dismembered to end his suffering. Didn't work. Burned his head to ashes to end his suffering. That worked.

GraveKnight_Death.text: I... will not be... a slave to evil!

ServiOnJungleOutskirts.text: You might think it no big deal, the hive broods livin' round there. But let me tell you, them no ordinary pests. Them are warriors - armies of crawlin' fiends. <continue>Them hide under the ground, waitin' to ambush the unwary. If you see hives or nests, keep well clear.

ServiOnTheSnakePit.text: There's danger in them Venom Crypts. Long time ago, they were a burial ground for the Vaal, but now snakes make homes in the ribs of the dead. <continue>In there, you see corpses walkin', made slaves by the snakes inside of them... a sight to haunt your dreams, it's true.

ServiOnDoorInTheJungle.text: Strange dreams, my friend. Strange dreams. Chaos doesn't bother me so much, but... we keep far away from that place, ya hear?

ServiOnTheCarverBog.text: The Azak, them are true monsters. Not cannibals, no, but them will not hesitate to feed you to their war beasts. The Azak and the Orok tribes been fightin' almost as long as the Vaal been gone. But the Azak are beyond cruel. <continue>Their queen-witch, Ignagduk, she takes a child every blood moon night... for what, I won't say. If you cross into their territory, only death awaits you there.

ServiOnTheLake.text: The Vaal built massive waterways to turn swamp into richer lands. But when them betrayed nature and cracked the world, nature did what she do best and took back the earth. Sad story, I guess, but too long ago to matter now.

ServiOnTheMachinarium.text: Past the Wetlands, there's an ancient ruin. My tribe has spoke of it for generations now. We seen strange creatures there - made of stone, unnatural, with unblinkin' eyes. <continue>That place? It is forsaken. I warn you, don't go there. But I know... you won't listen to Servi, will you?

ServiHandsPlayerVial.text: Heh heh heh! Drink this. A foul brew, but you'll thank me... if you survive.

ServiOnLakeDrained.text: You shoulda never drained the lake. My tribe depends on the waters for our safety. How will we fend off the Orok or the Azak now? And worse, you have unleashed the horrors of the Vaal once more. <continue>Know this: you bring up bad omens from the depths that shoulda stayed buried, and you will regret it.

ServiOnDoryaniAndFarewell.text: You bring someone we only talk 'bout in our darkest tale. That man is not just a myth - him a monster from the shadows of the past. His arrogance helped crack the world. And now you bring him here, to us, and expect him to help you? You would doom us all.

ServiOnTimePortal.text: You know not what you do. A great darkness comes. You meddle with what has been, and who knows what will happen because of it. What is dead should stay dead. Close the gateway and leave it alone, I say.

ServiOnSonFirst.text: This... this is my son. When he did not return from the jungle, I feared the worst, but I still had hope. The warring tribes have taken that hope away from me. Curse the Azak, curse the Orok... And curse this day.

ServiOnSonSecond.text: Promise me... You will not tell Apus his father is dead. Let him remain a child, for one more day...

ServiOnGraveBackInTown.text: It hurt me deeply to find him there... To find him... Like that. Still, I thank you for findin' his body. <continue>His spirit roams the jungle with his father's now. The warring tribes... the Azak... The Orok... They have a lot to answer for.

ViperNapuatzi_Intro_Reply_A.text: Which one of you activated the gate? Which one of you is of Vaal blood?

ViperNapuatzi_Emerge.text:
Bring her to Doryani!

As for you, I will pay back every drop of Vaal Blood you have spilled.

DannigA4OnKingsmarch.text: This little jewel on the sea might have been granted an official charter by the King, but it's those of us here on Wraeclast that have built it into the trading hub it is today. Many of us came here to investigate the ancient colonisation of this land, and somehow, we ended up following the footsteps of our intrepid ancestors.

DannigA4OnTheKing.text: The King commissioned this port through a trading company charter after we'd already been operating it as an outpost for many years. We ourselves would like to investigate the remnants of our own culture, he is... <i>{very} interested... in Vaal artefacts instead.

DannigA4OnColonisation.text: Kingsmarch is actually our second attempt at colonising Wraeclast. Our first expedition, thousands of years back, was mysteriously lost. My colleagues and I came here two decades ago in search of that ancient historical truth, and in search of the artifact of power they brought with them to Wraeclast. It has become my life's work: the search for the Triskelion Flame!

DannigA4OnTriskelionFlame.text: The most powerful artifact in our known tales was brought to this continent by the first expedition thousands of years ago. The songs tell of it incinerating evil, purifying tainted fields, and warding off those of ill intent. We could certainly use a relic like that now, in these troubled times... we've been searching for it for nigh on twenty years now, and we're just as motivated as ever. I still intend to get out there and excavate, I just get bogged down by the work of running Kingsmarch.

DannigA4OnRunes.text: The runes on our armour essentially capture and shape starlight. Sounds poetic, but don't be fooled. The smiths of the Kalguur turned these runes toward killing work long ago, as soon as we discovered we could compel arrows to find their mark and blades to bite deeper. The greatest smiths became known as artificers, and produced work of singular genius. I'm not quite there yet, but it's only a matter of time and determination.

DannigA4OnVirtueGems.text: We've had twenty years on Wraeclast, and those gems you use continue to perplex me. Clearly, they grant you mystical abilities, but they simply don't do anything in the hands of a Kalguuran. We have our own methods of mystical power, to be fair, but your gems remain an enigma. Somehow, I suspect the power is actually inside <i>{you}, and these 'virtue gems' are just the particular way you believe the world works. I'm no priest, though, so take my opinion for what it's worth.

DannigA4OnGods.text: There's something about you natives of Wraeclast. I didn't believe your gods existed until I saw the leader of a murderous cult begin to... <i>{change}. It was about eighteen years ago now, when our expeditions took us into the wrong little enclave. His worshippers' faith had a physical effect on his appearance, and his strength grew even as we fought him, because they were watching and becoming further inspired by his prowess. It was a legendary battle, one with a clever solution: we slew his worshippers instead. That put an end to the problem, at least for the moment. The route to godhood still exists for every little despot <i>{this} side of the ocean. We must all remain vigilant against men of dark ambition.

DannigA4QuestForge.text: I'd very much like to know where you found such pure quality Verisium. Usually, this material is a Kalguuran pursuit. In any case, I can forge this into spikes, and rune them in a way that will help open that ancestral Karui prison. It sounds like you need the runes for 'Authority,' 'Break,' and 'Release...'

DannigA4QuestEtch.text: I'd very much like to know where you found such pure quality Verisium. Usually, this material is a Kalguuran pursuit. In any case, I can forge this into spikes, and show you the runes you'll need to etch on that ancestral Karui prison. It sounds like you need 'Authority,' 'Break,' and 'Release...'

TujenA4IntroLookingForABoat.text: So you're looking for a ship? I can direct ya. Name's Tujen. I'm the harbourmaster 'round here. We got one ship in looking for work. Give the captain a shout, why don't ya? Name of Makoru. She's Karui, but helming a Kalguuran galleon. She'll get you where you need to go.

TujenA4IntroNotLookingForABoat.text: The name's Tujen. I'm the harbourmaster 'round here. If no one else has said it, welcome to our fair little town. If you're looking for a ship, I can direct ya.

TujenA4AboutABoat.text: Ah, so you need a ride. We've got a ship in looking for work. Give the captain a shout, why don't ya. Name of Makoru. She's Karui, but helming a Kalguuran galleon. She'll get you where you need to go.

TujenA4OnKingsmarch.text: I ain't a tour guide. This here's the harbour. Got a harbour concern, that's me. For all other concerns... Do you know who to go to? Someone else.

TujenA4OnMakoru.text: Makoru's got something to prove. Lucky for the both o' you, she's got the talent to back it up. You won't go wrong gettin' on that ship. It's a damn shame the other captains give her guff. Damn shame. She's got her people's spirit. I quite like the Karui. They value honour, and ancestral tales of bravery. For real, not just talk. They live the way we <i>{claim} we do... and they've got no King breathin' down their necks! They're wild. Free.

TujenA4OnRog.text: Now there's a true friend. Me and him have been on the campaign here in Wraeclast nigh on twenty years now. Sort of. Somewhere along the way, we built a small supply lodge. Then a farmer showed up, looking for a small unclaimed plot for his family. Then his family followed. And a logger. A hunter. A merchant. A priest. Next thing you know, it all got away from us... and here we are, with a whole town somehow grown up around us. I'm just now realizin' I haven't been on an expedition in six bloody years. How did time get away from us like this?

TujenA4OnGwennen.text: So you ran into Gwennen? She's a distant cousin of mine, so I do what I can to protect her and Rog's little ones while she's out scratchin' up the ground in search of artefacts. My fightin' services haven't been so needed these last few years, though, what with Kingsmarch bein' so peaceful and all. Kinda makes me miss the old adventurin' days.

TujenA4OnDannig.text: He's a good man. A man of two worlds. Part aspiring dreamer, part cynical realist. I'll follow him to the ends of the world, which you know, because I already have... and here we are.

TujenA4OnTheKalguur.text: I used to believe a whole load 'a bunk about honour and tradition. 'We do this not for ourselves, but for our children.' The words were hollow, but the intent was good. It really is all about making a better world for those that'll follow us. Speaking of children, I've got a few of them myself runnin' around Kingsmarch here... and a cloud o' harpies to go with 'em, always clawing at my pay... it's enough to make a man quit drinkin'. Almost.

TujenA4OnTheKing.text: Why are you asking? Who sent you? Bugger off!

TujenA4OnExpedition.text: I've half a mind to get back out there. You look like the adventuring type. Maybe I'll see you around one day. Maybe we'll blow something up together. You never know.

TujenA4OnThePreacher.text: Ugh. We're a bit <i>{too} free with who we let settle in Kingsmarch, if you ask me. That Twilight Order set up shop on an island 'round here several years ago. Not sure where they're from, but they ain't Kalguuran. They're consistently bothersome, always preachin' and shoutin'... but don't tell the preacher, I kind of agree. Those 'gods' you Wraeclast folk have... doesn't sound right. Sounds like mortals who want to be Kings over the rest o' ya.

TujenA4ResponseToPreacherA1.text: Call me that again, ya git!

TujenA4ResponseToPreacherA2.text: Call me that again, ya git!

TujenA4ResponseToPreacherA3.text: Call me that again, ya git!

TujenA4ResponseToPreacherB1.text: Just one swing at him, Dannig. One swing!

TujenA4ResponseToPreacherB2.text: Just one swing at him, Dannig. One swing!

TujenA4ResponseToPreacherB3.text: Oh come on, one swing at him, Dannig! One swing!

TullinaA5Introduction.text: [DNT-UNUSED] This Sniper has been keeping me here all day. I need you to navigate through the Estates and kill this Sniper. Be sure to hide behind objects and buildings to avoid their fire!

TibbsA5ReachTibbsSniperDead.text: Stroke of good fortune you happened across us when you did, mate! I wasn't sure we were ever going to get out of that alive.

TibbsA5IntroAndQuestOutside.text: My name's Tibbs. This here's Tullina. No point in hiding what we do, since we need your help. We... procure things. We came to Oriath to snag a rather large payday, and the job sounded simple on its face. All we had to do was recover an exotic bottle of wine from a certain pleasure den... and then it all went horribly wrong. We're not far from the place. The den is right up ahead. Why don't you meet us there?

TibbsA5IntroAndQuestInside.text: My name's Tibbs. This here's Tullina. No point in hiding what we do, since we need your help. We... procure things. We came to Oriath to snag a rather large payday, and the job sounded simple on its face. All we had to do was recover an exotic bottle of wine from this secret pleasure den... and then it all went horribly wrong. I can't do much with this injury. If you slip in there and grab the wine, we'll share our payday with you. In and out, smash and grab, simple enough... hopefully.

TibbsA5JustQuestInside.text: Here we are. This is the place. I can't do much with this injury. If you slip in there and grab the wine, we'll share our payday with you. In and out, smash and grab, simple enough... hopefully.

TibbsA5OnTheWine.text: The wine we were hired to... 'acquire'... was the subject of rather vivid rumours. Ingesting trace amounts of Corruption with alcohol supposedly removes any and all inhibitions, letting the drinker chase their darkest desires without limit or shame. Couldn't pay me enough to attend one of those parties... the rumours said, when they ran out of pleasures to pursue, they turned to pain instead, looking for new realms of experience... I feel like vomiting just thinking about it...

TibbsA5QuestReturn.text: I imagined some pretty terrible things happened in that den, but it turns out, the reality is far worse. I didn't think there'd be anyone still here after all this time. Those people... they must have stayed behind when Oriath was evacuated. They must have already been addicted by then. Add twenty more years of Corrupted wine, it's... it's unthinkable...

TibbsA5OnCorruption.text: The makers of that wine did something terrible. They mixed it with distilled Corruption drawn from a virtue gem with some ancient tool of the monster Maligaro... they thought they could avoid the most harmful effects of Corruption by diluting it to trace amounts, while keeping the intoxicating properties. Now we know they were horribly wrong.

TibbsA5OnTown.text: You've got a bolt-hole for us to hide in? Much appreciated. We'll meet you there.

TibbsA5IntroInTown.text: You could have mentioned how small this place is. I have to lean down or risk bumping me head constantly! Still, I appreciate the chance to rest and heal. Many thanks.

TibbsA5OnOriath.text: I thought it would be worth sneaking past the Twilight Order to see Oriath again. Nah. This place needs to be abandoned. I have a few good memories of the time before, but that's all over now. This is not an island fit for people. Not anymore.

TibbsA5OnSabbatical.text: This kind of life comes with its own rather harsh time limit built in. That damn Citizen Vanguard caught me one cold Fiero morning with a sudden rush of a hundred men... and offered me a job. An honest hardworking job that would capitalise on my unique talents to 'benefit mankind.'

TibbsA5OnRogueHarbour.text: The Ring is the closest thing I have to a home. We're all thieves and scoundrels, and proud of it. I'm not a callous man, though. I do keep tabs on those I care about. If you ever see a woman with stark white skin and red eyes, let me know. She might be part of a troupe still, might not. I just want to make sure she's safe, and grew up happy.

TibbsA5OnCitizenVanguard.text: That was another life, my friend. Another era. Best not to dwell on the past.

TibbsA5OnHonestJob.text: Yeah, I took the Vanguard job offer. Did that for a few years, saw some battle, got traumatised by horrors that still haunt my dreams... you know, the standard cost of war. One day, couldn't do it anymore. Went back to the regular old criminal life. I took the contract to steal the Corrupted wine because I thought that maybe a little sip might help me forget, or, at the very least, stop caring. I'd just like to sleep through one night without dreaming about the horrific things I've seen...

TibbsA5OnHorrors.text: Believe me, you don't want to know...

TibbsA5Rewards.text: Interesting find! I can take that off your hands. Here's your cut.

TibbsA5Wild.text: With this injury, I'm not going anywhere until that sniper is dead. You'll have to sneak through the manors to reach the bastard!

ImposterWomanWildShout.text: Stop! Don't come near the circle.

ImposterWomanIntroduction.text: Cadigan preserve me! I thought you were going to blunder in here like I did. I've been stuck in this ancient trap for days, and you're the only <i>{living} person I've seen on this horrible isle of the dead. My son and his crew went to search for some Verisium to crack this mystical prison open, but they haven't come back... please find him! He'll know what to do!

ImposterWomanTotems.text:
These totems might <i>{look} like relics of an abandoned Karui settlement, but I can assure you that there is more to them than meets the eye. When I walked in here, they flared brightly with power, and now I can't get out!

This is clearly some sort of Karui prison imbued with their ancestral magic. The only thing I can think of that would break this type of trap might be the metal we came here to find in the first place, Verisium.

ImposterWomanVerisium.text: You don't know about Verisium? Oh, dear. It's a metal found in craters when rocks fall from the sky. It's the foundation of all Kalguuran smithing and runework. We call it Verisium, or 'truth metal,' because what is runed becomes reality...

ImposterWomanRunes.text: You really don't know about these things? Oh, <i>{dear}. How do I explain this? Hmm... if a smith imprints the rune for 'deadly' on a sword, that sword <i>{becomes} deadlier, in accordance with the smith's own skill. Similarly, my son was hoping to imprint some spikes with the proper runes to break me out of this prison...

ImposterWomanKedgeBay.text: It was my son's idea, as captain of our family's vessel, to come here. This island is widely considered cursed. The stories say that if the mists open and reveal themselves to you, it is only as a siren song, a vision dancing before the mind. Dozens of ships have broken themselves upon these shoals, and we thought we could slip through the mists and salvage their Verisium cargo for our own. I warned my son, but he didn't listen...

ImposterWomanTrove.text: While climbing along a ridge, we sighted a large amount of Verisium on the far side of the island. When I became trapped here, my son took his crew in search of that trove. Please, find them! It's been so long, I'm certain they must have run into trouble!

ImposterWomanPlayerReturnsWithVerisium.text: My boy is dead? In my heart, I knew. He'd been gone so long. My family line is over, and life no longer has meaning. I don't know what to do now. Please, forge that Verisium into spikes and get me out of here, so that I may go lay down and die next to the body of my son.

ImposterWomanPlayerReturnsWithSpikes.text: My boy is dead? I knew. In my heart, I knew. He'd been gone so long. My family line is over, and life no longer has meaning. I don't know what to do now. Please, use those spikes and get me out of here, so that I may go lay down and die next to the body of my son.

ImposterWomanOnBlacksmith.text: You should be able to find a skilled blacksmith among the Kalguurans at Kingsmarch. He can't be just anyone. He has to be able to forge runes.

ImposterWomanOnDannig.text: Yes, I know Dannig. As the leader of Kingsmarch, he should be able to direct you to a Kalguuran blacksmith with the proper skills!

ImposterWomanShoutAboutSpikes.text: You have the Verisium spikes? Quickly, impale these totems!

G4CaptainOnG4_1_1.text: That's less an island and more an active volcano. There's a swarm of deadly little things that make their home in the warrens within. They'll eat the flesh off your bones while you're still screaming. Ugh... but it's their 'god' I'm thinking of. Spyglass reports say he's getting bigger every time they spot him. Sounds to me like he might have one of the artefacts you're seeking.

G4CaptainOnG4_2_1.text: That island has been shrouded in mist since the time of my eldest forefathers, before the Vaal empire was even a notion in some bloodthirsty noble's head. The tale told by the Hatungo was quite simple: if the mists part and the island shows itself to you, you will be compelled to land. You'll claim you hear the voices of loved ones, or of your gods, or whatever else suits your proclivities. If the crew let you go there, the ship will never return. But sure, we can take you there. What could possibly go wrong?

G4CaptainOnG4_3_1.text: That's one of the most beautiful and verdant islands in this region. Some time ago, I did hear that one of the more nomadic Karui tribes decided to stop and settle there. They'll know the region well by now, so it would be worth asking them if they have seen any sign of powerful Corruption. It would also be good to see some Karui who don't know me...

G4CaptainOnG4_5_1.text: That island contains a prison built by the Eternal Empire. It's been 300 years since the cataclysm, but the inmates still remain. Nobody ever let them out. You can still hear them clamoring at the bars. There is definitely something wrong at the heart of that place, which I'm certain means you'll want us to sail straight there.

G4CaptainOnG4_7.text: For generations, that island was used for the coming of age trial of several tribes. Young Karui try to sneak onto the rocks, climb the cliffs, and steal the eggs of the shrikes that nest there. The eggs are a valuable delicacy that many would pay dearly for. In recent years, though, the trial became far more deadly. There is some sort of massive horrific thing nesting at its apex... it immediately makes me think of the corrupting effects of the artefacts you're looking for.

G4CaptainIntroductionContractAccountCrea.text: We're looking for work, yes... if you have enough credit with the trade guild. Let me see here... wow, okay, I can take you wherever you need. We'll set sail right now if you want!

G4CaptainIntroductionContractAccountNotC.text: We're looking for work, yes. I can take you wherever you need, even places the other captains would never dream of going! But if you want to work with a Kalguuran ship then you'll have to arrange a contract account. You can't just turn up with gold and demand passage. Talk to the port's logistics man, Rog, about that.

G4CaptainContractAccountCreated.text: Ah, got a contract account sorted out? Then we can set sail whenever you like.

G4CaptainCareer.text: I'm a new captain, as you've probably guessed. The Kalguurans are skeptical of my people, but they respect our seafaring skills. I joined the Trade Guild as a young deckhand after I ran away from home, and I've worked my way up over the last twenty years. I'm the first Karui captain on a Kalguuran ship, so I've got to make a name for myself, or it'll turn the tide against all of us.

G4CaptainKalguur.text: They don't talk much about their homeland. I'm not allowed to sail there, not because I'm not Kalguuran, but because nobody has yet woven the accomplishments and honours of my family line into an epic poem to be told at their royal court. Their custom is not too different from Karui oral tradition, but it's a difficult situation. In my case, I am no longer part of my tribe, so I have no family line to immortalize in song. Tujen suggested that I could join his, but he was drunk at the time, so...

G4CaptainTheKing.text: I don't know what to make of the Kalguuran King. I've only heard whispers. Rumours. He's very interested in Vaal artefacts, but I'm secretly wary of selling him relics I come across. Others are hesitant, too... I have noticed that certain types of ancient devices <i>{disappear} before being loaded on merchant ships headed for Kalguur. If you mention this, they will deny it, just like they denied me when I asked... and just like I will deny I ever told you this.

G4CaptainTheFirstMate.text: Rhodri has been my mentor in the Trade Guild for many years now. He took me under his wing at a time when nobody else wanted to even so much as speak to me. I would never have been able to move up the ranks if not for his advice and support, though you'd never see any of that through his outward gruffness. He tasks the crew into action, and they hate him for it, but that's the first mate's role. He gets the crew's ire, and I get the crew's trust. It must be this way if we are all to survive.

G4CaptainTheWay.text: My people's traditions have remained the same for thousands of years... until my generation. When I was a young girl, our god of war was slain by a mortal Exile. That impossible event shook everything I believed in. I am looking for my own Way now. I thought I might find my path in trade and commerce, sailing for the Kalguurans. Other <i>{kaivanas} have spread out across Wraeclast in search of meaning. Those that chose to stay true to the old traditions despise us. They think we have rejected the Way, that we dishonour our families. When I visited the Halls of the Dead, my ancestors told me that the Way was meant to empower us, not control us! Who am I dishonouring by seeking my own truth? It's a debate that has fueled the fires of discontent, and separated me from my family...

G4CaptainTheChallenge.text:
I became a captain against the wishes of the Trade Guild Council. To lead a Kalguuran ship, one must pass a test. I was given a temporary crew and tasked with sailing a certain course in a certain amount of time, a crucial skill for an organisation that 'aims to operate like clockwork over unpredictable seas,' as they put it. At the most dangerous point of the course, between vast rocky shoals on a moonless night, our cargo of refined Verisium caught fire. It was due to explode in mere moments.

I was faced with a choice: abandon ship, or command some of my men to enter that lethal smoke and put out the fire at the cost of their own lives. A rather horrible death, they say, gasping for breath with lungs that no longer work. So, I chose to put out the fire myself. It's how I was raised...

Luckily, the explosive powder was fake, and it was all part of the test. It turns out, one passes or fails based on the votes of the crew that served. I had earned their loyalty with my unexpected act, and many of them still follow me today, on this very ship. The Council does not aid me in any way, but neither do they interfere. It is the best I can hope for until I show some true profit.

RhodriIntroduction.text: Rhodri's my name. I'm the first mate. Don't get in my way, and we'll be alright.

RhodriCrew.text: If the crew doesn't despise the first mate, then he ain't doin' his job. That bein' said, I'd lay down my life for any of my men, the captain included. Just how it is. Here's hopin' I don't have to, though.

G4RhodriRowingG4_1_1.text: Anyone who comes too close to this place gets torn to shreds. Speaking of which... I think this is a good distance for me to drop you off.

G4RhodriRowingG4_2_1.text: So many shipwrecks... imagine the treasures within... but all the coin in the world wouldn't be enough to get me to dive into those waters... did you hear that? I swear I heard... no, but it couldn't be... she's been dead for fifteen years...

G4RhodriRowingG4_3_1.text: I'm considerin' makin' landfall with you. These people are... very friendly. Had a right good time last visit - how strange! They seem to have left a bunch of <i>{waikoama} to rot on the beach... that's 'canoes' in Karui. Don't mind me. Learned a bit o' culture to impress the ladies here.

G4RhodriRowingG4_7.text: You see those Karui rotting on the rocks there? Damn fools, they are. Sneakin' here and stealin' eggs is some sort of test of manhood, Makoru tells me. The Kalguuran rite of manhood involves getting drunk with your family at a tavern. Much prefer that over bein' stabbed by a Shrike.

G4RhodriHaventHiredYetIntro.text: Eh? You'll have to speak to Rog about setting up a charter account. We can't do business if you don't have one. It's Trade Guild law.

G4RhodriBackHaventHiredYetIntro.text: Got a charter account now? Good. Deal with the captain. I'm the first mate. Rhodri's my name. Don't get in my way, and we'll be alright.

G4RhodriAboutMakoru.text:
We've served a few years together, but I always tried to look out for her, even when she was just a new deckhand with no experience on large vessels. Gave her a piece of advice now and then. We Kalguurans can be a bit hard-headed when it comes to foreigners. When she worked her way up in the Trade Guild, I wasn't surprised. When she passed the Captain's Challenge with a unanimous vote, I was right proud.

Never took the Challenge meself, though. Happy where I am. Much prefer she serve as Captain, and I'll just continue being a grumpy old cur shoutin' at the crew.

G4RhodriAboutTradeGuild.text: We all operate under the Meridian Free Traders. We gather what resources and wealth we can here, send it back home, get a cut. Decent charter. Could do worse. That Rog has stuck his neck out repeatedly to keep the terms fair for the sailors. Maybe that's why it ain't so bad.

G4RhodriAboutTheKing.text: Oi, don't go askin' me about <i>{him}. I was just startin' to like you.

G4RhodriOnTheWeapon.text: [DNT] So, you've got the Weapon have you? We should hurry to Ngakanu then. Speak to me again when you're ready to set sail.
