A4HoodedOneIntroduction.text: If you have not already done so, you should seek out the use of a sailing vessel. We are in the correct region, but there are countless islands to search, and we have no idea where to start looking for the pieces of the Precursor weapon. We took too long exploring Utzaal. I fear that time is shorter than we know... If our unknown enemy germinates the Seed of Corruption before we find the weapon, then all will be lost.

A4HoodedOneKalguurans.text: I know nothing of the Kalguurans, but I remember their continent, Middengard. Believe it or not, I once had wings, and I journeyed the world in my wanderlust days. Middengard is very far away, to the east. It was a cold and rocky climate, and the people there were hardy survivors who eked out a living around numerous hotsprings and molten vents that dotted the land. Come to think of it, they were just developing a method of forging when I was there, one that used volcanic heat, magma... and starlight, of all things. How odd. I remember watching the process with a growing sense of unease that I could not explain. It was a system of power that made no sense to me. In Ogham, the Count used a Kalguuran-runed sword to pin me to the Tree of Souls...

A4HoodedOneKarui.text: I roved Ngamakanui for a time, but its people had no interest in me. The Karui were a highly focused people, welcoming to those they respect, but wary of strangers who did not know their ways. They had reason to be wary, for the Vaal would often harass them on the borders of the empire...

A4HoodedOneTukohama.text: Twenty years ago, the gods arose in the wake of the slaying of the Beast, and many awoke in a mad and destructive fit born of two thousand years of nightmare-wrought sleep. I worked with a powerful Exile who defeated Tukohama, and I took his divine spark. It was necessary at the time, but now, I think it is time to return Tukohama's essence to his people...

A4HoodedOneTheWeapon.text: [DNT-UNUSED] We have now recovered three pieces of the weapon, but one piece remains. We must find the fourth and final piece of the weapon. Speak to Makoru and pay close attention. You should be able to decipher where we must go next.

A4HoodedOneOnTavakaiCured.text: [DNT-UNUSED] We have cured Tavakai of his affliction and put the Weapon to great use. We should continue our journey by recruiting the Ezomytes, Maraketh and the Vaal. Speak to me when you are ready.

CedrusIntroduction.text: Gird yourself, there's a contingent of soldiers between us and safety. If we want to get out of this rain, we'll have to get bloody.

CedrusIntroduction_2.text: No time to get into it here. Suffice to say, they're hunting us. We have to move!

CedrusIntroduction_3.text: The damned Twilight Order camped right outside our hideout. I ran out here to lead them astray. That's how I got strung up. It was the only choice I had left. They're still there, so they might figure it out at any moment! We have to move!

CedrusShoutForHelp.text: Bloody awful weather we're having today, ay stranger? Would you mind doing me a small favour... get me down from here...

CedrusWild_Brothers.text: I try to avoid killing my former brothers when I can, but they've given us no choice...

CedrusWild_Ohdig_1.text: Ohdig, you fat bastard! Why don't you try stringing me up again!

CedrusWild_Ohdig_2.text: What happened Ohdig? Why did you have to side with her?

CedrusWild_Battle_1.text: My former brothers must be stopped! I will do what I must, and fight by your side!

CedrusWild_Battle_2.text: This has to end! Now! Before it's too late!

CedrusWild_Lumerius_1.text: So, they chose you, Lumerius. You're the saviour.

CedrusWild_Lumerius_2.text: Too bad you couldn't save the eight other children.

CedrusReturnToTown_2.text: Hey, it's alright, it's alright. I'll live. This stranger cut me down.

CedrusIntroductionTown.text: Ah, some days, caring is a thankless job. Well, welcome to our little bolthole. Wouldn't call it home, since we're always on the move, but it keeps us dry. Now, what brings you here? Nobody who has any sense comes to Oriath. Nobody.

CedrusIntroductionTownShorter.text: Welcome to our little bolthole. Wouldn't call it home, since we're always on the move, but it keeps us dry. Now, what brings you here? Nobody who has any sense comes to Oriath. Nobody.

CedrusIntroductionTownShortest.text: Welcome to our little bolthole. Wouldn't call it home, since we're always on the move, but it keeps us dry.

CedrusInfiltratingTwilightOrder.text: You want to Infiltrate the Twilight Order? Not stupid then, just crazy. The main gate by land is on the other side of the Plaza of Patrons, for all the good that will do you. When we fled the enclave, that's what we used. But, it'll be heavily guarded now. If you're really that determined to get there, you'll have to go through the Slums. Your only option after that is the Cisterns. It won't be pretty, but it'll get you there.

CedrusOnTheMove.text: The Twilight Order sends patrols every now and again, but they're only human. With the Templars gone, and their dark secrets left to run amok, the city itself boils over with unimaginable horrors; of a different type every season. We've seen undead, ice creatures, living statues infected with black ichor and a dozen other nightmares I never got close enough to discern. So, for today, this is where we live.

CedrusOnOriath.text: It's easy to say this island is cursed. But the dangers here are the fault of man. Over untold centuries of ambition, the templars collected countless strange creatures and forbidden magiks in their archives. In my day, there were always rumours of dark experiments and artifacts from cultures long forgotten. With nobody left to contain those secrets, Oriath became a ravaged patchwork quilt of horrors.

CedrusOnFleeing.text: Save Elwynian, we all used to be devout followers of the order. Everyone here joined me when I left. The things they are doing now... We just couldn't be part of it.

CedrusDontWantToTalk.text: I'm freezing cold and I'm wounded. If you survive long enough, I'll tell you about it. But, later.

CedrusDontWantToTalk_2.text: But that's a story for another time.

CedrusOnElwynian.text: She's an orphan daughter of Oriath in the truest sense. She was alone here for most of her life. I can't imagine it. If I'd known she was out there while I was sitting safe behind high walls, I.... Ah, I don't know what I would have done. I was too devout at the time. Now though, I can't stomach the thought of her being out here, on her own. Meeting her changed me! Made me question my faith for the first time! If I couldn't take care of one person, how could I be part of changing the entire world? Lofty questions for a simple man.

CedrusOnElwynian_2.text: I first met her in an Order jail cell. They'd caught her stealing food, and they didn't know what to do with her. They tried to convince her to join us, but she refused. They couldn't just throw her back out on her own, that was as good as a death sentence! So, the issue was brought to my attention and I went to question her myself. We got to talking. Confiding in someone else outside the order for the first time in two decades. Well, it gave my misgivings form.

CedrusGladiatorArenaQuestIntrodution.text: Back when Oriath was a thriving city and I was a much younger man, the gladiatorial slavers brought a beast of a man in from the mountains near Trathus. I'm not sure <i>{man} is even the right word. Got one eye, center of his massive tusked skull. He absolutely dominated his competition, the most brutal fighter I'd ever seen! None could match his raw strength, or his ambition! He's still in there, you know. They all are. Dead, but still walking. I highly suggest you avoid that arena. No mortal man could match that horrific might.

CedrusGladiatorArenaQuestComplete.text: You took down the Cyclops of Trathus?! Incredible! I don't even know what to say. This one's on me, for boasting no mortal man could take him down.

CedrusGladiatorArenaQuestCompleteShort.text: You took down the Cyclops of Trathus?! Incredible! I don't even know what to say.

CedrusAnotherWayIn.text: Well, you've certainly caused some havoc here. You're never getting in that gate now. I wonder though, Elwynian used to know another way in...

CedrusTwilightLoreDump_1.text: I was an initiate, a young man freshly graduated from the academy when High Templar Venarius disappeared. Accusations flew, infighting became rife. Good men and women were burned at the stake for heresy! Only power could protect a man, and I had none. I myself was in line to be executed, when Dominus ascended to the position of High Templar and put a stop to the chaos. Small relief, that. He was not interested in prayer and piousness, he paid lip service to god but secretly sought power through the workings of corruption and thaumaturgy. Serving him, I lost my faith. And that was when the Twilight Order approached me. They said that there was a way to protect mankind from tyranny, to protect them from men like Dominus. So, I agreed to join.

CedrusTwilightLoreDump_2.text: The Templars, or rather the cult of Innocence, is thousands of years old. The order has been with them from the beginning. A secret resistance to their ideals. The founders of the order were a handful of newcomers to Wraeclast, who, unlike their fellows, held suspicion in their hearts. They had themselves escaped across the sea from an ancient tyrant, and they felt a discomforting similarity of events unfolding here. The first High Templars' teachings and tenets changed often in the early days; in ways that seemed to suit his old power, rather than true faith. There were some who suspected Maxarius himself was the one wearing the golden mask during those miraculous manifestations of god. When innocence finally did appear, and could not be denied, Maxarius supposedly died the same day, and was laid to rest. In the dead of night, our founders snuck into the crypt that would later become the Templar ossuary, they pried open his sarcophagus, and found it to be empty. The Twilight Order was born in that moment. Maxarius was not dead, he had become a god! Because of the faith of his worshippers, all based on lies. The gods are just men. Ambitious men, tyrannical men, but men just the same; and not deserving of their power of prestige. I happen to still agree with their ideals, just not the way the Order is going about things.

CedrusTwilightLoreDump_3.text: We remained a silent and hidden organisation within the Templars, until the gods returned. When Innocence and Kitava wreaked havoc on Oriath, belief within the Order burned bright, and our ranks swelled. When the Island was abandoned, we remained. And we went about our work with fervour, no longer restrained by the need for secrecy.

CedrusTwilightLoreDump_4.text: Our faith was founded on distrust of the gods, but when they mysteriously vanished thousands of years ago, the ancient members of our order dedicated themselves to understanding why. Eventually, they discovered the existence of the Beast. A nightmarish entity, with the power to divert and eat the faith of followers and zealots. We had not created this creature, though we absolutely would have made such a thing if we had the capability. No, the truth was far more shocking. The vilified one, of our own false faith - the Cult of Innocence, was the one who had betrayed his brother and his fellow gods by germinating an end to divinity. Our order almost dissolved over the following millenia, dwindling to just a few keepers of the faith. Those few only kept our tenets in their hearts out of a latent fear that the gods may one day return. Until, Malachai.

CedrusTwilightLoreDump_5.text: From afar, my order witnessed Malachai enter the Beast, assume control of it, and begin to reshape Wraeclast to his will. In the centuries since, we have been focused on bringing about utopia with that power. We ask the question: what if someone good of heart, without flaws, was to reshape the world for the better? The elders began a guided series of marriages and resulting children, with the aim to bring about a perfect leader, the saviour! Then, it all came crashing down when the Beast was slain twenty years ago, and the gods returned.

CedrusTwilightLoreDump_6.text: Our worst fears became real. When the Beast was slain by some bad exile, Oriath was immediately thrown into chaos, first by Innocence and then by Kitava. The mainland was ravaged by god after god, each returning from their millenia of slumber bloodthirsty and deranged! Our plans, our faith.. were challenged to the extreme. The world needed us, but we didn't know what to do after the loss of the Beast. That is when the Countess returned from her travels, and I began to find myself on the wrong side of history.

CedrusTwilightLoreDump_7.text: The Countess reported divine devastation in every culture across Wraeclast. It was impossible for man to thrive when their best and brightest continually found themselves caught up in the sinister madness that ambition and godhood can bring. We knew things were bad, but she also came bearing word of an ultimate solution. The vilified one once more walked the land. He lurked in the shadows, avoiding people, trying not to be seen. But she had found him, and he was carrying a dark seed. One that could regrow the beast! For a time, we were hopeful. But as the years passed, as he did not plant the seed and start the process, we began to realise that he had no intention of repeating his ancient act. He was not seeking to help us a second time. He was keeping the seed away from us! The Countess swayed the elders, and then many of my bretheren. She told us that <i>{we} had to act, <i>{we} had to take the seed, and bring it to fruition! We could put the gods to sleep and bring about utopia! If we had to stomach to do what was necessary..

CedrusTwilightLoreDump_8.text: You've seen some of what the order had to do to germinate the seed. I can tell by the darkness in your eyes. My forebears had thousands of years to research the knowledge of the Vaal, and of those civilisations that came before. We had a fairly comprehensive idea of a <i>{method} that could grow the seed through mortal means. Since we lacked the divine energies that the vilified one once used to do it himself, our method was to involve flesh, corpses, countless thousands freshly murdered and fed to the seed. A literal mountain of death. And that was only the first step. To create a new Beast, to reshape the world, we would have to risk another cataclysm of our own making. If the saviour wasn't absolutely perfect, if he had even a shred of enmity or jealousy or ambition, the cost would be enormous. I couldn't do it. When a decision was handed down, a few years ago now, I feared the plan would cause the deaths of innocents like Elwynian, who I had grown quite fond of by then, and many, many more. How could a utopia be founded on such a horrific beginning? So, I ran. And I took everyone I could convince. The order has hunted us ever since.

CedrusOnCompanions.text: You know those two? If you vouch for them, that's good enough for me. We can use every ally we can get right now.

CedrusCataclysmIntro.text: What.. Happened? Where are we? Is this... Did we fail? No.. we're still alive. There must still be time! I'm heavily wounded, but I'll do what I can to support you from here. This is it, my friend. Time to do, or die.

CedrusOnCataclysm.text: I have no idea what's happening out there, but Elwynian isn't alone. Lets just focus on getting this done.

ElwynianIntroduction.text:
Keep your distance. Cedrus might have let you in here, but the bastards on the other side of the island would do anything to capture us. You make one unexpected move, you'll find yourself choking on a smoke bomb.

You want to trade? Then we can talk.

ElwynianOnCedrusPlan.text: Why're you asking me? Only he knows why he's being so rash. Y'know what? Just leave me alone.

ElwynianOnCedrus.text: I argue with him at times, but I don't mean it. I was.. alone, for a very long time. I thought I would always be alone. I thought I would die and.. nobody would know or care. Sometimes, it's nice to have someone at home who gets mad at you when you run off and do dangerous things, y'know?

ElwynianOnOriath.text: This wasteland of stone and nightmare is the only home I've ever known. It's <i>{my} city. The order have their own enclave cut off from it all, that makes me the last true Oriathan. Any other stupid questions?

ElwynianOnOriathAlt.text: It's the only home I've ever known. I don't know if I'd be able to survive anywhere else. The horrors and the nightmares in the other cities would probably get me before I had a chance to adapt.

ElwynianOnCisterns.text: They are the best way to get around the city. Most of the horrors are up top. The order never goes down there either, not sure they even know about the Cisterns. Still, plenty that can kill you down there, but that's Oriath for you.

ElwynianIceCisternQuest.text: Something's wrong with the city's water supply. I would say I'm amazed it still functions after twenty years fallow, but this is different. Just had a big storm, and the fountains and aqueducts aren't flowing. There's a network of cisterns under the city that supply this whole area. If you're thirsty, do us all a favour. Dive in there, and find out what's wrong. Otherwise, we might be drinking seawater soon.

ElwynianIceCisternQuestSummoned.text: If you ever want another drink of water in this forsaken city, you're gonna have to go in there and.. deal with whatever's at the heart of this unnatural ice. Have fun with that.

ElwynianOnIceCisternSummoned.text: I didn't think I'd have to explain this, but this ice isn't supposed to be here. Even in winter it never gets cold enough down here to freeze the flow. Shouldn't you know things like this?

ElwynianOnIceCisternAltSummoned.text: This city is full of random horrors. Don't know how, or why. I'm pretty sure one of them is responsible for this ice, and you're going to have to deal with it. Please don't die.

ElwynianIceCisternQuestComplete.text: The water's flowing again! I don't know what you did, but it's been a long time since something went our way around here.

ElwynianAnotherWayIn.text: Past the Temples, there's an old graveyard. After that, gardens surround the estates where I grew up. Find the biggest mansion at the back, right up against the order's wall. Let me know when you get there, I'll show you the way in.

ElwynianOnGemlingsSummoned.text: I grew up here surrounded by Gemlings, they'd been ordered to guard the wealthy families in the estates, and so they did. Everyone was dead. I was a child. They protected me. But the Gemlings aren't people anymore, not really. The one that could give them orders is long dead, so they can never leave, can never disobey... a living nightmare. You'll be doing them a favour if you kill them.

ElwynianOnSurvivalSummoned.text: The Gemlings protected me from the dangers of the city, but I was on my own for everything else. It took a few years, but eventually I foraged everything edible in these estates. I started getting desperate. That's when I found the passage under the wall. After being alone for so long imagine my suprise when I discovered there were countless people living right on the other side! The Twilight Order had been a stone's throw away the entire time!

ElwynianOnTwilightOrder.text: At first I didn't know what to make of the order. I didn't know if they could be trusted. I lurked in the shadows and listened. What I heard frightened me, and I decided to avoid their notice. They had massive stores of food lying around in the cellars, so I figured they wouldn't miss a little bit. For many years, I only took as much as I needed, and only when I really couldn't find anything in the gardens around the estates. Eventually though, I got careless, and they caught me.

ElwynianOnImprisonment.text: I was right to be wary of the order. They clapped me in irons and threw me in a cell. Ironically, I ate better there than ever before. That's when I met Cedrus. He came to ask me questions: "Who was I?", "How had I survived?". For some reason, I trusted him. He wasn't mad at me. He didn't try to preach to me. We got to talking, and he visited often. He had things on his mind. Heavy things that he didn't dare tell his fellows.

ElwynianOnEscape.text: You'll have to ask him, it's not my place to tell. But... One night, I awoke to him opening my cell. He had his loyal men with him, and they were fleeing. He risked everything to take me with them. It was the only act of kindness I've ever known. We went out that gate in the Plaza, and ran as far and as fast as we could. The Order have been after us ever since.

ElwynianOnPassageSummoned.text: Here's the passage you wanted. I hope it's worth it. Make them pay.

ElwynianBlightedGraveyardIntroduction.text: [DNT-UNUSED] That Blighted Blockage that you found is something I'm familiar with. If you make your way to the Blighted Crypt, you should be able to find some Fancy Component that I can use to build you a bomb that should be able to clear the Blockage. Bring it back to me if you manage to find it!

ElwynianBlightesdCoreComponent.text: [DNT-UNUSED] So you ventured into the Blighted Crypt and found the Blighted Core Component? Fantastic. Hand it over and I should be able to make that bomb for you. Ah yes, that is just what was needed. Here, take this; it should do the trick.

ElwynianCedrusReturnToTown_2.text: Damn you for running out there like that! You should've sent somebody else, anybody else!

ElwynianPlayerUsesWell.text: Hey! We've only got a little water left, don't be greedy!

ElwynianIceCisternReact.text: Everything's frozen! No wonder the water stopped flowing.

ElwynianGateClosedReact.text: I suppose this is one way to prove you're not from the order. You won't be getting through that gate now though.

ElwynianAnotherWayInSummoned.text: I do know another way in, but getting there is not going to be easy. I never thought I'd go back home, but if you really need to get past that wall, it's the only way. Follow me.

ElwynianLeaving.text: I'll be all right! Now it's my turn to run off and do something dangerous. I'll see you back at home.

ElwynianOnTemples.text: You'll have to go through the old Pantheon. After the flooding, it's the only way to get to the estates beyond. It's actually been barricaded since before the city was abandoned. It's anybody's guess what's inside.

ElwynianLockpicking.text: Insert lockpick like so... Twist.... Press up.. Got it!

ElwynianFindMansion.text: Find the big mansion at the back of the estates!

ElwynianEstatesReaction.text: This is it.. Never thought I would have to come back here.

ElwynianSearchForPassage.text: The passage is behind a fireplace in the main dining room. Should still be wide open. Although, I don't know why all these doors are closed. I think someone's been here.

ElwynianEstateBossKillReact.text: It's okay... You can rest now..

A5CountessCedrusReact.text: Cedrus! Does your betrayal have no limit?

A5CountessTooLate.text: Oh my dear friend, it already is.

A5CountessLumeriusDeathReact_01.text: No! <i>{No!} My son! What have they done!

A5CountessLumeriusDeathReact_02.text: No! There is still time! We will have utopia!

A5CountessGlyph.text: The time is finally nigh. I've spent most of my life in service to our ideals, and our reward is nearly at hand. I'm so proud of Lumerius, I knew he would be chosen. I never doubted it, even though I made contingency plans. That was just.. Insurance. For the unlikely eventuality that the fathers chose incorrectly. I would never have let them harm my son. <i>{Never.}

Midwife_Phase_Change_1.text: My dear child... Your time has come!

Midwife_Summon_Children_3.text: Come my children, mother knows best!

Phanos_FallenGodBoss_Death_Random.text: You are worthy... take my staff...

Phanos_FallenGodBoss_Death_2.text: Take my staff... carry on her influence...

Phanos_FallenGodBoss_Death_3.text: Auria! I have found your next... bearer...

Phanos_FallenGodBoss_Emerge.text: Another intruder! Kitava's cursed madness never ends!

Phanos_FallenGodBoss_HalfLifePhase_Rando.text: I alone remain! I will not allow this world to forget my goddess!

Phanos_FallenGodBoss_HalfLifePhase_2.text: I alone remain! I will not allow this world to forget my goddess!

Phanos_FallenGodBoss_MinionsDie_Random.text: I will not let Auria's influence diminish!

Phanos_FallenGodBoss_MinionsDie_2.text: I will not let Auria's influence diminish!

Phanos_FallenGodBoss_TemplarReact_Random.text: And where is your lord Innocence now, Templar?

Phanos_FallenGodBoss_TemplarReact_2.text: And where is your lord Innocence now, Templar?

Midwife_Summon_Children_4.text: Come my children, mother knows best!

Midwife_Duelist_Player_1.text: Careful, Duelist, one of these bastards might be yours!

Midwife_Female_Player_1.text: Childless one, you could never understand the duty of a mother!

Midwife_Karui_Player_1.text: Slave-born! Your filthy bloodline is unwelcome here!

Midwife_Male_Player_1.text: Ursea shall take pleasure in your castration!

Midwife_Sorceress_Player_1.text: Childless Maraketh, you do not know a mothers pain!

TullinaA5UnderFireWild.text: Hey, who the hell are you? I... - Shite!

TullinaA5PlayerDiesWild.text: You can't be serious right now...

TullinaA5SniperWild.text: There's some bastard with a bow up the street taking shots every time we poke our heads out!

TullinaA5RescueTibbsWild.text: My friend Tibbs is injured down there. I don't know what brought you to this forsaken city, but that gemling sniper doesn't care what side you're on. If you can take the long way round and sneak up behind him, I'll do my best to keep him distracted.

TullinaA5IntroSniperWild.text: Are you seriously asking me my name right now? I'm Tullina. Come on, let's rescue Tibbs!

TullinaA5RundownWild.text: Tibbs can give you the rundown on what you're in for.

TullinaA5LeavingDenWild.text: Come on, Tibbs, let's get you out of here.

TullinaA5TownIntro.text: Thanks for giving us a hand back there. This bolt-hole reminds me of my old home. This'll be a good place for Tibbs to rest up and heal. Did I mention my name's Tullina? Well, now I have.

TullinaA5ExoticWine.text: Thanks for retrieving that exotic wine. A shame I had to hang back with Tibbs, that Den sounded like my kind of party!

TullinaA5OnOriath.text: We knew Oriath was a dangerous place, but we figured we could sneak our way through for a big enough payoff. That was a huge mistake. All the monstrous little secrets the Templars kept hidden are now free to roam. This place is beyond deadly. It's outright cursed.

TullinaA5OldHome.text: Family is whoever won't rob and kill you when you're vulnerable. Seems pretty relevant right now, what with Tibbs' injury, and this collection of strangers holed up together. I never truly feel safe, but I'll be less on edge once we get back to the Rogue Harbour, especially now that Tibbs is back from his... sabbatical.

TullinaA5OnRogueMarkers.text: You did pretty well back there. You're still green to the whole thievery thing, but don't worry, we can work on that. Rogue Markers aren't just the currency of the Ring. They also serve a purpose. If you activate one, it'll give you access to the Rogue Harbour. If you're interested in joining us, I'll vouch for you.

TullinaA5OnTibbs.text: You'll never meet a stronger - or kinder - man. He doesn't let on, but I know he has a heart of gold... and boy, do I love trying to steal gold...

TullinaA5OnOthers.text: Don't worry, we'll take them with us when we go. Wouldn't feel right to leave them in this cursed wasteland of a dead city.

Count_DigYouFools1.text: Dig! Dig you fools, or I'll feed you to the Beast myself!

Count_DigYouFools2.text: The time is nigh! Our triumph is at hand!

Count_DigYouFools3.text: Yes, another one. He's under there.

Count_DigYouFools4.text: You can rest when you're dead. Keep digging!

Count_YesMore.text: Yes! More! Don't stop! The beast hungers!

Count_AhItsYou.text: Ah, it's <i>{you}. The little rabbit that hopped away and kept its neck!

Count_NoNooseThisTime.text: No noose this time. I'll remove your head myself!

Count_OpenTheCage_A.text: Oriana! Open the cage. Release the Beast! Give me what you promised!

Count_OpenTheCage_B.text: Woman! Open the cage. Release the Beast! Give me what you promised!

Count_HowDareYou_A.text: You manipulative whore! How dare you abandon me! After! All! I've! Given! You!

Count_HowDareYou_A_A.text: You manipulative whore! How dare you abandon me!

Count_HowDareYou_B.text: How dare you abandon me! After! All! I've! Given! You!

Count_Skill_Promised_Random.text: I will have what I was promised!

Count_Skill_Promised_2.text: I will have what I was promised!

Count_Skill_Promised_3.text: I will have what I was promised!

Count_Skill_Suffer_Random.text: You will suffer in her place!

Count_Skill_Suffer_2.text: You will suffer in her place!

Count_Phase1_HeavyStun_Random.text: Argh! You will pay for that.

Count_Phase1_HeavyStun_4.text: Argh! That... Will not go unpunished!

Count_PhaseChangeMap_Random.text: I pledge my body to the pack!

Count_PhaseChangeMap_2.text: I pledge my body to the pack!

Count_EmergeMap.text: You cannot stop us... We will take the power that we deserve!

CorruptWolf_Skill_GroundStab_Random.text: I smell your blood... And I am ravenous.

CorruptWolf_Skill_GroundStab_2.text: I smell your blood... And I am ravenous.

CorruptWolf_Skill_GroundStab_3.text: I will take out your heart... And savor each bite.

CorruptWolf_Skill_GroundStab_4.text: I will take out your heart... And savor each bite.

CorruptWolf_FogSonnet_Random.text:
Winter's chill... 
Sought the unworthy.
Through an endless night... 
They wither and tarry...
Forsaken frosts... 
As cold as death...
Of Beira's misery... 
The pack won't forget.

CorruptWolf_FogSonnet_2.text:
Agnar the runed...
Agnar the impaler...
Imbued of the moon...
Swift as death...
Cursed or gifted...
Branded and afflicted...
Your veins chilled...
Agnar again has slain.

CorruptWolf_FogSonnet_3.text:
The Eternal impure...
With bloodlust empowered...
Our Ezomyr endured...
But soon all were devoured...
Unending war...
Death waited at the door...
Then hour by hour...
Men fell as summer soured.

CorruptWolf_FogSonnet_4.text:
Fang, tooth or claw...
The pack suffered but endured...
Torture and pain...
Unseen, unheard...
No tales were told...
Of their ravenous hunger...
And their night...
Grew ever colder.

CorruptWolf_FogPoem01_End.text: Of Beira's misery... The pack won't forget.

CorruptWolf_FogPoem02_End.text: Your veins soon chilled... Agnar shall slay again.

CorruptWolf_FogPoem03_End.text: Then hour by hour... Men fell as summer soured.

CorruptWolf_FogPoem04_End.text: And their endless hunger... Grew ever stronger.

CorruptWolf_DeathSequenceFirst.text: The madness... It consumed my being. Oriana used it against me.

CorruptWolf_DeathSequenceSecond.text: I found messages... From the desert.

CorruptWolf_DeathSequenceThird.text: Yes... Find her. Kill her. But first, please stop the madness.

IronManorGargoyleIGlyph.text: First Ones, hear our laments! Sanity recedes ever further into the dark. Shadows hover above us, in the corners, watching and waiting. What sickness has come among us that so unsettles our minds? It sits, poised to strike... Nowhere is safe!

LeitisWildAtExecutioner.text: Don't do this... stop! Just wait! Surely... surely we can—NO!

LeitisWildRescued.text: He killed Eamon. Just killed him. I... I don't know what to do... I...

LeitisWildClearfell.text: Clearfell is safe... we have to get out of here. We can talk there.

LeitisIntro.text: For what it's worth, my name is Leitis. I appreciate the rescue, but... Eamon... everything I know... it's all gone. <continue>It isn't worth much, but take this. Perhaps it will aid you against that monster.

LeitisIntroQuest.text: There is only one thing for certain. Count Geonor must die. He ordered the guard to round up everyone in the village, and when we resisted, they burned it to the ground. <continue>Enter the Manor. Take our vengeance upon him!

LeitisEndOfAct.text: So, it is done. The Count is dead. Where once there was a fire in my heart, there is now nothing but ash. <continue>For enacting my vengeance, you have some measure of thanks from me. Now please, go. Do what you must, but leave me be.

LeitisOnSeed.text: So... you know of it. I remember the night it all began—the Count and his men returned in the witching hour, carrying something hidden from sight. <continue>We didn't know what it was at the time, but we certainly learned soon. It was alive, and he needed to feed it.

LeitisOnFeedingTheBeast.text: The changes came slowly. There were whispers of the downtrodden and clanless going missing. Nobody of consequence. The Count's men were simply cleaning up the ne'er-do-wells. Those that contributed nothing. <continue>But then the Count started changing the penalties for common crimes. Five men were arrested after a simple scuffle over payment. A woman was arrested for <i>{adultery}, like we were somehow living under the tyranny of the Eternals all over again. <continue>Charges became commonplace for almost anything. Living in the Manor, my... my husband... and I were somewhat protected, but we saw what was happening. All of these 'criminals' were sentenced to hard labour, digging away beneath the Manor, until their strength was spent. <continue>When that happened... he hanged them, and threw their bodies to that... <i>{creature.}

LeitisOnDigging.text: I don't know what the Count is looking for beneath the Manor. Perhaps he hopes for proof that his heritage is actually pure. Perhaps he's just gone well and truly mad. <continue>He's torn a massive hole right in the middle of the Manor, a living testament to what he's done to our way of life.

LeitisOnManor.text: That place is a madhouse. Every day was spent threading a careful line. Question the Count, and you'd get arrested. Flatter him too much, and he'd grow paranoid, and arrest you anyway. <continue>The Countess watched all of us with cold eyes. The nobles began to change... strange proclivities emerged. <continue>They brought lone villagers into their rooms in the dead of night, never to be seen again. Eamon and I tried to flee, but they caught us.

LeitisOnCountess.text: When she came to us from the Vastiri Desert, we nobles were just happy the Count had finally found a wife. If we had known what was to come, we never would have celebrated. <continue>From the moment she arrived, she spent her time whispering dreadful little barbs in his ear. He became rather agitated, and started doubting himself... doubting his bloodline. He had a scholar repeatedly investigate whether the Eternals had... <i>{dirtied}... his ancestry. <continue>When he found out that he might have had an unwelcome interloper in his family tree, he became fixated on proving himself, even though we all repeatedly assured him he already <i>{had} our loyalty. He's been obsessed with gaining power ever since, and I think the Countess promised him a way to achieve it.

MarakethMatriarchOnTravelToSandstorm.text: [DNT-UNUSED] If we have all we need, we can clear the Sandstorm!

MarakethMatriarchOnBanishSandstorm.text: [DNT-UNUSED] Good job. Now we can reach our Burial Towers once again.

CountessA1OpenerHim.text: Husband, this interloper has the power we need! Kill him, and you shall have everything I promised!

CountessA1OpenerHer.text: Husband, this interloper has the power we need! Kill her, and you shall have everything I promised!

CountessA1SoMean.text: I think not. I expected so much more from you. Since you are too weak to do the job, I'll find someone who can. Goodbye, <i>{'husband.'}

CountessA1PlayerDies1.text: That corpse should prove rather exceptional. Feed it to the Beast!

CountessA1Letter.text:
Fool, do not send me missives here at Ogham! There is no way to guarantee that prying eyes do not see our letters. 

The Countess of Ogham

CountessA2Opener1.text:
You again! The fool under the Hooded One's sway. Do you even know what he is? No matter. You'll find my King far more capable than Count Geonor.

My King—take the power you were promised. Put an end to this nuisance!

CountessA2PraiseKing1.text: Show them the might of the Faridun, my King!

CountessA2PraiseKing2.text: We're running out of time. End this!

AsalaA2TownIntroSorceress.text: I am Asala, the <i>{Sekhema} of the Ardura. I have heard of you, of course, but Zarka assures me you have almost served your time of banishment. Time will tell.

AsalaA2TownIntro.text: I am Asala, the <i>{Sekhema} of the Ardura. I care not where you came from, nor what caste you might have been there. All that matters is that you have shown yourself capable in battle, <i>{jingakh}. <continue>Remain a friend to the Ardura, and you shall have nothing but respect from us.

AsalaA2PursuingTheBeastQuestGive.text: So, the Beast <i>{has} entered the world once more. We were following a trail of Corruption before we were waylaid, and now we shall resume the hunt. <continue>We Maraketh are honour bound to seek and contain Corruption wherever it may be found. It seems this sacred duty falls on us once more. <continue>The trail connects to two locations, but we don't know where the Beast currently resides. I am willing to begin wherever you and your Shade think is wisest.

AsalaA2RecentEventsGossip.text: Corruption has returned to the Vastiri. Before this season, the hyenic warriors you fought would never have dared raid a caravan. <continue>The dead have begun to rise again, and other creatures of the desert have started... changing. By Zarka's accounts, the land is returning to the way it was before. These are ill times.

AsalaA2RankAndStatusGossip.text: Foreigners often misunderstand the concept of the <i>{Sekhema}. I am no dictator, and do not make some pathetic claim of divine right. <continue>Emperors are for nations filled with the weak-minded and soft, as history has proven every time an empire falls and we endure. <continue>I am Sekhema because others have put their faith in me as the strongest and most capable among us. I lead because there is no better replacement. It is a role I deserve, by definition.

AsalaA2MapUIAncientGatesOne.text: One of the trails of Corruption leads towards the Halani Gates. Anyone who would wish to leave this region must pass through them.

AsalaA2MapUIAncientGatesTwo.text: The Halani Gates are closed for the first time in one thousand years! This can only be related to the Beast. We should investigate the Faridun camp and demand answers.

AsalaA2MapUIAncientGatesThree.text: The Halani Gates are closed, and the Faridun hold them in defence of the Beast. We will have to find another way.

AsalaA2MapUIAncientGatesFour.text: The Halani Gates are closed, and the Faridun hold them in defence of the Beast. We will have to use this... traitors passage instead.

AsalaA2MapUIAncientGatesFive.text: We have reclaimed the Halani Gates from the Faridun, but Jamanra's foul sorcery holds us at bay with a sandstorm. Speak to Zarka. She may know of some way forward.

AsalaA2MapUIAncientGatesSix.text: We have reclaimed the Ancient Gates from the Faridun, but Jamanra's foul sorcery holds us at bay with a sandstorm. Only a reforged Horn of Vastiri can open a way through.

AsalaA2MapUIAncientGatesSeven.text: It is time to use the reforged Horn of the Vastiri to open the way through. Prepare yourself. War is nigh.

AsalaA2MapUITheQuarry.text: Outcasts currently make their home in the forgotten Quarry in the hills of Mawdun. They call themselves the Faridun. We should travel there and find out what it is they are doing.

AsalaA2MapUITraitorsPassage.text: Let us see if the defector's information is truthful. Infiltrate this passage, find your way to the top of the Halani Gates without being detected, and then call for aid. I shall answer.

AsalaA2MapUIKeth.text: Once the seat of power for our people, now a buried testament to a glorious past. We will build a new Keth someday, when all this is over, and the Maraketh will shine under the sun once again. That is a promise.

AsalaA2MapUIMastodonBadlands.text: That valley of the Badlands, where Mastodon bones rot under the sun for all time, is proof that a culture can vanish entirely if the world changes too much. <continue>I will not let my people diminish and disappear the same way...

AsalaA2MapUIValleyOfTitans.text: I am forbidden by the terms of the Third Pact from invoking the Rite of Flame myself. I must send an emissary... as must they. I do not know in what form it will come.

AsalaA2MapUIBurialSpires.text: Enter Deshar, and take our vengeance upon the Faridun within! We will flank them while you ascend and undertake your duty.

AsalaA2MapUISandstorm.text: We now have their trail. They will not escape!

AsalaA2RisuQuestioningGive.text: This <i>{balbalakh} will live or die based on her usefulness in pursuit of the Beast. Ask her what questions you will, then we Ardura will decide her fate.

AsalaA2ResponseAboutBurialSpires.text: So, the outcasts have raised their new 'King' from the grave, and he seeks to violate Deshar— to feed our honoured dead to the Beast. Such a transgression... those <i>{vile dogs!} <continue>Our city of the dead lies beyond the Halani Gates—we should move to crush the Faridun immediately. <continue>Let us see if this defector's information is truthful. Infiltrate this supposed passage, find your way to the top of the Gates without being detected, and then call for aid. I shall answer.

AsalaA2RisusFateGossipBefore.text: If her information proves to be truthful, <i>{then} she will live. If she is a deceiver sent to misdirect us, she will be left to die in the open desert... once again.

AsalaA2RisusFateGossipAfter.text: The <i>{balbalakh} has her life, for she was truthful. If she also wishes to be accepted here, that will be up to her.

AsalaA2AfterAscendingSorc.text: Your success in the trial will go a long way to redeeming you with your <i>{akhara}. I congratulate you. You will always have a place aboard my caravan.

AsalaA2AfterAscending.text: You participated in our trial, <i>{jingakh?} Well, it is unusual, but no less impressive. We welcome you now as a <i>{dekhara.} As far as I am concerned, you are one of us.

AsalaA2AncientGatesBattleSummonedIn.text: Hold them back while I open the gate!

AsalaA2AncientGatesBattleFirstGateOpen.text: Advance with me! There are two more gates we must open!

AsalaA2AncientGatesBattleFaridunNoLonger.text: The Faridun have never organized in such numbers before. They fight as if they no longer fear death!

AsalaA2AncientGatesBattleRandomCallout1.text: A dark shadow has fallen across the land...

AsalaA2AncientGatesBattleRandomCallout4.text: Continue the assault! Slay them all!

AsalaA2AncientGatesBattleSecondGateReach.text: If we can allow the caravan through all three gates, my warriors will swarm them under.

AsalaA2AncientGatesBattleSecondGateOpene.text: Onwards! Give these demons no quarter!

AsalaA2AncientGatesBattleFindFigurehead.text: Let us find the leader of this horde.

AsalaA2AncientGatesBattleFaridunEyesGlea.text: The Faridun have fallen to Corruption. Their eyes gleam with madness!

AsalaA2AncientGatesVsKingResponseToBow.text: The Maraketh do not bow to kings. We skin them.

AsalaA2AncientGatesVsKingDestroyTheBeast.text: We shall destroy the Beast here and now!

AsalaA2AncientGatesVsKingChaseHim.text: Make haste! He must not escape!

AsalaA2AncientGatesAfterKingSandsConjure.text: Quickly! He conjures the very sands against us!

AsalaA2AncientGatesAfterKingReturnToTown.text: This is no natural sandstorm! We must battle sorcery with sorcery. Let us return to the caravan and entreat Zarka's wisdom.

AsalaA2HornOfVastiriQuestGo.text: Ah, yes, the Horn of the Vastiri... I know the tale. The ancient city of Keth, the Badlands, and the Valley of the Titans... We can retrace Orbala's steps in any order.

AsalaA2MastodonBadlandsGossip.text: That valley of the Badlands, where Mastodon bones rot under the sun for all time, is proof that a culture can vanish entirely if the world changes too much. <continue>I will not let my people diminish and disappear the same way...

AsalaA2MastodonTusksComment.text: The last remnants of a wise and powerful race of creatures. A lesson in bone for those whose numbers dwindle from generation to generation.

AsalaA2KethGossip.text: Once the seat of power for our people, now a buried testament to a glorious past. We will build a new Keth someday, when all this is over, and the Maraketh will shine under the sun once again. That is a promise.

AsalaA2WaterGoddessBurnedSorceress.text: Ah, you found the essence of water! I expected something like this to be tended to by a goddess, but I suppose Keth has been abandoned far too long for that.

AsalaA2WaterGoddessBurned.text: There was a <i>{water goddess} in Keth? It is a shame that she chose to be burned alive rather than to stand and fight, but it is not our shame to bear, only her own.

AsalaA2ValleyOfTitansGossip.text: I am forbidden by the terms of the Third Pact from invoking the Rite of Flame myself. I must send an emissary... as must they. I do not know in what form it will come.

AsalaA2TravelToSandstorm.text: It is time to use the reforged Horn of the Vastiri to open the way through. Prepare yourself. War is nigh.

AsalaA2AboutBurialSpiresSorceress.text: Enter Deshar, and take our vengeance upon the Faridun within! We will flank them while you ascend and undertake your duty.

AsalaA2AboutBurialSpires.text: I am hesitant to allow you access to sacred Deshar, but better a single <i>{jingakh} than an army of spiteful enemies. Our city of the dead must be protected, no matter the cost.

AsalaA2OnSeeingLetter.text: Why would you show me this? You fool! This folly is only harmless because there are no names on this letter. Otherwise, tradition would demand unhappy duties of me. <continue>I value each and every one of my dekhara. This is why I say: get this out of my sight.

AsalaA2OnChoosingDreadnought.text: We have their trail now. They will not escape!

AsalaA2FinalBattleTime.text: The Faridun have assembled a tremendous Dreadnought, a war caravan larger than we have ever seen. <continue>As we speak, it is barreling through the heart of the Vastiri, leaving devastation in its wake.

AsalaA2MapUIDreadnought.text: The time has come for a final confrontation. We must attack the Dreadnought and face Jamanra and the Beast ourselves. This must end here.

AsalaA2DreadnoughtPepTalk.text: Ready yourself. We must prevail, no matter what!

AsalaA2DreadnoughtRespondToKingBow.text: The Maraketh do not bow to kings. We skin them.

AsalaA2DreadnoughtWakesUp.text: This is not over. Not yet.

AsalaA2DreadnoughtSentenceToDeath.text: Jamanra! I return you to the embrace of death!

AsalaA2SpeechOne.text: Jamanra, the pretender King... returns to his grave!

AsalaA2SpeechTwo.text: Let it echo across the Vastiri! I, Asala, <i>{Sekhema} of the Ardura, vow to unite the <i>{akharas!} The Faridun will be granted clemency, should they seek it. Every woman, man and child not fallen to Corruption will be welcomed as one... <i>{of our own!}

AsalaA2SpeechThree.text: We will build a new Keth, and we shall shine under the sun once again. That... is my promise!

AsalaA2AfterSpeechClassWitch.text: We shall see what comes of that speech. The Faridun will fall in line, or they will suffer the same fate as their so-called <i>{King.} <continue>We women of ambition must have each other's backs, wouldn't you say? You have my thanks.

AsalaA2AfterSpeechClassSorc.text: We shall see what comes of that speech. The Faridun will fall in line, or they will suffer the same fate as their so-called <i>{King.} <continue>You have my gratitude, as a sister in arms.

AsalaA2AfterSpeechClassDruid.text: We shall see what comes of that speech. The Faridun will fall in line, or they will suffer the same fate as their so-called <i>{King.} <continue>Your kind are too rare in the Vastiri. Tell your brothers they are always welcome. You have my thanks, druid.

AsalaA2AfterSpeechClassTemplar.text: We shall see what comes of that speech. The Faridun will fall in line, or they will suffer the same fate as their so-called <i>{King.} <continue>You are a credit to your order, Templar. You have my thanks.

AsalaA2AfterSpeechClassDuelist.text: We shall see what comes of that speech. The Faridun will fall in line, or they will suffer the same fate as their so-called <i>{King.} <continue>You'll never find another arena quite like the Vastiri. You have my thanks.

AsalaA2AfterSpeechClassMercenary.text: We shall see what comes of that speech. The Faridun will fall in line, or they will suffer the same fate as their so-called <i>{King.} <continue>You live to fight another day, mercenary. You have my thanks.

AsalaA2AfterSpeechClassShadow.text: We shall see what comes of that speech. The Faridun will fall in line, or they will suffer the same fate as their so-called <i>{King.} <continue>Your skills have been appreciated, Shadow. You have my thanks.

AsalaA2AfterSpeechClassMonk.text: We shall see what comes of that speech. The Faridun will fall in line, or they will suffer the same fate as their so-called <i>{King.} <continue>I never thought a servant of the Dreamer would... well, here we are. You have my thanks.

AsalaA2AfterSpeechClassRanger.text: We shall see what comes of that speech. The Faridun will fall in line, or they will suffer the same fate as their so-called <i>{King.} <continue>Descendant of the Maji. Yes, I recognise your lineage. You have my thanks, for all that you have done here.

AsalaA2AfterSpeechClassHuntress.text: We shall see what comes of that speech. The Faridun will fall in line, or they will suffer the same fate as their so-called <i>{King.} <continue>You have my thanks, Azmerian. I hope you find what you are looking for.

AsalaA2AfterSpeechClassWarrior.text: We shall see what comes of that speech. The Faridun will fall in line, or they will suffer the same fate as their so-called <i>{King.} <continue>You have my thanks, mighty one. You're a good man. Better than most.

AsalaA2AfterSpeechClassMarauder.text: We shall see what comes of that speech. The Faridun will fall in line, or they will suffer the same fate as their so-called <i>{King.} <continue>You have my thanks, Karui. I hope we never meet in battle.

AsalaA2AboutCuttingOffKingsHead.text: The war is over. I have given him an honourable death. This may prove to heal the wound between the Faridun and the Maraketh. <continue>Return with me. I must address my people.

AsalaA2EndOfAct.text: Yes, we can take you to the edge of the desert. Then, we will continue to track the Beast. You <i>{must} find a way to contain it. When we find out where it is being taken, we will seek you out. <continue>Until then, may the winds ever be calm on your path.

AsalaA2TheCountessGossip.text: This 'Oriana' would find no allies among our <i>{akharas...} we are no strangers to the eternal war against Corruption. If she has allies in this region, they cannot be of the Maraketh.

AsalaA2HonorBoundGossip.text: After the Beast of Highgate was slain, all other <i>{akharas} vowed to pursue and eradicate Corruption should it ever return. Never again will a sole akhara suffer the weight of history.

AsalaA2EndOfActGossip.text: Jamanra is back where he belongs. I have given him a proper death. By removing his head, I acknowledged him. Though, he was never a King, despite what the Faridun may choose to believe. <continue>Those who have survived this war will be given a choice. It would be a waste to kill the Faridun who have proven themselves in battle... they may choose to be acknowledged. To have a place at the table. Or... they can remain outcasts. Either way, it is time to write a new chapter. <continue>Who knows what the future holds? After what has happened here, the other <i>{akharas} must consider joining the Ardura. I intend to be... persuasive.

HoodedOneA2Intro.text: This outpost seems to be part of a trade route, so we should be able to find a Maraketh caravan. They are an honourable people, and I have no doubt they will assist us.

HoodedOneA2OurNextMoveOne.text: The Beast is on the move, twisting the desert as it goes, waking ancient dead and unknown horrors alike. The Countess brought it here as part of some nefarious plan. <continue>I assume she has allies here. We must track them down and convince them to give up this madness.

HoodedOneA2OnAsala.text: Asala has agreed to aid us, exactly as I expected. The Beast represents an existential threat to all the peoples of Wraeclast, but even beyond that, she seems to be quite driven. <continue>She reminds me of a rambunctious young woman I once knew in Keth, who eventually rose to power, attained divinity, and led her people to greatness.

HoodedOneA2OnShambrin.text: I am accustomed to others shivering and turning away when my gaze falls upon them, but I must confess, for once the feeling is reversed. <continue>Although she is blind, I sometimes have the strangest notion that she is looking at me - even at night.

HoodedOneA2OnRisu.text: It takes courage to go against one's people. I once faced a similar decision. There were men and women like me, who believed themselves to be exceptional, and they were correct... terribly, horribly correct. <continue>I cursed myself to a permanent exile from my own peers by betraying them. I was unlike mortals, but hated by immortals. I was alone. <continue>I would do it all again... and I still might.

HoodedOneA2OnZarka.text: You have no idea how much restraint it requires to listen to tales of peoples and places I knew, yet <i>{not} correct her. <continue>She's close, I shall grant her that. Often startlingly so, in certain details or sequences of events, but the spirit of what happened thousands of years ago, the <i>{essence} of that life... it has been embellished. Yet other times, the stories convey only a pale shadow, and the true magnificence is lost. <continue>Or is it my memories that have drifted with time? I suppose we shall never know, because those days are gone, never to return... all that I once loved has been dust hundreds of years longer than you have even been alive.

HoodedOneA2OnSunClanHyenas.text: Those creatures are too coherent and intelligent to be manifestations of Corruption. I suspect they are the descendants of Divine tampering. <continue>There was a being I once knew in the ancient days, a trickster who would have appreciated someone to laugh at his ill-conceived humour. What more perfect audience for a sickening jester than a pack of gibbering hyenas?

HoodedOneA2OnTheMaraketh.text: The Maraketh have a cultural history deeper than most know. Theirs is a strict tradition, bordering on brutal, but it is that adherence to shared beliefs that has kept them strong when entire Empires have come and gone around them.

HoodedOneA2OnSlavery.text: Yes, I have seen the slaves pulling the carts. I am uncomfortable with the practice, but from what I understand, it allows those captured in battle to serve rather than simply being executed. <continue>There are not enough resources to keep prisoners who do not work. In this harsh land, it is perhaps the lesser of two evils. That is... what I tell myself, at least.

HoodedOneA2OurNextMoveAfterAncientGates.text: The Countess has used Corruption to resurrect Jamanra, and they have escaped with the Beast... thankfully, we have some idea what the Faridun intend. <continue>We must reach Deshar as soon as possible.

HoodedOneA2OnTheFaridun.text: They call themselves the Faridun in this era, but they have died out and been reborn many times. They are not an independent culture. They are the Maraketh's dark secret, the inevitable consequence of life's haphazard nature. <continue>A society cannot simply purge itself of the weak, the ill, or the disadvantaged. Those unwanted newborns who are abandoned among the dunes... they rarely die, no matter how much the Maraketh wish to make them simply disappear. <continue>No, they live. The Faridun are the shadow of the Maraketh, always just out of sight, always watching. They rescue those children and raise them on the outside, looking in. An unspoken relief for the father and mother that must give up their child, but a gathering storm fated to one day return home with a fury.

HoodedOneA2OnKethAfterVisiting.text: Ah, Keth. Now nothing but dunes of sand, but once, it was glorious. The waters flowed in patterns crafted by artisans of skill beyond belief. The hanging gardens could impress even the most jaded heart.

HoodedOneA2OnTheValleyOfTitans.text: Do not tarry long in that valley. There are ancient pacts in this world that govern more than you and I are meant to know, but we still may suffer the consequences if we break them. Do what you must, and then abscond.

HoodedOneA2OnTheMastodonBadlands.text: The lost-men of the Badlands have no knowledge of our wars. They will attack you because they do not understand you. It is unfortunate, but we cannot allow them to stand in the way. <continue>This conflict will determine their fate as well, so in a sense, we are saving them despite themselves. The greater good is all that matters.

HoodedOneA2OnTheSpires.text: I am not Maraketh, but I did come to love this land and its people. They built their necropolis during the height of Keth's power, so I am pleasantly surprised to find that the towers are still standing. <continue>In the end, the works of Man may outlast the gods themselves.

HoodedOneA2OurNextMoveAfterBlowingHorn.text: The path to Deshar has been opened. Infiltrate the towers, and stop the Faridun from feeding the Beast!

HoodedOneA2OurNextMoveAfterSpires.text: We are out of time. The Beast may already be too dangerous to contain through mortal means. The time for all-out war has arrived. <continue>Help the Ardura attack the Faridun war machine before it is too late!

HoodedOneA2RevealIntroduction.text: My worst fears have been realised. The Beast is beyond our means now.

HoodedOneA2RevealIntroduction_HoodDown.text: My worst fears have been realised. The Beast is beyond our means now.

HoodedOneA2RevealIntroductionTwo.text: You're right. I have not been entirely forthcoming ... it is time I told you who I truly am.

HoodedOneA2RevealIntroductionTwo_HoodDow.text: You're right. I have not been entirely forthcoming ... it is time I told you who I truly am.

HoodedOneA2RevealConfession.text: I am... a god. I am the Thief of Virtue. I am Sin. And I have failed once again. <continue>It was I who created the Beast... the Seed of Corruption that now threatens to grow anew, and it is my responsibility. As it is my creation that once again threatens all of Wraeclast, it is by my hand that it must be contained. <continue>All I can ask is that, knowing who I am, you still see the importance of our task.

HoodedOneA2RevealConfessionContinue.text: The Beast has grown beyond our ability to contain it. We must search for something greater than we currently possess, something that can drain its power and bring it back to a more manageable form. <continue>While I slumbered under the numbing effects of Corruption, there was an empire that mastered the use of that deadly energy. We must go to the jungles of the long-ago Vaal. <continue>Their ruins may yet hold the secrets we need. That is where we must go, to the sunken city of Utzaal. It is our only hope.

HoodedOneA2RevealConfessionContinue_Hood.text: The Beast has grown beyond our ability to contain it. We must search for something greater than we currently possess, something that can drain its power and bring it back to a more manageable form. <continue>While I slumbered under the numbing effects of Corruption, there was an empire that mastered the use of that deadly energy. We must go to the jungles of the long-ago Vaal. <continue>Their ruins may yet hold the secrets we need. That is where we must go, to the sunken city of Utzaal. It is our only hope.

HoodedOneA2RevealOnThisPlace.text: I am thousands of years old. I was mortal first, but then I was deified against my will by my brother... but that is a story for another time. <continue>I spent my early divine life in Keth. I loved, and was loved. I even had a daughter. This shrine depicts them both. They were revered by the Maraketh.

HoodedOneA2RevealOnWife.text: Garukhan was the true jewel of the Vastiri, at least to me. Divine love is much like mortal love, at least from what I can remember, and we were happy for a time longer than the lives of many mortal men. <continue>The time came, however, when love was not enough. Her humanity sifted through the cracks of her life like fine sand, leaving a divine shell that held her image, but nothing of her soul. <continue>It is a trap, you see. Divinity. Faith empowers, but faith also shapes. To gather more power, a god must play the part, becoming more and more the icon their followers perceive. <continue>When does perception become reality? It's impossible to pinpoint, and that's the most sinister thing about it. You never know the moment you cross the line.

HoodedOneA2RevealOnDaughter.text: You want the truth? I betrayed her, and had her killed. <continue>There are not enough excuses in all of Wraeclast to make up for what I did. I thought it was the right thing to do at the time. I thought it was the only way to save humanity. <continue>And yet, here we are again, chasing the Beast and fighting for the fate of the world. I am beginning to suspect that the cycle of history may never end, unless we surpass ourselves and find another way. <continue>But until we do, we will solve this the only way we know how: with violence.

HoodedOneA2OurNextMoveLast.text: The Ardura can take us south, to the edge of the jungle. The sunken city of Utzaal is not hidden, nor hard to reach... it is protected by a different danger, but we will deal with that when we come to it. <continue>When you are ready, we should begin the journey as soon as possible.

HoodedOneA2OnJamanra.text: I was asleep during the era of Jamanra. I cannot attest to the truth of Risu's tale... though I cannot say it is outside the realm of possibility. The Maraketh have strict traditions, erring on the side of brutal.

RisuA2PerennialKingAlternate.text: I know what Jamanra intends. Atop the burial spires of Deshar lie the Maraketh's most honoured dead. The King has become driven by madness to seek any trace of ancient flesh from those of renown or power in life. <continue>He intends to feed their bodies to the horrific creature he keeps in a cage behind his throne. They call it the Beast. I have seen it, and the sight haunts my nightmares...

RisuA2GatesAreClosed.text: The Halani Gates are closed! Then Jamanra must have succeeded in capturing them. He planned to close the gates to prevent the Maraketh from interrupting his... harvest. A siege from the front would be impossible now. <continue>But there is another way. An ancient passage lost to time. It was used by the traitor Balbala. I can show you where it is, if you will use it to stop Jamanra before it is too late.

RisuA2TraitorsPassageHover.text: The Maraketh forgot the location of the Traitor's Passage long ago, but we Faridun kept the knowledge of it for many generations, in the hopes one day we could use it against them...

RisuA2HereIsTraitorsPassage.text: Here is the entrance. Please. Try to end this before my people are lost forever.

RisuA2OnZarkaEndOfActSorceress.text: Now that we two peoples have become one, Zarka has begun teaching me her tales. She thinks she does not have many years left, but I hope that she does. <continue>I would be honoured to replace her... but only if you do not desire the role for yourself. I will do my best, my friend.

RisuA2OnZarkaEndOfAct.text: Zarka thinks it is likely our two peoples will become one. She says she will teach me her tales. She thinks she does not have many years left, but I hope that she does. <continue>I would be honoured to replace her, but I do not want to lose her just yet.

ZarkaA2IntroductionSorceress.text: Welcome to the Ardura—oh, hmm. I know who <i>{you} are. Don't worry... I won't hold it against you, young one, but we cannot travel anywhere at the moment. <continue>Hyenic raiders are harassing the trade route ahead. For the time being, we are stuck here.

ZarkaA2Introduction.text: You are seeking passage on our caravan? We cannot travel anywhere at the moment. <continue>Hyenic raiders are harassing the trade route ahead. For the time being, we are stuck here.

ZarkaA2ReturnFromHyenasSorceress.text: <i>{You} defeated the raiders? Despite your past, we could use someone of your skill. Welcome to the Ardura <i>{akhara}. <continue>You may travel with us in exchange for your service. You will even have the respect of one of our own for as long as you stay. If anyone says otherwise, tell them to speak to me.

ZarkaA2ReturnFromHyenas.text: <i>{You} defeated the raiders? Fate sends us a fortuitous stranger! Welcome to the Ardura <i>{akhara}. <continue>You may travel with us in exchange for your service, as a <i>{jingakh}, and you will have nearly the respect of one of our own for as long as you stay.

ZarkaA2ResponseToBalbalaSoulCoinSorceres.text: Ah, you released Balbala, the Traitor? Then it is your duty to redeem her soul, by allowing her to serve as a mentor Djinn during your dance with the scorpion. This will not be a simple matter, the old ways are required. <continue>Speak to Asala. The ancient trial is not far from here, and the caravan is duty-bound to carry you there.

ZarkaA2ResponseToBalbalaSoulCoin.text: Ah, you released Balbala, the Traitor? Then it is your duty to redeem her soul, by allowing her to serve as a mentor Djinn during your dance with the scorpion. <continue>In modern times, we give aspiring <i>{dekharas} a straightforward test. For <i>{this} task, however, the old ways are required. You will have to face a much deadlier trial. <continue>Speak to Asala. The original trial is not far from here, and the caravan is duty-bound to carry you there.

ZarkaA2AscendancyCompletedSorceress.text: I'm proud of you, young one. Few have the strength to redeem themselves, let alone others. Perhaps, one day, you will lead an <i>{akhara} of your own.

ZarkaA2AscendancyCompleted.text: This is a time of change indeed! For at least eighty generations, the tale of Balbala has remained the same, but now you have changed the ending. The desert is a little kinder this day.

ZarkaA2SandstormSeen.text: A sandstorm barrier! Foul sorcery, right out of the tales!

ZarkaA2HornQuestGive.text: Jamanra can control the sands? This was not an ability he had in life. It must be born of Corruption. <continue>There <i>{is} something in the tales that could help us overcome such a power. It was said that the Horn of the Vastiri could control the winds. I believe the Horn's location has been lost to time... <i>{but}... perhaps it is possible that we can reconstruct it. <continue>We would have to retrace the steps of our greatest heroine, Orbala, on her final adventure. Speak to Asala. She knows the tale, and where it might take us. Let her know how you wish to begin. Or, you may seek my wisdom if you have further questions.

ZarkaA2HornQuestExplanation.text: Ah, the Horn... how to condense a seven-day tale? It was created during Orbala's eighth adventure, her final quest before becoming the <i>{Sekhema} of <i>{Sekhemas}... she wrested control of the three elements. <continue>Her trusty war-steed, the great mastodon Ekbab, gave its tusks for the carving and the channeling of lightning. The essence of water was a secret held at the heart of Keth... and primordial fire must be earned from those that originally brought it to Wraeclast. <continue>We will find <i>{them} at the Valley of Titans. Yes... those are the three elements we will need.

ZarkaA2HornOfVastiriStory.text: This is not the first time the sands themselves have been used against us. The Necromancer of Weeping Black, Saresh, once waged war upon the Maraketh out of the nascent desert regions of that era. He commanded not only armies of the dead, but vast roiling storms as well. <continue>Hearing of this threat, Orbala set forth on a quest to master the elements, and, in three places of power, she proved herself to the winds. Her reward came to be known as the Horn of the Vastiri. <continue>When she drew in a mighty breath and sounded the Horn, it was <i>{so powerful}, every tent across the entire Plains blew open. You can imagine what it did to the Necromancer's sandstorms... Seizing their moment, the united <i>{akharas} stormed forth to savage the undead armies of Saresh. <continue>For this victory, Orbala was made the <i>{Sekhema} of <i>{Sekhemas}, and, after ruling with strength and cunning for many years, later became our Queen of the Wind, greatest goddess of the Maraketh. Her divine name was Garukhan, which means 'ultimate sovereign.' <continue>The tales, unfortunately, make no further mention of the Horn after that.

ZarkaA2AcceptsFlameRuby.text: This ruby is beautiful and quite haunting. Perhaps it is simply my imagination, but I feel as if there is something staring back at me from deep inside.

ZarkaA2AcceptsTusks.text: These tusks are truly worthy of Orbala's steed!

ZarkaA2AcceptsEssenceOfWater.text: There was a goddess of water lying at the heart of Keth? I wonder what her role in the past involved. It is my sacred duty to keep our tales, but I know nothing of this goddess! How could we Maraketh have forgotten something so important?

ZarkaA2AcceptsEssenceOfWaterNamed.text: There was a goddess of water lying at the heart of Keth? Halani! I wonder what her role in the past involved. It is my sacred duty to keep our tales, but I know nothing of this goddess! <continue>The tales say that Halani was the name of Keth's Second River, so the truth must have drifted over the generations. How could we Maraketh have forgotten something so important?

ZarkaA2TwoMoreThings.text: Keep following Orbala's trail, young one. There are still two more acts to her story.

ZarkaA2OneMoreThing.text: Keep going, young one. We are nearly at the end of Orbala's tale.

ZarkaA2CraftsHorn.text: Impressive, young one! Now we have everything we need to recreate the Horn of the Vastiri. <continue>It'll take a bit of carving... hmm, I think the Flame Ruby goes here... imbue the essence of water with the proper motions... maybe I'll just tighten that there... snap that off... oh! I hope that wasn't important... alright. It's <i>{a bit} like the original Horn. <continue>If my fingers were more nimble, I could have done better. This won't blow a gale across the entire Vastiri, but it will serve our purpose. Here. Take it. You retraced Orbala's journey, so you should be the one to sound the Horn.

ZarkaA2MapUIMastodonBadlands.text: We need more than just common tusks from the Badlands. You must find the greatest among them, the remains of the mastodon war-steed Ekbab. You will know his remains when you see them.

ZarkaA2MapUIKeth.text: The essence of water was said to be kept at the heart of Keth, from whence the seven rivers sprung. The sands have reclaimed the city, but there must still be ways inside. Seek the sanctum at the heart of the shrines.

ZarkaA2MapUITitanValley.text: We must still respect the ancient agreements. You are permitted to enter the Valley of the Titans, but only for the Rite of Flame. Find the crystalline dais, call for the rite, prove yourself... and then depart, with haste.

ZarkaA2MapUIAscendancyTrial.text: During the Winter of the World, the trial to become a <i>{dekhara} was brutal and unforgiving. It was overseen by one of our earliest goddesses, Varashta, in a series of chambers beneath the sands. There, an aspirant and a mentor may both earn honour.

ZarkaA2BanishmentGossip.text: The tale-women still talk of you rejecting the honour of our role. I hope your time of banishment has taught you some respect. <continue>If I were to count the days, I suspect I might find you have returned to the Plains of Vastiri somewhat early... but it seems my infirmities are suddenly clouding my sense of the seasons. I won't tell if you won't, young one.

ZarkaA2TheDreamerGossip.text: It is rare to see one of your kind here, Monk. Tread carefully. The Third Pact still governs both you... and your master.

ZarkaA2TitanValleyForMonkGossip.text: As a servant of the Dreamer, the Third Pact explicitly forbids your kind from entering the Valley of the Titans. Hmm... but necessity sometimes overrides tradition. Do what you must, and speak of this to no one.

ZarkaA2OnDesharSorc.text: Ah, Deshar, the City of the Dead! In these harrowing times, one could be forgiven for thinking the risen dead live there—if that form of existence can even be called living. No, no. Long before we had to worry about the dead rising, we built towering spires to return our people to the sky. <continue>Our Honoured Dead lie openly, enjoying the sun, not hidden from it under the earth. Over time, they are scoured away, becoming the wind and sand you feel on your skin at this very moment. <continue>I will soon make the journey to Deshar myself, once I train a replacement. I could wait, but I prefer to meet Death on my feet. Who knows? I may even be the first mortal to win my battle, and defeat Nekraata in spiritual combat. <continue>I might not look the part now, but when I was younger, you would have found me to be a formidable rival!

ZarkaA2OnDeshar.text: Ah, Deshar, the City of the Dead! In these harrowing times, one could be forgiven for thinking the risen dead live there—if that form of existence can even be called living. No, no. Long before we had to worry about the dead rising, we built towering spires to return our people to the sky. <continue>Our Honoured Dead lie openly, enjoying the sun, not hidden from it under the earth. Over time, they are scoured away, becoming the wind and sand you feel on your skin at this very moment. <continue>Deshar is our most sacred monument... I myself will soon make the journey there, once I train a replacement. Most do wait for their bodies to fail, but I would prefer to meet Death on my feet. Who knows? I may even be the first mortal to win my battle, and defeat Nekraata in spiritual combat. <continue>It might not look like it now, but I was a rather powerful Sorceress in my time.

ZarkaA2OnJamanra.text: Jamanra? That's a tale I rarely tell. Every few generations, the Faridun stir up trouble. Jamanra was their most successful attempt at causing problems. A very long time ago, he spread dangerous ideas among the outcasts, and spoke to the Maraketh as if they were equals. <continue>His offences were so great, the <i>{Sekhemas} joined together to approach and rebuke him. The tale says that he was so in awe of the glory of our leaders, he ended his own life, and chose to fall forgotten in the sands. <continue>It is a strange conclusion to his tale, I must admit. But this is what is told. If he has been somehow reanimated through Corruption, he will have only one goal: harming us.

ZarkaA2OnJamanraPostRisu.text: I must confess that my knowledge of Jamanra seems rather tainted by historical... biases. I am honour-bound to do more research before I tell his tale again.

RisuA2WildBreakLock_Random.text: Please! Get me out of here!

RisuA2WildBreakLock_2.text: What are you waiting for? Get me out of here!

ShambrinIntroSorceress.text: Who goes there? Oh, a newcomer to our caravan. <continue>I am Shambrin, tradesmith and weaponmaster for the Ardura. Do not hesitate to ask if you require anything.

ShambrinIntroWitch.text: Who goes there? By the sound of your voice, you cannot be Maraketh. It is always intriguing to meet foreign warriors and learn their ways of war. <continue>I only hope I have weapons and armour that might be useful to you. I am Shambrin.

ShambinIntroTemplar.text: Who goes there? By the sound of your voice, you cannot be Maraketh. <continue>You may trade with me, for trade is the lifeblood of survival in the desert, but expect no kindness.

ShambrinIntroDruid.text: Who goes there? By the sound of your voice, you cannot be Maraketh. <continue>You may trade with me, for trade is the lifeblood of survival in the desert, but expect no kindness.

ShambrinIntroGladiator.text: Who goes there? By the sound of your voice, you cannot be Maraketh. <continue>You may trade with me, for trade is the lifeblood of survival in the desert, but expect no kindness.

ShambrinIntroMercenary.text: Who goes there? By the sound of your voice, you cannot be Maraketh. <continue>You may trade with me, for trade is the lifeblood of survival in the desert, but expect no kindness.
