ShambrinIntroAssassin.text: Who goes there? By the sound of your voice, you cannot be Maraketh. <continue>You may trade with me, for trade is the lifeblood of survival in the desert, but expect no kindness.

ShambrinIntroMonk.text: Who goes there? By the sound of your voice, you cannot be Maraketh. <continue>You may trade with me, for trade is the lifeblood of survival in the desert, but expect no kindness.

ShambrinGiveTraitorsQuestSorceress.text: If you are traveling through Traitor's Passage, there is something I wish to ask of you. <continue>Did your <i>{akhara} keep the tale of the Traitor, Balbala? She is still sealed there, somewhere along the tunnel as an undying Djinn. She served her sentence long ago, but knowledge of the location was lost. It is long past time to release her.

ShambrinGiveTraitorsPassageQuest.text: If you are traveling through Traitor's Passage, there is something I wish to ask of you. <continue>The Traitor, Balbala. According to the tales, she is still sealed there, somewhere along the tunnel, as an undying Djinn. She served her sentence long ago, but knowledge of the location was lost. It is long past time to release her. <continue>I will tell you her story, if you wish, but I doubt it will mean much to a <i>{jingakh.}

ShambrinBalbalaGossipSorceress.text: Your <i>{akhara} did not tell this tale? It's one of my favourites. <continue>Long ago, when Keth was the shining jewel of the Vastiri and our trade routes were the envy of the known world, a weak-willed <i>{Sekhema} named Balbala betrayed her <i>{akhara} for a promise of <i>{welakath,} a mythical elixir said to bestow great power. <continue>She led a band of foreign warriors through secret paths to the top of the Halani Gates. Taken by surprise, the <i>{akhara} was slain to the last woman. <continue>What was her reward? Not <i>{welakath.} The bandits put a spear through her gut in that very passage. A cautionary tale, yes. For her betrayal, the wise women of that era enacted an ancient ritual, trapping Balbala's soul as a Djinn for a sentence intended to be one thousand years. <continue> It has been far more than one thousand years. By Zarka's reckoning, at least two or three. The stain of Balbala's betrayal has been lifted from her legacy, yet the knowledge of her prison was lost long ago...

ShambrinBalbalaGossipNonSorc.text: Long ago, when Keth was the shining jewel of the Vastiri and our trade routes were the envy of the known world, a weak-willed <i>{Sekhema} named Balbala betrayed her <i>{akhara} for a promise of <i>{welakath,} a mythical elixir said to bestow great power. <continue>She led a band of foreign warriors through secret paths to the top of the Halani Gates. Taken by surprise, the <i>{akhara} was slain to the last woman. <continue>What was her reward? Not <i>{welakath.} The bandits put a spear through her gut in that very passage. A cautionary tale, yes. For her betrayal, the wise women of that era enacted an ancient ritual, trapping Balbala's soul as a Djinn for a sentence intended to be one thousand years. <continue> <i>{Jingakh}. It has been far more than one thousand years. By Zarka's reckoning, at least two or three. The stain of Balbala's betrayal has been lifted from her legacy, yet the knowledge of her prison was lost long ago...

ShambrinTraitorQuestEndSorceress.text: So, you released Balbala from her prison, and she fought well. Good. I'm sure you know what to do next, but touch the <i>{barya} and ask her, if your time away from the Maraketh has faded your knowledge of the tales.

ShambrinTraitorQuestEndNonSorc.text: So, you released Balbala from her prison, and she fought well. Good. She may now earn her redemption, if the ancient places still hold power. Her <i>{barya} contains her soul. She will tell you what to do next.

ShambrinGiveTraditionsTollQuest.text: As we approach Deshar, I feel I must ask something of you once more. There is someone... I care about. Let us leave it at that. I have learned she went on a lone journey to the spires three moons past... and she has not returned. <continue>The others cannot know of this, for there was neither sickness nor injury involved. Do you understand? I simply wish to know the truth of what happened, to end the pain of not knowing. <continue>If you happen to find Lailuma's body in the dunes below the spires... And if you bring me something of hers, then I will know. If you do not, then no one ever will...

ShambrinBurialSpiresExplanationSorceress.text: I don't know how things are done in your akhara, but here, those that cannot earn burial in the sky have a tradition of their own. Because they are not allowed to rest above, when they feel sickness or injury taking hold, they leap from the windswept heights of Deshar to the dunes below. <continue>Though their bodies will still be lost in the sands —our greatest fear— lying at the base of honour is the next best thing to lying upon it. You can understand why I was concerned that Lailuma chose to travel there alone...

ShambrinBurialSpiresExplanationNonSorc.text: Those Maraketh that prove themselves in life earn burial in the sky, but the weak and unfortunate have a tradition of their own: because they are not allowed to rest above, when they feel sickness or injury taking hold, they leap from the windswept heights of Deshar to the dunes below. <continue>Though their bodies will still be lost in the sands —our greatest fear— lying at the base of honour is the next best thing to lying upon it. You can understand why I was concerned that Lailuma chose to travel there alone...

ShambrinTraditionsTollEnd.text: You found a letter? For your sake, do not speak of its contents. I will burn it. <continue>When I have the opportunity, I intend to return to Deshar and mark the location of Lailuma's body... A stone perhaps, something inconspicuous. Others will not know, but I will. She will be remembered.

ShambrinA2OnBlindness.text: Does the scorpion's sting carry less poison at night? In the hopes of taking on fighting duty again, I am still practicing the art of the sword. Red-eyed Nasima, she of the Second Sight, proved that there is more to combat than mere vision. <continue>However, there is still honour in serving the role of tradesmith and weaponmaster. I served as a <i>{dekhara} for as long as I was able, and I intend to fulfill this duty with just as much dedication.

ShambrinA2OnTheFaridun.text: Publicly, I will decry them as loudly as anyone else. Privately, I understand. I do not condone their actions, but I have suffered some small portion of what they must feel their entire lives. <continue>To be honest, I <i>{expected} them to turn on us eventually.

ShambrinA2OnTheDefectorBeforeHelping.text: This defector, Risu, will never be accepted by the Ardura. You may trust her, and she may provide information about the enemy's intentions, but remember, she is a traitor to her people. <continue>We deal with our own traitors using... excessive means. She is not one of us, so we do not consider it our duty to punish her, but neither will we protect her when the time comes.

ShambrinA2OnTheDefectorAfterHelping.text: Risu has proven herself, at least to me. She has spoken only the truth, and I believe she means well. In another life, we might have been fellow <i>{dekhara,} or even friends.

ShambrinA2OnTheHoodedOne.text: When I face his direction, there is a faint... impression. Even the sun does not intrude upon my blindness, so this is a new sensation for me. What am I seeing from your strange companion?

ShambrinA2OnZarkaSorceress.text: I have heard that you <i>{rejected} the life of a tale-woman. Please don't hold bitterness against Zarka for her role. She holds all the wisdom and knowledge of the Ardura, and the stories of many other akharas as well. <continue>Our traditions helped us survive as these lands turned to dust over the generations, and in many ways, that lush beauty still exists for us through her words.

ShambrinA2OnZarkaNonSorc.text: Zarka holds all the wisdom and knowledge of the Ardura, and the stories of many other akharas as well. Our traditions helped us survive as these lands turned to dust over the generations, and in many ways, that lush beauty still exists for us through her words. <continue>Especially now the gods have returned to Wraeclast, we know that our beliefs have power. Perhaps we can bring back those verdant forests and gleaming rivers, if only we have enough faith in a leader strong enough to make it real.

ShambrinA2OnAsala.text: I remember her face, from before the battle where I lost my sight. She is quite beautiful, and she has strength and cunning to match. I can think of no better leader for us. <continue>We Ardura have put all of our faith in Asala, and though we do not number enough to spark Divinity in her, we have still thrived under her leadership.

ShambrinA2EndOfActSorceress.text: You came to us a banished stranger, but you will leave as a friend. For that reason, I must tell you this, though it may sound like a child spinning tales. <continue>When I turn toward your stealthy companion, I see a glimmer of fearful light in my perpetual darkness. When I gaze unseeing toward the swamps you intend to brave, I see the opposite on the horizon. A darker night than blindness itself. <continue>The backside of a sunset, over a temple drenched in blood. I do not know what this vision means, but I fear for you. Be wary.

ShambrinA2EndOfActNonSorc.text: You came here a <i>{jingakh,} but will leave as a friend. For that reason, I must tell you this, though it may sound like a child spinning tales. <continue>When I turn toward your stealthy companion, I see a glimmer of fearful light in my perpetual darkness. When I gaze unseeing toward the swamps you intend to brave, I see the opposite on the horizon. A darker night than blindness itself. <continue>The backside of a sunset, over a temple drenched in blood. I do not know what this vision means, but I fear for you. Be wary.

ShambrinA2OnJamanraRisen.text: Jamanra has risen... It is... almost unthinkable. To resort to necromancy and Corruption... The Faridun's desperation knows no limits. In a way, it is rather sad. In another, it is harrowing. Either way, this King of theirs must return to his death.

ShambrinA2OnSandstormCleared.text: Now the sandstorm is cleared, we have a chance to chase down Jamanra. Though I am not gifted with sight, I clearly see the dangers ahead of us. You must keep your wits about you.

ShambrinA2OnJamanraKilledSorc.text: The risen <i>{King} is dead once again. Another tale of the harsh desert. This time, his death was honourable. Asala did this intentionally and I admire her for it. <continue>The Faridun have already begun the process of taking his body to Deshar for a proper sky burial. Asala allowed this... You understand the significance here. Perhaps... We could be stepping into the light of a new era for our people.

ShambrinA2OnJamanraKilled.text: The risen <i>{King} is dead once again. His tale is yet another tragic outcome of the harsh desert. At least this time, the death was honourable. Asala did this intentionally and I admire her for it. <continue>The Faridun have already begun the process of taking his body to Deshar for a proper sky burial. Asala allowed this. It feels like... We could be stepping into the light of a new era for the Maraketh.

ShambrinA2OnAsalaSpeech.text: With that speech, she has woven a hopeful tapestry for our future. Our <i>{Sekhema} leaves nothing to chance. By beheading Jamanra, she has both dealt a deadly strike and begun the process of healing an old wound. <continue>Perhaps it is enough to begin a conversation with the Faridun. Perhaps... there is a way forward for all.

FaridunKing_SpiresSummonEnd.text: The time of the Faridun is nigh!

FaridunKing_SpiresSummonStart.text: You are relentless... But that makes you predictable.

UnaNewTreeOfSoulsQuestStartSon.text: You must have heard the rumours in the village. All this began the night Count Geonor took his most loyal men into the Grelwood. That's when his growing madness began. <continue><i>{Something} happened out there... Please, I beg of you, travel to the forest and begin your search. There must be some clue as to what took place. <continue>I fear that our land's sickness will only deepen unless something is done.

UnaNewTreeOfSoulsQuestStart.text: All this began the night Count Geonor took his most loyal men into the Grelwood. After he returned, a madness grew in him. <continue><i>{Something} happened out there... Please, I beg of you, travel into the forest and begin your search. There must be some clue as to what took place. <continue>I fear this land's sickness will only deepen unless we do something.

UnaNewTreeQuestGive.text: This shade... Is it... still alive? Perhaps it can give us the answers we seek. Only the Count's sword has the power to bind souls to the Tree like this. We must free it somehow. <continue>To release that being from the Tree of Souls we'll need more than simply cutting his rope... The ancient runes that imbue the count's blade created the binding, and only ancient runes can break it.

UnaNewOnCountsSword.text: The greatsword Agnar is <i>{currently} in Count Geonor's possession... but the mighty runed blade was not always his to wield. <continue>It is an ancient weapon of the old magicks, inspired by the Greatwolf himself. Legend says it was forged and runed for the original clan leader so he might lead his people to a new, safer land. This brought them to Phaaryl where they founded Ogham. Ever since, Agnar was passed down to the leader of the strongest clan. <continue>When the position of Count was established in Ogham, the sword was bound to the role. But now... Geonor sullies its remarkable history with his misdeeds. I hope I will live to see the day when someone worthy takes up the sword once more.

UnaNewRedValeUnexplored.text: There is a battlefield not far from here that runs red with rust, where the weapons and armour of countless Ezomytes still remain... We call it the Red Vale. You should search the area. There may still be power in some of those centuries old relics. <continue>Renly will know how to forge them. Bring the runes to him, and then, perhaps, we shall find some answers.

UnaNewRedValeExploredPartial.text: I see you've already found the vale, and some of the runes we need. But I don't think they will be enough. Return to the vale and search for more. Renly will know how to forge them.

UnaNewRedValeExploredFull.text: I see you've already found relics with the runes we need. What luck! The First Ones are truly watching over us. <continue>Renly will know how to forge them. Bring what you've gathered to him, and then, perhaps, we shall find some answers.

UnaNewTreeGossip.text: My mother's mother told me tales of this Tree. Our ancestors used it to attract fey spirits, until it was given a darker purpose under the Eternals. <continue>They would leave Ezomytes strung up on the tree... alive... to starve... to be pecked at by birds...

UnaNewAfterSpikesInTown.text: Renly's done a fine job forging those spikes. Meet me at the Tree of Souls.

UnaNewUnconciousComment.text: He's unconscious, but he's breathing. Though... this wound... We should take him back to Clearfell. He may be the only one who knows what truly happened out here.

UnaNewTreeOfSoulsEnd.text: The wound... It should be fatal, but somehow he clings to life... I fear it will not be long until his song ends. He will never heal while the count's binding still holds sway. <continue>Only by a Count's hand can this binding be released. I know an old tale. One that speaks of a ring we might be able to recover, buried three centuries ago in our ancient graveyard...  A count's signet ring, bearing his rune of Authority. But how to reach it in time... <continue>The Grim Tangle! The overgrown sinkholes and gullies that run beneath Ogham can lead you there. The path is dangerous but... go back to the Grelwood. Find the entrance. We shall see if the spirits of this land still have the will to see you through.

UnaNewEntranceToGrimTangle.text: If the fey spirits are still watching, I believe they will help us. Please, wait a moment.

UnaNewAfterSinging.text: The old magicks still thrive! The way is open. Please, hurry.

UnaNewSignetRingResponse.text: You found the ring! This will most certainly break the Count's binding. Give me a moment...

UnaNewCutIn_One.text: This...'Seed'... is that the source of Ogham's affliction?

UnaNewCutIn_Two.text: So if we are to heal this land, we must find this 'Seed'. Beyond our clan graves is the Hunting Grounds. Cut through those to reach the village. Please, go as quickly as you can and see what you can find. I fear there is not much time!

UnaNewGrimTangleGossip.text: My mother and I would come here to gather mushrooms when I was young. Ervig the Druid, one of the Grelwood's resident mystics, would meet us and allow us entry. He was well versed in the tongue of the old magicks. <continue>But now... Well times have certainly changed. Please, don't eat any of the mushrooms. We need you alive!

UnaNewOnSpiritsOfGrelwood.text: It fills my heart to see the spirits of the forest answer my call like that. It just goes to show... there are still energies in this world that mean to aid us.

UnaNewOnErvigSeen.text: You saw the Druid? Ervig? Oh no... It saddens me to hear he is lost to the sickness as well. It is up to you what you will do about him...

UnaNewOnErvigKilled.text: I understand you did what you had to. Please... let us not speak of it further.

HoodedOneNewCountWarning.text: How long has it been? I was hunted... The Count... He stole something that is beyond dangerous... It will cause sickness... Then madness... <continue>It can still be contained... We must put the Seed back...

HoodedOneNewUnaResponse.text: Yes... please... find it... I am still too weak.... this will only grow worse...

HoodedOneNewReleaseThanks.text: I must... thank you... for releasing me. I am... indebted to you... but you must find the Seed. I will aid you in any way that I can. I am still weak, but I have some knowledge that may be of use. <continue>Bring me any magical objects you find. I can identify them for you.

HoodedOneNewOnTheSeed.text: The Count accosted me and stole a very dangerous object—a Seed that I have kept hidden from humanity. Somehow, he knew that I possessed it. He cannot possibly know how dangerous it is. His attempts to harness its power will court disaster. <continue>You must hurry to the Village. At the very least, those who are still sane may be convinced to aid in containing the Seed.

HoodedOneNewTravelEast.text: The trail of Corruption leads east, so east we shall go. It seems fate conspires to return me to the Plains of Vastiri...

HoodedOneNewSeedGossip.text: The boundless horrors of mishandled Corruption cannot be conveyed simply through words. I only hope that you can find and contain the Seed before it is too late.

HoodedOneHuntedGossip.text: Twenty years ago, in the wake of those tremendous events, mankind was busy with its own survival. No one was looking for me, and no one saw me. I lurked in high places, and dark places, seeking to keep the Seed safe from men of ambition. <continue>In recent years, however, I found myself continually forced to move from place to place. There was always one more hunter, one more patrol, one more grove being cut down or cave being mined. <continue>There was nowhere to hide, and my path inexorably took me here... which was, apparently, exactly where someone wanted me to be. <continue>This was all a trap, laid over the course of years, and at colossal expense. Someone wanted the Seed at any cost, which surely bodes ill for their intentions...

DoryaniPastPostFight.text: Stop! Stop... I can contain the Beast...!

DoryaniPastDefeatedOne.text: If only I had more time... <continue>There is an ancient weapon. A weapon that was used against Corruption, from a civilization lost to the ages. I have one piece of it. Three others were scattered... I have been searching for them, but the Karui have interfered at every turn.

DoryaniPastDefeatedTwo.text: I suppose I must... It is too late for us here. This era is over. I pleaded with Atziri for her patience... but she would not abide me. She will attempt her communion with the Beast, and utter devastation will ravage our people. <continue>But... the fact that <i>{you} are here... a living descendant of our people... it gives me some hope for our future. <continue>I will come to your era. Perhaps there is still time.

DoryaniPresentUtzaalReaction.text: Utzaal... my people... they're all long dead. It is one thing to hear it, but... another to see it. This city is nothing but a grave. <continue>I can't change their fate, but the Vaal are not entirely gone. Alva—and her Vaal ancestry—is proof of that. I will do what I must to protect what remains, and perhaps one day we can rebuild. <continue>For that to happen, we need the Weapon. We must travel to the archipelago the Karui call Ngamakanui. If the pieces still exist, that is where they will be found.

DoryaniPresentOnUtzaal.text: I gathered the greatest minds of our era in one place. We embarked on journeys of discovery that mankind could never before conceive. No ethical bounds. No moral limits! <continue>We sought immortality, both in flesh, and in machinery. We sought understanding of Corruption. We even sought to master Time itself. In the end, it was all for naught...

DoryaniPresentOnBeast.text: Study of the Beast was my life's work, and the work of many Vaal scientists before me. Despite its danger, I still consider it a thing of beauty. A work of genius. It is capable of changing something fundamental about the nature of our existence. <continue>The Beast showed us it <i>{can be done.} Our experiments with life... with death... with machinery, and augmentation... they were all inspired by it. We <i>{can} surpass the impossible, if only we are willing to sacrifice enough.

DoryaniCataclysmFirstTalk.text: Now then—it is time we departed. Activate the portal, and we will see about the-

DoryaniGodVoiceStopIntruderMale.text: The intruder is <i>{here?} What of Napuatzi...? I see. No mercy then! Kill him on sight!

DoryaniGodVoiceStopIntruderFemale.text: The intruder is <i>{here?} What of Napuatzi...? I see. No mercy then! Kill her on sight!

DoryaniGodVoiceCeaseAssault.text: Fool! There's no time for this! Atziri will soon commune with the Beast! Cease your assault!

DoryaniGodVoiceStopAtOnce.text: Stop this at once! I take no pleasure in harming one of my own, but if you persist, I will do with her what I must.

DoryaniEndgameOnZiggurat.text: You're finally awake. That's a small consolation. We have lost so much. <continue>The Hooded One used the Weapon to keep us alive during the Cataclysm. <continue>We were too close. It absorbed too much energy, and was shattered. <continue>I retain only a piece of it. <continue>The situation is grim... the Hooded One has become comatose. <continue>Wraeclast has been devastated... and is no longer habitable. <continue>Grieving would only be a waste of precious time. We must face reality, and make difficult choices.

DoryaniEndgameOnWhatNow.text: We <i>{are} living the worst possible outcome, but I did anticipate <i>{every} contingency... <continue>Before us is a translocation device, which <i>{should} allow us to open portals to a wide range of coordinates across Wraeclast. <continue>With this, we can reclaim the world from the grasp of Corruption, so that civilisation can one day return to its former heights.

DoryaniEndgameOnOurWork.text: There was some damage but while you were unconscious, we worked to repair the machine. I believe it will function as desired... But it must be tested. That is where you come in. <continue>By placing Waystones in the machine, they will help calibrate the journey. The Corruption at the destination will respond to both the energies we use, and that we ourselves expect to find. <continue>Let us use this malleability to our advantage... Let us see if the machine is still capable.

DoryaniEndgameSeekCorruptedBiome.text: Wraeclast is wounded and broken. We must reshape its future, and heal it anew. <continue>The initial Cataclysmic event is over, but Corruption is still radiating from certain locations. <continue>From these points, it spreads like a disease. <continue>Travel to one of these regions and investigate. We must know why it is still spreading. <continue>Report back to me with your findings, and we will plan our next move.

DoryaniEndgameFindSourceOfCorruption.text: So, these densely Corrupted regions contain an active source. Despite the risks, you must venture within. <continue>Find the source of Corruption. <continue>When you have identified it and dealt with any danger, call for me. I will cleanse what remains.

DoryaniEndgameSeeTower.text: This is the first Precursor tower we've seen. You should take control of it, so that we may research its properties. <continue>There may be considerable foes in proximity... these towers channel forces we do not yet understand. <continue>If you see any sort of 'central tower' or nexus to the network, be sure to let me know...

DoryaniEndgameSeeMonolith.text: There is a tremendous amount of energy radiating from that new structure. If it was Corruption, I would understand, but it's like nothing I have ever seen before. <continue>My intuition tells me that you must absolutely be the first to reach it. <continue>If it should fall into the hands of the Corrupted, there is no telling what may happen.

DoryaniEndgameFirstMapComplete.text: The device still functions, despite the damage the Cataclysm caused. Good. <continue>Now, using the device, you must seek out major sources of Corruption for us to cleanse.

DoryaniEndgameFirstMapFail.text: The device still functions, despite the damage the Cataclysm caused, but that is little solace if you are not up to the task. <continue>Gather your wits. There are far greater dangers to come. <continue>Using the device, you must seek out major sources of Corruption for us to cleanse.

DoryaniEndgameFirstCorruptMapComplete.text: You have done well. That area has been cleansed, and the land may now return to its original state. By all means, continue.

DoryaniEndgameFirstCorruptMapFail.text: You do know the fate of humanity rests upon your shoulders? Make whatever adjustments you require for success. Get back out there. Do better.

DoryaniEndgameAssignFirstAtlasPassive.text: Using the cleansed Corruption you retrieved, I was able to modify the device to accommodate your request. You should find things somewhat different next time you venture out.

DoryaniEndgameFirstTimeHideout.text: I believe it unwise to base our operations outside of the Ziggurat. This seems like an unnecessary risk to take. <continue>And Atalui is constantly complaining about the lack of facilities. However, I will make this concession, since you have done such critical work.

DoryaniEndgameTowerQuestStart.text: Ah, a Tower has been secured? Timely. <continue>It seems they can provide us with an advantage of learning more about the surrounding area. It would be wise to use them to plan our next course of action.

DoryaniEndgameTowerTabletUse.text: The tower... the surrounding landscape has indeed been altered. This could be of great use to us. <continue>These towers are part of some long ago experiment on a grand scale... I will do more research while you continue to explore.

DoryaniEndgameSanctifyQuestStart.text: [DNT] Get out there and kill some Corruption Nexus bosses and a Sanctified Boss!

DoryaniEndgameFirstFaction.text: The source of Corruption was a creature? I wish I could perform a detailed autopsy of its corpse, but its passive emanations alone would quickly kill us. <continue>It looks to be significantly more mutated than other beings we've encountered. I don't like having insufficient data on new threats... we are vulnerable until we know more.

DoryaniEndgameSecondFaction.text: This creature is far different from the type you defeated before. It looks to be the center of a hive mind. <continue>A legion of mutated creatures, without brains, acting as one. <continue>I never even considered such a thing possible, or we would have experimented with it at Aggorat... <continue>In any case, I will continue my dissections... There is something very disturbing about the arc of these mutations...

DoryaniEndgameThirdFaction.text: A third stratum of creatures, different yet again... <continue>I am starting to see a pattern here, one that bodes ill for us, but I cannot quite discern the meaning yet. <continue>Worse, these creatures appear to have been sentient. The mindless ravagers we first encountered could be outsmarted, and the hive-mind had an obvious weak point. <continue>But these ones can actually think. We are in grave danger...

DoryaniEndgameFinishCorruptionQuest.text: The current situation is finally stable. We have done enough to ensure humanity's survival, however meager our dignity may be. <continue>We should continue cleansing Corruption, however. <continue> It is true that we have ensured the future. Now, we should begin <i>{improving} it.

DoryaniEndgameOnCleansedAreas.text: Cleansed regions of Wraeclast are still dangerous, but only in the ways with which we are familiar. The demon you know, as they say. <continue>These regions should also contain substantial amounts of neutralised Corruption, which may manifest as orbs or crystals of anomalous material. <continue>Collect them if you see them. They may prove useful.

DoryaniEndgameOnCrystallinePower.text: Corruption, at a fundamental level, is a form of energy. <continue>Much of Vaal technology was based on using that energy, because it is freely available in the environment... <continue>My piece of the Weapon cannot destroy that energy, only render it inert, in the form of crystalline precipitate. <continue>In that form, it cannot hurt us, and might even be put to new uses.

DoryaniEndgameOnWeaponPiece.text: On its own, my piece of the Precursor Weapon can only neutralise <i>{passive} Corruption. <continue>That is why you must destroy the <i>{active} source in each deadly region first. <continue>This will be a long and grueling task, one that may take the rest of our lives... however long that may be.

DoryaniEndgameOnBosses.text: There is something... a secret horror that hides in the broken puzzle pieces we possess... a pattern that even my intellect cannot quite grasp. <continue>Not with such limited information. <continue>It may surprise you to discover that a man like me can feel fear. I admit it. Fear is healthy. I feel fear when I know I am in danger, but do not have enough information. <continue>It is impossible to act with precision unless we know, so I have always sought the truth...but in this instance, for the first time in my life, I fear <i>{knowing,} too... and I don't yet know why...

DoryaniEndgameOnDream.text: Yes, that strange voice torments me in my sleep... so I more or less avoid sleeping. <continue>Thankfully, the light of our Inner Sun can remove the need for sleep, if you're willing to gaze directly into it for a time... <continue>Just don't do that for longer than a few days. It's not a perfect substitute.

DoryaniEG_SecondTowerP2.text: Find your way over there as soon as you can.

DoryaniMapOnRealmgate.text: The Realmgate was the sister project to the Timegate that brought you to us. The Realmgate can, theoretically, give us access to other planes of existence. Unfortunately, it has never been activated, if it works at all. <continue>We need sizeable energies or materials from those planes to help us locate them in the vast expanse of all that is. <continue>If you find otherworldly splinters and fragments, keep them. With enough of them, we can find out if the Realmgate truly works.

DoryaniMapOnHideout.text: You have located a... <i>{relatively safe} hideaway. <continue>We could establish a base of operations there, if you feel it necessary. <continue>We will always have the Ziggurat to fall back on, so the risk is not existential.

DoryaniMapOnReliquary.text: The disciples of Kamasa stockpiled a great many things in their modern lust for wealth. The right key may open doors long forgotten...

DoryaniMapOnZiggurat.text: The Ziggurat is the heart of our operations, the only truly safe place on Wraeclast. From here, we can reclaim the world for humanity.

DoryaniMapOnReactors.text: [DNT] The Waygate was never meant to stand alone. Its design was born of Precursor genius, and through their grid, it can be made to draw far more power than it ever should. Four Reactors still anchor that network; to the North, East, South, and West. Rekindle each one and the grid will answer. When the circuit is whole, return to me, and we shall bend the Waygate to purposes the Precursors themselves feared.

DoryaniEndgameOnTheFortress.text: There is a tremendous amount of energy radiating from that new structure. If it was Corruption, I would understand, but it is like nothing I have ever seen before. <continue>My intuition tells me that you must absolutely be the first to reach it. If it should fall into the hands of the Corrupted, there is no telling what may happen.

DoryaniEndgameOnFlameSeed.text: From what you've told me, the guardian of the Flame Seed seems to have been purposely molded for his task. The Precursors created him, but he is not one of them. I can only theorise as to his purpose...

DoryaniEndgameOnDefeatFlameSeedGuardian.text: I understand that... something... stole the Flame Seed as your battle drew to a close. This is concerning. There is little we can do until we know more.

DoryaniEndgameTier1Task.text: You must start with the areas of least Corruption. They are still deadly, but should be survivable for short spans. Cleanse enough of them to give us an outside foothold.

DoryaniEndgameGiveTasksOne.text: Keep up your work. It is a long and dangerous task, but there is an end in sight.

DoryaniEndgameGiveTasksTwo.text: Continue clearing Corruption. It is the only thing we can do right now.

DoryaniEndgameGiveTasksThree.text: Why are you wasting time here? Continue clearing Corruption!

DoryaniEndgameGiveTasksFour.text: You don't look sick or injured. Why are you lingering here? Continue your work.

DoryaniEndgameReceiveRewardOne.text: The space you cleared allowed us to reclaim several important tools. We can now upgrade our machine.

DoryaniEndgameReceiveRewardTwo.text: We found a handful of survivors in the area you cleared. We'll put them to work.

DoryaniEndgameReceiveRewardThree.text: A renowned scientist was... recovered... from the area you cleared. His acumen will add to our own.

DoryaniEndgameReceiveRewardFour.text: Valuable resources were located in the area you cleared. We can augment our capabilities.

DoryaniEndgameReceiveRewardFive.text: I have had time to increase the capabilities of the machine. We have a few choices to make.

DoryaniEndgameReceiveRewardSix.text: With each success, we grow closer to our goal.

DoryaniEndgameTier15TaskComplete.text: The current situation is finally stable. We have done enough to ensure humanity's survival, however meager their dignity may be. <continue>This is not a victory, but it is a success. You may continue to cleanse Corruption as you wish. I will begin work on greater plans...

DoryaniEndgameFirstMapCompleted.text: The device still functions, despite the damage the Cataclysm caused. Good. <continue>Now, using the device, you must seek out major sources of Corruption for us to cleanse.

DoryaniEndgameDefeatBreachBoss.text: I had a suspicion that the Cult of the Purple Flame was dangerous. They did not know the true nature of the forces they beseeched. <continue>I'm not certain anyone will ever know the breadth of what lies beyond this world... but Chayula alone kept his word, in what little dealings were had. <continue>Perhaps one day, we will find out what happened to create this... Xesht.

DoryaniEndgamePrecursorGossip.text: I have invested considerable resources and many years of effort in the search, but my knowledge of the Precursors still remains scarce. They are as ancient to us as we are to you. On such time scales, geological events tend to obscure remnants of civilisation. There is evidence of great fires. Eruptions. Impacts from the sky. <continue>All I know is that they, too, delved into the secrets of this world. Corruption was just one of many forms of energy that they mastered. I have come across simple pictographs in their ruins, intended as a contingency, should others come without knowledge of their language. Most pictographs were quite clear: <i>{'Death lies within.'} <continue>One, however, held faded instructions for what we should do if that death should ever escape; if it should ever plague the land. That is how I know the Weapon exists, and... generally... how to find it. Someone in the past wanted us to know about it, in case the worst should ever happen... and clearly, it has...

DoryaniEndgameUberBossGossip.text: Out in the Corrupted wastelands, you will no doubt encounter 'survivors.' Do not fall victim to the trap of empathy. Though their bodies do not yet know it, they are <i>{dead.} They sicken and taint everything they touch. They would slowly kill us by their very presence. They have no future. It would have been a mercy for them to die in the initial devastation. <continue>They will slowly waste away, and in their wasting, they will become disoriented... and then, enraged. They will seek to survive as long as possible, even if that means they doom the rest of us. They will be drawn to resources, and to power. <i>{You} cannot allow them to possess that which we need. If you see them, kill them, and do not hesitate for even a moment.

DoryaniEndgameUberBossGossipTwo.text: In the wake of the Cataclysm, reality is not what it used to be. There are far fewer of us now, and the mad outnumber the sane. You will see things out there that you will not understand. <continue>As much as I despise this truth as a man of science, it is quite possible they cannot <i>{be} understood. Carry on with what must be done, and eventually, Wraeclast will... calm.

DoryaniEndgameUberBossTask.text: As I predicted, the Corrupted 'survivors' out in the wastelands have banded together like primal animals. They refuse to accept their own doom. <continue>You must become proactive in your approach. Their warlords are perverse figments of reality that the Cataclysm has distorted. Find these tainted realities and cut the head off the snake, so to speak.

DoryaniEndgameOnUberDoryani.text: I should warn you... in my search for ways to stop the Cataclysm, I entreated the ultimate wisdom in this world, and I paid a terrible price. <continue>That price is out there, still—and he is even more cunning and dangerous than I am, for he does not have my purity of purpose. When you meet him, destroy him utterly, and do not trouble yourself with your usual moral quandaries.

DoryaniEndgameOnPrecursorTowers.text: The sheer force of the Cataclysm scoured away much of the surface, and disrupted what remained. Sturdier than most, ancient Precursor towers have been left exposed. You should find one, and secure it for our research.

DoryaniEndgameOnPrecursorTowersGossip.text: I believe that the Precursor towers are part of a network created specifically to alter terrain and biomes. This may have been to make Wraeclast more habitable initially... or perhaps it had a larger purpose, later in their era. <continue>These ideas are just conjecture, of course.

DoryaniEndgameOnSecuringTower.text: Ah, a Tower has been secured? Timely. <continue>It seems they can provide us with an advantage of learning more about the surrounding area. It would be wise to use them to plan our next course of action.

DoryaniEndgameOnActivatingFirstTower.text: The tower... the surrounding landscape has been altered! This could be of great use to us. These towers are part of some long ago experiment, perhaps... or a contingency... I will do more research while you continue to explore.

DoryaniEndgameOnEndgameMapCorruption.text: In a time of minimal sentience—and most of it mad—what you encounter out there can be quite malleable. What we expect to find can shape things. The energies we use in our translocation device can influence outcomes. <continue>That device was made possible, after all, by a very special patron. They are likely watching us even now, and finding great humour in our travails...

DoryaniEndgameOnTabletFound.text: Hmm... this tablet you have found, I believe it is capable of altering energies in the area at the waystone's destination. <continue>Place a waystone along with a tablet into the machine. Activate it and travel there... let us see what comes of it.

DoryaniEndgameOnPatron.text: I was told many cryptic things. I was asked to—no, I shouldn't say. I don't understand, at least not yet. <continue>I was told this was the only way, yet still, I fought to find another path. I believe we make our own fates, but... here we are. If only I had the full picture...

DoryaniEndgameClassQuestComplete.text: [DNT] You've done it. You killed and sanctified that boss, but there are still others that remain. Track them down and defeat them as well, then return to me.

DoryaniEndgameClassQuestCompleteFinal.text: [DNT] You've done it. They're all dead and sanctified. Great job exile.

DoryaniBossConversationFive.text: Perhaps... I just need a moment to think... To make a new plan... There must be a way...

DoryaniBossConversationSix.text: The intruder! Where is Napuatzi?! Ah... then I'll have to handle you myself.

AlvaOnDelirium.text: Ever since you encountered that strange mirror, this place is darker now, in a way I can't describe... Somebody's here. Someone that isn't us. <continue>I keep thinking I hear laughter, mocking us... but I look around, and I don't see anything. <continue>You just... keep your guard up, alright?

AlvaOnCollectingDeliSplinter.text: You found a splinter of strange material beyond one of those creepy mirrors? Let me see... This marking... we've come across it in our excavations. <continue>In context, it was treated as something quite negative, something Karui myths referred to as 'sealed away,' or 'imprisoned.' You should try to gather more of these splinters.  <continue>With enough of them, perhaps we can decipher the story of these markings. As a treasure hunter, I know: the past holds all the answers, if you're willing to look hard enough.

AlvaOnFindDistilledEmotion.text: Hmm... we once excavated a ruin where the engraved pictures seemed to tell a story. It appeared as if they were teaching their children new knowledge by imbuing <i>{emotions} in a piece of jewellery. <continue>It was a very <i>{old} ruin and we couldn't identify it, but... maybe the distilled energy you found is a remnant of that lost culture. <continue>If you find a few more, you might be able to instil knowledge in something yourself...

AlvaOnFirstSimulacrumHeld.text: Now we know where we might find our unwelcome guest. Let's hit the trickster where he lives, in his so-called 'Simulacrum.' <continue>It might still be a trap, but... it's the only way. He will never leave us alone until we face him.

AlvaOnFirstSimulacrumFailed.text: How was the 'Simulacrum?' <continue>Oh. That sounds bloody awful! I suppose he was simply toying with you. A shame you didn't beat him at his own game.

AlvaOnSimulacrumComplete.text: You beat that shadowy entity at his own game! Maybe now he'll stop frequenting our minds and tormenting us with all those whispers and shadows... <continue>That <i>{was} him, right?

AlvaOnUnidentifiedRuins.text: The ruins we couldn't identify... they weren't from any other culture I've seen. Not Vaal, not Primeval, not 'Precursor.'  <continue>Do you think your 'Strange Voice' might be from that long lost people? He'd have to be very old... If you ever get the chance to ask him in person, I'd be curious to see what he says.

AlvaDreamSequenceOne.text: As I've studied these grey splinters you found, I've come to believe that they have a kind of... knowledge imbued in them. <continue>It's fragmented, of course. Not enough to glean a conscious thought. But I keep having dreams... Nothing coherent yet... but I'll let you know...

AlvaDreamSequenceTwo.text: I had a more coherent dream after working with a larger number of splinters... I saw a feast. A peaceful, tranquil place. I felt... smiles. I felt calm. <continue>I didn't get the impression that this was part of a vast empire, or a grand civilisation, or anything like that. Just a rare haven from the world's ills. <continue>I really wish I could have written it down... but it's gone. I can't hold on to the sensations...

AlvaDreamSequenceThree.text: I had another dream... more like a nightmare. There was so much anger, so much hate. They were all dead. <continue>The haven... bloodied. Bodies everywhere, mutilated, all because of a harmless little lie I told, the kind any child might. They made me watch. <continue>I was alone. Traumatized. I vowed to make them suffer. I vowed to darken the places they felt safest. To turn their very homes into prisons of paranoia and fear. I did it, too. <continue>Countless faces twisted in agony and misery. I kept hurting them, but it never made me feel better... it just made the void bigger. When I woke up, I felt... empty.  <continue>What... What do you think it means?

AlvaDreamSequenceFour.text: Once you put all those splinters together, I believe I had the final dream. I think I felt... Divinity, as crazy as that sounds. <continue>In the dream, I was hollow. Completely empty. I was a liar. A torturer. A deceiver. I'd perfected the art of shaping reality with words, purely to enact misery. <continue>I was so good at deception, I lied to myself, told myself that I was a god... I was so convincing, even I believed it. And you know what? It became true... <continue>But I knew that if I ever stopped being alone, if I ever let go of my agony, if I ever let myself care... it would all unravel... and I woke up feeling hopeless. <continue>Divinity isn't wonderful. It's isolating. <continue>I think I'm done with those splinters. I don't want to know anymore. The completed object... it's a fruit. <continue>A stone carving of a fruit we used to gather from the shore. Sweet and juicy, like summer, now lost forever... Sorry, what <i>{they} used to gather...

AlvaEndgameOnWakeUp.text: You're awake! Oh, I thought you might not make it... <continue>There's a lot to go over... When you've pulled yourself together, speak with Doryani.

AlvaEndgameOnDoryani.text: It's a good thing we resolved our differences when we did. Without Doryani, we'd have died out there. I saw... the sky... the people... they were... well... <continue>Let's just say, I now understand why Vaal ruins look the way they do.

AlvaEndgameOnCurrentTask.text: If it helps, history does tell of a slow recovery after the Cataclysm. It's likely the future we knew was only possible because of the work we're doing here. <continue>Every bit of Corruption you cleanse helps build Wraeclast as we experienced it. And if you don't, well... perhaps you and I might never exist. Crazy to think about, isn't it?

AlvaEndgameOnPillarOfFlame.text: I've heard about that massive pillar of flame you've spotted. Try to get to it as quickly as you can. I imagine anyone else that's seen it will be trying to get there before us. <continue>I'll do some research, and see if I can figure out what it is...

AlvaEndgameOnPinnacleRoomOne.text: I initially believed that there was nothing in the historical record about that strange fortress you found, but then it occurred to me... a great deal has been written about times of ash. Fires that scorched the land, clouds that blotted out the sun, the Winter of the World... <continue>If that place is somehow connected, then we may be dealing with an ancient disastrous force that has plagued Wraeclast for far longer than anyone can guess. It may have ended entire civilisations. <continue>You really must get in there first. Everything may depend upon it.

TrialmasterG3_FirstIntro.text: Long have I awaited a suitable challenger. My master, Chaos, has charged me with this task. <continue>Many have attempted my trials in search of greatness.  Scholars, criminals, heroes, and the meek. All have stepped forward, and most have fallen.  <continue>The rules never changed for them, and the rules will not change for you.  Bring only that which you can afford to lose - including your life.

TrialmasterG3_OnThisPlace.text: This once-mighty temple was the bridge from mere peasant to high priest. All were welcome to attempt the Trials of Chaos, and those that attained a true victory were gifted a small measure of power to help forge their own destinies. <continue>That is still true, though we have far fewer challengers in this era.

TrialmasterG3_OnChaos.text: My master is the essence of all that might be. They are the flip of the coin, and they are the roll of the die. Whether you win or lose, their purpose is still served.  <continue>And yet—your chances can be influenced by your skill, by your intellect, and by your might. That is what fascinates Chaos. Skilled mortals can bend their chances, for in the headwinds of the unknown, the arrow of a master falls more assuredly than the arrow of a novice.  <continue>Show them your mastery, and they will smile upon you. Surprise them with utmost talent, and they may even laugh. Fortune will rain upon those who bring humour to Chaos.

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_Random.text: What a life, ey? Out at sea... ahh. Beautiful.

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_2.text: What a life, ey? Out at sea... ahh. Beautiful.

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_3.text: What a life, ey? Out at sea... ahh. Beautiful.

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_5.text: It's the sailors life for me!

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_6.text: Ahh, it's the sailors life for me!

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_7.text: It's the sailors life for me!

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_8.text: Ahh... I love the smell of salt on the air.

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_9.text: Ahh... I love the smell of salt on the air.

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_10.text: There are worse places to be exiled to, I reckon!

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_11.text: There are worse places to be exiled to, I reckon!

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_12.text: There are worse places to be exiled to, I reckon!

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_13.text: You don't get seasick, do ya?

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_14.text: You don't get seasick, do ya?

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_15.text: Just gimme a nudge if I get suckered in by the ol' siren song.

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_16.text: Just gimme a nudge if I get suckered in by the ol' siren song.

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_17.text: You hungry? The smell of the sea makes me peckish. And I'm always at sea.

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_18.text: You hungry? The smell of the sea makes me peckish.

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_19.text: Hear that? Me neither! Won't get silence like that on land.

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_20.text: Hear that? Me neither! Won't get silence like that on land.

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_21.text: Me old lady don't like the ocean! Breaks me heart, to tell you the truth.

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_22.text: Me old lady don't like the ocean! Breaks me heart, to tell you the truth.

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_23.text: You smell that? No? Eh, good.

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_24.text: You're not much of a talking type, are ya.

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_25.text: You're not much of a talking type, are ya.

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_26.text: You're not much of a talking type, are ya.

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_27.text: Hope you can swim! No reason. Just in case.

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_28.text: Egh! Sorry 'bout that. Dozed off for a second there.

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_29.text: Egh! Sorry 'bout that. Dozed off for a second there.

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_30.text: I ever tell you about the time I saw a Golden Rhoa?

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_31.text: I ever tell you about the time I saw a Golden Rhoa?

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_32.text: I ever tell you about the time I saw a Golden Rhoa?

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_37.text: Do do doo, do do do... Just sittin' in a boat, with someone else...

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_38.text: Bit awkward you just starin' at me like that.

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_39.text: Bit awkward you just starin' at me like that.

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_LowChance_3.text: How about a spot of fishin'?

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_LowChance_4.text: How about a spot of fishin'?

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_LowChance_5.text: How about a spot of fishin'?

FirstMateMTX_Chatter_LowChance_9.text: Well, ho ho ho and rattle my toe, a Rhoa bit me on my nose. So here and there, everywhere that I go, I seem to be the butt of the joke! People laugh and people point, cause me nostril looks well out of joint! So to hell with the land, to hell with the beasts, I'd rather be sleepin' out at sea!

FirstMateMTX_Goodbye_26.text: And don't come back! Heh, just kiddin'. You're welcome any time.

FirstMateMTX_Goodbye_27.text: And don't come back! Just kiddin'. You're welcome any time.

FirstMateMTX_Goodbye_28.text: And don't come back! Just kiddin'. Please come back.

FirstMateMTX_Greeting_Random.text: Keep your arms, legs, hooks and pegs inside the vessel at all times!

FirstMateMTX_Greeting_2.text: Keep your arms, legs, hooks and pegs inside the vessel at all times!

FirstMateMTX_Greeting_3.text: Got your sea legs? Then off we go!

FirstMateMTX_Greeting_4.text: Got your sea legs? Then off we go!

FirstMateMTX_Greeting_5.text: Got your sea legs? Then off we go!

FirstMateMTX_Greeting_6.text: Anchors aweigh! ... We don't actually have an anchor, but I still like to say it. Force of habit, see?

FirstMateMTX_Greeting_7.text: Anchors aweigh! ... We don't actually have an anchor, but I still like to say it. Force of habit, see?

FirstMateMTX_Greeting_10.text: Hop on in, and hold on tight!

FirstMateMTX_Greeting_11.text: Hop on in, and hold on tight!

FirstMateMTX_Impact_6.text: Agh! Now, where'd that rock come from?

FirstMateMTX_Impact_7.text: Ugh! Now where'd that rock come from?

FirstMateMTX_Impact_8.text: Ag, the sea's a fickle mistress, she is.

FirstMateMTX_Impact_9.text: Ugh, and I haven't even been drinkin'! Well, not much anyhow.

FirstMateMTX_Impact_10.text: Ugh, and I haven't even been drinkin'! Not much anyhow.

FirstMateMTX_Impact_12.text: Ugh, who put that there, then?

FirstMateMTX_Impact_14.text: What's a trip without a bit of danger, ey?

FirstMateMTX_Impact_15.text: What's a trip without a bit of danger, ey?

FirstMateMTX_Impact_16.text: Oops! You might wanna hold on a bit tighter.

FirstMateMTX_Impact_17.text: Oops! You might wanna hold on a bit tighter.

SamuelWildCallout.text: By the First Ones! You're alive!

SamuelOnInjury.text: I'm glad to see another living soul... <continue>The Miller went off to warn Clearfell 'bout a strange <i>{sickness}, plaguing our men. I was fixin' to go after him, until that <i>{bloody} thing got to me first. <continue>Now, all those who drowned in the floodin'... suddenly they ain't so dead no more.

SamuelWildAttacked.text: I would appreciate it if you could– argh!

TrialmasterBoss_DeathA_Random.text: Ugh... my service is finally over...

TrialmasterBoss_DeathA_2.text: Ugh... my service is finally over...

TrialmasterBoss_DeathA_3.text: Ugh... my service is finally over...

TrialmasterBoss_DeathA_4.text: Ugh... my service is finally over...

TrialmasterBoss_EmergeFirstTime.text: Well done, Challenger, but there is one more trial you must complete. Defeat me, and prove your worth to Chaos!

TrialmasterBoss_MeleeKnockdown_Random.text: Ugh... tah! You'll need more than that!

TrialmasterBoss_PlayerDeath_Random.text: Maybe next time, avoid that one.

TrialmasterBoss_PlayerDeath_4.text: Return when you have improved your skills.

TrialmasterBoss_PlayerDeath_9.text: Ooh... this must feel awfully embarrassing for you.

ZarokhBoss_Death_Random.text: Ugh... who are you to overthrow your fate?

ZarokhBoss_Death_2.text: Ugh, this is not the future I had forseen!

ZarokhBoss_Death_3.text: This cannot be... it is not my time...

ZarokhBoss_Death_Sorc.text: You would have made a worthy <i>{Sekhema}...

ZarokhBoss_Emerge_Random.text: I have seen how this ends, <i>{taljari}. Your time has come.

ZarokhBoss_Emerge_2.text: Come, <i>{taljari}. I shall enact your fate.

ZarokhBoss_Emerge_3.text: I have seen what has come, and what will be.

ZarokhBoss_Emerge_4.text: Your defeat has been predestined. It is written in the sands.

ZarokhBoss_Emerge_5.text: Rage against the shackles of fate if you so desire.

ZarokhBoss_Emerge_Chronomancer.text: Come, Chronomancer... Behold true mastery of time.

ZarokhBoss_Emerge_Sorceress.text: You will suffer the same fate as the 'great' Varashta.

ZarokhBoss_Emerge_ReturnAfterWin.text: You seek to turn back the hands of time? Such a feat is beyond your grasp.

ZarokhBoss_Emerge_ReturnAfterLoss.text: Your persistence is admirable... but your fate remains unchanged.

ZarokhBoss_TimeTrialFail_10.text: You are not the first to fail. Nor will you be the last.

ZarokhBoss_TimeTrialSpeedUp_4.text: Fate smiles upon you... for now.

ZarokhBoss_TimeTrialSpeedUp_5.text: Fate smiles upon you... for now.

ZarokhBoss_TimeTrialSpeedUp_6.text: Fate smiles upon you... for now.

ZarokhBoss_TimeTrialStart_Random.text: The sands of time wait for no one...

ZarokhBoss_TimeTrialStart_2.text: The sands of time wait for no one...

ZarokhBoss_TimeTrialStart_3.text: The sands of time wait for no one...

ZarokhBoss_TimeTrialSuccess_Random.text: You surprise me, <i>{taljari}. But you have yet to cast off the shackles of fate.

ZarokhBoss_TimeTrialSuccess_2.text: A small victory... but your war is not yet won.

ZarokhBoss_TimeTrialSuccess_3.text: You possess a modicum of skill...were it only enough...

ZarokhBoss_TimeTrialSuccess_4.text: You may have delayed your destiny... but you have not diverted it.

ZarokhBoss_Godvoice_Balbala_Random.text: Balbala thinks she can be forgiven, but can you ever truly forgive a traitor?

ZarokhBoss_Godvoice_Balbala_2.text: Passing the trial was the beginning... not the end... Your foolish Djinn should have known better.

ZarokhBoss_Godvoice_Chronomancer_Random.text: What do you truly know of Time, Chronomancer?

ZarokhBoss_Godvoice_Chronomancer_2.text: Time stops for no one... not even you.

ZarokhBoss_Godvoice_Chronomancer_3.text: You will run out of time eventually, Chronomancer...

ZarokhBoss_Godvoice_General_Random.text: For you, time is of the essence... But it is of no consequence to me.

ZarokhBoss_Godvoice_General_2.text: A traitor and a <i>{jingakh...} What a fitting pair...

ZarokhBoss_Godvoice_General_3.text: Time works against you. But I am its master.

ZarokhBoss_Godvoice_General_4.text: What do you pursue here? You will suffer the same fate as the Winter <i>{Sekhema}.

ZarokhBoss_Godvoice_General_5.text: Do you truly know what you pursue here? You will suffer the same fate as Varashta.

ZarokhBoss_Godvoice_Sorc_Random.text: A traitor and a banished tale-woman... fitting...

ZarokhBoss_Godvoice_Sorc_2.text: A traitor and an arrogant failure... fitting...

ZarokhBoss_Godvoice_Sorc_3.text: You forsake your people, only to come crawling back to the sands? Pathetic.

ZarokhBoss_Godvoice_VarashtaGossip_Rando.text:
So... You found her. Varashta... The Winter {Sekhema}. She and I share a unique... bond. A bond in time. A bond in pain. Together, we could have ruled the Vastiri. Perhaps, we could have ruled all of Wraeclast. The dutybound Maraketh may be honourable... but I found her lack of ambition... pathetic.

If you attempt to remove her... She will perish with her first breath of air outside that chamber... Her fate and mine are already sealed.

TujenEndgameOnWhatHesDoing.text: Rog and Dannig showed me a few techniques. I'm no expert, but I can manage a couple of basic upgrades.

TujenEndgameOnWhyHesHere.text: We came to Wraeclast in search of some, let's say, historical goings on. Had a bit a trouble finding anything after so long. We figured, why not go back to when it was fresh? <continue>Met a rather talented young woman- well, I shouldn't say. But this Cataclysm, this Corruption, it's the damndest thing... it's like we brought our business with us somehow...

TujenEndgameGreeting.text: You're still here? This must be when you... ah. Right, we're not supposed to say much. We just met, aye.

KetzuliOnKillingXesht.text: Congratulations on your success. <continue>This new Breach Lord, Xesht... you've shown it that Wraeclast will not be so easily trifled with. <continue>Perhaps we will have enough time now... time to research the problem, and seal the weak points in the walls of our reality. <continue>Until I can manage that, keep fighting back the Breach Lord's drones.

KetzuliOnKillingXeshtFinal.text: You've dealt Xesht a serious defeat. <continue>I can see why Doryani has grown to respect you, even if he still doesn't quite like you. <continue>You've given me the time I need to research the breaches, and I believe our devices can begin pushing back. <continue>The Breach Lord's drones may still enter our world temporarily, but the risk of a permanent invasion is minimal.

KetzuliOnBreach.text: The breach you encountered was a weakness in the walls of reality. <continue>I've read about the Cult of the Purple flame in our archives... <continue>They worship beings from beyond this world. <continue>These creatures may seek to use our vulnerability to enter Wraeclast. <continue>If you find and collect residual splinters of breach energy, I will study them, and learn what I can about this threat.

KetzuliOnBreachstone.text: The completed breachstone is a gathering of their energies large enough to take to the Realmgate. <continue>There, you can turn their own intrusion against them, and enter the realm those creatures call home. <continue>Remember everything you see, so that we may learn about our enemy.

KetzuliOnDyingBeforeBoss.text: Your excursion through the Realmgate gave us valuable information about the creatures beyond, but we need to know which Breach Lord we're dealing with. <continue>Try again, until you encounter the being in charge.

KetzuliOnDyingAtBoss.text: Such a violent defence of their home! <continue>Xesht... this is a new Breach Lord. I am not certain what has happened... <continue>If the Cult of Purple Flame here, they might be able to tell us more. <continue>Without that, we must remain wary, and again attempt to defeat this 'Xesht.'

KetzuliOnXeshtGossip.text: It was my understanding that there were five Breach Lords. <continue>Xesht was not one of the names I learned. <continue>I do know that the Cult of Purple Flame believed... strangely enough... <continue>... that the Breach Lords would one day unite into a single being named Xesht-Ula... <continue>... but that is not what you faced. Not exactly. <continue>I wonder if they attempted to merge as prophesied, but something went wrong? <continue>The missing factor seems to be Chayula...

KetzuliOnChayulaGossip.text: Among the mysterious Breach Lords, Chayula alone had followers here on Wraeclast... <continue>... and historically, was successfully communicated with—by the Maraketh—on at least one occasion. <continue>That means, fundamentally, Chayula shares some aspects of thought with us. <continue>He is not a mindless ravager. <continue>We have no idea what his agenda truly is, of course, but if he is not part of Xesht... <continue>It may be in our interest to find him...

KetzuliOnCultMonkGossip.text: I don't think I like your tattoos. Oddly familiar. <continue>I'll keep my thoughts on the Cult private.

KetzuliOnCultGossip.text: Their beliefs were born out of otherworldly remnants and strange dreams. <continue>The Cult itself was a fringe element of Vaal society for centuries... <continue>... with its members often getting themselves banished to far-off lands like Trarthus or Phaaryl. <continue>They never quite died out, though, and pushed for legitimacy. <continue>By the... end... they were influential enough to vie for their own chamber in the Temple of Atzoatl. <continue>If their Lord, Chayula, truly has some measure of attachment to Wraeclast... <continue>... then where is he now, in our time of greatest need?

KetzuliOnDream.text: Shadows plague me in my dreams... <continue>I spend each night running in my nightmares, and I wake exhausted. <continue>This <i>{must} end.

KetzuliOnAcolyteMonkGossip.text: You choose to maintain your faith even after realising the truth. <continue>That is a powerful choice... <continue>We face countless dangers from beyond this world, so any alliance, no matter how strange, might make the difference between survival and annihilation. <continue>I can only hope your faith is justified.

ZolinNewIntroduction.text: I am Zolin. I will assist you in any way I can, for Doryani has ordered me to do so. <continue>Conversation beyond that is not required.

DannigEndgame_QuestExplanation.text: Legendary work! Oh, you're a natural at this. <continue>Wraeclast certainly does spill forth a surprisingly endless amount of undead horrors, doesn't it? <continue>All the better, so that tales of what we do here will inspire others all the more!

DannigEndgame_QuestExplanationFull.text: The most powerful artifact in our known tales was brought to this continent by the first expedition thousands of years ago. <continue>The songs tell of it incinerating evil, purifying tainted fields, and warding off those of ill intent. We could certainly use a relic like that now, in these troubled times... but to find it, we'll have to retrace the steps of those long ago souls. <continue>Only they can tell us the Triskelion Flame's unknown fate. That is why we're here. That is what we seek.

DannigEndgame_MoreOnWhyHere.text: I wish I could tell you more about our grand quest, hero, but the time isn't right. You could say, we're trying to put right what once went wrong. <continue>With the power of refined Verisium, we're rupturing a few holes in Wraeclast's skin, in search of a particular triumph of Kalguuran artifice. We seek... the Triskelion Flame! <continue>Oh, you haven't heard of it yet? Yes, of course. We need it for something very important, and time is growing short...

DannigEndgame_OnRemnants.text: Apparently, there have been a number of civilisations on Wraeclast. We've certainly been finding our fair share. <continue>Each remnant reacts with its own kind of... resentment whenever we unceremoniously destroy it. <continue>Hazard of the job.

DannigEndgame_OnFriends.text: You may encounter my companions out there. Rog, Tujen, Gwennen... we are the intrepid four that boldly sailed across the sea to undertake this grand quest! <continue>If you see them, do tell them you've joined our mission.

DannigEndgame_OnLogbooks.text: To retrace the steps of our forebears, we'll need to find their logbooks. The men and women who recorded our journeys were known as Remembrancers, and they wrote down every detail for posterity. <continue>Logbooks were designed to be durable, and to survive through the ages, so you should still be able to find them... wherever they've ended up. <continue>Bring them to me, and we'll set up an expedition. Ultimately, we must find the resting place of Olroth, the legendary hero... and with him, hopefully, the Triskelion Flame!

DannigEndgame_FoundLogbookInTown.text: You found a logbook! <continue>Let me decipher it, and we'll set up an expedition!

DannigEndgame_FoundLogbookInMap.text: You found a logbook! <continue>Let's bring it somewhere safe, so I have time to decipher it. Then, we'll set up an expedition!

DannigEndgame_ExpeditionBossDefeated.text: [DNT-UNUSED] Good work on defeating Olroth, Origin of the Fall. Keep clearing Expeditions!

DannigEndgame_IfFailedLogbook.text: Can't win them all. That expedition was simply too dangerous. <continue>We'll press on to new territories.

DannigEndgame_FirstLogbookNoOlroth.text: I hardly expected to find Olroth on our first successful expedition together, but one does get one's hopes up. <continue>In any case, you held your own. Worthy of a song!  <continue>Let's keep looking.

DannigEndgame_DieToOlroth.text: Olroth was <i>{the} great hero. There's no shame in being defeated by such a force. <continue>Still, lives depend upon our success. Let's keep at it.

DannigEndgame_PostOlrothFirst.text: The hero returns! We simply must hear your glorious tale! <continue>That battle certainly sounds like one for the ages! The Triskelion Flame was destroyed, I take it? Yes... I expected as much. Wraeclast is a torturous mistress... all we can do is press on. <continue>Triumph is not found in a single victory, but in the will to keep working on a task that may never end. This isn't the first time I thought our long search was finally over, and it won't be the last.

DannigEndgame_PostOlrothSubsequent.text: Triumph is not found in a single victory, but in the will to keep working on a task that may never end. This isn't the first time I thought our long search was finally over, and it won't be the last.

DannigEndgame_OnTriskelionFlame.text: Twenty years is a very long time to search for something. I've wanted so badly to find the Flame, and for so long... it's an agonizing feeling, a close kin to madness, to finally find what you seek—only to cause its destruction. <continue>For years, I lived with that secret, that pain, that I kept from the others. And then... I found Olroth again. The Flame, too. Was the first a fake? My heart soared at the prospect of another chance, only to have my hopes dashed for a second time. Then, a third. And a fourth. <continue>Every few years, Wraeclast twists the knife in my gut. Are these memories real? Are they nightmares? This land has become my home, but I'll never feel truly at ease so long as the very earth itself offers up twisted lies... and I can never give up, either, because I still hold on to the maddening hope that the next one might really be it... or the hope that, if I send you instead, things might turn out differently...

DannigEndgame_WhyWeAreHere.text: We are on a grand quest through time! We'll have to save the explanations for another time, however. All I can say is, we purposely came back to this city, Utzaal, before our own ancestors arrived on Wraeclast. <i>{Will} arrive on Wraeclast, I mean. <continue>We've got less than a year to achieve our aims. We have to be gone before they get here, or my historical sagas will get very complicated, very quickly.

DannigEndgame_IntroFirstTime.text: Hail, hero! I knew I'd find you here. <continue>You've made it this far. Clearly, you must have some talent. Care to lend your skills to a matter of honour?

DannigEndgame_OnBadDreams.text: Bad dreams? No. At least, not any new ones. <continue>For years, I've had recurring dreams of what was publicly done to our comrades-in-arms after we lost... well, I guess you could call it a war back home. <continue>Come to think of it, I distinctly recall a shadow-cloaked figure intruding on my nightmare not too long ago. He took one look around, and told me that he 'wasn't even going to get near this one'... <continue>Honestly, I don't blame him.

SanctumWinterSekhemaGlyphFirst.text:
The proving grounds for the sisterhood is complete. Though it broke many bones and some backs, the triumph is ours to behold. Zarokh has been a most helpful aid. 

He came to us a taljari but now he is something more.

SanctumWinterSekhemaGlyphSecond.text:
The akharas have embraced the trial. It is fortuitous that the sisters of the sands understand the value of tradition, even those that are forged anew. 

Zarokh has started the process of blessing the halls within. It worried some sisters, but he means well and I believe it will bring luck to the aspirants who come here.

SanctumWinterSekhemaGlyphThird.text:
The air has cooled. The sun is low... And I am betrayed. I see what he is. I see what a fool I have been. He is more than just some deceitful soothsayer though.... Zarokh... He manipulates time itself. Where did he gain such power? 

I must find a way to fix this.

SanctumWinterSekhemaGlyphFourth.text:
I have managed to trap him in the farthest halls of the Trial. Halls that are unrequired of the Sekhemas who will come here. I have also invoked the ritual. He is bound there for his crimes... A djinn. But as he is bound there, I am here. 

Whatever foul curse he has placed upon these halls has sealed me here... Not so much in place but in time. Caught between now and tomorrow, but never thereafter. 

I'm tired but... I must find my escape.

SanctumWinterSekhemaGlyphFifth.text:
Future Sekhema, should you read this message, do not venture further. My eyes are as dry as the sands in these halls. My lips shrivel and my bones ache. 

He has robbed me of everything. He and I shall remain bound in this eternal torment. But you must not continue. 

Now, I shall rest awhile.

JamanraGlyph_BookOfJamanra.text:
Our people have lived in the shadows of the dunes for too long. 

Countless generations have been forgotten, will be forgotten. We are not 'Faridun,' we are Maraketh, and if we work together — if we unite — then they will be forced to acknowledge us. 

We must show them that casting us off is a mistake. We must show them our strength. 

Perhaps we can one day rebuild Keth itself, for all those who live in the Plains of Vastiri.

RogEndgameOnWhyWeAreHere.text: Uh, it's a bit complicated. It's... hard to explain. You'll know more soon. I hope it's okay if I ask you to just trust us for now.

RogEndgameIntroFirstTime.text: Oh, it's you! Um, not that we know each other... nice to meet you, friend! <continue>I'm Rog. I specialise in logistics and planning. Now I don't know how you've survived out here on your own, but I'll do what I can to support you with my supply skills! From the back. Far from combat.

TreasureHunterSebastian_InfestedBarrens.text: This jungle isn't just alive—it's teeming with things that want you dead. Boars, bugs, ants, antlions... and that's just the wildlife. Fight through all that, and you've still got the undead to contend with. Now do you see why so many have drawn their last breath here?

TreasureHunterSebastian_Oswald.text: Oswald's a seasoned leader, and I've seen him guide many an expedition. Yet, this one has claimed more lives than any other. He puts on a brave face, but I suspect he feels the weight of every loss. He arms explorers with all the wisdom he can, but survival ultimately depends on their willingness to listen.

TreasureHunterSebastian_TheExpedition.text: The Vaal have captured the imaginations of archaeologists and adventurers for centuries, leaving little of their legacy untouched. It's no wonder the Kalguurans are paying so richly for what remains. As for their motives? That's a mystery I've yet to unravel.

TreasureHunterSebastian_TheWarringTribes.text: We were warned about the threat of the local tribes, but witnessing their brutality firsthand is... something else. No field report can prepare you for the sight of a man being flayed alive, or the sound of sinew torn from bone. The Azak are a vicious, unrelenting horde – and they train their beasts to be the same. The Orok, by contrast... not as sadistic, nor as smart. But just as lethal.

TreasureHunterGwendolyn_JungleRuins.text: I could've gone my whole life without watching snakes coil around a corpse or getting pounded into the dirt by a homicidal ape. It's enough to make a girl question her career choices. <continue>Still, the treasure keeps me coming back. You can't take two steps around here without tripping over some old Vaal ruin, all tangled up in the undergrowth.

TreasureHunterGwendolyn_OswaldAlva.text: They make an odd pair of colleagues, don't they? Oswald's the kind to worry about the jungle eating him, and Alva's the type to dare it to try. Perhaps that's why their partnership has been more lucrative than most - they balance each other out.

TreasureHunterGwendolyn_TreasureHunters.text: Survivors, halfwits and the occasional lunatic - that's our expedition in a nutshell. Used to be, we were seasoned veterans out here. These days, if a newcomer lasts more than a week, it's a cause for celebration. <continue>Still, with the Kalguurans throwing coin around, plenty of folks are willing to risk their lives for a shot at the spoils.

TreasureHunterGwendolyn_Quadrillas.text: Apes are one thing, but quadrillas? Now they're fearsome. <continue>The Vaal left these lands drowning in Corruption after their Cataclysm — guess it twisted the creatures here into something unnatural. <continue>Still, I can't help but think... four arms could come in handy, wouldn't you say? No pun intended.

TreasureHunterGwendolyn_SilverfistSeen.text: You saw the Mighty Silverfist and lived to tell the tale? Few can say the same. In fact, I've half a mind to call you a liar. But if you're telling the truth, don't let it go to your head. <continue>He's ruled this part of the jungle for a long, <i>{long} time. Any who wander too close tend to regret it... though not for very long.

TreasureHunterGwendolyn_SilverfistSlain.text: You killed him? Well, remind me not to cross you then. Should be a lot easier to move through the jungle without him around, so in that sense, you have my thanks. In another... wasn't really necessary, was it?
